reading: The 'shi' in 'sheep' — picture a sheep in a suit, serving tea to a gentleman, attending to his every need with a polite bow.

meaning: A person at the side (化) is the 'other' — someone standing apart from you, not part of your group. The 'to be' (也) part just adds a classical flavor of existence, but the image is that side person being the other.
reading: タ — Imagine a 'ta' (like 'taco') being handed to the person at the side — they are the 'other' who gets the taco, not you.

meaning: A person at the side (化) holds a vertical stroke (｜) with a one (一) and a dot (丶) — the dot is the tip of a cane, and the person leans on it as a walking stick.
reading: The sound is 'jou' — imagine a traveler saying 'jou' as he taps his cane on the ground, each tap a 'jou'. (ジョウ)

meaning: A person at the side (化) hands a measurement (寸) to you — you attach it, adhere it, and append it to the wall.
reading: Think of 'foo' (フ) — a person at the side says 'foo!' as they attach a measurement tape to your arm, sticking it on firmly.

meaning: A person at the side of a mountain, living alone in the peaks — that's a hermit or wizard, far from the world.
reading: A hermit sits on a mountain and says 'sen' (as in 'sensei') to the clouds below. (セン)

meaning: A hat on top (个) sits above a mountain (山) — the hat is blown off by the wind and flies up, soaring over the peak.
reading: The sound is 'ken' — think of a kite (ken) flying high above the mountain, soaring like the hat. (ケン)

meaning: A person at the side (化) is a young girl, but she acts strange — she sweeps a hook stroke (乙) with a sweeping stroke (ノ) as if it were a wand, and the one (一) line above her head is her odd halo.
reading: The young girl says 'ta' as she taps her foot impatiently — 'ta' like the first beat of 'taco' — and the strange part is she's tapping to a rhythm only she hears.

meaning: A person at the side (化) measures a fathom with a sword (刀) that has a dot (丶) on its tip — the dot marks the exact length of one fathom.
reading: The fathom is measured by a 'jin' — imagine a genie (jin) stretching his arms exactly one fathom wide, holding the sword with the dot.

meaning: A person at the side (化) counts a thousand using a sweeping stroke (ノ) and a ten (十) — the sweeping stroke sweeps away nine hundred, leaving just one ten, but the person insists it's a thousand.
reading: The thousand is counted by a 'sen' — imagine a senator (sen) counting a thousand votes, each vote a tiny sweeping stroke (ノ) on a ten (十) tally sheet.

meaning: A person at the side (化) is strong and valiant — he lifts a hook stroke (乙) with one (一) hand, while a sweeping stroke (ノ) is his cape blowing in the wind.
reading: The strong one shouts 'kitsu' as he lifts the hook — imagine a kitsune (kitsu) fox spirit, strong and valiant, lifting the hook stroke with its tail.

meaning: A person at the side (化) holding a piling (弋) — they step in to substitute for the one who left, changing the setup.
reading: Imagine a substitute teacher walking in and saying 'DIE' (ダイ) as the class groans — he's the replacement.

meaning: A hat on top (个) sits over a seal (卩) and a one (一) — the seal stamps the one law, and the hat is the authority that issues the command.
reading: レイ — The command is a “ray” (レイ) of light from the seal — it strikes down and everyone must obey.

meaning: A vertical stroke (｜) stands next to a person (人) with a dot (丶) — the person uses the stroke as a pointer, saying "by means of this, compare that."
reading: イ — Imagine a person pointing with a stick and saying "Ee!" (イ) — like "Ee, look at that!" — to compare two things.

meaning: This character has no parts listed, but it means 'tribe' — picture a tribe of people standing together, each one a simple stroke, forming a tight group with no single leader.
reading: The tribe's name is 'mu' — imagine the tribe chanting 'mu' in unison, a low hum that vibrates through the ground as they march.

meaning: A person at the side (化) measures a fathom with a sword (刀) that has a dot (丶) on its tip — the dot marks the exact length, just like 仞 but with a sharper edge.
reading: The fathom is measured by a 'jin' — imagine a genie (jin) again, but this time he's using the sword's dot (丶) to poke a hole exactly one fathom deep.

meaning: A person at the side leans on a cliff, using a right hand to hold up a temporary shelter — this is just a sham, not a real home.
reading: The sham is a cheap cardboard 'ka' (car) — you park it under the cliff, but it's only interim.

meaning: A person at the side (化) looks up at a seal (卩) stamped high on a wall — you must face-up to read it, depending on the seal's authority.
reading: You look up and gasp 'gyo!' (ギョウ) at the towering seal — the sound of awe as you tilt your head back.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands between two mouths (口) — that person is the go-between, keeping the relationship alive.
reading: Think of 'CHOO' — the go-between sneezes 'CHOO' as he runs between the two mouths. (チュウ)

meaning: A person at the side (化) holds a spoon (匕) — they part company, each taking their own spoon and going separate ways.
reading: ヒ — 'HE' (ヒ) leaves, separating from the group — he goes his own way.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands next to a dry (干) ten (十) — they look similar, like two dry sticks of the same length.
reading: コ — 'CO' (コ) — two similar twins say 'co-' as in 'co-pilot', both alike.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands next to a cow (牛) — this is a specific affair or case, like a farm incident to be handled.
reading: ケン — Imagine a KEN (ケン) — a wooden sword — used to settle a case between a person and a cow.

meaning: A person at the side is holding a hat on top, but underneath that hat is a pair of legs — this odd figure is a man with shellfish, a merchant who carries his wares on his head.
reading: カイ — The man with shellfish shouts 'KAI! KAI!' as he sells his clams at the market.

meaning: A person at the side (化) hands a duty to a king (王) who is also a gentleman (士) — the king takes on the responsibility and term of office.
reading: ニン — Imagine a NIN (ニン) — a ninja — entrusted with a secret mission by the king, responsible for its success.

meaning: A person at the side hands you a portion — the two splayed strokes are the knife cutting a slice, and the sword marks the boundary of your duty.
reading: フン — You get your portion and go 'FUN!' — a quick puff of satisfaction as you take your share.

meaning: A person at the side with a pig's head variant on top, and three stacked strokes below — the pig's head is heavy, so the whole figure bows its head low, drooping down.
reading: テイ — The head hangs so low it touches the ground — 'TEI' like the low 'tide' pulling everything down.

meaning: A person at the side stands still, holding a direction — the one dot and sweeping stroke show them hesitating, imitating a statue, not moving anywhere.
reading: ホウ — The person imitates a 'HOE' — they stand still holding it like a tool, copying a gardener's pose.

meaning: A person at the side with two splayed strokes and the katakana-mu shape — the strokes are arms flailing, the mu shape is a mouth open wide — this person is excited, jumping up and down.
reading: ショウ — The excited person shouts 'SHOW!' — like a performer bursting onto stage, all energy.

meaning: A stop sign is under a hat on top. The hat is a disguise — someone stops, puts on the hat, and schemes a plan to sneak past.
reading: キ — Picture a 'key' (キ) that unlocks a secret scheme hidden under the hat.

meaning: A person at the side with a barb and a マ-shaped stroke — the barb is a sharp jawline, the マ is a stylish hat — this person is handsome, striking a pose.
reading: ヨ — The handsome one says 'YO!' — a cool greeting, like a stylish friend nodding at you.

meaning: A person at the side has a heart that is trembling — they are nervous and fearful, like someone waiting for bad news.
reading: The nervous person's heart goes 'shin' as it jumps — imagine a loud 'shin' sound echoing from their chest.

meaning: A person at the side stands next to a table with a lid on it — they are the same kind as the other, so they compare with each other side by side.
reading: They compare their heights at the table — 'ko' says one, 'u' says the other, making a 'kou' sound as they measure.

meaning: A vertical stroke stands beside three stacked strokes, while a person at the side points to that one — that one is Italy.
reading: You see that one person in Italy, and you say 'ee' (like 'e' in 'eel') — that's the sound of '伊'.

meaning: A person at the side has a dot on their head, a right hand reaching out, and a 'from' mark — they are deceptive, hiding their true intent behind a fake gesture.
reading: The deceptive one says 'kyuu' as they reach out with a right hand — like a sly 'kyuu' of a trickster.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands next to the number five (五) — that's the fifth member of a five-man squad, lined up in a file.
reading: The squad marches in step, counting 'GO' — each step is a firm 'GO' on the ground.

meaning: A person at the side holds a branch in their right hand with ten leaves — their deed is a skill, like a performer's trick.
reading: The skilled performer does a 'gi' move with the branch — a sharp 'gi' as they strike a pose.

meaning: A person at the side (化) lies prostrated next to a dog (犬) — both bow down low, covering the ground, as if hiding from something above.
reading: You 'fuku' (フク) down flat like a folded cloth — the sound of flopping to the floor in submission.

meaning: A person at the side (化) raises a halberd (戈) to strike down a tree — that's the act of felling, and also attacking or punishing an enemy.
reading: The halberd comes down with a loud 'BATSU' as it chops the trunk — imagine the sharp crack of the strike.

meaning: A person at the side (化) leans against a tree (木). The person is tired and rests against the tree, taking a day off from work.
reading: Say 'cue' (キュウ) — you take a rest when you hear the cue to stop working, like a bell or a whistle.

meaning: A person at the side carries a large load with two hands — they are a common laborer, doing heavy work for others.
reading: The laborer shouts 'fu' as they lift the large load — a grunt of effort, 'fu'.

meaning: A person stands under a hat on top, and another person is beside — but there are three people total, so it's a multitude, a crowd, the masses.
reading: The crowd chants 'gin' together — a low, humming 'gin' from the masses.

meaning: A person at the side (化) is holding a fire (火) — that's your companion, sharing the cooking fire and the utensils.
reading: カ — Imagine a companion saying 'Ka!' as they toss a log onto the fire, the sparks flying like a 'car' (カ) engine revving.

meaning: Under the 'two' lines (a roof) and the 'a hat on top' (a person's hat), the 'katakana-mu shape' (厶) is a person sitting — so you see two people meeting under a roof, having a party.
reading: You meet at a 'kai' (カイ) — like 'kite' but with a short 'a' — imagine a kite flying at a meeting, that's the on-reading カイ.

meaning: A person at the side (化) of a nine (九) and a ten (十) — this is your son, standing beside you, a mix of your nine and ten parts.
reading: Imagine your son is a 'sigh' (サイ) of relief — every time he comes home safe, you let out a long 'sigh' (サイ).

meaning: A person at the side (化) hands a message to another person, who walks along (二) and passes it on, like a relay — the message transmits along the path.
reading: Imagine a 'den' (like a bear's den) where a message is passed from one person to another, each one walking along to the next den to transmit the news.

meaning: A person at the side uses a right hand to push against a woman — that's making a great effort, straining together.
reading: You DO (like 'do' in 'do it!') the heavy lifting, grunting with effort.

meaning: A person at the side of white — the chief or count stands beside a white banner, the highest rank among the elders (uncle).
reading: ハク — Imagine a HACK-saw-wielding earl who chops wood to build his estate — he's the chief, but he still does the dirty work.

meaning: A person at the side holds a mouth and a ten — they're talking prices, doing business, selling goods for ten coins.
reading: The merchant shouts 'KO' (like 'co' in 'cost') to set the price.

meaning: A person at the side wears a hat on top, with a little person underneath — that's 'you', the one addressed, the second person.
reading: You say 'NI' (like 'knee') — pointing at the other person's knee to say 'you'.

meaning: A person at the side (化) with two short strokes (并) and a vertical stroke (｜) plus ten (十) — this person stands beside you, accompanying you and bringing you along as a companion.
reading: ハン — Picture a 'han' (ハン) — a 'hand' (ハン) that reaches out to accompany you, bringing you along as a companion on the journey.

meaning: A person at the side (化) wears a hat on top (个) and holds a seal (卩) — that's the actor, performing with props and costume.
reading: The actor takes a bow on stage, and the crowd shouts 'RAY!' (レイ) — like a spotlight ray hitting him.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands by a vertical stroke (｜) that connects a day (日) to a rice field (田) — the descendent who inherits the family line through time.
reading: The descendent chews (チュウ) on a rice stalk from the field, tasting the family's history.

meaning: A person at the side stretches a vertical stroke across a day and a rice field — extending the line to cover more ground.
reading: シン — Think of a shin (シン) stretching forward as you extend your leg to take a long step.

meaning: A person at the side (化) has only one eye (目) open — that's dull and slow, unskillful at seeing clearly.
reading: The dull person says 'SHOW' (ショ) me again — they need everything repeated slowly.

meaning: A person at the side (化) with a mouth (口) and a barb (亅) on top of a one (一) — you approach that person to ask a question, paying respects.
reading: You visit a shrine and say 'SHI' (like 'she' but with a short 'i') as you bow — the respectful sound is 'シ'.

meaning: A person at the side (化) carries a dry (干) stick with ten (十) notches and two splayed strokes (ハ) — that's the messenger's tally to prove his errand.
reading: The messenger hops (ホウ) from door to door, delivering the news.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands next to a person (人) with a dot (丶) on top, both looking alike, becoming a counterfeit copy.
reading: ジ — A gee (ジ) like a 'gee whiz' moment when you see how much they resemble each other.

meaning: A person at the side (化) opens their mouth (口) to call for power (力) — that's nursing, attending to someone who needs strength.
reading: A nurse says 'KA (カ)!' as she lifts a patient — the sound of gentle care and support.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands with a vertical stroke (｜), a dot (丶), and a sweeping stroke (ノ) — all bold and strong, making him mighty.
reading: The mighty hero says 'HEY!' (ヘ) and the mountains tremble.

meaning: A person at the side (化) looks into a mouth (口) that is shaped like a vertical stroke (｜) — the mouth resembles the person's own, so they look alike.
reading: The child's face resembles the father's — 'JEE' (ジ) that's a spitting image!

meaning: A person at the side (化) works the rice field (田) — a cultivated rice field.
reading: The field is so 'ten' (テン)se, you can feel the tension in the soil.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands next to a day (日) that is marked by a single line (一) — that line is the 'but' that interrupts the day, so the scene means 'however, but'.
reading: タン — Imagine a 'tan' (like a suntan) line on your arm, but you say 'however' — the tan is only on one side, a but-mark.

meaning: A person at the side stands under a roof, holding a barb — they stop and linger there, a still figure in the doorway.
reading: Imagine the person at the side saying 'CHO' as they stop, like a choo-choo train that halts at the station.

meaning: A person at the side uses a towel to spread news across an upside-down box, while a sweeping stroke and a vertical stroke mark the public announcement.
reading: The towel flaps in the wind as the person shouts 'HO!' to spread the word far and wide.

meaning: A person at the side kneels on soil, holding the katakana-mu shape — this is the divine being whose surname is chanted in Sanskrit.
reading: The divine being chants 'KYO' — like 'kyo' in 'kyoto' — as they sit on the soil.

meaning: A person at the side hands a sword to a mouth, so the message can continue and be carried down through generations.
reading: The sword is passed with a shout of 'SHO' — like 'show' — to join the next in line.

meaning: A person at the side uses a spoon to stop a small thing from growing — the spoon and the stop sign both point to its tiny size.
reading: The small thing says 'SHI' — like 'she' — as she is tiny and easily stopped by a spoon.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands up (立) — that's the rank: the one who stands up first gets the highest throne.
reading: The rank is 'i' (like 'ee') — imagine a person standing up and saying 'Ee! I'm the highest!' with a squeaky voice.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands next to a family name (氏) with a one (一) mark — that person is lower, shorter.
reading: テイ — A 'tater' (テイ) is a short, low potato — humble and close to the ground.

meaning: A king (王) with a dot (丶) on his head stands beside a person at the side (化) — the king and his helper dwell together in the palace.
reading: The king dwells in a 'juu' (like 'jew' but with a long 'u') — imagine a jeweler living in a castle, counting gems.

meaning: A person at the side (化) uses craft (工) to help — the assistant stands beside you, lending skilled aid.
reading: SA (サ) — a samurai's assistant helps him with his craft, standing at his side.

meaning: A person at the side (化) opens their mouth (口) to call for help — that person is the one who assists, lending a hand when you're in trouble.
reading: Imagine a helper shouting 'YOU! (ユウ) I need assistance!' — the sound of the cry is 'yuu'.

meaning: A tree (木) with one (一) branch, and a person at the side (化) — the tree's trunk is like a body, and the person leans against it for support, making it real and solid.
reading: タイ — Imagine a TIE (タイ) wrapped around a tree trunk — the tree's body is now dressed, giving it substance and reality.

meaning: A person at the side uses a divining rod to poke a mouth, occupying it by force and usurping its speech.
reading: The divining rod pokes the mouth with a 'CHIN' — like 'chin' (the chin) — to take possession.

meaning: A person at the side (化) holds a mouth (口) open in confusion — asking 'what?' — while a barb (亅) pokes up from the ground and a one (一) lies flat beneath.
reading: You ask 'what?' (なに) when you see a 'nanny' (na-nee) holding a strange object.

meaning: A person at the side stands under a roof, holding a spoon — but they are alone, so they feel proud of their independence yet lonely.
reading: The lonely person at the side says 'ta' as in 'ta-da' — but no one is there to hear it. (タ)

meaning: A hat on top of two little lines, with a show of a person at the side — this is the surname of the one who wears the hat and shows off.
reading: The surname owner says 'sha' like 'shah' — a royal title, but here it's just a family name. (シャ)

meaning: One (一) and two (二) with two splayed strokes (ハ) sit under a hat (个), but a barb (亅) pokes out — too much stuff spills over, leaving surplus.
reading: The surplus spills like a yo-yo (ヨ) — picture a yo-yo rolling off the table, leaving extra string everywhere.

meaning: A person at the side with a sweeping stroke and a large two — the person hides the mistake, then finds peace in losing the evidence.
reading: The lost one says 'itsu' like 'it's you' — but you can't find them, so it's a mystery. (イツ)

meaning: A vertical stroke and a sweeping stroke join a person at the side with a bow — this is the France of the East, where the bow is for the Buddha.
reading: The bow-wielding person says 'butsu' like 'boots' — but they're not kicking, they're praying. (ブツ)

meaning: A person at the side (化) is using a sweeping stroke (ノ) to draw a vertical stroke (｜) and a one (一) on top of a 乞-shaped part (乞) — that's how they make something new.
reading: The maker says 'サク' as they quickly 'sack' the old version to build a fresh one.

meaning: A person at the side with a mouth and a wrapping enclosure — the foolish one is stooped over, mouth wrapped shut, unable to speak sense.
reading: The stooped fool says 'kou' like 'cow' — a cow that bends down to graze, looking foolish. (コウ)

meaning: A person at the side with a woman and two — the woman uses two words of flattery, but it's all insincerity.
reading: The flatterer says 'nei' like 'nay' — but they say 'nay' with a smile, meaning 'yes' insincerely. (ネイ)

meaning: A person at the side (化) stoops down (夂) to pick up a dot (丶) — that's the name of someone who's always bending to help others.
reading: トウ — A 'toe' (トウ) is the name of the part of your foot that bends down, just like the stooping figure.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands next to a little (小) dot (丶) and a one (一) — that person is 'you', the one being addressed.
reading: Imagine pointing at someone and saying 'NIce to meet you' — the 'ni' in 'NIce' is the sound of 你.

meaning: A person at the side (化) works for a commission fee, using (用) their skills — the vertical stroke (｜) and one (一) show the contract they sign.
reading: ヨウ — 'Yo!' (ヨウ) — you call out to the hired worker to get their commission fee.

meaning: A person at the side (化) has a towel (巾) on a table (几) with a one (一) on top — they are wearing a sword at their side.
reading: The knight's sword hangs from a HIKE (ハイ) — imagine him hiking up a mountain with the sword clanking at his side.

meaning: A person at the side (化) walks around a mouth (口) inside a box (囗) — going around in circles, hesitating.
reading: カイ — 'Kai' (カイ) — like a 'kite' (カイト) circling in the sky, going around and around, hesitating to land.

meaning: An old man (老) with a person at the side (化) and a spoon (匕) — a mature man, a big person (Cantonese 'man').
reading: ロウ — 'Row' (ロウ) — an old man rows a boat slowly, mature and steady — the sound is 'rou'.

meaning: A person at the side (化) pretends to be a king (王) with two short strokes on top (并) and a sheep (羊) — false, feigned royalty.
reading: ヨウ — 'Yo' (ヨウ) — you say 'yo' to a sheep (羊) pretending to be a king — the sound is 'you'.

meaning: A person at the side stands next to a white field with a single line (一) dividing it — that line is the east-west path between paddies, and the person is the leader of a hundred men working the rice fields.
reading: ヒャク — Imagine a hundred men all shouting 'HYAK!' as they stomp the paddies, the sound echoing off the white (白) path.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands on soil (土) — this person is excellent and beautiful, pleasing to all who see them.
reading: The excellent person is a KA (カ) — like a 'car' that runs smoothly, everything about them is good.

meaning: A person at the side joins with two hands and two short strokes on top — they all come together, uniting into one collective group.
reading: The two groups said 'HEY!' and joined hands, uniting into one team. (ヘイ)

meaning: A person at the side watches a gentleman (士) speak with a mouth (口) — the gentleman's words are healthy and correct, so the person nods in approval.
reading: キツ — The gentleman's correct speech is so sharp it 'KITS' the air like a knife, each word a clean cut.

meaning: A person at the side turns away from the northeast (艮) direction — they act contrary to the wind that blows from that corner, stubbornly going the other way.
reading: コン — The person stomps their foot and says 'KON!' (like 'con' in contrary) as they refuse to follow the northeast path.

meaning: A person at the side brings a mouth (口) and a tongue (舌) together — they meet to talk, gathering (あつ.まる) in one place to exchange words.
reading: カツ — Two people meet and slap hands with a 'KATSU!' (like a karate chop) — the sound of a successful meeting.

meaning: A person at the side leans against a cliff (厂) under a wrapping enclosure (勹) with a seal (卩) — they depend on this shelter for support, but the seal is crooked, so they go against the rules.
reading: キ — The person leans on the cliff and says 'KEY' (like a key) — they need a key to unlock the seal, but it's against the rules.

meaning: A person at the side wears a hat on top (个) and stands before a king (王) — this person is a fairy, a magical being who serves the king from the heavens.
reading: セン — The fairy floats down from the sky with a 'SEN' (like 'send') — they send blessings to the king below.

meaning: A person at the side (化) is standing on ice (冫) with a pair of legs (儿) that keep slipping — that's the essence of frivolity, a light, unserious wobble.
reading: The frivolous person at the side (化) is so light they float up like a 'cho' (チョウ) of air — imagine a tiny puff of breath lifting them off the ice.

meaning: A person at the side (化) is under a lid (亠) with a father (父) — the father hides his sly, beautiful tricks under that lid, deceiving everyone with a clever smile.
reading: The sly father (父) under the lid (亠) whispers 'kyo' (キョウ) like a fox's cunning call — that's the sound of his beautiful deception.

meaning: A person (人) at the side (化) holds a wrapping enclosure (勹) that lacks (欠) something — so they use a sweeping stroke (ノ) to pull a one (一) from the soil (土) to aid and help.
reading: The helper's swift move is a 'shi' (シ) — like a quick 'she' who darts in to aid, grabbing the one (一) from the soil (土) before anyone sees.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands with two splayed strokes (ハ) over a month (月) — that's the row of dancers, each with legs splayed in a line for the month's festival.
reading: The dancers' row moves in a single 'itsu' (イツ) beat — imagine them all stepping together with a crisp 'its' sound, like a metronome for the month (月).

meaning: A person at the side (化) holds a dart (矢) and a mouth (口) to give orders — this is a messenger sent on a mission.
reading: The messenger's mission is to deliver a 'she' (シ) — like saying 'she' goes, but the sound is 'shi'.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands on a pair of legs (儿) over ten (十) and soil (土) with a sweeping stroke (ノ) and a one (一) — that's a crowd, many legs trampling the soil in a line.
reading: The crowd's murmur is a low 'shin' (シン) — like a 'shin' of people shuffling, their feet scraping the soil (土) in a dense pack.

meaning: A person at the side (化) uses a sweeping stroke (ノ) to hand a spoon (匕) to someone under a dotted cliff (广) — that's the act of commissioning, entrusting that spoon to a deputy.
reading: The entrusted spoon is passed with a 'taku' (タク) — imagine a firm 'tock' as the spoon taps the dotted cliff (广), sealing the commission.

meaning: A person at the side stands firm by a mouth that speaks truth next to a stream of clear water — this is the image of a strong, righteous peacemaker who will not be swayed.
reading: The strong, righteous one is a KAN-do attitude leader — think of a KAN (カン) do spirit that never backs down.

meaning: A person stands on soil under a one, but the katakana-mu shape traps them — this is the stubborn nephew who refuses to move from his spot.
reading: Your nephew is a SHIT-su (シツ) — he’s a little shit who won’t leave the dirt.

meaning: A person gives a mysterious short thread under a lid to another person, but the two splayed strokes show it’s all wrapped up — this is giving something that is already prepared and embraced in the package.
reading: The gift is a KAI (カイ) — like a kayak, it carries everything inside, ready to go.

meaning: A person with two splayed strokes walks toward a tree, with a vertical stroke and a ten marking the path — this is the coming of someone due next, the cause of the arrival.
reading: The person comes with a RAI (ライ) — like a ray of light that arrives from the sun.

meaning: A person at the side lounges in the evening, surrounded by luxury — this is the pride of having too much, showing off at dusk.
reading: Luxury and pride make you SHI (シ) — like a sheik who flaunts his wealth at sunset.

meaning: A person at the side stands under esteem, with a pair of legs and a one — this is the big, grand figure who commands respect.
reading: The big one is a KOU (コウ) — like a cow that is huge and takes up the whole field.

meaning: A person at the side stands next to a bare bone that has been reaped — this is the custom or example of what happens to all.
reading: レイ — Picture a 'ray' of light shining on the bare bone as an example for the person at the side to follow.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands on soil (土) with a measurement (寸) in hand — this is the waiter or samurai who serves, measuring out portions precisely while waiting upon you.
reading: ジ — Picture a samurai saying 'gee' (ジ sounds like 'ji' as in 'jii' an old man) as he bows low — the sound of his respectful greeting is what a waiter or samurai does when serving.

meaning: A person at the side is pressing down on rice with their hand, soothing it into a flat, settled layer — like calming a fussy child by patting them down.
reading: ビ — Picture a bee (ビ) gently buzzing over the rice, soothing it to sleep with its soft hum.

meaning: A person at the side stands next to a cow that has a sweeping stroke on its back and a tree with two splayed strokes — this odd figure is a supporting post in a stage play, an actor holding up the scene.
reading: シュ — Imagine a shoe (シュ) being used as a supporting post to prop up a wobbly actor on stage.

meaning: A person at the side places a dish of blood under an upside-down box — the whole scene is hushed, so quiet you can hear the blood drip.
reading: キョク — Think of a quiet 'kyoku' (曲) — a slow, silent musical piece — where even the dish and blood make no sound.

meaning: A person at the side holds up a one and a month, offering them like a plate of food — urging you to eat, to take a bite of time itself.
reading: ユウ — Say 'you' (ユウ) to a friend while pushing a plate toward them — 'You, eat!' — that's the urge.

meaning: A person at the side stands next to a cow with a katakana-mu shape on its back — both are exactly the same height, equal in every way.
reading: ボウ — Picture a bow (ボウ) tied around both the person and the cow — they are equal, both wearing the same bow.

meaning: A hat on top sits over an upside-down box, which contains a tome held by two hands — you think carefully, methodically, stacking these parts in order.
reading: リン — Ring (リン) a bell slowly, one chime at a time, as you methodically think through each page of the tome.

meaning: A person at the side (化) under an upside-down box (冂) with a mouth (口) and one (一) is a big, ignorant rustic who stubs his toe.
reading: トウ (tō) sounds like 'toe' — imagine a big, ignorant rustic stubbing his toe.

meaning: A person at the side (化) under a roof (宀) with a sweeping stroke (ノ) and a hook stroke (乙) is proud and lonely, like a hermit saying 'ta-da' alone.
reading: タ (ta) sounds like 'ta-da' — imagine a proud hermit saying 'ta-da' in his lonely hut.

meaning: A person at the side (化) wrapped in a wrapping enclosure (勹) with a day (日) is fast, like a runner who shuns the slow.
reading: シュン (shun) sounds like 'shun' — imagine a fast runner who shuns slowpokes.

meaning: A person at the side (化) holds up two splayed strokes (ハ) like a tray, offering a meal to a vertical stroke (｜) standing on one (一) — this is how you submit and serve.
reading: You serve the meal with a polite 'kyo' (キョウ) — like a butler saying 'kyo-kyo' as he bows and presents the dish.

meaning: A person at the side (化) leans on a garment (衣) — they depend on it for warmth, so they are reliant on it, and consequently they stay close.
reading: イ — Picture 'ee' (イ) — a person leaning on a garment says 'ee' (like 'easy') because they feel reliant and safe.

meaning: A person at the side (化) — which is a person (人) with two short strokes on top (并) — plus a large (大) and two (二) — this tomboy stands beside you, full of chivalry and boldness.
reading: The tomboy says 'KYOU' (キョウ) — like 'kyo' — as she strikes a heroic pose, ready to defend the weak.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands next to the west (西) — the west side has the price tag, the value of the goods.
reading: The price is 'KA' (like 'car') — a car's value is its price — カ.

meaning: A deceased (亡) person at the side (化) with a woman (女) suggests flattery and insincerity — imagine a person flattering a woman about a deceased relative.
reading: ネイ (nei) sounds like 'nay' — imagine a flatterer saying 'nay' but meaning yes.

meaning: A person at the side (化) with a flag (尸) and a dot (丶) represents 'as it is' — imagine a flag with a dot marking exactly where it stands.
reading: ジン (jin) sounds like 'jinx' — as it is, you're jinxed.

meaning: A person at the side (化) looks at mother (母) and says 'do not (毋)' — but the 乞-shaped part (乞) is the sneer on their face as they scorn her.
reading: You 'BOO' (ブ) the person who makes light of your mother — that's the sound of contempt.

meaning: A person at the side (化) holds a dart (矢) and a ユ-shaped stroke (ユ) with a 乞-shaped part (乞) — this is the lord's ceremonial gear.
reading: The lord's courtiers all bow and chant 'コウ' (kou) — like a cow (コウ) mooing in the courtyard.

meaning: Three stacked strokes (ヨ) and a crown (冖) cover a person at the side (化) while a right hand (又) reaches in — the hand is encroaching and invading the person's space, raiding their crown.
reading: シン — The invader shouts "SHIN!" (シン) as they break through the crown, a sharp "shin" of a sword slicing into the territory.

meaning: A **person at the side** (化) walks with you, and a **mouth** (口) speaks softly — this is your **companion** on the journey.
reading: The sound is **リョ** — imagine a **ryo** (リョ, like "rio") river where you and your **companion** row a boat together.

meaning: A person at the side (化) wrapped in a wrapping enclosure (勹) with a mouth (口) and a flag (尸) is narrow and cramped — imagine a cramped room with a flag.
reading: キョク (kyoku) sounds like 'coke you' — imagine a narrow can of Coke.

meaning: A person at the side (化) leans on a vertical stroke (｜) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) over a day (日) in a rice field (田) — convenience is having a toilet nearby, even in the field.
reading: ベン — A bench (ベン) is a convenient place to sit, and also where you might leave your feces if you're careless.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands next to a large (大) mouth (口) that is open wide — this is a big, imposing figure.
reading: The big guy's name is 'Goo' — like the sound of a giant's grunt, 'グ'.

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) turns a person at the side (化) into a person in charge, who ties a short thread (幺) and a thread (糸) to a little (小) duty — that's their connection.
reading: ケイ — Imagine a 'kayak' (ケイ) where the person in charge ties all the ropes and threads to keep the boat secure.

meaning: A person at the side (化) is pressing on your leg (足) with their mouth (口) open, urging you to stop (止) and move faster — they are stimulating you to hurry.
reading: ソク — Imagine a coach shouting "SOCK!" (ソク) as he urges you to run faster, the sock hitting your leg as a demand for speed.

meaning: A person at the side (化) suddenly grabs a halberd (戈) with a hand (手) — the action is abrupt and improvised.
reading: The sudden grab makes you shout 'Ga!' — like 'ガ' in surprise.

meaning: A person at the side (化) wears an ornamental cap that has a dot (丶) and a one (一) on top, and water (水) drips from it — a fancy cap.
reading: The cap is so fancy you say 'Kyu!' (like 'キュウ') in admiration.

meaning: A person at the side (化) shouts through a mouth (口) while standing on soil (土) with a sweeping stroke (ノ) — that's an urgent message.
reading: The urgent shout sounds like 'Koku' — as in 'コク' — like a quick knock on a door.

meaning: A person at the side (化) with a pair of legs (儿) and a katakana-mu shape (厶) on top, while a stooping figure (夂) bends down — this person is so sagacious and excellent that even the stooping figure looks up in awe.
reading: シュン — Picture a genius named "Shun" (シュン) who wins every contest with a quick, sharp move — his excellence is like a "shoon" of brilliance.

meaning: A person (人) and an eye (目) are placed on a chopping board — this is the altar for sacrifice.
reading: The board is used for 'So' (ソ) — like 'saw' — you saw the meat on it.

meaning: A person at the side (化) has a little (小) mouth (口) and a month (月) shape — this person is pretty and resembles someone else.
reading: The pretty face makes you say 'Shō!' (ショウ) — like 'show' — you want to show it off.

meaning: A person at the side of a grain stalk that has been reaped — this person is so clever they can turn leftover stubble into useful tools.
reading: リ — Imagine a clever person saying 'リ' (ree) as they quickly tie a bundle of reaped grain with a ribbon.

meaning: A person at the side of a マ-shaped stroke that is being utilized — this is a clay effigy, a stand-in figure used in rituals.
reading: ヨウ — Picture a clay effigy that says 'ヨウ' (yo) as it wobbles, like a toy you wind up.

meaning: A person at the side of a see — they use their eyes to compare two things, or to spy on someone from a hiding spot.
reading: ケン — Imagine a spy with a magnifying glass saying 'ケン' (ken) as he compares two footprints in the dirt.

meaning: A person at the side of a mouth and a valley — this is the common folk, who talk loudly in the valley, following vulgar customs.
reading: ゾク — Picture a 'zombie' (ゾク) shuffling through a valley, following the vulgar manners of the crowd — it's all too common.

meaning: A person at the side of a child and a claw — a claw grabs a child, making that person a captive taken in war.
reading: フ — A captive shouts 'フ' (fu) as he is dragged away, like a puff of breath knocked out of him.

meaning: A person at the side of a ri — this person lives far out in the countryside, so their ways are rustic and ill mannered.
reading: リ — Imagine a rustic villager who says 'リ' (ree) as he points to his rice field, proud of his simple life.

meaning: A person at the side of an excuse with a pair of legs and a wrapping enclosure — they bow their head down (look down) and work diligently to avoid the excuse.
reading: フ — Picture a diligent worker who says 'フ' (fu) as he bends down to tie his shoes, focused on the task.

meaning: A person at the side (化) is holding a message wrapped in a wrapping enclosure (勹) that also contains a mouth (口) and a rice field (田) — they are trusted to deliver it, so you send them with your words.
reading: The messenger is a 'bay' (ヘイ) — like a horse's neigh echoing across the bay as they ride off with your message.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands by a mouth (口) and a tree (木) — they protect the tree by speaking for it, keeping it safe from harm.
reading: You HO (ホ) the tree like a gardener — you say 'HO-ho!' as you gently pat its bark to keep it healthy.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands with a dart (矢) and a katakana-mu shape (厶) — they are waiting, ready to throw, but depend on the signal from the 乞-shaped part (乞) before they act.
reading: You wait and 'she' (シ) finally arrives — she is the one you depend on to show up.

meaning: A person (人) with a person at the side (化) and a large (大) heart — this is the chivalrous one, a knight-errant who fights for others, even a tomboy with a big spirit.
reading: The knight-errant shouts 'Kyo!' (キョウ) as he charges into battle, his cape flying.

meaning: A person at the side (化) leans in to hear what the say (言) — that's faith and trust in their words.
reading: シン — Imagine a 'shin' (shin bone) standing upright next to a podium, and the speaker's words bounce off it, proving their truth.

meaning: A person at the side stands where a large two-part shape meets — the fork in the road, or the crotch where legs split apart.
reading: また — The fork is 'MA-TA' like 'ma-ta' (again) — you come to the fork and think, 'Ma-ta, which way?'

meaning: A person at the side (化) with a sweeping stroke (ノ) and a bow (弓) plus two short strokes on top (并) — the bow's curve and the strokes leave a shadow, a trace of a face you once saw.
reading: The visage is an 'omokage' (おもかげ) — think of 'omo' (heavy) + 'kage' (shadow) — the heavy shadow of a memory.

meaning: A person at the side (化) pulls a car (車) — that's the jinricksha, a human-powered rickshaw.
reading: The rickshaw's wheels go 'kuruma' (くるま) — 'kuru' (come) + 'ma' (now) — the driver calls 'come now!' as he pulls.

meaning: A person at the side (化) with a ten (十) and a mouth (口) — your companion is the one who speaks for you, your mate in the field of life.
reading: Your companion is your 'chou' (チョウ) — like a 'chow' dog that stays by your side, loyal and always there.

meaning: The person at the side (化) is struck by the strike (攵) with three (彡) strokes, so he must study and discipline himself to master it.
reading: Think 'シュウ' (shuu) — like 'shoe' — you study hard to master how to shine your shoes, disciplining yourself to do it well.

meaning: A person at the side leans under a dotted cliff, while a measurement is taken of how low they go — that's bending down, lying prostrate.
reading: フ — Think of a 'foo' (フ) — a soft sound — as the person bends down so low their face nearly touches the ground, making a muffled 'foo' against the dirt.

meaning: A person at the side stands with a measurement tool, and next to them a mouth — all together, they measure and speak as one group, accompanying each other.
reading: ク — Picture a 'coo' (ク) — the sound of doves — as the group of people all together coo in unison, accompanying each other's voices.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands next to un- (非) — an actor who is not themselves, playing a role in a haiku performance.
reading: ハイ — Say HI to the actor on stage, who bows and recites a haiku in a high-pitched voice.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands by a garment (衣) with a gentleman (士) and soil (土) under a lid (亠) with two (二) — they pack rice into a bag, a bale, a sack, counting each one.
reading: Hyou (ヒョウ) — 'hi-yo' the cowboy throws a bale of hay onto the wagon, each sack lands with a thud.

meaning: A person at the side holds a divining rod and a right hand, while a little bit of something begins — this is the start, the beginning, and it's good.
reading: シュク — Imagine a 'shuck' (シュク) — like shucking corn — at the beginning of a meal, the first good bite, as the person at the side pulls back the husk.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands next to a large (大) person (人) with a vertical stroke (｜) and a one (一) — the big boss hands the salary to the worker, the stroke is the pay slip.
reading: Your salary is 'ho' (ホウ) — you hope it's enough to cover your rent.

meaning: A person at the side with a hook stroke and a cover over a large — that's me, the one who covers my own identity.
reading: エン — 'En?' I said, pointing at myself, 'You mean me?'

meaning: A person at the side stands by a ten and a rice field, with a hook stroke above — this person is the tutor, guiding the field worker with a hooked stick.
reading: フ — Think of a 'foo' (フ) — a gentle push — as the tutor gives a soft 'foo' to nudge the student forward, like a feather-light touch on the shoulder.

meaning: A person at the side is long — stretched out — and that long person is the ghost of one devoured by a tiger, lying prostrate and lost.
reading: チョウ — Imagine a 'chow' (チョウ) — the sound of a tiger eating — and the long ghost is the leftover, the 'chow' that consumed them, now haunting the spot.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands next to a vertical stroke (｜) and a lid (亠) — they are all lined up together, combining into one row. Imagine them merging side by side into a single line.
reading: The combine harvester goes 'HEY!' (ヘイ) as it merges all the wheat into one pile.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands under a lid (亠) with ten (十) people (人) below — this is your son, the one who will inherit the family name and stand in your place.
reading: Your son is 'SAI' (サイ) — like 'sigh' — he sighs when you call him, but he's still your boy.

meaning: A vertical stroke stands next to a person at the side, who is holding an upside-down box — this person is so skilled they can balance that box on a stick.
reading: The skilled person is a 'ryo' (row) of soldiers, each perfectly trained — say 'ryo' as in 'row' of experts.

meaning: A flag (尸) hangs over a mouth (口) with a hat on top (个) and a one (一) below — this is the cold, dark godown where you store rice under a single roof.
reading: ソウ — Imagine a SOUR smell coming from the old warehouse, so strong it makes your mouth pucker.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands by a box (囗) with a mouth (口) and ten (十) items inside — each item is an individual, counted one by one.
reading: コ — 'Ko' (コ) the crow counts each individual in the box, cawing 'ko, ko, ko' for each one.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands under a roof (宀) with a mouth (口) — he's the groom who calls out orders in the wine shop, his mouth under the roof announcing arrivals.
reading: The groom shouts 'KAN!' (カン) — like 'can' — he can open any wine bottle with a pop.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands up (立) next to a mouth (口) — the person doubles the amount by standing up and shouting into the mouth.
reading: バイ — Imagine a person at the side (化) shouting "BYE!" as he doubles the crowd, then the crowd replies "BYE!" back twice as loud.

meaning: A person at the side (化) sees a dog (犬) with a stooping figure (夂) and a strike (攵) — the dog is struck and moves quick, darting away in a flash.
reading: Quick as a 'SHUKU' (シュク) — like 'shook' — the dog shook itself and was gone in a second.

meaning: A person at the side (化) watches a stooping figure (夂) drop fire (火) — the fire falls hastily, suddenly igniting everything around.
reading: Suddenly, 'SHUKU' (シュク) — like 'shook' — the fire shook the ground as it burst out.

meaning: A person at the side of a gate — many people standing by the gate, so the plural suffix is used for groups of people.
reading: The gate (モン) is where the crowd gathers — think of the English word 'mon' as in 'monster' crowd at the gate.

meaning: A person at the side (化) reaps (刈) the climax (至) of soil (土) with a katakana-mu shape (厶) — the person falls over, overthrowing the pile.
reading: The person falls with a 'TOU' — like 'tumble' but short, matching 'トウ'.

meaning: A person at the side with a vertical stroke, a mountain, and a flag — the person stubbornly stands like a mountain, refusing to move even when a flag waves.
reading: The stubborn one is 'kut' (クツ) — imagine a stubborn goat that goes 'kut-kut' and refuses to budge from the mountain path.

meaning: A person at the side with a lid, ten, spicy, and stand up — the person lifts the lid off a spicy pot and stands up in surprise, finding happiness and luck inside.
reading: Luck is 'kou' (コウ) — think of a lucky 'cow' that finds a spicy treat and dances with joy.

meaning: A person at the side with an upside-down box, a mouth, little, and esteem — if the person puts a little mouth inside the box, they esteem it, but if not, it's dull and empty.
reading: If (トウ) — imagine a 'toe' (トウ) that steps on a little mouth inside a box, and you say 'if only I hadn't stepped there'.

meaning: A person at the side (化) holds a dart (矢) and a ユ-shaped stroke (ユ) while waiting for the weather — the 乞-shaped part (乞) is the bent arm of the clock, marking the season. You wait for the climate to change.
reading: コウ — Picture a cow (コウ) standing in a field, waiting for the weather to clear — the cow says 'moo' but the word 'cow' holds the 'kou' sound.

meaning: A person at the side with a large mouth and a barb — the person leans on a large mouth that has a barb, resting against it for support.
reading: Lean on 'i' (イ) — think of the letter 'E' (イ) as a leaning post, and you rest your back against it.

meaning: A person at the side with a vertical stroke, two, an upside-down box, a mouth, and soil — the person raises high above the soil, with two hands and a mouth, unrestrained and free.
reading: Raise high 'teki' (テキ) — imagine a 'tech' (テキ) guy who climbs a tall pole and raises his arms high, unrestrained.

meaning: At sunrise, the person at the side (化) stands on ten (十) legs of light, while the day (日) and the say (曰) both glow — the dawn is so bright that even words are lit up.
reading: The sun rises with a KAN-dle (カン) flame — imagine a giant candle at dawn, its light spreading over the horizon.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands under a lid (亠) that is far away, with a mouth (口) calling out and a little (小) figure barely visible — the distance is so great that the voice is tiny.
reading: The far-off person shouts 'KYOU!' (キョウ) across the valley — the echo sounds like 'kyou-kyou' as it fades.

meaning: A person at the side (化) holds out two hands (廾) to take the day (日) from you — that's borrowing time, and the two (二) lines are the promise to return it.
reading: You borrow “shaku” — imagine a monk shaking a stick and saying “SHAKU, shaku, I'll give it back tomorrow!”

meaning: A person at the side (化) performs by the day (日) — this actor/prostitute entertains in the daylight, with the sun as their stage light.
reading: The actor bows and says 'SHOU!' (ショウ) — like a showman's shout, 'SHOW-time!' — the sound of the stage.

meaning: A person at the side (化) runs (走) with a head (疋) full of three stacked strokes (ヨ) and soil (土) underfoot — this fast, beautiful person moves so quickly that the ground blurs.
reading: The beautiful runner goes 'SHOU!' (ショウ) — like a swift 'SHOW' of speed, a flash of grace.

meaning: A person at the side (化) watches a direction (方) being struck (攵) by a 乞-shaped part (乞) — they imitate the exact motion they see.
reading: ホウ — The person at the side (化) says 'HOH!' as they mimic the strike (攵) toward the direction (方), copying the movement perfectly.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands next to a vertical stroke (｜) and an eye (目) over ten (十) — the eye checks the price tag, and the ten is the cost. The value is what you see when you look at the number.
reading: チ — Think of 'cheap' (チープ) — the price is cheap, and 'cheap' starts with the 'chi' sound.

meaning: A person at the side (化) is stuck in a hole (穴) under a roof (宀) with craft (工) tools and a pair of legs (儿) dangling — the urgent boorish person is trapped and frantic.
reading: The trapped person yells 'KOU!' (コウ) — like 'COW!' — a loud, urgent moo from the hole.

meaning: A person at the side has a large 'two' on top, but the seal below is stopped — they've lost interest because the work is just two short strokes repeated, and the person is already done.
reading: You tire of hearing 'ken' — like 'ken' in 'kennel' where a bored dog loses interest in the same old bark.

meaning: A person at the side (化) squats with legs outstretched like a flag (尸) on the ground, with a mouth (口) and ten (十) — this proud posture shows arrogance, sitting spread-legged.
reading: The proud squatter says 'KYO!' (キョ) — like 'KYO-king' — a haughty 'kyo' sound as they lounge.

meaning: A person at the side (化) of a blue (青) month (月) with a lid (亠) and two (二) soil (土) layers — they are carefully studying the soil, paying attention to every detail.
reading: The person at the side (化) is a SENator (セン) who attentively reviews every bill, staring at the blue month calendar.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands on a pair of legs (儿) next to a mortar (臼) — they stare into the mortar, watching the grain being ground.
reading: The stare is so intense it feels like a GAY (ゲイ) friend is watching you from across the room, unblinking.

meaning: A person at the side (化) holds a tome (冊) with two hands (廾) — this companion is so ethical they read the rules of morality aloud, with a barb (亅) marking each good deed.
reading: リン — The ethical companion rings a bell (RIN-RIN) to announce each moral lesson, like a clear chime of conscience.

meaning: A person at the side (化) holds up a ten (十) and a day (日) with a divining rod (卜) and a say (曰) — the person is large and clear, like a giant who says 'look at me!'
reading: The large, clear person is a TAKU (タク) — like a taxi (タク) that is so big and bright you can't miss it.

meaning: A person at the side (化) bows to a grain stalk (禾) while a woman (女) stands nearby — this is the ancient Yamato court, where rice and women held power.
reading: The Yamato queen says 'WA' as she waves her hand, calling the ancient Japanese people to gather.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands next to a tree (木) in a rice field (田) — they are bare and naked, having taken off all clothes to work in the field.
reading: The naked person shouts 'RA!' (ラ) as they run through the field, feeling the sun on their skin.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands with two splayed strokes (ハ) and an eye (目) under a one (一) — both people see the same thing together, alike.
reading: They both 'goo' (グ) at each other, together in agreement.

meaning: A person at the side (化) has a mouth (口) under a hat on top (个) with one (一) line — they speak little and use only one thing, staying frugal and thrifty.
reading: ケン — The person at the side (化) counts 'KEN!' — one (一) mouth (口) under a hat (个) — and decides that's all they need to spend.

meaning: A person at the side stands next to a home country, but an ear is attached — this is a phonetic character, so the ear hears the sound of the home country's name.
reading: The sound is 'ya' — like 'ya' in 'yacht', a boat you'd hear about in a Korean place name.

meaning: A person at the side holds up a claw over an upside-down box with a month inside — they state the time by pointing with the claw at the month in the box.
reading: You state it with a 'sho' — like 'show' — you show the month with your claw.

meaning: A person at the side lies down, and a woman is under a day inside a box-on-side enclosure — the dam is a weir that lays the woman down flat to hold back the day's water.
reading: The dam makes the water 'en' — like 'en' in 'engine' — the engine of the weir pushes the water down.

meaning: A person at the side uses a right hand to grab a temporary thing — the vertical stroke and the two short strokes are just an assumed name, not the real one.
reading: It's 'ka' — like 'car' — a temporary car you borrow (kari) for the interim.

meaning: A person at the side of a wrapping enclosure holding a spoon, with a day and a vertical stroke — this person is so fast and healthy they can rest only after praising Buddha in verse.
reading: Imagine a monk chanting a verse in praise of Buddha, and he says 'ゲ' (ge) as he hits a gong — the sound echoes 'ge' through the temple.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands next to tanned leather (韋) — the leather is so tough and impressive that the person admires its greatness. The mouth (口) is open in awe, but the person is also a bit conceited about their own remarkable strength.
reading: イ — Imagine an 'eagle' (イ) soaring over a mountain, its wings spread wide — that's admirable greatness. The eagle is remarkable, and a little conceited about it.

meaning: A person at the side of the name of a chinese emperor (禹) who has an insect in an upside-down box with a mouth — this person walks alone, self-reliant, not needing help.
reading: The self-reliant walker says 'ウ' (u) as he steps — like 'oo' in 'you' but short, as he moves alone.

meaning: A person at the side of grass on top and a mouth — this person says 'thus, so, like, such' pointing at the grass, as if to say 'like this' with a mouth.
reading: He says 'ジャ' (ja) — like 'ja' in 'jar' — as he points to the grass, 'such as this.'

meaning: A person at the side of a rice field and a garment — the person clings to the garment in the field, cuddling and embracing it for warmth.
reading: She clings and cuddles, whispering 'ワイ' (wai) — like 'why' but softer, as she hugs the garment.

meaning: A person at the side (化) leans against a door (戸) under an upside-down box (冂) with a tome (冊) and a flag (尸), while two hands (廾) hold a vertical stroke (｜) and one (一) — all tilting to one side, partial.
reading: The left-side radical leans 'hen' — like a hen tilting its head to read the character.

meaning: A person at the side of two short strokes on top, a stand up, a lid, a cliff, and three — this person makes a fake counterfeit of the standing figure under the cliff, with three strokes as a false mark.
reading: The fake is exposed when someone shouts 'ゲン' (gen) — like 'gen' in 'genuine' but it's not — it's counterfeit.

meaning: A person at the side of one, soil, a flag, and climax — this person fusses over the soil and flag, worrying until the climax, making a fuss about everything.
reading: He fusses and says 'アク' (aku) — like 'ack' in 'ack!' — as he sees the soil and flag in disorder.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands with a white (白) flag, and two people compare (比) their steps — they are together, walking in sync. The white flag shows they're a pair moving as one.
reading: Together they go 'カイ' (kai) — like 'kai' in 'kayak' — two paddlers in one boat, moving together. Picture them chanting 'kai, kai, kai' as they row in unison.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands next to an old man (老) who is looking at the day (日) — the old man says, 'Well, now, what shall we do today?'
reading: The old man says 'SHA' (シャ) as in 'shah, let me think' — imagine him stroking his beard and going 'sha...' while looking at the day.

meaning: A person at the side (化) uses a mouth (口) to order ten (十) workers, who strike (攵) with a 乞-shaped tool (乞) to make something.
reading: The workers 'SAKU' (サク) as in 'sack' — they sack the old materials to make new ones, with a loud 'saku, saku' sound of striking.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands under a lid (亠) and a crown (冖) — a shelter — with a barb (亅) stuck in the ground to halt the cart. The one (一) line is the brake.
reading: テイ — Imagine a train conductor yelling "TEI!" (like "tay") as he halts the train at the station.

meaning: A person at the side (化) sees a king (王) and a white (白) thing under the day (日) — the king is pacing, agitated, alarmed by the white flag of surrender.
reading: The king shouts 'KOU' (コウ) as in 'cow' — he's alarmed like a startled cow, mooing 'kou, kou' while pacing.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stares at a tree (木) where fire (火) burns near a grain stalk (禾) — a sweeping stroke (ノ) of smoke makes them stare in worry.
reading: They stare with a 'SHOU' (ショウ) as in 'show' — watching the fire like a dramatic show, unable to look away.

meaning: A person at the side (化) takes a long stride (廴) while holding a brush (聿) — this person is healthy and strong, with persistence to keep going.
reading: The 'ken' in 'kendo' — imagine a healthy kendo fighter taking a long stride with a brush-like shinai.

meaning: A person at the side (化) is squeezed between a one (一) and a rice field (田) with a mouth (口) — the field owner compels them to work, pressuring them.
reading: The pressure makes them go 'FUKU' (フク) as in 'foo-koo' — like a tight 'fuku' (clothing) squeezing them, forcing them to move.

meaning: A person at the side (化) has a dot (丶) on their heart (心) and a 'not' (勿) sign — the dot is a pain, and the 'not' means they cannot escape suffering.
reading: They feel a 'SOU' (ソウ) as in 'sore' — the pain is so sore, they groan 'sou, sou' while clutching their heart.

meaning: A person at the side turns their mask away from the group — they are transgressing the rules of the gathering.
reading: ベン — Imagine a person at the side wearing a mask, and they suddenly shout 'BEN!' as they leap over a fence to transgress the boundary.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands by a heart (心) in a rice field (田), trying to recollect a memory of someone they miss.
reading: The person at the side (化) sighs 'sigh' (サイ) as they recollect, but the sound is more like 'sigh-ee' — imagine them saying 'サイ' while wiping a tear.

meaning: A person at the side (化) sees a shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) and two splayed strokes (ハ) — they lean to one side, opposing the reap (刈) of the shellfish.
reading: Imagine a 'ソク' (sock) on the side of a foot — the person at the side leans over, regretting the shellfish that got away.

meaning: A person at the side (化) uses a shellfish (貝) as payment to get an eye (目) to watch — that's a spy. The spy's two splayed strokes (ハ) and divining rod (卜) are his tools for sneaking around.
reading: テイ — Picture a spy who always orders tea (テイ) at cafés to blend in, but he's really watching the target through the window.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands next to a rice field (田) inside an upside-down box (冂) with a katakana-mu shape (厶) — this odd couple (the person and the field) met by accident, an even number of them, like a married pair.
reading: The sound 'guu' is like 'goo' — imagine accidentally bumping into a couple and saying 'goo!' as you both stumble, making an even pair.

meaning: A person at the side uses a reap hook to cut a month-shaped bag off a hat on top of a one — they steal it while no one watches.
reading: トウ — The thief sneaks up and says 'TOW!' as they yank the bag — like 'tow'ing it away — from the hat.

meaning: A person at the side (化) is pretending to be someone else, but the wrapping enclosure (勹) around their true self is loose — the two short strokes on top (并) show they're just a fake, and the dot (丶) and sweeping stroke (ノ) are the cracks in their story. The four dots at the bottom (杰) are the sweat of a liar.
reading: The liar's excuse is 'ギ' — like a 'gig' (a fake performance) where the actor pretends to be someone else on stage.

meaning: A ghost (鬼) with a pair of legs (儿) and a spoon (匕) stands next to a person at the side (化) — the ghost is so large it towers over them, making the person feel tiny.
reading: The ghost is so large it blocks out the sky — you shout 'KAI!' (like 'kite' but with a long 'i') as it swoops down.

meaning: An old man (meaning) holds a branch (支) in his right hand (又) while standing next to a mortar (臼) with three stacked strokes (ヨ) on top — he's grinding grain, a task for the elderly.
reading: The old man sighs 'SOU' (like 'sow' as in planting seeds) as he slowly pounds the mortar.

meaning: A tutor (meaning) stands by a rice field (田) with a measurement (寸) and a dot (丶) — he measures out lessons precisely, like marking field boundaries.
reading: The tutor says 'FU' (like 'foo' in 'food') as he points with his measuring stick at the student's work.

meaning: A tribe (meaning) is a group of people — here shown as a person at the side (化) plus two splayed strokes (ハ) and a pair of legs (儿) — they all stand together, legs spread wide in a tribal dance.
reading: The tribe chants 'RITSU' (like 'lit' + 'sue') as they stomp in rhythm, their legs kicking up dust.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands next to a direction (方) with two short strokes on top (并) — that person is a bystander, watching from the side. The lid (亠) and crown (冖) cover the stand up (立) part, but the bystander just stands beside, not in the middle.
reading: ボウ — Imagine a 'bow' (ボウ) — a bystander stands beside you holding a bow, ready to shoot. The bow is at your side, while you watch.

meaning: To topple (meaning) — a person at the side (化) pushes over a stack: an eye (目) on top of ten (十) with a spoon (匕) and two splayed strokes (ハ) — the whole thing falls headfirst.
reading: The stack goes 'TEN' (like 'ten' pins in bowling) as it crashes down, scattering the pieces.

meaning: To ward off (meaning) — a person at the side (化) stands under a dotted cliff (广) with a mouth (口) and three stacked strokes (ヨ) — they shout from the shelter to keep out the wind and rain.
reading: They shout 'TOU' (like 'toe' as in kicking) to push back the storm, using their foot to block the door.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands next to a tree (木) with dancing (舛) branches in the evening (夕) — this person is so great that even the tree dances in admiration.
reading: ケツ — Ketsu the champion wins the race, and the crowd shouts "Ketsu! Ketsu!" as he leaps onto the podium, his greatness shining.

meaning: A person at the side (化) is holding a claw (爪) that grabs a short thread (幺), while a large (大) figure looms behind — this is the personal name of a servant who waits on the large one.
reading: The servant's name is Kay (ケイ) — imagine calling "Hey, Kay!" to get their attention, and they come running.

meaning: A person at the side (化) follows behind a grain stalk (禾) that grows from a tree (木), with three stacked strokes (ヨ) above and a one (一) below — this servant trails the harvest, always attending.
reading: The servant Ken (ケン) is always at your side — think "Ken, come here!" and he obeys instantly.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands under a hat on top (个) near a door (戸) with a flag (尸) and a mouth (口) — this vulgar country man shouts through the door, while a dot (丶) marks his rough speech and a day (日) passes outside.
reading: The country man shouts "Sho!" (ショウ) to scare crows — a rough, vulgar sound from the fields.

meaning: Ten (十) people (人) each hold a hat on top (个) — together they form a big umbrella over everyone. The hat on top covers all ten people, keeping them dry.
reading: サン — Imagine the 'sun' (サン) is out, but you open your umbrella to block it — 'sun' becomes 'san' as you say 'sun-blocking umbrella'.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands by a cliff (厂) with grass on top (艾), using a utilize (用) to equip and prepare for anything.
reading: You prepare a feast, and the chef yells "BI!" like a whistle — ビ.

meaning: A person at the side (化) watches a father (父) under a lid (亠) who uses a strike (攵) — the child imitates the father's every move, even the 乞-shaped part (乞) of his posture.
reading: To imitate is to "ko" (コウ) — think of a crow (カラス) copying another's call, "ko, ko, ko!"

meaning: A person at the side (化) lives in a mountain (山) village with an open box enclosure (凵) and a tin can (缶) — this minority tribe also has a claw (爪) for gathering, and evening (夕) brings them together.
reading: The tribe's name is Yo (ヨウ) — imagine them chanting "Yo! Yo!" around the evening fire.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands on two short strokes (并) next to a craft (工) and a king (王) — but the ground is unsteady, like a sheep (羊) trying to balance on a one (一) and a two (二) that wobble.
reading: The unsteady person sways "Sa" (サ) — like saying "sa-sa-sa" while stumbling on uneven ground.

meaning: Under a roof, a person at the side is arguing with a pig. The pig refuses to move, and the person is stubbornly insisting — that's the stubborn, obstinate scene.
reading: カ

meaning: A person at the side stands on soil, with grass on top of their head — this is the Dai minority, who live close to the land in South China.
reading: タイ

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands on a mountain (山) calling an old bird (隹) — they sponsor a meeting to give the bird a dinner.
reading: Sai — picture a sponsor shouting 'Sai!' (like 'sigh') as the old bird lands on the mountain, and the meeting begins.

meaning: A person at the side uses a brush to write a contract on a dotted cliff. That person is hired — employed to do the writing work.
reading: ヨウ — You hire a “yo-yo” (ヨウ) master to perform at your party. He stands at the side, using his brush to sign the deal, then shows off his yo-yo tricks.

meaning: A person at the side is wrapped in a wrapping enclosure, with a stooping figure and a heart inside. The heart is squeezed — this person is in a hurry, urgent, and feels suffocated by the pressure.
reading: ソウ — The urgent person is so stressed they “sow” (ソウ) seeds of panic everywhere, running around with a pounding heart, scattering seeds as they go.

meaning: A person at the side stands on soil, holding a direction sign, and strikes with a strike. Above, a lid and two lines — this person thinks they are above everything, proud and arrogant.
reading: ゴウ — The proud person says “Go!” (ゴウ) to everyone else, ordering them around from their high spot on the soil, striking down any advice.

meaning: A person at the side uses a measurement and a ten to measure a rice field, while a katakana-mu shape sits below. The person measures the field and then transmits the data — summoning others to hear the message.
reading: デン — The message is sent by “den” (デン) — like a den of spies. The person at the side measures the rice field, then runs to the den to transmit the secret info.

meaning: A person at the side bends over a box-on-side enclosure, with a mouth and goods inside. The person stoops low to peek into the box — bowing to see the goods.
reading: ク — The person bends over and says “coo” (ク) like a pigeon, stooping low to peek into the box-on-side enclosure, cooing at the goods inside.

meaning: A person at the side keeps an eye on shellfish (money) and two splayed strokes on soil under a lid—that's a bond.
reading: He sighs over his bond debt.

meaning: A person (人) with a sweeping stroke (ノ) is hurt by a person at the side (化) who has a day (日) and 'not' (勿) — the wound is wrapped in a wrapping enclosure (勹) with a 乞-shaped part (乞) on top.
reading: The 'shō' in 'shout' — you shout in pain when you get the wound. (ショウ)

meaning: A person at the side (化) is stuck under a hat on top (个) and a show (示) of evening (夕) rain — they are hindered and detained, unable to move on.
reading: The detained person is tied to a post and the guard says 'tei' — like 'tie' — as he tightens the rope, keeping them from leaving.

meaning: A person at the side (化) with a hat on top (个) and an evening (夕) mouth (口) — they look foolish, like an imbecile staring blankly.
reading: サ — 'Sah' (サ) — the silly person says 'sah' like a fool, drooling.

meaning: A person at the side (化) sees ten (十) days (日) of saying (曰) and standing up (立) with sound (音) — they are terror-stricken by the noise.
reading: ショウ — 'Show' (ショウ) — the terror-stricken person screams 'show!' as if watching a horror show.

meaning: A person at the side (化) leans toward a shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) and two splayed strokes (ハ) on a page (頁), while a spoon (匕) tips the whole thing over.
reading: The leaning tower of Pisa goes 'KEI' (ケイ) — it tilts, but never quite falls.

meaning: A person at the side (化) is bent over, carrying a ten (十) on their back while a woman (女) watches, all hunched under the weight — so they bend over.
reading: ロウ — Imagine a person bending over to pick up a 'loaf' of bread (ロウ sounds like 'loaf'), and the loaf is so heavy they stay bent.

meaning: A person at the side (化) is wrapped in a wrapping enclosure (勹) with grass on top (艾) and a utilize (用) tool inside — everything is ready and prepared for use.
reading: ビ — Picture a 'bee' (ビ) that is fully prepared, wearing a tiny grass hat (艾) and carrying a tool (用) in its little hands.

meaning: A person at the side (化) is so light they float, with two (二) little (小) feathers showing (示) to the west (西) — they are light and airy.
reading: ヒョウ — Imagine a 'hyo' (ヒョウ) like a snow leopard, so light it leaps across the west (西) without leaving a trace.

meaning: A person at the side uses a mouth to speak over soil, but only two tiny words come out — just a wee bit of speech, nothing more.
reading: キン

meaning: A person at the side watches as a hat on top falls off, and the ice below cracks into three pieces, while feathers drift down — all because someone was humiliated and treated with contempt.
reading: The humiliated person is tied to a rope (ル) and dragged through the mud — 'ru' as in 'rude' but shorter, like 'ruh'.

meaning: A mouth, a person, a hat on top, and a one — all these parts are gathered together, so this means 'all' of them are present.
reading: All the people say 'sen' (セン) — 'sen' sounds like 'send' — send all of them away.

meaning: A person at the side goes west, then sees a large stop sign — that person becomes a hermit, stopping all contact with the world.
reading: The hermit lives in the west (セン) — 'sen' sounds like 'zen' — a zen hermit meditates in the west.

meaning: A person at the side (化) uses power (力) under the day (日) sun, with a vertical stroke (｜) and one (一) — that's work.
reading: You 'doh' (ドウ) — like 'dough' — as you knead it with power, working the bread all day.

meaning: A person at the side uses a vertical stroke as a pole and two splayed strokes as a net to collect two items, then stops.
reading: He collects sen (the old Japanese coin) using a vertical pole and two splayed nets.

meaning: A person at the side (化) is wrapped in a wrapping enclosure (勹) with a pig (豕) and a mouth (口) on top of one (一) — this odd figure is a statue (像) you see in a park.
reading: ゾウ — 'Zoo' — you see a statue of an elephant at the zoo, and you say 'zoo' as you look at it.

meaning: A person at the side stands by an upside-down box with a mouth and a large figure inside — that person is living abroad, a temporary home away from home.
reading: キョウ — The expatriate lives in a 'kyo' (like 'key-oh') — a tiny keyhole apartment, and he says 'kyo' when he misses his real home.

meaning: The king's sheep with two short strokes on top and a large 'two' underneath — that's the servant (僕) who tends the royal flock, always saying 'me, me' (as in 'I, the servant').
reading: The servant bows and says 'BOKU' (ボク) — like a polite 'book' (ボク) he is read by the king, always at his service.

meaning: A person at the side enjoys watching a gentleman with a mouth eat ten beans and two short strokes on top.
reading: The key (ki) to this enjoyment is that the gentleman eats ten beans and two short strokes.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands next to a little (小) day (日) and large (大) figure — that's your colleague, an official companion who works beside you.
reading: Your colleague is a 'ryo' (リョウ) — imagine him shouting 'RYO!' as he jumps into a rowboat to join you for the commute to the station.

meaning: A person at the side abuses a child by waving a flag at them.
reading: He abuses the child with a sandal (san) while waving a flag.

meaning: A person at the side uses a claw to draw four dots at the bottom — that's a falsehood.
reading: He pretends and says 'Gee (gi), I just drew four dots with a claw!'

meaning: A person at the side boasts that he has two large days — that's a usurpation of authority.
reading: He boasts about his shin (shin) being as large as two days.

meaning: A person at the side works ten days in the rice field and speaks honestly with his mouth — that's sincere.
reading: He gets a tan (tan) from working ten days in the rice field.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands on soil (土) with a pair of legs (儿) — they are stretching up, desperately seeking luck and desire.
reading: The person's luck is a 'gyo' (ギョウ) — imagine them shouting 'Gyo!' as they spot a lucky coin in the soil.

meaning: A person at the side (化) puts a lid (亠) on a mouth (口) and a little (小) crooked-big (尢) reasonable (尤) thing — this is the rental agreement for a heir, all packed up.
reading: The heir rents out a room and says 'Shu!' (シュウ) — like 'shoo' — to the noisy tenant, but then sends a package (おく.る) anyway.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands in a rice field (田) under the day (日) with two short strokes on top (并) — that's the monk, meditating in the field.
reading: The monk chants 'SOU' — a deep, resonant hum that vibrates through the temple walls.

meaning: A person at the side (化) sees two splayed strokes (ハ) and ten (十) grass on top (艾) covering an eye (目) and a shellfish (貝) — the whole pile falls over, causing ruin.
reading: The ruin is a 'fun' (フン) — imagine the person going 'FUN!' as the shellfish crashes down, overthrowing everything.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands by a month (月) and a gate (門) — they are dignified and martial, guarding the gate with courage.
reading: The courageous guard shouts 'Kan!' (カン) — like 'can' — as he slams the gate shut, showing his martial might.

meaning: A person at the side (化) puts a lid (亠) over the day (日) and then adds nothing (无) — they boastfully usurp the throne, hiding the sun.
reading: The usurper sneaks in and says 'Shin' (シン) — like 'shin' (shin bone) — as he kicks the real ruler out, boasting all the way.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands next to a ri (里) and a stand up (立) — this is a child servant, standing at the village boundary, foolishly waiting.
reading: The child servant runs 'To!' (トウ) — like 'toe' — stubbing his toe on the stand up (立), and cries out in foolishness.

meaning: A person at the side (化) is dancing (舛) with rice (米) in the evening (夕), but they spill it and feel ashamed.
reading: Rin the cat feels ashamed of her messy dancing.

meaning: One dot (丶) on a flag (尸) and a door (戸) with an old bird (隹) — a person at the side (化) uses this to hire workers.
reading: Koala hires a door guard.

meaning: A person (implied by the radical) with a mouth (口) and a tree (木) — but here the parts are not listed, so think of a minority name as a person who speaks a different tongue, like a 'sù' (僳) person.
reading: The minority name 'Lisu' (傈僳) sounds like 'lee-soo' — imagine a person saying 'soo' (スー) as their name.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands by a rice field (田) with a one (一) and two (二) — but the field collapses, and the person falls down flat.
reading: The sound is 'キョウ' — imagine a loud 'Kyo-ump!' as the whole field collapses under the person.

meaning: A person at the side (化) holds up a shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) — the price is written on a west (西) tag, and the two splayed strokes (ハ) show the value going up.
reading: The sound is 'カ' — think of a cashier saying 'Ka-ching!' as the price rings up.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands by a flag (尸) in a rural area, but a mouth (口) with ten (十) spicy (辛) words twists their view — prejudice grows from that bias.
reading: The sound is 'ヘキ' — imagine a rural elder saying 'Hek, that's just my bias' about the city folk.

meaning: A person at the side (化) wears a crown (冖) and a stooping figure (夂) hides behind a claw (爪) — but the heart (心) shows they are 'like' someone, a faint resemblance.
reading: The sound is 'アイ' — say 'I like you' — 'Ai' — as the person's heart warms to the likeness.

meaning: A king (王) with a halberd (戈) and a hand (手) — the sheep (羊) has two short strokes (并) on top, and a barb (亅) pokes out — this is the formal ceremony where rules are set, a case for the court.
reading: GI (ギ) — 'GEE' (as in 'gee whiz') — at the ceremony, everyone says 'gee' in awe as the king raises the halberd.

meaning: A person at the side (化) with an old bird (隹) that sings beautifully — that's a talented person.
reading: Shun the talented bird, it's too good.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands under the sign of the dragon (辰) wearing a garment (衣) over a day (日) — that's me, the old dragon-lord, and also 'he' who wears the robe.
reading: The old man says 'WASHI' (わし) as he washes his robe in the river — the sound of water and his own name.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands by a heart (心) and a sound (音) — but the sound is a hundred million (10^8) echoes, each one a separate heartbeat, filling the day (日) with a standing-up (立) crowd.
reading: OKU (オク) — say 'OCT' (as in octopus, 8) — a hundred million octopus arms reaching out, each one holding a heart.
