meaning: A person at the side (化) gets a strike (攵) on the mouth (口) while grass on top (艾) falls — that's a warning: don't eat the grass, or you'll be hit.
reading: The warning bell goes 'KEI' (ケイ) — like a sharp 'kay!' shout to stop you before you touch the poison grass.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands between two hats (个) and a mouth (口) with a dot (丶) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) — the go-between who talks for both sides, holding a one (一) and a day (日) as his fee.
reading: The broker says 'KAI' (カイ) — like 'kite' — he flies between buyers and sellers, carrying messages on a string.

meaning: A person at the side (化) has a mouth (口) under a hat (个) with one (一) and another person (人) — he eats only one grain a day, that's economy.
reading: The thrifty man counts every coin with a 'KEN' (ケン) — like 'ken' as in 'kennel' — he keeps his dog in a tiny box to save wood.

meaning: A person at the side (化) carries a burden: a pair of legs (儿) under a crown (冖) with two splayed strokes (ハ) and a cliff (厂) — he bears a load of two jars, one on each shoulder, while saying (言) his chant.
reading: He bears the load with a 'TAN' (タン) — like 'tan' as in 'tank' — he carries a small jar that holds a tank's worth of water.

meaning: A person at the side (化) gets a strike (攵) from a direction (方) but the day (日) is white (白) — lucky! The strike misses because the white day shines in his eyes.
reading: He feels 'KYOU' (キョウ) — like 'kyo' in 'kyoto' — lucky he is in Kyoto, where the white sun protects him from the strike.

meaning: A person at the side (化) is standing on two splayed strokes (ハ) inside an open box enclosure (凵), while a stooping figure (夂) above drops a dot (丶) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) — this whole clumsy pile is what a silly imbecile looks like.
reading: The silly imbecile keeps saying “サ” (like “sah”) every time he drops his ice cream — a short, foolish sound.

meaning: A person at the side (化) is loading a car (車) with ten (十) bags of soil (土) using a halberd (戈) as a lever — that’s how you carry and contain a heavy load.
reading: The load is so heavy you say “サイ” (like “sigh”) as you lift it — a long, tired sigh.

meaning: To entertain guests, you stand beside them and guide them in. See a person at the side (化) holding a roof (宀) over the guests' heads, while an eye (目) watches their needs and a shellfish (貝) is offered as a gift — all with a vertical stroke (｜) as the host's upright posture.
reading: The host says 'hin' (ヒン) as he 'hints' at the next course — a quick, polite sound to keep the party moving.

meaning: Rain (雨) falls on a person at the side (化) and on 'and yet' (而) — a Confucian scholar stands in the rain, calmly teaching despite the weather.
reading: The Confucian is 'ju' (ジュ) — imagine a scholar named 'Ju' who recites classics under the rain, his voice like a gentle drum.

meaning: A companion is someone of similar kind who stands with you. See a person at the side (化) sharing a craft (工) with you, both under a mouth (口) that speaks the same words, with a gentleman (士) and a measurement (寸) showing you are equals in stature.
reading: The companion calls out 'chuu' (チュウ) like a 'chew' on a shared snack — a friendly sound of togetherness.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands with two hands (廾) raised, holding a lid (亠) over a family name (氏) that is alike (齊) to theirs — they are companions, all sharing the same name.
reading: Say 'セイ' — imagine a group of companions all shouting 'SAY!' together, like a cheer squad, each one pointing at the next as if to say 'you're my companion, say it with me!'

meaning: Ugly — picture a person at the side (化) looking at a retainer (臣) who has a dish (皿) for a face, with two (二) crooked eyes and a 乞-shaped part (乞) as a twisted mouth. The whole scene is so ugly you turn away.
reading: It's so ugly you say 'RAN' (ラン) — like 'runt' (a small, ugly animal) — and this person is the runt of the litter.

meaning: A person at the side (化) holds a dart (矢) and a large (大) head (疋) on a spoon (匕) — they compare the two to draw an analogy, measuring which is bigger.
reading: Say 'ギ' — imagine a 'gee-gee' (a horse) standing next to a person, and you compare the horse's head to a dart to see which is longer — 'gee, that's a big head!'

meaning: Three stacked strokes (ヨ) on top of a person at the side (化) who is holding a dish (皿) with four dots at the bottom (杰) — leave it as it is, don't touch the dish.
reading: The dish is left 'mama' — as in 'mama's cooking, leave it as it is' — don't stir. (まま)

meaning: A person at the side (化) is trying to buy (買) an evening (夕) under a crown (冖) with grass on top (艾) — but it vanishes, so fleeting and fickle.
reading: The fleeting dream fades with a soft “ボウ” (like “bow” as in a gentle bow that disappears).

meaning: A person at the side (化) dances with nothingness (無) in the evening (夕), using dancing (舛) steps — they skip about for joy, twirling with a vertical stroke (｜) as a pole.
reading: Say 'ブ' — imagine a 'boo' (ブ) from a ghost, but instead of scaring you, the ghost dances for joy in the evening, skipping around you — 'boo, I'm dancing!'

meaning: A person at the side (化) is under a roof (宀) with a barb (亅) stuck in their heart (心), and they try to buy (買) relief with one (一) coin — but they are weak and wearied, in distress.
reading: Say 'ドウ' — imagine a 'dough' (ドウ) that is weak and floppy, like a tired person who can't even lift a barb — they're in distress because the dough is too heavy.

meaning: The person at the side is making reparation — they have a shellfish (money) and an eye (watching) with two splayed strokes (hands) and a mouth (speaking) under a crown (esteem). They pay with money and words to redeem themselves.
reading: ショウ — Imagine a "SHOW" (ショウ) where a person on stage pays back a shellfish with a crown — the audience claps for the reparation.

meaning: Defeat — see a person at the side (化) slumped over a rice field (田) after losing a battle, their head bowed like a broken puppet. The rice field is trampled, and the person's arms hang limp.
reading: After defeat, you 'RAI' (ライ) — like 'lie' down in the mud, too tired to get up.

meaning: A person at the side (化) with a heart (心) under a crown (冖) and a stooping figure (夂) — this gentle, caring actor shows 'tenderness' and 'excel'.
reading: The actor (優) says 'you' (ユウ) with a tender heart (心) — 'you' as in 'you are excellent'.

meaning: A person at the side gives alms to a small eye that stands up — the eye is the needy one, and the person assists by reaching out with a coin.
reading: To assist is to 'shin' (シン) — imagine a helper saying 'shin' as they shine a light on the poor person's path.

meaning: A rude person at the side has a hook stroke for a mouth and a month of unfinished work — they are barbarous, never completing anything, leaving it all vague and rough.
reading: Rude and barbarous — think of a loud 'rou' (ロウ) — a barbarian shouting 'row!' as he breaks a month's worth of work.

meaning: A person at the side says 'old man' by day, and the old man's words turn into profit — this is being profitable.
reading: チョ — The old man counts his profit with a 'cho' (like a chopping sound) as he chops the coins in half.

meaning: A person at the side is obstinate and stupid, standing unevenly on a pair of legs, with a crown on their head and a spoon in their mouth — they refuse to mix with others, staying stubbornly apart.
reading: The reading is サン (san). Imagine the obstinate person saying 'SAN!' like a stubborn child refusing to move, as if saying 'sahn' (like 'son' but with an 'a') — they won't budge.

meaning: A person at the side stands next to a deer, and the deer's antlers are like a compare sign, showing two things side by side. This pair of companions—person and deer—means companion.
reading: Picture a companion saying 'レイ' (ray) of sunshine as they walk together—like a ray of light that always accompanies you.

meaning: A person at the side (化) grabs a buy (買) with a short thread (幺) and a thread (糸), while an old bird (隹) watches — this bandit is a dare-devil who steals and ties things up.
reading: The bandit shouts 'ラ' like 'la' — 'La! La!' as he dashes off with the loot.

meaning: A person at the side (化) piles up soil (土) and shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) and two splayed strokes (ハ) under a sweeping stroke (ノ) and a pair of legs (儿) — they accumulate and hoard it all in a store.
reading: To hoard, you say 'サン' like 'sun' — the sun stores up heat all day, accumulating it for the evening.

meaning: A person at the side (化) uses grass on top (艾) and an old bird (隹) with two (二) and a large (大) well (井) — this is the exorcism ritual, driving out spirits with grass and a well.
reading: The exorcist chants 'ナ' like 'nah' — 'Nah! Nah!' to scare away the evil spirits.

meaning: A person (人) at the side (化) stands under a crown (冖) and black (黒) clouds, while esteem (尚) and ri (里) are above — this person excels and surpasses all, perhaps by chance (if).
reading: The sound 'TOU' — imagine a champion who says 'TOU!' as they leap over a hurdle, excelling beyond all others.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands under a cliff (厂) with a mouth (口) and ear (耳), while a strike (攵) and the 乞-shaped part (乞) loom — this person is so serious and untouched that even the cliff seems to bow in solemn majesty.
reading: The solemn scene makes you say 'GEN' (as in 'gentleman') — a serious, majestic gentleman who never moves.

meaning: This is the legs radical — think of a pair of walking legs seen from the side, with the left stroke as the front leg and the right stroke as the back leg, striding forward.
reading: The legs are doing a 'jin' — imagine a tiny person (like a ninja) doing a high kick, shouting 'JIN!' as they strike a pose.

meaning: A pair of legs (儿) standing on a high, level line (一) — the legs are so high up that the head is bald from the wind, and it feels dangerous up there.
reading: Think of a bald man on a high cliff shouting 'KOTSU!' — like 'cots' (small beds) but with a 'ko' — he's so high he's cold, 'ko-tsu'.

meaning: The katakana-mu shape (厶) sits on top of a pair of legs (儿) — like a person kneeling to receive a license, showing sincerity and permission.
reading: The official says 'IN' (like 'in') — you're 'in' for the permit, granted with sincerity.

meaning: A hook stroke (乙) pierces through the one (一) and the sweeping stroke (ノ) on top of the crooked-big (尢) shape, like a hairpin stuck into a bun. The two (二) lines at the bottom are the clasp ends holding it in place.
reading: Shin (シン) — imagine a shiny hairpin that glints with a 'shin' sound as it slides into hair.

meaning: Two (二) legs (儿) stand at the beginning — the origin of a journey, the former time when you first stood up.
reading: The ゲン reading sounds like 'gen' (as in 'genesis') — picture the genesis of everything: two legs taking the first step at the beginning of time.

meaning: A mouth (口) on top of a pair of legs (儿) — the big brother who talks and walks ahead of you.
reading: Your big brother shouts 'kei!' (like 'kay') to get your attention. (ケイ)

meaning: A lid (亠) sits on top, a pair of legs (儿) stand below, and the katakana-mu shape (厶) is inside — you allot space and fill it up with these parts.
reading: You 'JUU' (like 'Jew' but with a long 'u') — fill the box with coins, saying 'JUU' as you stuff it full. (ジュウ)

meaning: A pair of legs (儿) stands on ice (冫), cracking it — that crack is a portent, a sign of danger ahead.
reading: A trillion is a huge number — imagine a CHOMP (チョウ) big enough to swallow the whole world, a portent of doom.

meaning: A pair of legs (儿) trapped in an open box enclosure (凵) with a dot (丶) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) above — this is wickedness, a villain lurking in a pit.
reading: キョウ — Hear the wicked villain's evil laugh 'Kyo!' (キョウ) as he sweeps his stroke (ノ) across the box, trapping the legs.

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) sweeps over the soil (土) while a pair of legs (儿) walks ahead — the legs are going before the soil, so they are in front.
reading: The pair of legs (儿) walks ahead, and you hear the sound 'SEN' (セン) — like 'sen'ior, the one who goes before you.

meaning: One (一) ray of light shines down, and a pair of legs (儿) walks toward it — the light is a beam that guides the legs, like a spotlight on a stage.
reading: Say 'ko' as in 'koala' — a koala holds up one ray of light, and its legs (儿) walk toward the light, saying 'ko' (コウ) in awe.

meaning: A mouth (口) and ten (十) stand on a pair of legs (儿) — you overcome obstacles by speaking ten times and walking on.
reading: コク — The pair of legs (儿) kicks a 'cock' (like a rooster) to overcome it — 'kok' sounds like 'cock'.

meaning: A mouth (口) with two short strokes on top (并) opens wide, and a pair of legs (儿) walk away — that's an exchange, giving something and taking something else.
reading: ダ — 'Dah' (ダ) — you say 'dah' as you swap items in a quick exchange.

meaning: A wrapping enclosure (勹) holds a mouth (口) and a pair of legs (儿) under a one (一) with a vertical stroke (｜) — you excuse them, dismissing them from duty.
reading: You say 'men' (メン) as you dismiss someone — 'men' are excused from the meeting, they can leave.

meaning: A rabbit hops along, its long ears flopping over a dot (丶) on its head, with a mouth (口) for nibbling and a pair of legs (儿) for jumping — the whole shape is a rabbit.
reading: The rabbit's name is 'Usagi' — imagine a rabbit wearing a tiny 'usa' (うさ) flag on its back, hopping through a 'gi' (ぎ) field of carrots.

meaning: A vertical stroke (｜) pokes through the day (日) to reveal a pair of legs (儿) — a newborn babe kicking under the sun.
reading: The babe's legs (儿) go 'ji' (ジ) as they kick — imagine a baby saying 'ji-ji' while wiggling its toes.

meaning: A child sits in a mortar (臼) to be bathed, with a pair of legs (儿) dangling over the edge — that's a young one.
reading: The child cries 'ji' (ジ) — imagine a toddler in the mortar, wailing 'ji-ji-ji' until you lift him out.

meaning: A rabbit hides under a wrapping enclosure (勹) for shelter, with a dot (丶) on its nose, a pair of legs (儿) for hopping, and an excuse (免) for stealing carrots — it's a rabbit.
reading: The rabbit says 'to' (ト) — picture it tapping its foot, going 'to-to-to' impatiently while waiting for a carrot.

meaning: A female rhinoceros stands with one (一) horn, a vertical stroke (｜) for its thick back, and a pair of legs (儿) — that's the beast.
reading: She snorts 'shi' (シ) — imagine the rhino blowing a 'shi-shi' whistle through her nose to call her calf.

meaning: A lid sits on top, with a pair of legs below, and two splayed strokes and a mouth inside — this is the official seal of one of the nine empire divisions, established by the emperor.
reading: The empire division was established by a man named 'En' (エン) who stamped his seal on the map.

meaning: A crown sits on top of an esteem, and below that a pair of legs. The esteem is so high that it needs a crown, and the legs are all marching together — that's your party or faction, all moving as one.
reading: The party's leader shouts 'TOW!' (like 'tow' a rope) to pull all the members forward together.

meaning: A white helmet sits on a pair of legs — the white part is the head piece, and the legs are the warrior wearing it.
reading: You put on the helmet and it feels like a 'TOU' (like 'toe') — you tap your toe on the ground to test the helmet's weight.

meaning: A sweeping stroke on top of a pair of legs, then another pair of legs on soil — the legs keep stepping forward, advancing over the ground.
reading: シン

meaning: A mouth (口) that says 'ten' (十) and a pair of legs (儿) that walk carefully — be discreet.
reading: Kyou (today) you must be careful.

meaning: The two splayed strokes look like a person walking into a doorway — the left stroke is the doorframe, the right stroke is the person stepping in. You are entering.
reading: Imagine a cow saying 'ニュウ' as it enters a barn — the sound is like a low moo that starts with 'nyu'.

meaning: A hook stroke (乙) hooks a person (人) and pulls them down into the ground — the person is swallowed, destroyed. The hook is the agent of destruction.
reading: ボウ — 'Bow' — the hook stroke bends like a bow, and the person is shot down by it — destruction comes from the bow's arrow.

meaning: A king (王) wears a hat on top (个) and raises two splayed strokes (ハ) like arms — this is the whole, complete ruler, nothing missing.
reading: ゼン — Imagine a Zen master saying "all is one" while wearing that hat — the whole universe is Zen.

meaning: Two (二) old coins sit inside an upside-down box (冂), with a vertical stroke (｜) splitting them and an enter (入) sign on top — that's the old coin, and also 'two'.
reading: The coin clinks 'ryo' (リョウ) — imagine tossing two coins into a box, hearing 'ryo-ryo' as they land.

meaning: A month enters under a hat on top, with a one below — when the month is at ease, you give an affirmative response, relaxed.
reading: You say 'You' (ユ) calmly, like a relaxed 'yes' to a friend's question.

meaning: The two splayed strokes are like two fingers spread apart, showing the number eight (like a peace sign but wider).
reading: Picture a chef slicing eight pieces of cake and shouting 'ハチ' — the sound is like 'hachi' (as in 'hatch' a chick).

meaning: Two splayed strokes on top of a katakana-mu shape — like a public park where the mu-shaped fountain is open to everyone.
reading: コウ — Imagine a 'ko' (コウ) sound echoing in a public square as a prince (公) announces a decree.

meaning: Two splayed strokes sit on top of a lid, like a tent covering six people huddled together.
reading: ロク — Imagine a giant clock striking six, and the sound it makes is 'rock' (ロク) as the hands hit the number six.

meaning: A 'bow' (弓) is drawn back, and the two splayed strokes (ハ) are the sound waves it makes — a breathy, musical 'ah' that adds emphasis to a poem.
reading: The bow twangs with a sharp 'kay' (ケイ) — like a hawk's cry echoing through a valley.

meaning: Two splayed strokes (ハ) sit on top of a vertical stroke (｜) that pierces through a one (一) and a two (二) — all these parts are together in one stack.
reading: Two splayed strokes (ハ) and the rest are all together, and you shout 'KYOU' (キョウ) — like 'co' in 'co-op', meaning together.

meaning: Two lines (二) crossing over a pair of legs (儿) — a frontier pass where you must close the gate and relate to the guards.
reading: グアン — Imagine a guard at the pass shouting 'Guan!' (like 'guan' in 'iguana') as he slams the gate shut, the two lines clanging.

meaning: A one (一) and an axe (斤) with two splayed strokes (ハ) — the soldier carries an axe and a spear, ready for the army.
reading: HEI (ヘイ) — a private in the army says “hei!” as he swings his axe, training with the troops.

meaning: A sweet (甘) thing sits on a plate with two splayed strokes (ハ) underneath — you point at it and say 'that' one, the one with the sweet topping.
reading: キ — Picture a key (キ sounds like 'ki') that you use to point at 'that' specific sweet thing on the plate — the key marks the exact one you mean.

meaning: One (一) eye (目) looks down at two splayed strokes (ハ) that are the legs of a tool, and the eye possesses the tool to see with it.
reading: The eye (目) stares at the two splayed strokes (ハ) and says 'GOO' — like 'goo' as in a sticky substance, but the eye is stuck to the tool and can't move, so it just goes 'guu'.

meaning: A vertical stroke (｜) and one (一) line on a day (日) with two splayed strokes (ハ) — that's the written code or law, a ceremonial document.
reading: You attend a ceremony where they read the law from a scroll — you hear 'ten' (テン) as they count the rules.

meaning: A lid covers a pair of legs and two splayed strokes, with a mouth below — you raise and support the mouth by feeding it, like a parent raising a child.
reading: You raise a sheep ('yang' — but here the sound is 'you'? No, this is the simplified form, so use the on-reading: 'yō' — but the list only gives kun? Actually the prompt says no reading given, so skip reading hook.)

meaning: Three stacked strokes (ヨ) and one (一) with two splayed strokes (ハ) on top of two short strokes (并) — all parts together, concurrently and in advance.
reading: You do it all at once, KEN (ケン) — like a 'ken' (a sharp glance) that sees everything beforehand.

meaning: A rice field (田) with two (二) splayed strokes (ハ) on top, a spoon (匕) and a left-side kata (爿) — you hope for a good harvest, wishing over the field.
reading: You hope and wish, 'key' to the future — like a key (キ) unlocking your dreams.

meaning: This is an upside-down box — picture a cardboard box flipped over, with the open side facing down and the two vertical sides hanging like flaps.
reading: The box is so big it covers a whole 'kyou' (a Japanese school classroom) — imagine the box dropping over the classroom, and the teacher yells 'KYOU!' in surprise.

meaning: An upside-down box (冂) sits on top of two (二) horizontal lines — the box is slowly sinking, its edges softening, like something tender and weak bending under weight.
reading: The box slowly sinks, 'zen' (ゼン) — like a gentle 'zen' meditation where everything gradually softens and weakens.

meaning: A person (人) is tucked inside an upside-down box (冂), like someone hiding inside a tent. The person is within the box, inside it.
reading: Picture a person inside a box, and the box says 'NAI' as it closes. 'ナイ' sounds like 'nigh' (as in 'near'), and the person is nigh — right inside.

meaning: The lid (亠) sits on top of the upside-down box (冂), with a vertical stroke (｜) and a one (一) inside — the lid seals the box into a perfect round coin. That coin is both a circle and the yen.
reading: エン — A yen coin rolls off a table and goes "EN!" as it hits the floor, spinning in a perfect circle.

meaning: A vertical stroke (｜) rises from the one (一) line, while the upside-down box (冂) wraps around the ten (十) cross, all tinted with a red, tan glow.
reading: Zen (ゼン) — picture a red-tan sunset over a desert, and a monk says 'zen' as he meditates on the color.

meaning: Two hands (廾) hold up an upside-down box (冂) with a vertical stroke (｜) and a barb (亅) sticking out — these are the bound pages of a tome, counted one by one.
reading: The tome is so thick it feels like a heavy 'satsu' (サツ) — picture a samurai slapping it down on a table with a loud 'satsu!'

meaning: The upside-down box (冂) encloses a mouth (口), but the mouth is empty and open — a dry, border prairie with no water, just a desert expanse.
reading: Kyou (キョウ) — imagine a 'kyou' (echo) in the empty desert, the sound bouncing off the box walls.

meaning: Two upside-down boxes (冂) sit side by side, connected by a one (一) line at the bottom, like a row of bound bamboo slips — a book volume.
reading: Satsu (サツ) — think of a 'satsu' (police badge) stamped on each volume to count them officially.

meaning: A vertical stroke pierces through the one and the upside-down box, then lands on the king. The king, annoyed, says 'again?!' — the stroke keeps coming back to bother him a second time.
reading: サイ — Imagine a 'sigh' (サイ) of frustration as the king sees the stroke return for the second time.

meaning: An upside-down box (冂) with a pair of legs (儿) and a mouth (口) inside — the mouth is open wide, letting in light, so the space is clear and bright.
reading: Think of a bright light that makes you squint and say 'KEI!' (like 'kay' but with a long 'a') — the 'kei' in 'KEI' is the sound of 冏.

meaning: A month (月) of risk — you face an upside-down box (冂) with two (二) swords crossed above it, daring to open it — that's brave.
reading: You brave the box and shout 'bo' (ボウ) — picture a hero kicking open the box with a loud 'BO!' sound.

meaning: A month sits inside an upside-down box, with a rice field and two on top — the helmet covers the head like a box over a field, protecting the warrior.
reading: The helmet makes a 'chu' (チュウ) sound as it clinks against armor.

meaning: You cover your eye (目) with a day (日) as a shield, then risk everything to face the danger head-on.
reading: You 'bow' (ボウ) forward into the risk, lowering your head like a boxer taking a punch to face the challenge.

meaning: An upside-down box (冂) with a vertical stroke (｜) and two (二) ones (一) and a ten (十) — all put together to form the inner palace, a secret room inside the box.
reading: The inner palace is where the KO (コウ) — like a 'ko' in 'kōbō' — holds court, putting together all the plans.

meaning: A crown sits on a pair of legs under an upside-down box, with a wrapping enclosure holding an excuse — this is the royal crown worn only with a formal excuse.
reading: ベン — The crown is so heavy it makes the king say 'BEN!' (like 'bend') as he bows under its weight.

meaning: This is the wa-shaped crown — it looks like a flat hat with a little bump on top, like the crown worn by a 'wa' (Japanese) emperor in old pictures.
reading: The crown is made of 'beki' (a type of hard wood) — imagine the emperor tapping the crown with his finger, and it makes a sharp 'BEKI' sound.

meaning: A crown sits on top of a table — but the table is already full, so the crown is superfluous, useless extra weight.
reading: You say 'JOU' (like 'joe') — 'Joe, this extra crown is useless!' — as you toss it off the table.

meaning: A crooked-big (尢) figure with a crown (冖) on its head, but a sweeping stroke (ノ) and a hook stroke (乙) pull it back — it wants to move forward but hesitates, doubtful.
reading: The crooked figure hesitates, going 'in' (イン) — like a person stuck 'in' a doorway, unable to decide to step out.

meaning: A crown sits on top of a wrapping enclosure, and inside that enclosure is a one. The crown is copying the design of the enclosure onto the one below, so you can describe or copy what you see.
reading: シャ — Imagine a 'sha' (like 'shah' of Persia) who is copying a royal decree, carefully describing every detail of the crown and the wrapped scroll.

meaning: A crown (冖) sits above an eye (目), and a one (一) is placed below — the crown fits perfectly over the eye, so it is suitable and proper.
reading: Imagine a judge saying 'This is GIven the right fit' — the 'gi' in 'GIven' is the sound of 冝.

meaning: A crown sits on a pair of legs, with a measurement and a beginning underneath — the crown marks the best, the peerless one who begins the reign.
reading: カン — The crown falls with a 'KAN!' clang onto the legs, the sound of metal hitting bone.

meaning: A crown (冖) sits on a pig (豕) with a dot (丶) on top — the pig is buried under a mound, only its crown showing, like a hillock grave.
reading: The mound is a CHO (チョウ) — like a 'chow' (チョウ) dog that digs a mound to bury its bone.

meaning: An excuse (免) with a dot (丶) on top is trapped under a crown (冖), while a pair of legs (儿) kick inside a wrapping enclosure (勹) — this is a false charge that wraps you up in hatred.
reading: The false charge makes you cry 'en' (エン) — like the sound of a long, drawn-out groan of injustice.

meaning: A crown covers the day, and two splayed strokes hang below — all light is hidden, so it's dark.
reading: In the dark, you say 'mei' (メイ) — like a ghost calling out 'mei' in the blackness.

meaning: A crown sits on top of a beginning, but below it a divining rod and a right hand grab a pair of legs — this is the foe who attacks from above, seeking revenge.
reading: The foe shouts 'KOH!' as he swings his sword, like a pirate yelling 'Koh!' before the strike.

meaning: A crown (冖) over a mouth (口) and a rice field (田) with one (一) line — the crown enriches the field, making it abundant and wealthy.
reading: The wealthy man says 'fu' as he counts his gold — a satisfied 'foo' of abundance.

meaning: A mortar (臼) under a crown (冖) with a wrapping enclosure (勹) and four dots (杰) — you write by grinding ink.
reading: Shark writes with a pen.

meaning: A large (大) day (日) is covered by a crown (冖) with grass on top (艾), and a towel (巾) hangs below — this covered, layered thing is like a power or exponent stacking up.
reading: The exponent grows so fast you shout “ベキ” (like “becky”) — Becky’s math power is huge.

meaning: This is the two-stroke water or ice radical — think of two small ice chips or two drops of frozen water sitting side by side on a cold surface.
reading: The ice is so cold it makes you shiver and say 'hyou' — imagine touching the ice and your breath turns to frost as you whisper 'HYOU'.

meaning: A stooping figure (夂) bends under a dot (丶) of snow, while a strike (攵) of cold wind hits them — that's winter's chill.
reading: トウ — Imagine a TOE (トウ) freezing in the snow, the stooping figure stamps it to warm up, but winter keeps striking.

meaning: Water (水) with ice (冫) on top — that's ice, and hail is just frozen water falling from the sky.
reading: ヒョウ — Picture a 'hyo' (ヒョウ) — a leopard — slipping on the ice (冫) and crashing into the water (水), making a splash.

meaning: Ice (冫) over a pig's head variant (彑) with one (一) and two (二) lines — freeze, be cold, and be clear as ice, attaining skill through cold focus.
reading: ゴ — Imagine a frozen pig's head (彑) saying 'Go!' (ゴ) as it freezes solid, the ice (冫) cracking with a clear 'go' sound.

meaning: The ice radical on the left cools the mouth in the middle, while a vertical stroke pierces upward through it — imagine the open sea where cold currents rise high into the sky, breaking the surface.
reading: チュウ — A chef in the open sea shouts 'CHOO!' as he tosses a giant ice cube into the water, making it splash high.

meaning: A person (人) with a sweeping stroke (ノ) and a ユ-shaped stroke (ユ) stands beside a large (大) block of ice (冫) — they must decide whether to cross the frozen river, and the ice cracks, forcing a quick judgment.
reading: ケツ — The judge slams his gavel and shouts 'KETSU!' (like 'get you') as he decides the fate of the frozen criminal.

meaning: Ice (冫) touches a tusk (牙) — the cold makes the tusk clear, sharp, and skilfully carved.
reading: The cold air makes the tusk 'SAY' (さ) a crisp, clear sound as it freezes.

meaning: The ice (冫) on the mouth (口) makes the legs (儿) shiver — so the situation is even more extreme, whether more or less.
reading: キョウ — Imagine a 'kyo' (like 'key-oh') concert where the singer's mouth is so cold from ice that they can only whisper, making the crowd want even more.

meaning: The mouth (口) of the furnace melts the katakana-mu (厶) shaped metal, with ice (冫) cooling it — that's smelting.
reading: ヤ — Picture a 'ya' (like 'yah') sound as the metal hisses when it hits the ice — a sharp, melting 'ya' hiss.

meaning: A hat on top (个) covers a seal (卩) that sits on one (一) block of ice (冫) — the ice makes everything cool and chill.
reading: The ice (冫) makes you say 're-i' (レイ) as you shiver — picture a frozen ray of light bouncing off the ice.

meaning: The bare bone on the left is frozen solid by the ice on top, while the reap on the right cuts through the cold air — the whole scene is bitingly cold.
reading: Imagine a cold wind that makes you say 'レツ' (retsu) as you shiver — like 'let's' but with a sharp, icy 're' at the start.

meaning: You use a vertical stroke (｜) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) to draw a hook (乙) on a pair of legs (儿) made of ice (冫), then wrap it (勹) with a mouth (口) to excuse (免) yourself – that's a request for a favour.
reading: Say 'バイ' (bai) like 'buy' – you're buying a favour by asking.

meaning: Ice, a vertical stroke, a sweeping stroke, a hook stroke, a pair of legs, and a hat on top — mud splashes up as you walk, covering your legs with a cold, wet layer.
reading: The mud makes a 'to' (ト) sound as you squelch through it — 'toe' deep in mud.

meaning: A woman stands on ice, her three stacked strokes of hair blown wild by a wind that also lifts a ten — this scene is so uncanny and threatening it feels horrible.
reading: The ice cracks with a sound like 'sai' as the weird woman steps — think of a horror movie where the villain whispers 'sai' before striking.

meaning: Ice covers the mouth of a box, and inside, ten mouths are frozen — the water withers and droops, leaving everything lame and dry.
reading: The withering plant goes 'KOH' as it snaps, like a dry twig breaking with a 'koh' sound.

meaning: Ice (冫) sits on an old bird (隹) — the bird is frozen, so it can only be a quasi-bird, semi-alive, an associate member of the flock.
reading: June (ジュン) is when the ice melts, but this bird is still half-frozen — it's only quasi-ready for summer.

meaning: Ice meets a barb, then three stacked strokes and a claw — the claw scrapes the ice clean, making it pure and spotless.
reading: The pure water is 'SOU' clear — imagine saying 'soh!' as you see it sparkle, like 'soap' but shorter.

meaning: A lid sits over a little mouth, and ice is beside it — the cool breeze makes the little mouth say 'ahh', nice and cool.
reading: The cool breeze makes you say 'RYOH' — like 'rio' but with a long 'o', as in 'Rio' the cool city.

meaning: Ice is next to a mouth, and the mouth is cold — this is the surname of a family known for their cool, calm demeanor.
reading: The surname is 'SEI' — imagine a cold 'say' — you say 'sei' and shiver, like 'say' but with an 'i'.

meaning: Ice is inside an upside-down box, and soil is at the mouth — the cold soil makes the plant wither and droop, lame and weak.
reading: The drooping flower goes 'CHOH' as it falls — like 'chop' but with a long 'o', as in 'chop' the stem.

meaning: A stooping figure (夂) with a pair of legs (儿) stands on soil (土) while ice (冫) forms above — they must endure the cold and keep the rain out to tide over the winter.
reading: リョウ — Imagine a person shouting 'RYO!' as they endure a freezing rainstorm, ice (冫) pelting their legs (儿) on the muddy soil (土).

meaning: Ice (冫) covers a day (日) and a tree (木) in a rice field (田) with a vertical stroke (｜) and one (一) — everything is frozen solid.
reading: The frozen field makes a TOE (トウ) — your toe goes numb from the cold.

meaning: Ice melts off a cliff, and a mouth shouts at a halberd — the water level decreases as the ice subtracts from the pool below.
reading: ゲン — The ice on the cliff cracks and falls with a 'GEN!' sound, like a giant 'gen'eration of water that diminishes the ice.

meaning: Ice, a dot, a sweeping stroke, two, and a large piece — all these parts are assembled together on a table to piece together a puzzle.
reading: ソウ — You 'sow' the pieces together like seeds — 'SOU' — to assemble them into one whole.

meaning: Ice sits on a tree to the west — the cold makes the tree shiver, and you shiver too from the severe cold.
reading: リツ

meaning: Ten drops of ice fall from an old bird's wing — the pattern matches exactly, like a standard to conform to.
reading: ジュン

meaning: Ice (冫) sits under a lid (亠) with a box (囗) and a mouth (口) inside, while a show (示) of two (二) little (小) strokes — all this makes a cold, strict, severe atmosphere.
reading: The cold air makes you shiver and say “リン” (like “ring”) — the ring of a frozen bell.

meaning: Ice (冫) under a lid (亠) with a grain stalk (禾) and a mouth (口) — the grain is frozen stiff, so the cold is strict and severe.
reading: The severe cold makes the grain stalk ring like a bell — “リン” (like “ring”).

meaning: The dart (矢) is stuck in ice (冫), and a spoon (匕) tries to chip it out, but the ice is so stiff that everything freezes solid — you're absorbed in trying to break it free.
reading: When the ice congeals, you shout 'GYO!' (ギョウ) as you slam the spoon down, but it just bounces off the frozen block.

meaning: A retainer stands on ice inside a box-on-side enclosure, while four dots at the bottom glow like embers — the whole scene is bright and splendid, as if lit by a glorious fire.
reading: The bright glow is like a 'key' turning on a brilliant light — think of a golden key (キ) unlocking a radiant, splendid hall.

meaning: This is a table or table enclosure — picture a low wooden table with a curved top and two legs, like a small desk you might sit at on the floor.
reading: The table is so rickety that when you lean on it, it goes 'ki' — imagine the table wobbling and making a creaky 'KI' sound as it nearly collapses.

meaning: A table (几) with a dot (丶) on top — the dot is ordinary, just sitting there, nothing special — commonplace and mediocre.
reading: ボン — Imagine a boring, ordinary party where everyone says 'ボン' (bon) like a dull drumbeat — so common it's mediocre.

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) sweeps over a table (几) and a hook stroke (乙) — this ordinary table is used by everyone, for any purpose, every day.
reading: The sound is 'ボン' — imagine a big 'BON' (like a bonfire) on an ordinary table, burning for everyone to see.

meaning: A table (几) is placed under a flag (尸) — you dwell there, sitting at the table beneath the banner of your home.
reading: Kyo (キョ) — imagine a 'kyo' (a giant) who dwells in a house, but his head pokes through the flag roof.

meaning: A stooping figure (夂) leans over a table (几) to dispose of papers, while a strike (攵) hits the table — you manage and deal with the mess by striking through items. The sentence is the final strike that disposes of the case.
reading: ショ — Picture a 'show' (like a courtroom show) where the judge strikes the table (攵) to sentence the stooping figure — that's how you dispose of the case.

meaning: A towel hangs from a table under an upside-down box, with a vertical stroke as the string — that’s a kite flying in the wind.
reading: The kite’s tail whips like a “TAKO” (octopus) in the sky — think of a tako-shaped kite.

meaning: A tree (木) stands beside a table (几) — but the wind blows so hard that the tree is bent over the table, and the wintry wind (こがらし) rattles the wood.
reading: こがらし — The wintry wind blows 'KO-GA-RA-SHI' through the tree, making the table legs shiver like a cold dog.

meaning: A stop (止) sign sits on a table (几) — when the wind stops, the sea becomes a lull, and the table is perfectly still, not a ripple in sight.
reading: なぎ — The sailor says 'NA-GI' (like 'naggy') as the calm sea makes the waves stop nagging the boat.

meaning: A person at the side leans on a table, but the gentleman on top is heavy — the table groans under the weight, so you recline on it.
reading: You lean on the table and sigh 'ヒョウ' (hyou) — like 'huh-yo' but said as one breathy sound, as if the weight pushes the air out of you.

meaning: A table stands under a one and a sweeping stroke, but the day and white inside it are blown around — the wind scatters them all.
reading: The wind howls 'フウ' (fuu) — like 'foo' but with a long, drawn-out 'u' as the gust passes through the table.

meaning: A king sits on a white table, and above him a female phoenix bird spreads her wings — she is the queen of all birds.
reading: オウ — The phoenix cries 'OW!' (like 'ouch') as she lands on the king's table — 'OU' is her royal call.

meaning: A mountain (山) of beans (豆) is on a table (几), with a mouth (口) singing and two short strokes on top (并) — that's the victory song after winning the bean-eating contest.
reading: The victory song rings out 'ガイ' (gai) — like 'guy' — as the winning guy sings loudly on the mountain.

meaning: A bench (凳) is a table (几) with a dotted tent (癶) overhead, holding beans (豆) and a mouth (口) while a hat (个) with two short strokes (并) sits on one (一) line.
reading: Imagine stubbing your toe (トウ) on a bench (凳).

meaning: The ice on the table is melting, and the horse leans on the table for support, relying on it to stay upright — this is evidence of its dependence.
reading: A horse leans on a table and lets out a loud 'HYOO' (ヒョウ) as it slips on the ice — that sound is proof it relied on the table.

meaning: This is an open box enclosure — think of a box with the top and one side missing, like a shallow tray or a U-shaped container open at the top.
reading: The open box is a 'kan' (a tin can) — imagine a tin can with its lid cut off, and you drop a coin in, it lands with a hollow 'KAN' clang.

meaning: The open box enclosure is a pit trap, and inside it a dot and a sweeping stroke are the villain's eyes peeking out — this is the face of disaster waiting to spring.
reading: The villain's evil laugh echoes as he shouts 'KYOU!' (like 'kyo' in 'kyoto') while the trap snaps shut.

meaning: Soil (土) is trapped inside an open box enclosure (凵) — a hard, dry dirt clod that breaks into pieces.
reading: Kai (カイ) — picture a 'kai' (shell) made of dirt, cracking open to reveal a clod inside.

meaning: A vertical stroke rises above a one and an upside-down box sitting on an open box enclosure — that’s a convex bump, like a beetle’s brow sticking out.
reading: The bump goes “TOTSU” as it pops out — like a sudden “tots” (tots of a hill) pushing upward.

meaning: An open box enclosure with a sunken middle — that’s a concave hollow, like a dent in a surface.
reading: The hollow is so deep you could pour “OU” (oh!) into it — you say “oh” as you see the sunken pit.

meaning: A mountain (山) is sitting inside an open box enclosure (凵) — but the mountain is pushing up and out of the box, with a vertical stroke (｜) as the escape route. The mountain is trying to exit the box, so this means 'exit' or 'go out'.
reading: You push open the exit door and shout 'SHUTSU!' (シュツ) like a ninja leaping out — 'SHUTSU' sounds like 'shoot' as you shoot out the door.

meaning: A one (一) water (水) drop falls into an open box enclosure (凵) — that's an archaic box (函).
reading: The box is 'kan' (カン) — like a can (カン) you store things in.

meaning: The open box enclosure is a container, and a right hand is putting something inside it — that’s a box you can open and close.
reading: カン — Imagine a big metal CAN (like a tin can) that you open with a right hand, and it’s the box you keep things in.

meaning: A vertical stroke is the blade, and a sweeping stroke is the curved edge — together they form a single-edged sword or saber.
reading: Imagine a sword slicing through a giant 'toe' (トウ) — the blade cuts the toe clean off.

meaning: A barb (亅) is stuck into a horizontal line (一), making it crooked and sly — like a tricky hook that catches you off guard.
reading: Imagine a tricky fox named 'Cho' (チョウ) who slyly steals a barb (亅) and hides it in a line (一).

meaning: This is the standing sword radical — it looks like a blade (刈) standing upright, ready to cut.
reading: Think of a sword that goes 'toe' (トウ) as it taps the ground — a sharp, standing blade.

meaning: A sword (刀) with a dot (丶) on its edge — that dot marks the sharp blade, the cutting edge of the sword.
reading: ジン — Picture a blade that 'ジン' (jin) — like a ringing 'zing' sound as it slices through the air — sharp and quick.

meaning: A sword (刀) with a tiny dot (丶) on its edge — that dot marks the sharp blade, the cutting edge.
reading: The sound is 'ジン' — think of a 'JIN' (like a genie) who slices through the air with a blade, leaving a shimmering edge.

meaning: A sword (刀) is flanked by a dot (丶) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) — the dot is blood, the stroke is a slash. The sword wounds, but from that wound something new is created.
reading: The sword strikes with a 'sou' (ソウ) — like a 'sow' (pig) that grunts as it digs up the earth to create a new furrow.

meaning: A sword (刀) cuts through two splayed strokes (ハ), splitting them apart. The sword divides the strokes into separate pieces — that's a part, a segment.
reading: Picture a chef with a sword slicing a cake into parts, and each slice goes 'BUN' as it falls. 'ブン' sounds like 'bun' (a bread roll), and each part is a bun.

meaning: A sword (刀) slices through a spoon (匕) — the spoon is cut clean in half, showing the sharpness of the blade.
reading: You 'setsu' the rope with a sword — 'setsu' sounds like 'set-sue', as in setting the blade to cut.

meaning: A sweeping stroke is the scythe blade, and the vertical stroke is the handle — together they reap a field, cutting and trimming the grass.
reading: You 'KAIRU' (like 'car' + 'ru') the lawn with a scythe, the blade clipping through the air with a sharp 'ka-ru' sound.

meaning: You reap (刈) a field of dry (干) wood, then carve it into a printing block — that's how you publish a book.
reading: The carved block is so heavy you grunt 'KAHN' (カン) as you lift it onto the press.

meaning: A sweeping stroke cuts through a reap, and then a ten — the result is a sharp whittling action, shaving off thin slices.
reading: Imagine a whittling knife that goes 'KAN' as it slices a piece of wood cleanly in two — the sound of the cut is 'kan'.

meaning: A reap (刈) action with a not (勿) sign — you reap the head, but the wrapping enclosure (勹) and sweeping stroke (ノ) show the head flying off — decapitate in one clean cut.
reading: フン — The executioner says 'FUN!' (like a quick puff) as the head is decapitated and lands with a soft thud.

meaning: Reap (刈) with two hands (廾) — but the top has a sweeping stroke, two, and one, like a judge's gavel — that's punishment, a sentence.
reading: The judge slams the gavel and shouts 'KEI!' — the sound of the sentence being passed.

meaning: A reap (刈) action with a halberd (戈) — you use the halberd as an oar to row a boat, slicing through the water with each stroke.
reading: カ — The rower shouts 'KA!' (like 'car') as he paddles the boat, the halberd cutting the water like a car engine.

meaning: A pair of legs (儿) stands on the beginning (元) of a field, but the reap (刈) tool trims away the edges — so you trim what's uneven.
reading: The 'gan' of 'gangrene' — you trim away the dead tissue. (ガン)

meaning: The reap radical on the left scoops out a ユ-shaped stroke from a large person on the right — leaving a hollow gouge in their side.
reading: ケツ — Picture a ketchup (ケツ) bottle being gouged open with a knife to scoop out the last bit of sauce.

meaning: The reap radical on the left cuts through the month on the right — but the month is shaped like a foot, so the cutting off of feet is the punishment.
reading: ゲツ — Say “getsu” like “gets you” — the punishment gets you right in the feet, chopping them off.

meaning: You reap (刈) what you sow, and the bare bone (歹) is laid out in a neat file — a row of bones in a rank.
reading: The row of bones goes 'RETS' as they click together — like 'rats' but with an 'e' — 'RETS'. (レツ)

meaning: A reap (刈) tool swings through a sentence (文), killing the words — this surname means kill or destroy.
reading: The 'ryu' of 'ryu' (dragon) — a dragon's breath destroys a sentence. (リュウ)

meaning: A sword (刀) cuts the cloth for the very first time — that's the beginning of making something.
reading: At the 'sho' (show) — the first time the curtain rises, the sword (刀) appears.

meaning: A vertical stroke (｜) and a reap (刈) with two (二) short strokes on top (并) and ten (十) — you judge by cutting through the parts to stamp a decision.
reading: You 'han' (hand) down the judgment — like a hand stamping the verdict on paper.

meaning: A mouth (口) and power (力) are wrapped in a wrapping enclosure (勹) — the power is separated from the mouth, so they fork off in different directions.
reading: You say 'bet' (ベツ) on which path to take when the road separates — a bet on the fork.

meaning: Soil (土) and a katakana-mu (厶) are cut by a sword (刀) — a threat that lasts for long ages, like a scar on the land.
reading: コウ — Think of a 'ko' (like 'core') threat: a sword stuck in the soil, its core rusting over long ages.

meaning: The reap radical (刈) on the left cuts, while the wrapping enclosure (勹) wraps around a stop (已) — you use the plane to scrape and stop the wood's roughness.
reading: The plane goes 'ホウ' as it shaves off a curl of wood, like a soft 'ho' sound with each push.

meaning: A grain stalk (禾) is reaped (刈) with a sharp blade — the profit is the extra grain you get from cutting it at the right time.
reading: The profit is 'ree' (リ) — like 'reap' but shorter, you reap the benefit.

meaning: A tome is being cut down by a reap tool, while an upside-down box and two hands hold it steady — the act of trimming a book down.
reading: Imagine a samurai (サン) using his sword to cut down a tome, slicing pages away with a loud 'SAN!'

meaning: The reap on the left scrapes against the mouth and tongue on the right — you scrape off the taste from your tongue with a sharp edge.
reading: You scrape off the grime and shout 'カツ' (katsu) — like 'cuts' but with a hard 'ka' at the start, as the blade cuts away the dirt.

meaning: You reap (刈) the climax (至) of your journey — you finally reach the soil (土) where you arrive, with the katakana-mu (厶) marking the spot.
reading: You arrive at the airport and the tower says 'toe' (トウ) — you land on your toe, reaching the ground.

meaning: A well (井) is cut by a sword (刀) while a vertical stroke (｜) and a dot (丶) and two splayed strokes (ハ) and a two (二) all come together — you establish something new by cutting into the well.
reading: You establish a new well with a 'ソウ' — like the sound of a sword slicing through earth to create.

meaning: A reap blade slices into soil, cutting it open — you use it to cut or slice off a piece, or pierce through.
reading: ケイ — Imagine a cake (ケイ) being sliced off with a sharp blade, the blade piercing the frosting.

meaning: A large hand with a sword reaps through the wrapping enclosure, cutting out the inside until only a cold, clear shell remains.
reading: The cold wind makes you say 'ko' as you carve out a hollow log with a sword.

meaning: A reap blade comes down on an ear — this is the punishment of cutting off ears.
reading: ジ — Picture a judge (ジ) ordering the ear-cutting punishment, the blade slicing with a decisive 'ji' sound.

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) cuts through a cow (牛) and a towel (巾) under two (二) — this is the system that controls and rules, like a law that trims and binds.
reading: The system is 'sei' (セイ) — picture a ruler saying 'SAY!' to enforce the law, like a strict 'SEI' command.

meaning: You reap (刈) a towel (巾) under a flag (尸) — the flag is printed with ink, and you brush the towel over it to make the print.
reading: The printing press goes 'SUTSU' (サツ) as it slams down — like a sharp 'sats' sound of the brush hitting the paper.

meaning: Two short strokes on top (并) sit above a person (人) and a large (大) sword (刀) — that's your ticket to the show, stamped with those strokes.
reading: ケン — Picture a ticket that you have to 'KEN' (as in 'ken' from karate) — you punch it with your fist to validate it.

meaning: A reap blade trims a tree with a sweeping stroke and a dot on top — this shapes a sacred temple spire.
reading: セツ — Imagine setting (セツ) a temple spire in place, the blade cutting the tree to a point.

meaning: A thorn is like a barb (亅) that pierces through a tree (木) and gets stuck in an upside-down box (冂) — you have to reap (刈) it out with a towel (巾) to stop the prick.
reading: The sound is 'shi' — imagine a thorny bush that says 'shhh!' like a librarian, but it's a 'she' (she) who pricks you with a needle.

meaning: A person (人) with a lid (亠) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) plus a dot (丶) uses a reap (刈) blade to engrave fine lines into wood.
reading: コク — The clock goes 'koku' as it engraves each hour into the wood.

meaning: A hat on top, a sweeping stroke, a dot, and a katakana-mu shape all sit above a sword — you use the sword to plunder and rob openly, taking everything under that hat.
reading: キョウ — Picture a robber shouting 'kyou!' (キョウ) as he openly plunders with a sword, the hat flying off.

meaning: A bow (弓) with a vertical stroke (｜) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) is used to reap (刈) hair, while two short strokes (并) mark the blade — you shave it all off.
reading: テイ — You shave with a steady 'TAY' (テイ) rhythm, like a barber's calm, repeated stroke.

meaning: You reap (刈) with a craft (工) tool near a curving river (巛) and a single line (一) — the act of cutting off a head, beheading.
reading: The beheading happens with a KAY (ケイ) — like a kayak paddle slicing through a neck, the curving river (巛) turning red.

meaning: A shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) and two splayed strokes (ハ) is reaped (刈) — the rule is to follow the law of the harvest, based on what the shellfish sees.
reading: ソク — A sock (ソク) is a rule — you must follow the rule of putting it on your foot, or it's just a floppy cloth.

meaning: A person uses a reap to cut into soil, trimming and filing it down — that’s cutting, filing, trimming.
reading: サ — Imagine a SAW (サ) — but it’s a reap — cutting into a pile of soil, filing it flat.

meaning: Reap (刈) the month (月) with esteem (尚) — you plane and sharpen it down to a fine edge.
reading: You whittle a stick and it goes 'SAKU' as each slice falls — サク.

meaning: A reap cuts through a mouth that is shouting, and a pair of legs stands on ten — that’s victory over the opponent.
reading: コク — Say “COCK” (コク) — a rooster crows victory with its mouth, standing on ten legs, after the reap wins the fight.

meaning: A vertical stroke and two splayed strokes are stuck into a tree, but the mouth is turned away — that’s opposed and biased.
reading: ラツ — Imagine RATS (ラツ) gnawing at a tree, but the tree’s mouth (a knot) is biased against them — opposed to their chewing.

meaning: A one (一) and a reap (刈) cut through a month (月), but two short strokes on top (并) point forward — so the cutting happens in front, before the month ends.
reading: ゼン — Imagine a farmer reaping a field, and a giant 'zen' (ゼン) bell rings — the bell is in front of him, calling him forward.

meaning: Two short strokes on top of two hands (廾) begin to build with a sword, but a sweeping stroke breaks it — that’s begin, break, fall.
reading: ソウ — Picture a SOW (ソウ) — a pig — using two hands to begin building a fence, but it falls and breaks, and the sword cuts it.

meaning: A reap knife slices through a day, but the not sign warns you to stop — so you only cut away the bad parts, leaving the rest. This is cutting out, not full reaping.
reading: テキ — A tech worker uses a reap knife to cut out a virus from a computer, saying 'テキ (tech) cleanup!'

meaning: A reap (刈) cuts through a mouth (口) and a stand up (立) — that’s dividing something into parts, like splitting a log.
reading: ボウ — Imagine a butcher’s cleaver going 'BOW!' as it divides a carcass in two.

meaning: A halberd (戈) is used to reap (刈) a field, but instead of cutting crops, it levels off the ground and trims the edges, leaving a smooth, pared-down surface.
reading: Imagine a SANdpaper block (サン) being used to trim and pare down a rough wooden edge, the sound of scraping 'san, san, san' as it levels the surface.

meaning: A mouth (口) opens wide as a barb (亅) on a halberd (戈) is thrust in, and the one (一) motion is a stab that pierces through, the seal (卩) of the wound closing around it.
reading: The stab goes 'SHI-ng' (シ) as the blade sinks in, like the sharp hiss of a snake striking, a quick, decisive 'shi' sound.

meaning: You reap (刈) with a sturdy blade, and the mount (岡) with its mountain (山) stands firm — plus two short strokes on top (并) and an upside-down box (冂) for armor, making you sturdy and strong.
reading: Sturdy means you can take a blow and go 'ゴウ' (gou) — like 'go' with a hard 'g', as in 'go hard'.

meaning: Under a roof (宀), in the evening (夕), a seal (卩) is used to press a mark, but then a halberd (戈) cuts it out, scooping the shape from the surface like carving a hole.
reading: You WANt (ワン) to scoop out the whole evening scene, and you say 'wan' as you dig the blade in, like a dog's bark echoing in the empty room.

meaning: A reap knife peels off a layer — the day fades and the color comes off, like skin peeling after a sunburn, leaving a pale patch.
reading: ハク — Haku (ハク) peels a sticker off a wall, the color fading as it comes off in one long strip.

meaning: A reap knife, a mouth, a large, a barb, and a one — you carve a large mouth onto a block, using the barb as a guide and the one as a ruler, chiseling out the shape.
reading: キ — Key (キ) carves a large mouth into wood, each stroke making the keyhole deeper and more precise.

meaning: A right hand holds a reap blade, repeatedly pricking a block to cut it into blocks or engrave it. The motion is sharp and repetitive.
reading: テツ — Imagine a metal 'tetsu' spike (like a railroad tie) pricking your palm as you try to engrave it.

meaning: A lid covers a mouth that is little, while a reap blade cuts a brand into the skin — the mark is small but permanent.
reading: ケイ — Picture a 'kay' (a small boat) being branded with a hot iron, the sizzle sounding like 'kei'.

meaning: Fire heats a reap blade, making it sharp-pointed — you sharpen the metal until it glows and can pierce.
reading: セン — A 'sen' (a coin) is so sharp it slices through paper — the edge is keen like a sen's rim.

meaning: A person with a hat on top (个) stands by a mouth (口) that is being reaped (刈) — the result is a sharp sabre that cuts through everything, even time, like a clock hand.
reading: ケン — Imagine a KEN (as in Ken the samurai) holding this sabre, and every time he swings it, the clock hand on his wrist spins wildly.

meaning: A sentence (文) is adjusted (斉) with two hands (廾) to reap (刈) a vertical stroke (｜) — this is the dose of medicine, carefully prepared.
reading: The dose is a ZAI (ザイ) — picture a 'zai' (like 'sigh') as you swallow the bitter pill.

meaning: Three stacked strokes (ヨ) are reaped (刈) by a blade, and water (水) spills out as the skin comes off — the peel falls away and the color fades.
reading: You 'haku' (ハク) the skin off — like a quick 'hack' (ハク) with a knife, then it peels.

meaning: A hook stroke and a large day under a cover — the cover hides the day, and the reap blade cuts away what is beneath, castrating.
reading: エン — An 'en' (a yen coin) is dropped into a dark cover, and the reap blade snips it — the sound is 'en'.

meaning: A grain stalk (禾) is left over after the reap (刈) — the left-side kata (爿) holds the spoon (匕) that scoops up the residue, but a vertical stroke (｜) marks the spot where nothing remains.
reading: JOE (ジョウ) — Imagine a waiter named Joe who scrapes leftovers into a doggy bag, saying, "Joe's got the remains!"

meaning: A hand with a reap (刈) cuts through a month (月) of growth, while two short strokes on top (并) mark the snipped ends — you clip and snip away the excess.
reading: The sound of scissors going 'sen, sen, sen' as you clip — that's the セン reading.

meaning: An upside-down box (冂) holds a mouth (口) inside a box (囗), and a reap (刈) slices it apart — you cut flesh from bones, separating the meat from the frame.
reading: You 'ka' (carve) the flesh off with a blade — that's the カ reading.

meaning: The 'reap' tool cuts a 'one' piece from the 'rice field' and puts it in the 'mouth' — that extra copy is the duplicate, and the one who carries it is the assistant or aide.
reading: フク — Picture a 'fuku' (a Japanese coat) that has a duplicate pocket — the vice-captain always keeps a spare fuku in his bag.

meaning: A vertical stroke and a sweeping stroke cross over a one, then a reap cuts it — after you reap the field, there's a surplus of grain left over, besides what you already gathered.
reading: ジョウ — Imagine a 'jow' (jaw) that has extra flesh — a surplus of chin — and you say 'besides this, there's more' as you point to the extra.

meaning: A mouth (口) and a person (人) stand under a hat on top (个), with a dot (丶) as the tip, all held by a sword (刀) — this is a sword, sharp and ready.
reading: The sword's blade gleams like a 'ken' (cane) in the sun — that's the ケン reading.

meaning: A lid (亠) sits on a roof (宀) over a mouth (口) and soil (土), while a reap (刈) cuts through — you divide the land and cut it into proportions.
reading: When you cut a cake into equal parts, you shout "KATSU!" like a karate chop — カツ.

meaning: A reap (刈) cuts grass on top (艾) while a mouth (口) under a hat on top (个) stays put — you use a sickle to cut, but the grass remains, so you stay and wait.
reading: You 'to' (toe) the sickle into the ground and stay — that's the トウ reading.

meaning: A scythe (刈) is suitable for cutting through a mountain (山) of beans (豆) and a mouth (口) — but the two short strokes on top (并) show it's not quite right for the job.
reading: GAI (ガイ) — Picture a guy (GAI) swinging a scythe at a bean mountain, but he keeps missing — "Guy, that's not suitable!"

meaning: A reap (刈) cuts a mouth (口) under a hat on top (个) with a one (一) — the cut creates a wound, the genesis of an injury. The reaping motion slices, and the mouth screams — that's the hurt.
reading: ソウ — Think of "sow" (ソウ) — you sow seeds, but a wound is like a cut in the soil — the genesis of growth and pain together.

meaning: A lid (亠) covers a cliff (厂) where soil (土) and a cow (牛) stand up (立), with a sweeping stroke (ノ) and a dot (丶) — you level off the ground, paring down the dirt with a reap (刈).
reading: You 'san' (sand) the ground smooth to level it — that's the サン reading.

meaning: A day (日) and an insect (虫) sit under a one (一) and a katakana-mu shape (厶), while a measurement (寸) and a reap (刈) cut through — you cut it all apart, clean and precise.
reading: You 'tan' (tan) the hide after cutting it — that's the タン reading.

meaning: Reap with a knife while showing two little things under the west — this is a threat: 'show me your two little treasures or I'll reap you.'
reading: The threat is 'hyo' (ヒョウ) — 'hyo' sounds like 'hio' — 'high-o' — the threat is to hang you high-o.

meaning: Reap the esteem of the rice field and the tree by the curving river — you destroy them all, cutting down both field and tree.
reading: Destroy with 'sou' (ソウ) — 'sou' sounds like 'sow' — sow the field, then destroy it by reaping everything.

meaning: A chisel (劂) is used by a person (人) to reap (刈) a cliff (厂) while wrapped in a wrapping enclosure (勹) with a left hand (屮) lacking (欠) one (一) and two short strokes (并).
reading: You engrave (劂) a 'kets' (ケツ) mark with the chisel.

meaning: To divide (劃) a rice field (田) using a brush (聿) and a reap (刈) tool, starting with one (一) line.
reading: Imagine dividing a field with a 'kaku' (カク) sound.

meaning: A brief note (劄) is a document where a person (人) writes one (一) word with a mouth (口) under two hats (个 and 个), then reaps (刈) it to separate.
reading: Think of a brief note (劄) as a 'satsu' (サツ) note.

meaning: A cliff holds a divining rod, a spoon, and tiger spots, while a pig is reaped by a right hand — this wild scene is a drama, a play.
reading: The drama is 'ゲキ' (geki) — like 'gecko' — a lizard that puts on a dramatic show.

meaning: A spicy (辛) mouth (口) screams as a sword (刀) and a flag (尸) stand up (立) — together they break and tear the air apart.
reading: The sound of a huge crack is 'HEK' — like a tree splitting with a sharp 'hekk'.

meaning: A reap (刈) tool made of gold (金) and a katakana-mu (厶) shape — this golden axe is a weapon of war used to kill en masse and peel paint.
reading: リュウ — Imagine a 'ryu' (リュウ) dragon wielding a golden logging axe, killing enemies in a war.

meaning: A day (日) of reaping (刈) with a sword (刀) — you amputate and cut off what's in the way.
reading: Imagine a surgeon saying 'KAI' as she chops off a limb — 'KAI' like 'cut' but with a sharp 'kai' sound.

meaning: A halberd with a barb and a cliff on top, plus a reap stroke and a stop — together they cut and injure, stabbing into whatever stands in the way.
reading: The sharp cut makes a 'kay' sound — like a blade slicing through with a high-pitched 'ケイ' as it strikes.

meaning: A person (人) with a hat (个) and a mouth (口) holds a reaping (刈) tool — but it's actually a sword (刀) — the sword is the star.
reading: The sword's clang is 'KEN' — like the sound of metal hitting metal, 'ken-ken'.

meaning: A lid sits above 'alike' parts, while a sword and two hands hold a family name — this is the measured dose of medicine, carefully prepared by hand.
reading: The dose is measured with a 'zai' — imagine a pharmacist saying 'zai' (ザイ) as they count out each precise pill.

meaning: A mouth and a person under a hat on top, with a dot and a sword — the person holds the sword, and the dot is the tip — this is the sword itself.
reading: The sword's blade rings with a 'ken' — like the clang of metal in a dojo, 'ken' (ケン) as it's drawn.

meaning: A nose with an eye and a rice field below, plus a reap stroke and two hands — the hands cut off the nose, a cruel punishment.
reading: The cut-off nose makes a 'gi' sound — like a gasp 'gi' (ギ) of shock as the blade falls.

meaning: A mouth and a person under a hat on top, with a dot and a sword — same as the other sword, but with a one added — this is a second, twin sword.
reading: The twin swords clash with a 'ken' — 'ken' (ケン) echoes as they strike together in a duel.

meaning: You use a reap blade to cut a frog into mince, but the frog's legs are still kicking — the wrapping enclosure holds it down while you chop, and the spoon scoops up the pieces.
reading: The reading is サン (san). As you mince, you chant 'SAN, SAN, SAN' with each chop — the sound of the blade hitting the cutting board.

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) and a vertical stroke (｜) over a one (一) and a pair of legs (儿) meet a tree (木) under a dotted cliff (广) with a non- (非) and a reap (刈) — you grind it all into mince with a blade.
reading: To mince, you say 'バ' like 'ba' — 'Ba-ba-ba' as the knife chops the meat into tiny bits.

meaning: A vertical stroke, a dot, and a sweeping stroke are being reaped by a wrapping enclosure that holds a flag, water, a buy, and an insect — all cut down at once. The flag and the insect are sliced by the reap, so the whole scene is a violent cut.
reading: The cut is so deep it goes through a thick 'chalk' (チャク) block, splitting it clean in two.

meaning: This is a single strong arm flexing — the hook stroke is the elbow, and the sweeping stroke is the forearm. It shows raw power.
reading: Think of a weightlifter grunting 'リョク' as he lifts a barbell — the sound is like 'ryoku' (rhymes with 'yoke').

meaning: Your craft (工) combined with raw power (力) produces a great achievement — the merit is the result of skill and effort.
reading: You win a medal for your achievement and the crowd chants 'KOH' (コウ) as you raise your power arm.

meaning: A mouth (口) is using its power (力) to join in and add more words to the argument — that's an addition to the conversation.
reading: カ — Imagine a car (カ) that can add more speed when you press the pedal — it increases its power.

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) over a little (小) thing, with power (力) below — the little one has less power, so it is inferior and worse.
reading: You say 'retsu' (レツ) when you see the weak one — like a short, sharp 'let's go' but for the loser, 'retsu' the lesser.

meaning: The power on the left and the axe on the right — both together make a strong force, like a mighty lumberjack.
reading: キン — A king (キン) with an axe in one hand and raw power in the other — he is strong enough to split a mountain.

meaning: An eye (目) is watching over you, and a power (力) comes to your side — that's help and rescue.
reading: ジョ — Imagine a 'Joe' (ジョ) who rushes in with his power to rescue you.

meaning: A woman uses her right hand to push against power — she toils and works as much as possible, straining against the force.
reading: ド — Imagine a diligent worker saying 'do it!' (ド) as they push with all their might, toiling without rest.

meaning: Soil (土) and a katakana-mu (厶) are crushed by power (力) — a threat that lasts for long ages, like a mountain pressing down.
reading: コウ — A 'ko' (like 'core') threat: the power of the earth's core presses the soil for eons.

meaning: The mouth (口) is wrapped in a wrapping enclosure (勹) while power (力) is used — you become tired from working busily, mouth shut, straining.
reading: ク — Picture a 'coo' (ク) sound of a tired dove, its mouth wrapped, working hard — a weary 'coo'.

meaning: A mouth calls out to a sword and power — the call to work hard and be beautiful in effort. The sword and power combine to show that this beauty is earned through diligence.
reading: ショウ — Imagine a SHOW where a performer balances a sword on their mouth, working hard to make it look beautiful.

meaning: An axe (斤) and power (力) under a cliff (厂) — you need both to encourage yourself to keep working hard.
reading: レイ — The cliff (厂) is where you shout 'ray!' (like a sun ray) to inspire yourself to keep going.

meaning: Under a crown (冖), a person works hard with their power (力) — that's labor and toil.
reading: ロウ — Think of a 'row' (ロウ) of workers laboring under a crown.

meaning: A person with two splayed strokes and a large two-part shape leans on power — but the power gives out, and they become fatigued and stop.
reading: ケン — Imagine a tired worker saying 'ken' (ケン) as they stop, their legs (two splayed strokes) giving way under the weight.

meaning: A father (父) uses power (力) under a lid (亠) — his effort has merit, making things work efficiently.
reading: The medicine is 'KO' (like 'co' in 'cough') — it works, easing your cough with real efficacy.

meaning: A king (王) is trapped in a box-on-side enclosure (匚), pushing against the walls with all his power (力) — he's flurried and frantic, rushing around in a zealous panic.
reading: The flurried king shouts 'KYOU!' (キョウ) as he bangs on the box walls, like a panicked 'kyoo!' cry.

meaning: A gentleman (士) with a mouth (口) uses his power (力) to carefully and hard-strive to speak the right words — he's cautious, grinding his effort into every syllable.
reading: He strives so hard he lets out a sharp 'KATSU!' (カツ) — like a karate chop of effort, 'katsu!' as he pushes through.

meaning: A person (人) with a lid (亠) and a dot (丶) uses power (力) to investigate — they censure and probe into your crimes.
reading: The censure comes with a 'GAI' (ガイ) — like a 'guy' in a trench coat, a detective who digs up the truth.

meaning: A curving river (巛) flows past a craft (工) workshop, and the power (力) of the water is so strong it bends the river's course — that's strength.
reading: ケイ — Imagine a strong man flexing his biceps and shouting 'KAY!' (like 'ケイ') as he bends a steel bar.

meaning: A child (子) suddenly rises up from under a crown (冖), grabbing ten (十) power (力) — the suddenness of the action startles you.
reading: ボツ — 'Bots' (ボツ) are sudden robot uprisings — picture a child (子) robot suddenly popping up with power (力) and ten (十) arms.

meaning: A mother (母) says 'do not' (毋) to a sweeping stroke (ノ) and one (一) power (力) — but the child is still active and clever, dodging quickly.
reading: ビン — 'Bin' (ビン) is a smart, quick bin that jumps away when you try to throw trash — it's active and clever, just like the mother (母) warns.

meaning: An imperial order is a vertical stroke (｜) of power (力) from a single (一) mouth (口) over a tree (木) – a decree carved on wood.
reading: チョク sounds like 'choke' – if you defy the imperial order, you'll be choked.

meaning: A rice field (田) is being pushed by a マ-shaped stroke (マ) and power (力) — that power is courage, and it cheers you up to see it.
reading: The brave soldier shouts 'YUU!' as he charges, the sound echoing across the rice field.

meaning: You have an excuse (免) to use your power (力) — but instead you use it to strive and exert yourself. The excuse is a pair of legs (儿) running away, but you grab it with power to study.
reading: You 'BEN' — like 'bend' — you bend your back over books to study with exertion.

meaning: A seal presses down on a power that is split by two splayed strokes and a one-two — the labor exhausts the power until it is tired.
reading: ケン — A 'ken' (a sword) is heavy to lift, and after swinging it you are tired — the effort is 'ken'.

meaning: A lid over a mouth and a little power — the mouth is fierce, and the power is strong, like a shout that shakes the ground.
reading: ケイ — A 'kay' (a kayak) paddled with fierce strength — the strong strokes make the water roar 'kei'.

meaning: A person with power (力) under a tree (木) receives an imperial degree — the tree is the royal seal, and the power is the authority it grants. The degree itself is a daoist magic scroll that makes the tree bow.
reading: The imperial degree is announced with a loud 'BAU' (バウ) — like a royal herald shouting 'Bau!' to silence the crowd before reading the decree.

meaning: A person (人) uses power (力) to straighten a tree (木) — this is the reward for good behavior: the power to correct and govern. The tree is the subject, the person is the ruler, and the power is the reward itself.
reading: The reward is a 'RAI' (ライ) — like a knight being rewarded with a shiny 'rye' (ライ) coin, a golden grain of payment for service.

meaning: The leather part of a horse's bridle is the halter, and the bit is the metal piece in the mouth — but here, the leather is being pulled tight by power, so you cinch the halter and bit firmly.
reading: ロク — Imagine a horse's halter and bit made of solid rock (ロク) that clinks like stone as the horse moves.

meaning: A mask (面) is pressed down by power (力) — you must endeavor and make effort to keep the mask from slipping, urging yourself onward.
reading: ベン — Picture a bench (ベン) where you sit, straining with effort, pushing against a heavy mask with all your power.

meaning: A vertical stroke (｜) and one (一) over a day (日) — the sun moves across the sky, pulled by a ri (里) of power (力) — that's motion.
reading: The sound is ドウ — picture a 'dough' (ドウ) ball rolling down a hill, moving and changing shape as it goes.

meaning: An upside-down box (冂) holds two (二) eyes (目) — you look inside and see power (力) — this is a stern enjoinment, a preaching to yourself to get moving.
reading: キャク — Imagine a preacher shouting 'キャク!' (like 'cack!') to wake up a sleepy congregation, urging them to act.

meaning: The day (日) and an eye (目) both watch your power (力) — so you must be diligent, working hard all day under that watchful gaze.
reading: キョク — Think of a diligent student who says 'キョク' (like 'kyoku' — a tune) while practicing scales every day, never slacking.

meaning: A box-on-side enclosure holds a sweet thing, but a pair of legs kicks it away — you must use your intuition to check and compare what's inside before you act.
reading: A detective uses his intuition to find the hidden 'kan' (can) of beans in the box-on-side enclosure.

meaning: A halberd (矛) with power (力) strikes (攵) — this is your task, your duty, something you must do with force and effort.
reading: ム — Imagine a 'moo' (ム) from a cow — you have the duty to milk it, and the halberd and power are your tools for the task.

meaning: A meritorious deed earns you a rank — the eye (目) sees the shellfish (貝) prize, while two splayed strokes (ハ) and power (力) push you up, but the mouth (口) must stay shut about the secret merits.
reading: KUN (クン) — Think of a brave knight (KUN) who gets a medal for his deed — "Kun, you've earned this rank!"

meaning: A person (人) with two short strokes on top (并) and a month (月) of power (力) — that person wins by outlasting everyone.
reading: ショウ — Imagine a winner shouting 'SHOW!' as they reveal their victory trophy to the crowd.

meaning: To thank for a reward, you crown (冖) the fire (火) with power (力) — the fire works hard, so you reward it with a thank-you note.
reading: ROU (ロウ) — Imagine a row (ROU) of workers sweating by a fire, and you thank each one with a reward — "Row, thank you!"

meaning: Grass on top (艾) covers a large (大) day (日) of power (力) — you recruit people for a campaign, gathering contributions under the sun.
reading: ボ — Imagine a billboard (ボード) on a street corner, advertising a recruitment drive — 'ボ' for the bold letters.

meaning: Feathers and power, with a hat on top, ice, and three — combine all these forces: feathers (air), power (strength), ice (cold), three (many) — join forces together.
reading: Join forces with 'riku' (リク) — 'riku' sounds like 'rick' — Rick joins forces with you to lift the ice.

meaning: Soil (土) and power (力) combine with a dot (丶) and a pair of legs (儿) plus nine (九) — the forces gather like a military march.
reading: The forces have SEI (セイ) — picture a say (sei, as in 'say cheese') command that rallies an army, their energy surging forward.

meaning: A shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) and two splayed strokes (ハ) sits under a lid (亠) on soil (土), while power (力) pushes it up — that's a hard-won merit, an achievement piled on the ground.
reading: The merit of a warrior is measured in 'seki' (セキ) — imagine a samurai stacking his trophies next to a giant 'seki' stone (a Japanese stone marker) in the field.

meaning: Soil (土) with two (二) and one (一) lines, plus a mouth (口) and power (力) under grass on top (艾) — diligence means serving with steady effort, becoming employed.
reading: キン — Picture a king (キング) working diligently at a desk, serving his kingdom with tireless effort.

meaning: Esteem (尚) for a rice field (田) and a tree (木) is ruined when a curving river (巛) floods, and power (力) is used to destroy and steal what's left.
reading: To 'sou' (ソウ) is to swoop down like a hawk — imagine a thief with a 'sou' (soul) stealing rice from the field, then destroying the tree with a swipe of power.

meaning: An old bird (隹) holds a dart (矢) and a from (ノ) part, while a 乞-shaped part (乞) and power (力) push you — together they persuade and encourage you to act.
reading: カン — You recommend (勧) something so strongly that you say 'CAN!' (カン) — you can do it!

meaning: To work hard (勩) is like a shellfish (貝) using its power (力) to lift a generation (世) of one (一) vertical stroke (｜) and two splayed strokes (ハ) while keeping an eye (目) on the goal.
reading: Toil (勩) sounds like 'eight' (エイ) — you work eight hours.

meaning: Three powers (力) and three hearts (心) in a rice field (田) — all working together, peaceful and harmonious.
reading: Harmony feels like a gentle 'KYO' — like a calm 'kyo' sound in a quiet temple.

meaning: The Chinese emperor (禹) with grass (艾) on his head puts forth effort (力) inside an upside-down box (冂) — striving forward with all his might.
reading: Striving forward is 'BAI' — like 'by' but with a determined 'bai' as in 'bai-bai' (goodbye) — you push on.

meaning: A vertical stroke (｜) with power (力) under a day (日) and one (一) plus a sweeping stroke (ノ) — the day's power is earned through a meritorious deed, marked by the stroke of honor.
reading: クン — A knight earns a 'coon' (クン) medal for a brave deed, the medal shining under the sun.

meaning: A vertical stroke of power pierces through a rice field, and four dots at the bottom scatter like seeds — this is the mark of a meritorious deed that earns rank.
reading: The emperor awards a medal for merits with a loud 'KUN' (like 'coon' in raccoon) — imagine a heroic raccoon saluting as it receives the honor.

meaning: A rice field under a cliff, with the name of a chinese emperor standing beside it — the emperor's decree pushes you to strive and encourages the farmers below.
reading: The emperor shouts 'REI' (like 'ray' of sunlight) to encourage the workers — a bright ray of light strikes the field, making them strive harder.

meaning: In haste, you run with a garment over your head, a lid on top, and power in your mouth — you're helping someone urgently, but you're so rushed you've put your clothes on wrong.
reading: The reading is ジョウ (jou). Picture someone running in a hurry shouting 'JOU!' (like 'joe') — 'Joe, hurry up!' — as they rush to help.

meaning: An old bird sits on grass on top, while a mouth with ten power urges it to move — you persuade and encourage the bird to fly, but it just stares back.
reading: The reading is カン (kan). Imagine you 'can' persuade the bird — 'kan' sounds like 'can' — you know you can encourage it to take off.

meaning: A wrapping enclosure — the shape is like a bent arm (亅) pulling a cloth (一) around something, wrapping it up tight.
