reading: ダツ — 'Dats' like 'darts' — she throws darts at a board with her name on it.

meaning: A woman (女) is holding a spoon (匕) and a barb (亅) under a sweeping stroke (ノ) and two splayed strokes (ハ), all wrapped in a wrapping enclosure (勹) — this is a woman you address directly, like 'you' (female).
reading: The 'nai' in 'naiad' (a water nymph) — picture a female 'you' as a graceful naiad rising from a river, calling out to you.

meaning: The younger sister (妹) is a woman (女) with a lid (亠) on her head, standing by a tree (木) with two splayed strokes (ハ) and two (二) vertical strokes (｜).
reading: My (マイ) younger sister is the one I adore.

meaning: A woman (女) stands next to a tree (木) — but this is not just any woman; she is the infamous wife of the last Xia ruler, remembered as a tree of ruin.
reading: The 'bai' in 'bail' — picture her being 'bailed out' of trouble, but she's the one who caused the dynasty's fall.

meaning: A wife is a woman (女) who stands under three stacked strokes (ヨ) and a one (一) — like a roof and a line of authority over her household.
reading: Imagine a wife sitting at a table, and her husband hands her a 'sigh' (サイ) — she sighs deeply, 'SAI...' as she takes the bills.

meaning: A woman (女) with a sweeping stroke (ノ) and a heart (心) — she's exceedingly feminine, a lady attendant who sweeps the floor with a heart-shaped broom.
reading: ヒ — 'He' — she says 'he he' as she giggles while sweeping, the maid.

meaning: A woman (女) who stands up (立) when her master enters — she is the concubine, always at attention.
reading: ショウ — Imagine a concubine saying 'SHOW' as she presents herself to the lord, like a performer on stage.

meaning: A woman (女) wrapped in a wrapping enclosure (勹) with a mouth (口) inside — like a beautiful face framed by a veil, so the whole image means beauty.
reading: The beauty's name is 'Kuu' — imagine saying 'coo' softly to admire her, like 'coo, what a beauty!'

meaning: A woman (女) who stops (止) at one (一) — she is presentable, composed, and knows exactly where to stand.
reading: セイ — She says 'SAY' with a poised smile, as if introducing herself at a formal gathering.

meaning: A woman (女) who is like a mother (母) but also says 'do not' (毋) — she is the wet nurse, caring yet firm with the children.
reading: ボ — The wet nurse hums 'BO' as she rocks the baby, a soft lullaby sound.

meaning: A woman (女) who stands up (立) with a hat on top (个) and a マ-shaped stroke (マ) — she's a wise sage, her knowledge lifting her above others.
reading: The wise woman's name is 'Rei' — picture her saying 'ray' of wisdom, like a sunbeam from her mind.

meaning: A woman (女) under a lid (亠) holding a towel (巾) — that's your elder sister, always tidying up the house.
reading: シ — Your elder sister says 'she' (シ) did it — she's the one in charge.

meaning: An elder sister (女) with a tusk (牙) — she's the one who 'tusks' you gently, like a big sister's playful nudge.
reading: Call her 'Ane' — imagine saying 'ah, nee-san!' as she walks in, the elder sister you look up to.

meaning: A woman (女) opens her mouth (口) to speak the first word, and the katakana-mu shape (厶) is the seed she plants — that's the commence.
reading: She says 'SHI' (she) as she begins — the woman starts with 'shi' — シ.

meaning: A woman (女) is dragging a tome (冊) with two hands (廾) — she moves so slowly it looks like she's slandering the ground with each step, and people ridicule her pace.
reading: サン — Imagine a woman (女) slowly dragging a tome (冊) and someone yells 'SAN!' (like 'sand' but short) at her to hurry up.

meaning: A woman (女) with a big eye (目) — she's the elder sister who watches everything you do, like a maidservant keeping an eye on the household.
reading: ソ — Picture your elder sister (姐) saying 'SO?' (ソ) with a raised eyebrow when you ask for something.

meaning: A woman (女) who has a mouth (口) that talks ten (十) times more than you — that's your mother-in-law.
reading: The mother-in-law says 'KO' (コ) like a crow, cawing orders at you from her perch.

meaning: A woman (女) with a dot (丶) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) — she's the wife of your elder brother, a small but sharp presence who sweeps in and takes charge.
reading: シ — She's the wife of your elder brother, and she always says 'SHI!' (シ) like 'shh!' to quiet the kids.

meaning: A woman (女) gives life (生) to a family, and that family's name is the surname — the name passed down through her line.
reading: Your surname is on your SEat card (セイ) at the wedding — everyone calls you by that name when you sit there.

meaning: A grain stalk (禾) leans on a woman (女) — you entrust the harvest to her. She carries the stalk, so you leave the task to her.
reading: イ — Picture an 'eel' (イ) that you entrust to the woman. She holds the grain stalk in one hand and the slippery eel in the other, and you leave it all to her.

meaning: A woman (女) is lying down like a sweeping stroke (ノ) next to a person at the side (化) who is a gentleman (士) — she is pregnant, and the gentleman is her partner.
reading: The pregnant woman is a NINja (ニン) sneaking around with a big belly.

meaning: A woman (女) with a pair of legs (儿) stands on ice (冫) — her graceful pose is beautiful, like a dancer on a frozen lake.
reading: She is so beautiful that you say “yo” (ヨウ) — like “yo!” in awe, as she glides across the ice.

meaning: A king and a woman stand under two short strokes on top, while a sheep grazes nearby — this is the ginger-flavored dish served at the royal table.
reading: キョウ — Picture a giant ginger root singing 'kyo!' (キョウ) like a karate shout as it's chopped.

meaning: A beautiful girl (女) stands under a tree (木) with a single (一) sweeping stroke (ノ) of hair — she is the prettiest in the grove.
reading: She is so beautiful she makes you say 'SUE' (ス) — like the name of a stunning girl.

meaning: A woman (女) is with a gentleman (士) who has a mouth (口) — she is his concubine, kept quiet and obedient.
reading: The concubine is a KIT (キツ) — a small fox that follows the gentleman around.

meaning: A woman (女) with a lid (亠) on her head and a father (父) beside her — she is beautiful and handsome, like a perfect daughter.
reading: She is so pretty, she makes you say 'KO' (コウ) like a crow admiring her.

meaning: A woman (女) meets a mouth (口) under a single (一) sweeping stroke (ノ) — they mate and become good partners.
reading: They meet and mate with a 'KO' (コウ) sound, like two doves cooing.

meaning: An old man (老) holds a spoon (匕) and a woman (女) — she is the old woman who feeds him.
reading: The old woman is a 'BO' (ボ) — like a grandma who says 'boo' to scare kids.

meaning: Three women in a room — each one gossiping and scheming. The overlapping voices create wicked mischief, and the chaos leads to seduction and worse.
reading: A wicked villain shouts 'KAN!' as he slams his fist on a table, making the three women scatter in fear.

meaning: A woman (女) is pinned under a dry (干) branch with a one (一) and ten (十) marks — she's trapped, and the situation is wicked and mischievous.
reading: The villain says 'KAN!' again, but this time he's using a dry stick to poke the trapped woman.

meaning: A woman (女) with a bow (弓) and a large (大) person (人) beside her — she's the younger sister who follows the big sister around, always ready to shoot arrows.
reading: The younger sister shouts 'TEI!' as she shoots an arrow from her bow, hitting a target shaped like a big 'T'.

meaning: A woman (女) reaches the climax (至) of a story — she's the niece, and her uncle is telling her a thrilling tale that ends with a soil (土) and a katakana-mu (厶) twist.
reading: The niece says 'TETSU!' as she jumps up at the climax, knocking over a soil pot shaped like a 'T'.

meaning: A woman (女) who is served by a retainer (臣) — that’s a princess, always attended and never alone.
reading: The princess says 'ひめ' (hime) — imagine her whispering 'hee-me' as she hides in her tower, like 'he me' (she’s me).

meaning: A lady (女) stands under the sun (日) with a one (一) line drawn across the sky — she's a noble lady, calm and composed, watching the day pass.
reading: The lady bows and says 'KOU!' as the sun rises, her one line of shadow stretching long like a 'K'.

meaning: A woman (女) with a large (大) wrapping enclosure (勹) around two (二) items — she's beautiful and elegant, carrying her treasures gracefully.
reading: She says 'KA!' as she opens the wrapping enclosure, revealing a beautiful 'K' shaped jewel inside.

meaning: A woman (女) sits under a hat (个) with a mouth (口) that stays shut and a single (一) calm line — she's good-looking because she's quiet.
reading: The 'ai' in 'aisle' — she walks down the aisle looking good-looking and quiet.

meaning: A woman (女) under an open roof (冂) with a barb (亅) and a vertical stroke (｜) — she's so beautiful that even the frame of the mirror can't contain her, and she stands out like a perfect picture.
reading: ケン — She's so beautiful you say 'KEN!' (ケン) like 'can you believe it?' — short and sharp.

meaning: A woman (女) stands inside a large (大) box (囗) — she is boxed in by matrimony, the marriage bond.
reading: イン — Think of an 'inn' (イン) where a wedding is held — the bride and groom marry there.

meaning: A woman (女) stands in the ice (冫) — but she lacks (欠) warmth, so her figure (姿) is a frozen, still shape.
reading: シ — Picture a 'she' (シ) — a woman's silhouette — that's her figure, her shape.

meaning: A woman (女) holds a halberd (戈) with a sweeping stroke (ノ) over a single (一) line — this is the name of a legendary concubine, a woman of war and myth.
reading: Think 'shoo' — you shoo away the concubine's name, it's just a historical footnote.

meaning: A woman under a cliff faces a halberd — she intimidates with dignity, her majesty menaces.
reading: The queen raises her halberd and cries 'I!' (イ) — her presence alone intimidates the crowd.

meaning: A woman (女) stands on soil (土) — she's beautiful, like a statue planted in the earth.
reading: The 'wa' in 'waltz' — she waltzes beautifully across the soil.

meaning: A woman (女) carries rice (米) — she wears the surname of a constellation, a starry burden of grain.
reading: The 'ru' in 'ruler' — the ruler of the constellation wears the rice.

meaning: To ask after a woman's name, a man sends a messenger with a vertical stroke (｜) as a pointer, a woman (女) standing by a rice field (田) with a one (一) line drawn in the dirt, and a wrapping enclosure (勹) holding a gift. The messenger points to the woman and asks her name — the whole scene is about that polite inquiry.
reading: The marriage inquiry is a formal 'hei' — imagine the messenger bowing and saying 'hei' (like 'hay') as he presents the gift, the sound echoing across the rice field.

meaning: A brother's wife is a woman (女) who lives in the same ri (里) — the village unit — so picture her standing in the center of the ri, with the woman radical on the left and the ri on the right. She is the woman of the household, tied to the same village as her husband's brother.
reading: The brother's wife is called 'ri' — like 'ree' — imagine her calling out 'ri!' to her husband's brother from across the rice fields, her voice carrying over the ri.

meaning: A woman stands on a cliff, holding a halberd with a barb at the top—her posture is so straight and slim that she looks slender and beautiful.
reading: Say 'say' as you admire her slender form—'セイ' (sei) sounds like 'say' when you point and say, 'Say, what a beautiful body!'

meaning: An old woman stirs a little water at the side of a bowl with a sweeping stroke—she's too frail to do more, so she's just an old woman.
reading: She shuffles with a 'sha' sound—'シャ' (sha) like the 'sha' in 'shamble', the slow, dragging walk of an old woman.

meaning: A woman with a 'do not' sign over her head, but she's also a mother—she's the matron who tells everyone 'do not' run in the halls.
reading: She says 'bo' like a gentle 'bo' in 'bob'—'ボ' (bo) as in 'bob your head' when the matron nods at you.

meaning: A woman under a flag, stroking fur—she complies with orders, agreeable and calm, like a cat being petted under a banner.
reading: She purrs 'bi' like a soft 'bee'—'ビ' (bi) as in 'bee' that hums agreeably, complying with the flower's call.

meaning: A woman (女) stands in the northeast (艮) corner of the house — she is the daughter, the girl of the family.
reading: The daughter is a JOE (ジョウ) — think of 'Joe' the girl, who always answers 'jo' when called.

meaning: A woman in a rice field with power—she's shouting so loud that the whole field hears her loud talking over the power of her voice.
reading: She yells 'nan' like 'nan' in 'nanny'—'ナン' (nan) as in 'nanny' who scolds loudly across the field.

meaning: A woman with a sword from her home country, standing on two lines—she moves with graceful, elegant steps, like a dancer with a blade.
reading: She dances 'da' like 'da' in 'dance'—'ダ' (da) as in 'dah' when you see her graceful move, 'Da-ah, so graceful!'

meaning: A woman (女) with a mouth (口) that curves like the month (月) — her beauty is in her face, especially her smile.
reading: エン — Imagine a beautiful face so striking it makes you say 'EN-core!' every time you see it.

meaning: A woman (女) wears a garment (衣) that stretches over the sign of the dragon (辰) — she is with child, and the cliff (厂) of her belly rises.
reading: The pregnancy makes her glow — she hums 'SHIN' (シン) like a soft shin-dig of new life.

meaning: A woman (女) who is a younger sister — she has a bow (弓) and two short strokes (并) on top, like a little sister's hair tied up, and a vertical stroke (｜) with a sweeping stroke (ノ) marking her as the second daughter.
reading: テイ — Picture the younger sister serving tea (テイ) to her older sister, always polite and obedient.

meaning: A woman (女) dressing up — she stands beside a left-side kata (爿) (a wooden frame) and a gentleman (士) who watches her put on her finery.
reading: ソウ — She dresses up to go to a 'sow' (ソウ) — a pig — no, wait, she's going to a fashion show (ソウ) where she struts on the runway.

meaning: A woman (女) with a barb (亅) and a halberd (戈) — she is so beautiful that even her weapon looks graceful, like a dancer's prop.
reading: ガ — Her beauty makes you gasp (ガ) — 'GA! She's stunning!'

meaning: A woman (女) with a mouth (口) that is smiling, and two short strokes on top (并) like decorative hairpins, plus a pair of legs (儿) standing gracefully — she is simply good looking.
reading: The good-looking woman says 'tai' as in 'tie' — she ties her hair back to show off her face.

meaning: A woman with an excuse (a pair of legs wrapped in a wrapping enclosure) — she's busy bearing children, so she's excused from work.
reading: She bears a child with a BEN — like a bell going 'ben' as the baby is born, a soft ring in the delivery room.

meaning: A woman (女) with a dart (矢), a large (大) body, the katakana-mu shape (厶), and a sweeping stroke (ノ) over one (一) — she plays around, joking and darting about, a lively maid servant.
reading: キ — She's always joking, so you call her 'key' (キ) — she's the key to the party's fun.

meaning: A woman (女) with a mouth (口) open in laughter, and two splayed strokes (ハ) like raised arms — that's recreation and pleasure.
reading: At the amusement park, you 'go' (ゴ) on rides for pure pleasure.

meaning: A woman with an ear and a right hand — she listens to the proposal, then takes the groom's hand to marry.
reading: She says 'SHU' as she blushes — like 'shoo' but softer, the sound of a bride shyly accepting the ring.

meaning: A woman with an ear and a right hand — the man holds her hand and whispers in her ear to arrange the marriage.
reading: He arranges the match with a SHU — like 'shoo' the pigeons away, but here he shoos away all other suitors.

meaning: A woman (女) who works by the day (日) — she sells her company by daylight, a prostitute.
reading: The prostitute says 'SHOW' (ショウ) me your money before you touch me.

meaning: A woman with a mouth, a barb, a thousand, and one — she flirts with a thousand men, each one hooked by her charm.
reading: Her charm is an AH — like 'ah' as you sigh at her beauty, a single breath of admiration.

meaning: A woman tied to a vertical stroke, one, and a mouth — she's frequently bound, tied up in a loop, always repeating the same tie.
reading: She ties it again and again — ROU, like 'row' a boat, each stroke a repeated tie, frequently pulling the rope.

meaning: An old woman (女) is sitting by a puddle of water at the side (汁), holding a pelt (皮) with her right hand (又). She's the grandma who always has a wet cloth and a furry skin to dry things.
reading: The old woman says 'バ' (ba) like 'ba-ba' — she's the grandma who babbles. Hear her go 'ba ba ba' as she rocks in her chair.

meaning: A woman (女) under a roof (宀) at evening (夕) with a seal (卩) — she moves gracefully, like a sealed promise of elegance.
reading: エン — Imagine a graceful woman at evening (夕) saying 'en' as she bows, like 'en' in 'elegant'.

meaning: A woman (女) by a tree (木) in a rice field (田) on a day (日) — she is the maid who tends the field, graceful and obedient.
reading: ワ — The maid says 'wa' as she bows, like 'wa' in 'water' — she brings water to the field.

meaning: A woman (女) with three stacked strokes (ヨ) running (走) over soil (土) — she is handsome, her beauty runs like a streak of soil.
reading: ショウ — She runs (走) and shows off — 'show' (ショウ) her handsome face.

meaning: A woman (女) marries into a family name (氏), and the ceremony happens on a bright day (日).
reading: The bride says 'KON-nichiwa!' to her new family on her wedding day.

meaning: A woman (女) with one (一) dry (干) ten (十) and two short strokes (并) on soil (土) — she hates the dry, stubborn soil that won't yield.
reading: ケイ — She hates the dry (干) soil — 'kay' (ケイ) like 'kay' in 'kayak' — she paddles away in hate.

meaning: A woman (女) who works under the rice field (田) — she is the one who carries the ten (十) heavy baskets of rice from the field to the house. She is the maidservant.
reading: ヒ — Think of a maidservant who is always saying 'hee hee' (ヒ) nervously as she bows, trying to please her master.

meaning: A woman (女) between left-side kata (爿) and one-sided (片) — she is the bride, connecting two families like two sides of a broken board.
reading: イン — The bride says 'in' (イン) as she enters the family — 'in' like 'in' in 'in-law'.

meaning: A woman (女) stands under a lid (亠) holding a divining rod (卜) on a day (日) — she is so beautiful that even the heavens pause to admire her.
reading: The beautiful woman's name is 'Doe' (ドウ) — like a graceful deer, she moves with elegance.

meaning: Three stacked strokes (ヨ) sit on a towel (巾) like a headband, and a woman (女) under a crown (冖) is the bride — she is the lady of the house.
reading: The bride says 'fuu' (フ) as she sighs, adjusting her towel headband before the wedding.

meaning: A woman (女) with a lid (亠) over two (二) lines of soil (土) under a blue (青) month (月) — she is modest and supple, bending like a willow.
reading: She is 'Say' (セイ) — as in 'say' a gentle word, for she is too modest to speak loudly.

meaning: Two women (女) under a tree (木) — they covet every fruit above, their greedy eyes fixed on the branches.
reading: They 'run' (ラン) to grab the fruit — covetous hands reaching, never satisfied.

meaning: A woman (女) with a sweeping stroke (ノ) over a gentleman (士) and a claw (爪) — lewdness drips from her wild, uncontrolled gestures.
reading: She is 'in' (イン) — as in 'in' the bedroom, where licentiousness takes hold.

meaning: A woman (女) with a vertical stroke (｜) and one (一) line — she is the mutual term of address between two sisters-in-law, connected by a single bond.
reading: She says 'Ah' (ア) — the sound of recognition when meeting her sister-in-law.

meaning: A woman (女) stands under a lid (冖) with a mouth (口) below, all balanced on a barb (亅) and one (一) — she is so graceful that even her posture is a perfect composition.
reading: The graceful woman is a 'tei' (テイ) — like a 'tay' in 'tay-lor' the elegant tailor, who moves with beauty.

meaning: A woman (女) holds a halberd (矛) and strikes (攵) with a マ-shaped stroke (マ) — this is the star's fierce, martial name.
reading: The star's name is 'bu' (ブ) — like 'boo' as in a ghost's 'boo', a star that shines with a spooky, striking glow.

meaning: A woman with a month and an upside-down box, plus a dot and a person — she is handsome, stealing glances from a person in the box under the month.
reading: トウ — The handsome woman says 'TOW!' as she tosses her hair, making the person in the box swoon.

meaning: A woman (女) sees a bridegroom's head (疋) glowing like a pale month (月) — that's her son-in-law, the groom.
reading: The bridegroom says 'MUKO' as he bows — imagine him muttering 'moo-ko' like a cow's low 'moo' plus 'ko' (child) — he's the cow-child of the family.

meaning: A sweet woman sits by a tree — she is the go-between. The sweet woman under the tree arranges marriages.
reading: バイ — The mediator buys (バイ) both sides a drink to make peace.

meaning: A large woman stands under grass on top, like a statue in a garden — her form is so striking that you stop and call it beauty.
reading: エイ — Imagine saying 'Aye!' (エイ) as you spot a beautiful woman under the grass canopy, like a queen in a parade.

meaning: A woman waves a flag (尸) with a vertical stroke (｜) while her eye (目) watches you — she's flattering and flirting to get your attention.
reading: ビ — Picture a bee (ビ) buzzing around a woman's eye as she flatters you with sweet, sticky compliments.

meaning: A woman (女) with a claw (爪) and a right hand (又) — she uses both to fix her hair, a beautiful princess in the mirror.
reading: エン — 'En' (エン) — the princess says 'en?' when you ask her name, as she claws (爪) her hair back.

meaning: A woman holds a divining rod (卜) and two splayed strokes (ハ) over a shellfish (貝) — this is a name for a girl, like a fortune-teller's title.
reading: テイ — Think of 'tay' (テイ) as in 'tea' — a refined lady's name, served with a cup of tea and a shellfish snack.

meaning: A woman rests her head (疋) on a day (日) — she's at ease, lounging in the sun without a care.
reading: シ — Say 'she' (シ) — she is the one at ease, relaxing on a sunny day.

meaning: A woman climbs a tree (木) with a generation (世) of branches, but a vertical stroke (｜) pokes her — she acts lewd and lusts after the fruit, indecently.
reading: セツ — Imagine 'sets' (セツ) — she sets her sights on the fruit, but her lewd grabbing is a set-up for trouble.

meaning: A woman leans on a craft (工) under a sweeping stroke (ノ) and a one (一) — she's too lazy to work, just beautiful and languid by the month (月).
reading: タ — Picture 'ta-da' (タ) — she does nothing but look beautiful, and you say 'ta-da' as she lounges lazily.

meaning: A woman (女) with two (二) eyes (目) inside an upside-down box (冂) — she's peering out, jealous of what others have, her envy burning.
reading: ボウ — 'Bow' like a jealous archer aiming at a rival — she draws her bow, envious of the target's success.

meaning: A woman (女) with a mouth (口) inside an upside-down box (冂) — she's the snail goddess, her shell-like mouth whispering ancient secrets.
reading: カイ — 'Kai' sounds like 'kite' — imagine a snail goddess flying a kite, her shell trailing like a tail in the wind.

meaning: A woman plays as she pleases, climbing a mountain at evening with a claw and a tin can, while a dot and an open box enclosure sit nearby.
reading: She plays 'yo-yo' (ヨウ) on the mountain at evening, tossing the tin can up and down.

meaning: A woman with a spoon and a mouth compares herself to another, using a compare radical to match pairs for marriage.
reading: She says 'hei' (ヘイ) as she pairs up the spoons, matching each one to its mate.

meaning: The daughter-in-law has a woman's heart, but her own eye and self are watched by the family's heart.
reading: She is 'seki' (セキ) — like a 'sexy' daughter-in-law who steals the son's heart, but she's family now.

meaning: A woman with a large month and an upside-down box escorts the bride, carrying two short strokes on top and a one with a dot and a sweeping stroke.
reading: She 'yoh' (ヨウ) — like 'yo-ho-ho' — as she escorts the bride with a chest of gifts over the month.

meaning: An ugly woman has a left hand and an insect on a mountain, with a one on top — she's so ugly even the insect flees.
reading: She is 'shi' (シ) — like 'she' is so ugly, you just say 'sheesh' (シー) when you see her.

meaning: A woman (女) stands on a mountain (山) under a table (几) with a pair of legs (儿) and a strike (攵) — she is so beautiful that even the mountain bows to her.
reading: ビ — A beautiful woman says 'Bee' (ビ) as she admires her reflection in a honeycomb.

meaning: A woman (女) uses a right hand (又) to push a boat (舟) with a pike (殳) inside an upside-down box (冂) — she moves the boat forward.
reading: ハン — The boat moves with a 'Han' (ハン) sound as it hits the dock.

meaning: An old woman (女) sits by a dish (皿) under the day (日) sun — she is the grandma who cooks for everyone.
reading: オウ — The old woman says 'Ow' (オウ) as she bends to pick up her dish.

meaning: A woman (女) rides a horse (馬) with four dots at the bottom (杰) — she is the mother who takes you to the stable.
reading: ボ — The mother says 'Bo' (ボ) as she pats the horse's neck.

meaning: A woman (女) and a man meet under a table (几) with a vertical stroke (｜) and a ten (十) inside an upside-down box (冂) — their association is intimate but formal.
reading: コウ — They share a 'Ko' (コウ) cup of tea to seal their intimacy.

meaning: A woman (女) sees a ghost (鬼) with a spoon (匕) and a katakana-mu shape (厶) in a rice field (田) — she feels ashamed for being caught stealing rice.
reading: キ — She feels 'Ki' (キ) — a sharp pang of shame — as the ghost points at her.

meaning: A woman (女) under a roof (宀) with a pig (豕) — she marries into the house and brings the pig as her dowry.
reading: カ — The bride says 'ka' (カ) as she carries the pig over the threshold into her new home.

meaning: A woman (女) who works in the rice field (田) with a right hand (又) holding a tool — she's your elder brother's wife, the one who helps manage the household.
reading: The elder brother's wife says 'SOU' as she sighs, 'So much work!' — imagine her saying 'SOU' while wiping her brow.

meaning: A woman (女) under a cliff (厂) with a little (小) day (日) and white (白) light — this is the ancient mother Qiang Yuan, who gave birth to a legendary emperor.
reading: Her name 'GEN' sounds like 'gen' in 'generation' — she's the mother of a whole generation of emperors.

meaning: A woman (女) wearing a crown (冖) and holding fire (火) — she's a lady of high status, but the fire makes her look both beautiful and ugly (the two meanings).
reading: The lady says 'SHOU' as in 'show' — she's putting on a show of beauty, but the fire might burn her.

meaning: A woman (女) throws a dart (矢) at a carbuncle (疔) that looks like the 乞-shaped part (乞) — she's jealous of the carbuncle's attention, so she aims to burst it.
reading: Her envy makes her hiss 'SHITSU' (シツ) — 'Shitsu! I want that!' — as the dart flies.

meaning: A woman (女) with a bow (弓) and ice (冫) — she's so supple and delicate, like a willow bending in the wind, and cold as ice to the touch.
reading: Her movements are 'JOU' like 'jello' — wobbly, pliant, and slender, just like the meaning.

meaning: A woman (女) with three stacked strokes (ヨ) and two splayed strokes (ハ) on top, plus a vertical stroke (｜) — she sees the two short strokes (并) and says 'dislike'. The woman hates the messy strokes.
reading: The woman says 'kera' (ケン) like a harsh 'ken' — she detests the sound. Picture her slamming a door with a 'ken' noise.

meaning: A woman (女) with a dot (丶) and katakana-mu (厶) on top of a home country (邦) with a day (日) — she guards the library where the Supreme Being stores his books, a place of learning for the whole country.
reading: The library is 'ROU' — imagine a 'row' of bookshelves stretching endlessly, and the woman is the librarian.

meaning: A woman (女) in a rice field (田) with power (力) — she's frolicking and playing, using her power to flirt with someone, teasing them in the field.
reading: She says 'DOU' as in 'do' — 'Do you want to play?' she asks, flirting with a playful tone.

meaning: A woman (女) under the west (西) with a show (示) and two (二) little (小) strokes — she's wanton, flaunting herself in the western style, showing off with little restraint.
reading: ヒョウ — Picture a 'HYO' (ヒョウ) — a leopard — wild and wanton, prowling in the west, with a woman riding it.

meaning: A woman (女) with a box-on-side enclosure (匚) full of goods (品) and a mouth (口) — she's an old woman who keeps her goods in a box, and she warms her hands over the mouth of the box (like a heater).
reading: ウ — Think of 'OO' (ウ) — the old woman says 'oo' as she warms her hands, and 'oo' is the sound of her gentle exclamation.

meaning: A woman (女) who uses her right hand (又) to buy (買) things by day (日) — she scorns others and is rude to them, treating them like objects she can just purchase.
reading: バン — Imagine a rude woman slapping a 'ban' (バン) sheet on someone's face, scorning them in public.

meaning: A woman (女) who stands up (立) to make a sound (音) of jealousy — she's the older brother-in-law's wife, and she's jealous of the father-in-law's attention, all under the ten (十) family rules.
reading: ショウ — Picture a jealous sister-in-law shouting 'show' (ショウ) me respect, as she stands up to the whole family.

meaning: A woman (女) who lives under a cliff (厂) with one (一) tree (木) — she's been struck (攵) by loss, so she's now a widow, alone and stripped of her husband.
reading: リ — The widow says 'lee' (リ) — she's left alone, like a leaf (リ) fallen from the tree.

meaning: A woman stands under a lid, with a mouth, ten, two short strokes on top, and an upside-down box — she is the legitimate wife, the one who gets the direct descent, not the bastards.
reading: The legitimate wife has a CHAKU (チャク) — like a chakram, a sharp ring that cuts through all rivals.

meaning: A woman (女) who stops (止) a bird (鳥) with one (一) glance — her beauty is so striking that even the bird's four dots (杰) at the bottom freeze in awe.
reading: エン — Her beauty is like an 'en' (エン) chant — everyone says 'en' (エン) when she walks by, as if in a trance.

meaning: A woman (女) who uses a measurement (寸) to measure a day (日) with a vertical stroke (｜) and a katakana-mu (厶) — she's wholly and solely focused on one thing, like an insect (虫) on a leaf, and she's a lovey who dotes on her man.
reading: セン — She's 'sen' (セン) — like a cent (セン) — she gives her whole heart, wholly and solely, to one person.

meaning: A woman (女) who holds a towel (巾) and speaks with her mouth (口) — she esteems (尚) the moon goddess, and this is her proper name, Chang'e, who lives on the moon.
reading: コウ — She's 'ko' (コウ) — like a 'ko' (コウ) in a koto song, her proper name is sung with reverence.

meaning: A young woman (女) stands by a tree (木), but a strike (攵) from a mouth (口) makes her weak — she sways like two splayed strokes (ハ) under a 乞-shaped part (乞).
reading: The young shoot is so weak it can't even say 'don' (ドン) — it just whispers 'don' like a soft thud on the ground.

meaning: A woman (女) with feathers (彡) and wings (羽) hankers for a lover, but ice (冫) and a hat (个) block her — she pines under a sweeping stroke (ノ).
reading: She hankers so hard she lets out a low 'row' (ロウ) like a boatman's groan, pulling at the oars.

meaning: A beautiful girl (女) stands under rain (雨) inside an upside-down box (冂) with a wrapping enclosure (勹) — she holds a one (一) and two (二) as her pride, a vertical stroke (｜) marks her grace.
reading: Her beauty makes you say 'ko' (コ) — like 'ko' in 'koh-i-noor', the famous diamond, she shines even in the rain.

meaning: A woman with a sweeping stroke and a vertical stroke on top, plus the four dots at the bottom and nothingness — she charms by making you see nothing but her, her beauty is enchanting.
reading: ブ — 'Bu' as in 'boo' — she's so charming that when she says 'boo', you're still enchanted, not scared.

meaning: A woman stands by the gate, and the day shines through — she is refined and elegant, skilled at waiting gracefully by the entrance.
reading: カン — 'Kan' as in 'can' — she can do anything with elegance, like a 'can-do' refined lady.

meaning: A woman (女) stands inside a gate (門), calmly arranging wood (木) into a neat pile — she is so composed and practiced that her every move looks elegant and refined.
reading: カン — Picture a can of tea being poured by that refined woman; the smooth, practiced pour is so elegant it's like a ceremony, and 'kan' sounds like 'can'.

meaning: A woman (女) with a large (大) head and little (小) body plays under the sun (日), while a say (曰) bubble above her shows she's chatting — she's just playing with her friends.
reading: ロウ — Imagine a woman playing with a 'row' of toy boats in a puddle; she splashes and laughs, and 'rou' sounds like 'row'.

meaning: A woman (女) with a claw (爪) and a barb (亅) stands by a river (the four dots at the bottom are like water splashes) — she's crafty, using her sharp tools to fish in the Shanxi river.
reading: キ — Picture a crafty woman holding a 'key' that she uses to unlock a secret river gate; 'ki' sounds like 'key'.

meaning: A woman (女) with a pair of legs (儿) standing on soil (土) under a single line (一) — she sways gracefully, her charm making the ground itself seem to move.
reading: ニョウ — Imagine a graceful woman doing a 'nyo' dance, her movements so fluid they're like a flowing 'nyo' (as in 'nyotaimori' — but here she's just charming).

meaning: A mouth (口) smiles wide, a gentleman (士) and a woman (女) share beans (豆) with two short strokes (并) on top — all together, they feel glad and rejoice.
reading: You feel so glad you shout “KEY!” (キ) like unlocking a treasure chest of joy.

meaning: A woman (女) stands in a rice field (田) with a mouth (口) and ten (十) — she is so beautiful that even the rice plants and the ten farmers stop to stare, all mouths open.
reading: セン — Picture a beautiful woman who is a 'sen' (like a 'sen' in Japanese for a thousand) — she's so stunning that a thousand people turn to look.

meaning: A woman (女) with a large (大) mouth (口) under an upside-down box (冂) — she pouts and flirts, her attractive charm coming from that big, expressive mouth.
reading: キョウ — Imagine an attractive woman who is a 'kyou' (like 'kyoto' but shorter) — she's so charming that she could be the star of a 'kyou' drama.

meaning: A woman (女) stands by a spicy (辛) mouth (口) and ten (十) hands, with a flag (尸) — the woman is the agreeable person who always says yes, pleasing the spicy-tongued boss who raises ten flags of approval.
reading: ヘイ — Imagine saying 'HEY' (ヘイ) to an agreeable woman — she always responds with a cheerful 'hey!' and a smile, making her the favorite of the group.

meaning: A woman (女) under a lid (亠) with a mouth in a box, and a day (日) and one (一) — the woman passes the throne (the box with the day) to the next person, one day at a time, in a slow succession.
reading: セン — Think of a SEN (セン)ator who hands over the throne — the woman gives a speech, and the senator takes the crown, marking the succession to the throne.

meaning: A woman (女) stands inside a box (囗) with soil (土) under her feet, while a person (人) watches from the mouth (口) of the box — she's the lady of the house, but also a concubine kept close.
reading: ショウ — Imagine a lady shouting "SHOW!" as she presents herself to the court, her beauty on display.

meaning: A woman (女) who buys (買) a garment (衣) with one (一) mouth (口) — she's clever at flattering the seller to get a good deal.
reading: ケン — Picture a clever sycophant saying "KEN you help me?" with a fake smile, always angling for favor.

meaning: A woman (女) with a bird (鳥) perched on her white (白) day (日) garment (衣), moving with a delicate, graceful sway like a willow in the wind.
reading: ジョウ — She moves like a "JOE" (ジョウ) — a graceful dancer who floats across the stage.

meaning: A woman (女) with a heart (心) under a crown (冖), her claw (爪) reaching out to a stooping figure (夂) — she is your beloved daughter, the apple of your eye.
reading: アイ — You call your daughter "EYE" (アイ) — she's the light of your life, always in your sight.

meaning: A woman (女) wearing a garment (衣) with a lid (亠) on her head and two splayed strokes (ハ) as her arms — that's a proper young lass, a Miss, a daughter.
reading: The lass is called 'Jo' (ジョウ) — imagine a girl named Jo who always wears a fancy garment and a lid hat.

meaning: A woman (女) with an old bird (隹) and feathers (羽) stands by ice (冫) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) — she is slim and captivating, like a dancer in an ancient play.
reading: チョウ — A butterfly (チョウ) flutters around a beautiful, slim woman — her charm is as light and captivating as its wings.

meaning: Under a roof (宀), a woman (女) with little (小) shellfish (貝) and an eye (目) looks at two splayed strokes (ハ) — she is the bride, ready for marriage.
reading: ヒン — Picture a bride (ヒン) who is 'hinting' at her wedding — she wears a small shellfish necklace and looks at you with a shy eye.

meaning: Rain falls on the 'and yet' roof, and the woman inside is too weak to fix it — she's just a mistress, not the wife.
reading: Rain and 'and yet' and woman — a weak mistress named 'Ju' who can't even hold up her umbrella in the storm.

meaning: A woman with two splayed strokes for milk streams, under an upside-down box of a chest, mixing with the 'to mix with' pattern — she suckles, her breasts full.
reading: The baby suckles — 'dai' as in 'dairy' — milk from the woman's breast, a daily feed.

meaning: A shellfish and an eye sit on two splayed strokes, and a woman holds them — the baby is sharp, crying for attention, wrapped in a shell-like blanket.
reading: The baby's cry is sharp — 'ei' like the 'ey' in 'eye' — the eye sees the baby, sharp and loud.

meaning: Two women and a rice field with power — they sport with each other, teasing and ridiculing, pulling power over the field.
reading: They tease and ridicule — 'do' as in 'do' it again — the two women 'do' the sport, over and over.

meaning: A deceased (亡) person's name on a table (几) with a dot (丶) and a lid (亠), plus a woman (女) and a month (月) — this surname wins by having surplus of everything, even time.
reading: エイ — To win, you shout "AYE!" (エイ) like a captain claiming victory — you have the surplus to spare.

meaning: A woman with a nose and two hands, in a rice field, sees herself — she's the wife, vulgarly called 'kaka', the one who noses around and works the field.
reading: The wife is 'kaka' — like 'cackle' — she cackles as she works the field with her two hands.

meaning: A woman under a roof, next to a rice field, with rice in her hands — she's the aunt who always feeds you. The rice and field show her role in the family, the roof shows she's part of the household.
reading: シン — Imagine the aunt saying 'shin' as she shins up a ladder to reach the rice stored under the roof, calling down 'shin, shin!' to you.

meaning: A woman (女) sits with her head tilted back, mouth (口) open, eyes (目) half-closed, while a page (頁) of work lies on a tree (木) stump beside her — she's too lazy to even pick it up, and her body feels languid like a vertical stroke (｜) that can't stand straight.
reading: The lazy woman's languid sigh sounds like 'run' — she'd rather let the day run away than move. (ラン = 'run')

meaning: Rain (雨) falls on a woman (女) who sits under a tree (木) with an eye (目) — she is a widow, alone and watching the rain, her life now bare like the branches.
reading: The widow is 'ソウ' (sou) — imagine her saying 'SOU' (like 'sow') as she plants a seed alone in the rain, a lonely sound.

meaning: A woman under the rain, crowned with a mouth that speaks for spirits — she is the shrine maiden who channels the divine.
reading: The shrine maiden's voice is a clear 'rei' — like the ring of a bell calling the spirits, 'rei-ng' through the wet air.

meaning: A woman under a lid, with a garment and a mouth — this is the young Miss, dressed and quiet, waiting in the house.
reading: The Miss says 'ジョウ' (jo) as she bows — like 'Joe' the polite young man, but she is the girl.

meaning: A woman with a person holding a halberd over a leek — the leek is so thin and delicate, the halberd could slice it in a whisper.
reading: Her touch is 'セン' (sen) — like 'sensitive' — so delicate she feels the air move.

meaning: A woman (女) who is so lovely and docile that she is like a small (小) bundle of short threads (幺) and threads (糸) wrapped around her words (言) — she never argues, just gently agrees.
reading: The lovely, obedient woman is a 'ren' (レン) — like a 'wren', a tiny, sweet bird that sings softly and never fights.

meaning: A child wrapped in a blanket, with a tiny head poking out — the shape is a small person curled up, a CHILD.
reading: A child says 'KO!' as it points at a cookie — the sharp 'こ' sound is the child's excited cry.

meaning: A child with only one arm (the missing left stroke) — that's a mosquito wriggler, a lonely little larva wiggling alone in the water.
reading: The lonely child wriggler says 'ketsu' — like 'ketchup' — but there's no one to share it with. (Reading: ケツ)

meaning: A child with a barb stuck in its head (the 亅 on top) and a one-stroke body — this is the mosquito larvae, all twisted and short. The barb makes it look like a wriggling hook.
reading: The larvae wriggles and says 'ketsu' — same as its cousin — but this one has a barb, so it's 'ketsu' with a twist. (Reading: ケツ)

meaning: A hook stroke (乙) is the mother, and a child (子) is the baby — the baby peeks out of a cavity in the wall, a small hole just big enough for its head.
reading: You peer into the hole and see a tiny 'KO' (like 'co' in 'coyote') — the baby is calling out from the dark.

meaning: A child is wrapped in a sweeping stroke under a 'from' — the child comes from within, becoming pregnant.
reading: ヨウ — Picture a woman saying 'YO!' as she feels the first kick, her belly swelling with the child.

meaning: Two children (子 子) side by side — they are twins, born together.
reading: シ — The twins both say 'shi!' (シ) as they point at each other — they are identical.

meaning: A child (子) under a roof (宀) — the child learns characters and letters while sheltered at home. The roof keeps the child safe to study words.
reading: ジ — Imagine a child under the roof writing the letter 'G' (ジ) on a page — the sound 'ji' is the letter G in Japanese.

meaning: A vertical stroke and a sweeping stroke cross over a one, and under that a child sits. The child exists because the strokes above are like a parent's protective roof — so the child can be, and we suppose they are safe.
reading: Imagine a 'son' (ソン) who exists in a room, and you suppose he's there even if you can't see him — you just believe he is.

meaning: A claw (爪) gently covers a child (子) — the claw nourishes and encases the child, keeping it safe and sincere.
reading: Fu (フ) — a 'foo' dog (like a fluffy pup) sincerely nourishes its puppy under its claw.

meaning: A gentleman (士) under a crown (冖) stands beside a child (子) holding a ten (十) — but the scene is dark and obscure, like a comet's shadow.
reading: Hai (ハイ) — 'hi' (as in hello) — a comet says 'hi' as it darkens the sky, but it's just a fleeting 'bye'.

meaning: A child (子) is being struck (攵) by a 乞-shaped hand, yet keeps working — that's industriousness.
reading: Imagine a worker saying 'SHI-ft' as they tirelessly keep at their task, like a diligent student.

meaning: A child (子) supports an old man (老) on their back — that's filial piety, the child's respect.
reading: The child bows low and says コウ (kou) — like 'kowtow', the deep bow of respect.

meaning: A child (子) sits on a dish (皿) — the child is the chief of the dish, the beginning of the meal, the first one served.
reading: モウ — 'Mow' (モウ) — the chief begins by mowing down the first dish of food, like a leader starting the feast.

meaning: A grain stalk (禾) grows, and a child (子) watches it — each season the child sees the grain change, so this is the seasons.
reading: キ — The child says 'key' to unlock each new season's door.

meaning: A child (子) alone with a melon (瓜) — no parents, no friends, just the melon. That's an orphan's lonely life.
reading: The orphan cries 'ko' (コ) — a single, hollow sob echoing in an empty room.

meaning: A child (子) held by a woman (女) with a right hand (又) — this is your child, your wife, and your servant all in one: the whole family you must carry.
reading: ド — Picture a child (子) and a woman (女) both pulling on your right hand (又) — you groan 'DO!' (ド) like 'doh!' from the weight.

meaning: A child (子) under a crown (冖) with a lid (亠) on top — the child wears a scholar's crown to study and learn. The crown is the reward for learning.
reading: ガク — A child under a crown says 'GAKU!' (like 'gah-koo') while opening a heavy science book — the sound of study.

meaning: A child (子) under a lid (亠) with a sweeping stroke (ノ) and a dot (丶) — a baby, tiny and tucked away.
reading: The 'gai' in 'guy' — the little guy is a baby.

meaning: A child (子) is tied to you by a short thread (幺) that runs through a thread (糸) — that little (小) connection is your grandchild, and all your descendants hang from that same thread.
reading: Your grandchild is a little 'son' (ソン) — just add a 'g' and you've got the sound.

meaning: A dot (丶) over a lid (亠) with a mouth (口) and a child (子) and nine (九) — you ask 'which' one is the child's, how, and who — all questions swirl around this odd mix.
reading: You 'juke' (ジュク) — as in fake left, fake right — to decide which way to go, which answer to choose.

meaning: A child (子) under a flag (尸) — the flag is heavy, the child is weak, and the ground is steep — they can barely climb.
reading: セン — 'Sen' sounds like 'send' — you send a weak child up a steep hill, but they can't make it — you have to send help.

meaning: A child (子) with one (一) short thread (幺) and two short strokes (并) — the child grows, multiplying like threads, bearing more children.
reading: ジ — 'Ji' sounds like 'gee' as in 'gee whiz' — the children increase so fast you say 'gee, they're everywhere!'

meaning: A claw (爪) with a dot (丶) sits over a child (子) inside a seal (卩) — the claw hatches the child by tapping the shell.
reading: The egg goes 'fu' (フ) — like 'foo' — as the chick pops out, a soft puff of air.

meaning: A child (子) under a crown (冖) holds a mortar (臼) — learning is grinding knowledge into the child's head, like pounding grain in a school.
reading: ガク — The child goes "GAKU!" (ガク) in surprise as the teacher drops a heavy book — that's the sound of learning.

meaning: Rain falls on 'and yet', and a child sits under it with a vertical stroke and one — the child is young, needing shelter from the rain.
reading: The child is young — 'ju' like 'juvenile' — a juvenile under the rain, still a baby.

meaning: A child (子) born from a left hand (屮) reaching out of a spicy (辛) stand-up (立) situation — this is a misfortune, a sin that sprouts like a side shoot from the family tree.
reading: ゲツ — The sin is a GETSU (ゲツ) — like a bad 'gets you' — it gets you into trouble, a misfortune that clings.

meaning: A child under a spicy stand-up with a mouth, grass on top, and a sweeping stroke — this is the evil son of a concubine, a bitter sprout that brings ghostly trouble.
reading: The evil ghost moans 'ゲツ' (getsu) — like 'get you' — it will get you in the dark.

meaning: A baby girl with two splayed strokes for hair, an eye and a shellfish — she is the infant, staring at the shiny shell in her tiny hand.
reading: The baby cries 'エイ' (ei) — like 'hey' — a soft call for attention.

meaning: Two children (子) born together, each holding a small (小) short thread (幺) and a thread (糸) that are tangled in their words (言) — they are twins, always connected and talking over each other.
reading: Twins are a 'san' (サン) — like 'sand', two grains that are always side by side on the beach, inseparable.

meaning: This is a shaped crown — like a roof or a lid placed over something. It looks like the katakana 'u' (ウ) but with a flat top, so it's a crown that covers.
reading: The crown sits on a head and the wearer says 'ben' — like 'bend' — because the crown is so heavy it makes you bend. (Reading: ベン)

meaning: Under a roof, a one and a barb stand still — a calm, peaceful space where nothing moves, keeping you healthy.
reading: チョ — Imagine a calm 'cho' (like a slow choo-choo train) resting under a roof, serene and still.

meaning: A roof over a spoon — but the spoon is bent and twisted, not for eating. This is a strange, other thing, not your usual tool. Think of a foreign spoon that lives under your roof, clearly not belonging to your kitchen.
reading: タ — Imagine a giant 'ta' (like 'taco') sitting on your roof, but instead of a taco, it's a bent spoon. You say 'Ta-da!' as you pull the weird spoon out from under the roof.

meaning: Under the roof, a nine is hiding — but it's not a number, it's a sneaky person. The nine has turned into a traitor, plotting villainy inside your own house. The roof hides the crime.
reading: キ — A villain with a key (キ) sneaks into your house, but the key is shaped like a nine. He uses it to unlock your roof and let the rain in — what a traitor.

meaning: Under a roof, a sweeping stroke, a one, and a hook stroke sit together. The roof covers them — that's your home, where all your stuff lives.
reading: タク — Imagine a 'tack' (タク) pinning your address to the front door of your house.

meaning: A roof (宀) over a dry (干) barb (亅) — that's the eaves of a house, reaching up to heaven.
reading: The roof of the house is so high it touches the sky — you say 'U!' in awe, like 'oooh' but short.

meaning: A roof (宀) over a measurement (寸) — the guard measures everything under the roof to protect it. The measurement is his tool for guarding.
reading: シュ — Picture a guard shouting 'SHOE!' (シュ) as he throws a shoe at an intruder under the roof. The shoe sound is 'shu'.

meaning: A woman (女) under a roof (宀) — she's safe, so you can relax, and the price feels cheap.
reading: アン — "Ann" (アン) sits under the roof, sipping tea — calm and quiet, no worries.

meaning: A roof (宀) over a tree (木) — a tree that has been brought inside to dwell under shelter, like a houseplant that lives in your home.
reading: Imagine a tree under a roof, and the tree is a 'sou' (sow) — you sow a seed under the roof, and it dwells there growing.

meaning: Under a roof (宀), the beginning (元) has a pair of legs (儿) and two (二) marks — the work is done, the beginning is sealed off, perfect and complete.
reading: A 'kan' — imagine a can of paint that is completely full, and you say 'kan!' as you finish painting the roof.

meaning: Under a roof (宀) sits a lid (亠) covering two splayed strokes (ハ) — that's raw meat, muscles packed tight, waiting to be cooked.
reading: Think of a butcher saying 'NIKU (ニク) — that's the meat!' as he slaps a slab on the counter.

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) and one (一) sit under a roof (宀), with the katakana-mu shape (厶) — the house is wide and large enough for all.
reading: コウ — The roof (宀) is so wide you can shout 'ko!' (like 'ko' in 'kodo') across it.

meaning: Under a roof (宀), a sweeping stroke (ノ) rests over a heart (心) — the house is so quiet and still that your heart beats slowly, and you feel in good health.
reading: ミチ — Under the roof (宀), your heart (心) is quiet — you whisper 'MI-CHI' (ミチ) like 'me, chee' — a soft, peaceful sound.

meaning: Under a roof (宀), a mouth (口) and a stone (石) block the way — you must pass through a cave, going deeper and deeper.
reading: The cave echoes 'TOU' — like a 'TOW' truck pulling you in, the sound bouncing off the stone walls. (Reading: トウ)

meaning: Under a roof, a little show of two — the two small strokes represent the main point of the religion, the sect's core teaching displayed for all to see.
reading: The monk said 'SHUU' as he pointed to the little show under the roof — that's the main point of the sect. (シュウ)

meaning: Under the roof, a vertical stroke stands like a pillar — this is the bureaucrat's office, the government building that holds up the state.
reading: The bureaucrat's office is full of KAN (cans) of files stacked to the ceiling — カン.

meaning: Under a roof (宀) that stretches over a rice field (田), the day (日) is open — that's the mid-air space between the roof and the ground, the sky you see from inside.
reading: Imagine a giant 'chew' toy floating in mid-air above a rice field — you chew (チュウ) on it while floating in space.

meaning: Under a roof, a head (疋) is placed on a mat — this is how you fix a decision and determine the truth. The head under the roof is the one that settles everything.
reading: テイ — Imagine a judge slamming a gavel and shouting 'TEI!' (like 'tay') to fix the verdict under the courthouse roof.

meaning: Under a roof, an evening seal is addressed to someone — just like a letter. The seal stamps the address, and the roof covers the sender's intent, making it fortunate to arrive.
reading: エン — Imagine a letter addressed to 'En' (a friend named En) — you write 'To En' on the envelope, and the evening seal makes it just like a lucky charm.

meaning: Under a ROOF, an EYE and a ONE — the one eye looks up, giving best regards to the host, saying 'all is good here.'
reading: ギ — Picture a GEE (ギ) — a person under a roof with one eye, politely saying 'gee, thanks, best regards!'

meaning: A king sits under a roof, and a dot marks his crown — the king's hidden dot is the treasure, the wealth kept safe inside.
reading: ホウ — Imagine a 'hoe' (ホウ) digging up a buried treasure chest under the king's roof.

meaning: Under a roof (宀), a gentleman (士) with a large (大) body holds a seed — this is the reality of the fruit. The gentleman's large body is the truth of the seed.
reading: ジツ — The gentleman under the roof bites into a real fruit and says 'JITSU!' (like 'jee-tsoo') — the taste of reality.

meaning: A stooping figure (夂) with a mouth (口) enters under a roof (宀) — that's your guest, visitor, or customer bowing as they come in.
reading: The guest says 'KYAKU' (キャク) — like 'cackle' — as they laugh at your terrible welcome joke.

meaning: Under a roof, a day is proclaimed — the roof (宀) covers the day (日) with a one (一) on top, and you announce it loudly to everyone.
reading: セン — A senator (セン) stands under a roof and proclaims a new law to the crowd.

meaning: Under a roof (宀), a climax (至) of soil (土) with a katakana-mu shape (厶) on top forms a sealed chamber — like a greenhouse or apartment room.
reading: You sit in the room and say 'SHITS' (シツ) — as in 'this room shits on my style' — it's cramped.

meaning: Under a roof (宀), a sweeping stroke (ノ) and a one (一) calm the month (月) — you soothe and pacify the passing time.
reading: The 'yuu' in 'you' — you soothe yourself under the roof.

meaning: A retainer sits under a roof, but this is no ordinary servant — this is an official who serves within the palace walls, a eunuch bureaucrat.
reading: The official's car (カン) is parked under the palace roof, ready to take him to his duties.

meaning: Under a roof, a cliff holds a barb and a sweeping stroke — this is the dark, guarded room where archives are stored, like a stone vault.
reading: The archives are sealed with a 'say' (セイ) — you must say the password to enter the stone room.

meaning: Under a roof, a mouth (口) speaks a sacred command — this is the palace where a princess lives, and also a Shinto shrine where constellations are honored.
reading: The princess in the palace says 'kyuu' (キュウ) — like a cat's 'meow' but with a royal 'k' — as she looks up at the starry constellations.

meaning: Under a roof (宀), a manager stands up (立) with a spicy (辛) ten (十) — he rules by making everything hot and ordered.
reading: The manager's rule is so strict that everyone says 'SAI' (サイ) — like a sigh of 'sigh' when he walks in.

meaning: Under a roof (宀), a lid (亠) covers a mouth (口) and soil (土) — that's harm and injury to the house.
reading: The injury makes you cry 'GAI' (ガイ) — like 'guy' — ouch, that hurts!

meaning: Under a roof, a woman enjoys a day of feasting — the banquet is held in her honor.
reading: The banquet is held in an 'EN'ormous hall, so big it echoes.

meaning: Under a roof (宀), the month (月) is still high but esteem (尚) fades — this is the wee hours, when evening turns to early night.
reading: In the wee hours, you whisper 'show' (ショウ) to the moon — it's the only sound in the dark.

meaning: A roof over a pig — the pig lives under the roof, so that's the house, home, and family all together.
reading: The house is 'KA' (like 'car') — you park your car in the garage of your home.

meaning: Under a roof, a cliff shelters a garment and the sign of the dragon — this is the imperial eaves, where the dragon emperor's robes hang, and where courtiers show deep courtesy.
reading: The emperor's eaves shine with a 'shin' (シン) — like a shiny new palace roof reflecting the sun.

meaning: Under a roof, a hole and a mouth open into a valley — the shape of a container that holds form and looks, like a face or a vessel.
reading: ヨウ — Imagine a 'yolk' (ヨウ) contained inside a cracked hole in a roof, its yellow form filling the space — the yolk is the contained form.

meaning: Under a roof, two legs kick a woman while a child (二 + 儿 + 女) — this is the cruel tyrant who plunders and robs, even in the safety of a home.
reading: The tyrant's 'ko' (コウ) is a cold, cruel 'cow' — a cow that stomps and steals under the roof.

meaning: Under a roof (宀), a person at the side (化) turns white (白) from exhaustion after a long journey — they need an inn to dwell in for the night.
reading: シュク — Picture a shuttle (シュク) on a loom weaving a white cloth that becomes the bedding in a cozy inn.

meaning: A roof over a tree, with a claw reaching down from it — this is the feudal estate, where the lord's claw (tax) takes from the tree (the people's produce) under his roof.
reading: サイ — Imagine a feudal lord sitting under his roof, saying 'サイ' (sigh) as he counts his taxes, because the estate is so large and tiring to manage.

meaning: Under a roof, three stacked strokes (a ladder) sit on soil, and a run figure dashes past — this is quick, fast movement, like someone rushing out from under the roof.
reading: サン — Picture a runner under a roof who is so fast he leaves a 'サン' (sun) trail behind him, like a blur of sunlight.

meaning: A roof (宀) covers a little (小) divining rod (卜) and a right hand (又) — all alone under that roof, you feel the quiet loneliness of a mellow, mature evening.
reading: The sound 'sabi' is like 'sabby' — imagine a lonely, quiet room where everything is covered in a sad, gray 'sabby' dust. (ジャク is less common; use さび for the kun reading.)

meaning: Under a roof, an excuse (a person with a dot on their head) is wrapped in a wrapping enclosure — this is a grievance, an injustice, where the excuse is trapped and wronged.
reading: エン — Imagine a person under a roof crying 'エン' (en) — like 'en' in 'end' — because their grievance has no end.

meaning: A person with a barb (亅) pokes their head under a roof (宀) to draw near a large (大) mouth (口) that is calling them over — so they stop in for a visit.
reading: キ — Imagine a key (キ) turning in a lock, and the person with the key draws near the door and stops in to say hello.

meaning: A roof over a rice field with two splayed strokes and a one — this is the tiger's hour, when the tiger prowls the field at 3-5AM.
reading: The tiger's roar sounds like 'In!' (イン) as it pounces at 3AM.

meaning: Under a roof, a mountain and a heart are hidden away, with a dot and a sweeping stroke marking a secret passage — this is secrecy and carefulness.
reading: The mountain is so dense with trees that you can't see through it — 'mitts' of fog cover everything.

meaning: Under a roof, a divining rod and two (marks) are held by a right hand, while a beginning (person) with a pair of legs runs away — these are bandits invading, stealing from the beginning of the home.
reading: コウ — Picture bandits under a roof shouting 'コウ' (kow) — like 'cow' — as they invade, scaring the cows outside.

meaning: Under a roof, an old bird perches — this is a crane (bird), a tall, elegant bird that might stand under a roof for shelter.
reading: つる — Imagine a crane under a roof, stretching its neck like a 'つる' (tsuru) — the sound of a long, winding vine — as it looks around.

meaning: Under a roof (宀), a rice field (田) with a mouth (口) and one (一) — that field is your wealth, abundant and rich.
reading: Your wealth is “フ” (like “foo” in “food”) — you have so much food from the rich field that you’re rich.

meaning: Under a roof, a heart sits on a dish — this is a state of calm comparison, like weighing two options peacefully.
reading: ネイ — Imagine a 'neigh' (horse sound) coming from under the roof, as the heart on the dish calmly compares two hay piles.

meaning: A roof over a heart on a dish, but the heart is trembling — the whole scene makes you feel drowsy and uneasy, like a fever dream.
reading: ヘイ — Say 'hey' to the drowsy heart under the roof, but it's too sleepy to answer — just a weak 'hey' back.

meaning: A roof over a bed, with a barb and two splayed strokes on the left-side kata — you're so tired you collapse onto the left-side kata, pull the roof over you, and sleep, ignoring the barb that pokes up.
reading: ビ — A bee (ビ) buzzes in your ear as you try to sleep, but you're too exhausted to swat it away.

meaning: Under a roof (宀), a person (人) with two splayed strokes (ハ) for shivering arms stands next to a well (井) — the well is frozen, and a dot (丶) of ice drips from the roof, making everything cold.
reading: The cold makes you say 'kahn' (カン) — like the sound of your teeth chattering against a tin can, 'kahn-kahn-kahn'.

meaning: A roof (宀) over a rice field (田) with an upside-down box (冂) and a katakana-mu shape (厶) — plus the Chinese emperor (禹) lives there temporarily, so it's a temporary abode that implies something.
reading: A temporary abode is 'guu' — imagine a goose (guu) squatting in a tiny hut, implying it will leave soon.

meaning: Under a roof, a day and a head — this is the real, genuine thing, like a head that has seen many days of truth under one roof.
reading: ショク — You shop (ショク) for real, genuine goods, not fakes.

meaning: A crown sits on a roof, while a right hand slowly pours water at the side from three stacked strokes — each drop comes a little at a time, step by step.
reading: The water seeps in slowly, like a 'shin' (shin) of rain soaking through a roof — think of a shin bone getting wet gradually.

meaning: Under a roof, a heart and a month are separated by a vertical stroke and a sweeping stroke — the peaceful wish for time to pass quietly, like a surname passed down.
reading: Say 'neigh' (ネイ) like a horse's calm, peaceful whinny under the roof — a quiet, gentle sound.

meaning: Under a roof, an eye and a page sit above a spoon and ten — you put aside the page and eye, discarding them into a box with two splayed strokes, putting them down for good.
reading: The sound 'shi' (シ) is like 'she' — she puts down the heavy page and eye, discarding them under the roof.

meaning: Under a roof, a king holds a tin can filled with a mountain of treasure, while an open box enclosure guards it — this is the precious, valuable bullion.
reading: The treasure is 'ho' (ホウ) — like 'hoard' — the king hoards the tin can of gold under the roof.

meaning: Under a roof, a see-er sits on grass on top. The see-er is relaxed and tolerant, letting the grass grow freely beneath the roof.
reading: The relaxed person under the roof says 'KAN' (カン) as they take a long, easy breath, letting go of all tension.

meaning: Under a roof (宀), a left-side kata (爿) lies down, while three stacked strokes (ヨ) and a right hand (又) rest beneath a crown (冖) — all together, it's time to sleep.
reading: シン — You lie down (寝) and hear a soft 'SHIN' (シン) as your head hits the pillow.

meaning: Under a roof, a large day is covered with grass on top — the grass muffles all sound, making the day lonely and quiet.
reading: The quiet is 'baku' (バク) — like 'back' — you go back into the lonely, grass-covered room and hear nothing.

meaning: Under a roof (宀), a dotted tent (癶) covers a show (示) of two (二) little (小) clues — you must guess or presume what's hidden.
reading: サツ — Picture a detective saying 'sats' (サツ, like 'sats' in 'satsuma') as he guesses the culprit from the clues under the tent.

meaning: A roof (宀) over a poor woman (女) with a mouth (口) and a day (日) — she has only one (一) vertical stroke (｜) to her name, so she's impoverished.
reading: She's so poor she can only afford a 'ku' (ク) — like 'coo' of a hungry bird, a tiny sound from her empty mouth.

meaning: Under a roof, a widow (oneself) holds a sword, but only a few (two splayed strokes) are left to defend her — she is the minority.
reading: カ — A widow living alone under a roof says 'ka' (like 'car') — she has few visitors, so she hears only the occasional car passing by.

meaning: A roof (宀) with a crown (冖) covers a left-side kata (爿) and a right hand (又) — the hand rests on the bed, and three stacked strokes (ヨ) show the sleep posture.
reading: You sleep and dream 'shin' (シン) — like 'shin' in 'shin-bone', the part that rests on the bed.

meaning: Under the roof, a left-side kata (爿) leans against a mouth (口) that is shouting 'five' (五) — the noise jolts you awake, and suddenly you understand everything.
reading: The 'go' in 'go-kart' — you wake up and understand you're about to crash into a go-kart track under the roof.

meaning: Under the roof, ice (冫) drips from feathers (羽) onto a hat (个) with three (彡) cracks — the cold, empty room makes you feel lonely.
reading: The 'ryo' in 'ryokan' — a lonely inn where you sit alone under the roof, ice dripping from the feathers.

meaning: Under the roof, a shellfish (貝) with one (一) eye (目) sits on a rice field (田) with two splayed strokes (ハ) — this is the truth, the real reality of the harvest.
reading: The 'jitsu' in 'jitsuryoku' (real power) — you see the shellfish's eye, and it's the truth of your actual strength.

meaning: Under a roof (宀), a heart (心) sits on a dish (皿) next to a barb (亅) and a buy (買) sign — but you'd rather stay home, peaceful and quiet, than go out to buy anything.
reading: ネイ — Picture a peaceful, quiet room where a sleepy neighbor (ネイ) is snoring softly on a cushion, the only sound in the house.

meaning: Under the roof, a vertical stroke (｜) and one (一) line hold up two splayed strokes (ハ) on a tree (木) — this is a fort built high in the branches.
reading: The 'sai' in 'sai' (rhino) — the fort is guarded by a rhino that charges at the tree, but the vertical stroke holds it back.

meaning: Under a roof (宀), a rice field (田) and rice (米) are separated by 釆 (the rice-separating part) — a judge hears the case of the rice field, weighing the rice to decide the trial.
reading: シン — Think of a 'shin' (シン) guard: a judge with a shiny badge hears a trial, and the gavel goes 'shin'.

meaning: A mortar sits under a roof, with a wrapping enclosure and four dots at the bottom — you copy the scene by photographing it, then describe what you see.
reading: シャ — Imagine a photographer shouting 'SHA!' as the flash goes off, capturing a copy of the moment.

meaning: Under a roof (宀), a flag (尸) waves over a wide, open space, with a sweeping stroke (ノ) and a vertical stroke (｜) marking the vast expanse — broad and spacious.
reading: The broad roof (宀) of a grand hall makes you say 'kan' as in 'Kansas' — wide open plains under a big sky.

meaning: Under a roof, you see a little day and two short strokes on top of a large person — that's a dormitory where many people live together, like a hostel or villa.
reading: リョウ — Imagine a dormitory resident shouting 'RYO!' (like 'Rio' in 'Rio de Janeiro') as they run under the roof to escape the rain.

meaning: A roof over a garment, with a mouth and a buy sign inside — this is the imperial domain, a vast enclosed world where everything is under one roof and can be bought.
reading: The emperor's domain is a huge 'can' (カン) of territory — imagine a giant tin can labeled 'WORLD' with a roof on top.

meaning: Under a roof (宀), a king (王) guards a shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) on it, while a little (小) 乞-shaped part (乞) begs for it — this is the precious treasure, rare and jewel-like.
reading: ホウ — The treasure is a HOARD (ホウ) — you hoard it under the roof, precious and rare.

meaning: Under a roof (宀), a stand-up (立) figure offers a month (月) of devotion — this is affection, love, and patronage from a higher power.
reading: チョウ — The patron gives a CHOICE (チョウ) gift — affection that is a special favor, like a chosen one.

meaning: Under a roof, a king with an eye and a shellfish, plus a tin can in an open box — this is the treasure, the precious jewel the king keeps safe.
reading: The treasure is 'ホウ' (hou) — like 'hoard' — you hoard it in your vault.

meaning: A barb (亅) pokes out from a one (一) — this is a tiny measurement, just a little bit, like a small barb's length.
reading: スン — Picture a tiny tailor measuring cloth with a 'sun' (スン) — the sun is small, just a little measurement of light.

meaning: A measurement (寸) of soil (土) marks the ground where a Buddhist temple stands.
reading: You walk into a temple and hear the monks chant 'JI!' — the sound of the bell resonating.

meaning: A claw (爪) pinches a measurement (寸) — you take a handful, exactly a pinch's worth.
reading: Ritsu (リツ) — 'lit' (as in lit up) — a pinch of salt makes a dish 'lit' with flavor.

meaning: The sentence (文) on the left is being measured (寸) against the one on the right — they face each other as equals, vis-a-vis.
reading: Imagine two opponents in a duel, each holding a measuring stick (寸) and a written challenge (文), facing off across a table — the referee shouts 'TAI!' to start the match.

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) and a one (一) sit above a two (二) and a measurement (寸) — this is a long life measured out, a congratulation for many years.
reading: Longevity is 'ju' (ジュ) — like 'jew' — a jewel of a life, precious and long-lasting.

meaning: Soil (土) is measured (寸) and packed into a mound — that's how you seal a letter or close a container.
reading: You blow 'FOO' (フウ) on the wax to seal it shut, making a soft puff of air.

meaning: A rice field (田) with a measurement (寸) of ten (十) — this is the specialty of the farmer, who works only on this one field.
reading: The farmer's specialty is 'sen' (セン) — like a sensei who teaches only one art.

meaning: A woman (女) with a mouth (口) and a measurement (寸) stands on a cliff (厂) to announce to the people below. The sweeping stroke (ノ) and the barb (亅) are the tools she uses to measure and proclaim.
reading: The announcer shouts 'Fuu!' (フ) to get everyone's attention before making the announcement.

meaning: Somebody (身) takes a measurement (寸) with an arrow — they line up the bow, aim at the target, and shoot.
reading: The shot is “sha” — imagine an archer yelling “SHA! SHA!” with each arrow he lets fly.

meaning: A mouth, ten, a measurement, and a pair of legs — you use your mouth to give ten commands, each measured, and your legs to march forward, subduing and destroying all obstacles.
reading: You 'koku' (コク) like a 'cock' — a rooster's crow that overcomes the night and brings the dawn of victory.

meaning: The leader stands on the left-side kata (爿), raises a claw (爪) to command, and uses a measurement (寸) to plan the battle — that's your general.
reading: ショウ — Picture the general shouting "Show!" as he orders his troops to show their weapons, with his claw raised high.

meaning: A left-side kata (a wooden frame) holds an evening (moon) and a measurement (hand) — this is a commander, who measures the evening battle plans with his hand on the frame.
reading: ショウ — Picture a commander under the evening sky, shouting 'ショウ' (show) — like 'show' — to his troops, showing them the plan.

meaning: A hand holding a measurement (寸) over a rice field (田) with a katakana-mu shape (厶) and a one (一) on top — this is the specialist's exclusive plot, tended only by them, so it's their specialty and sole concern.
reading: The specialist's セン (sen) is like a 'sen'ator who owns that one rice field — he speaks only about his specialty, exclusively, in the senate.

meaning: A flag (尸) with a measurement (寸) and a show (示) of two little items — this is the military officer's rank, measured by his flag.
reading: The officer says 'I' (イ) as he salutes — 'I' am the rank.

meaning: A bottle of fine wine (酉) sits on a stand with a measurement (寸) mark, and two short strokes on top (并) show it's been sealed with reverence — this is a sacred, precious vessel.
reading: The monk bows and says 'SON' (as in 'son of a temple') when he sees the revered golden cup.

meaning: Three stacked strokes (ヨ) and a mouth (口) ask a question, while a craft (工) and a measurement (寸) are used to fathom the depth of the answer. The mouth inquires, and the craft measures what it finds.
reading: ジン — Picture a 'jin' (ジン) genie who appears when you inquire (尋) — you ask him a question, and he measures the answer with a crafty ruler.

meaning: A gentleman uses a measurement to stand up a bean plant — the two short strokes on top are the leaves, and the mouth is the pot.
reading: The standing tree is 'shu' — like 'shoot' (a plant shoot) but shorter, matching the on-reading シュ.

meaning: A king (王) with two short strokes on top (并) faces a sheep (羊) across a measurement (寸) — they are opposed, but the king is correct to stand his ground.
reading: The 'tai' in 'taiko' (drum) — the king and sheep face off, each beating a taiko drum to signal their correct stance.

meaning: Oneself (自) with a neck (首) leads, while two short strokes on top (并) and a measurement (寸) guide the way, and the crowded (込) path is shown by this leader.
reading: ドウ — Dough (like bread dough) — the leader with the neck and measurement rolls out the dough to guide the crowd along the path.

meaning: A vertical stroke (｜) with two small dots on either side — like tiny drops of rain, each one LITTLE and SMALL.
reading: A tiny mouse squeaks 'SHO!' as it squeezes through a SMALL hole — the 'ショウ' is the squeak.

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) cuts through the little (小) pile, leaving only a few grains — so few you can count them on one hand.
reading: When you have few things, you say 'sho' — like a short 'sho' of surprise at how little there is.

meaning: A little sweeping stroke separates you from the rest — this is your mark.
reading: You say 'gee' when pointing at yourself — 'gee, that's me' — and the sound is 'ji'.

meaning: A little stroke on top, then a small 'you' below, but the bottom is the 乞-shaped part — like a hook. This 'you' is pointing at 'that' thing over there, not here. The hook pulls your attention to that distant object.
reading: ニ — Imagine saying 'knee' (ニ) while pointing at 'that' — you tap your knee and say 'that one, right there.' The little stroke is your finger tapping your knee.

meaning: A little (小) thing sits on top of a large (大) thing — the little point makes the whole shape sharp and tapering.
reading: The point of a pencil is what you use to SEND (セン) a message — it's sharp enough to write with.

meaning: A little (小) brother is so small he's just a one (一) next to a divining rod (卜) — the younger of brothers, or the father's younger brother.
reading: Imagine a younger brother who is a 'shuck' of corn — small and humble, like the 'shu' in 'shuck'. The reading is シュク.

meaning: An upside-down box sits on top of a mouth, as if the box is a hat being held up for esteem — the mouth below is still talking, but the box shows it's being honored further.
reading: Imagine a show where the host still talks while wearing an upside-down box on his head — the crowd esteems him further for it. (ショウ = 'show')

meaning: A large fire under a day (the sun) with a dot and a sweeping stroke as sparks — little flames consume the fuel for the sacrifice.
reading: The fuel burns with a 'ryo' — like 'rio' in 'Rio Grande' (a fiery river), matching the on-reading リョウ.

meaning: A sweeping stroke and a little head sit above a stop and a day — with only a few steps, the fresh path is scarce, like a surname that is rarely seen.
reading: The sound 'sen' (セン) is like 'sen' in 'sensitive' — a fresh, sensitive little head that stops, scarce and rare.

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) cuts through a sweet (甘) little (小) thing, while a pair of legs (儿) stands inside a box-on-side enclosure (匚) — the result is so plentiful that it's 'at least' not a little.
reading: Imagine a 'sen' (senator) who, despite being embarrassed, still has at least a little dignity left — he limps away with a box of sweets.

meaning: A stooping figure with a crooked leg (the bent line) — this is the crooked-big radical, showing someone who is big but bent over, not standing tall.
reading: The crooked figure says 'ou' — like 'ouch' — because his crooked leg hurts. (Reading: オウ)

meaning: A pair of legs (儿) is bent and twisted under two splayed strokes (ハ), making a crooked, lame walk.
reading: Imagine a lame person saying 'Ow!' (オウ) as they stumble on their bent legs.

meaning: A dot (丶) sits on top of a crooked-big (尢) figure, straightening it out — that's reasonable and just.
reading: Think 'you' (ユウ) — 'You are reasonable and superb!' — the dot on the crooked figure is you.

meaning: A crooked-big (尢) dog with three (彡) strokes of shaggy hair, plus a dot (丶) on its head — it's a shaggy-haired dog.
reading: Bou (ボウ) — 'bow-wow' — the shaggy dog barks 'bow-wow'.

meaning: A pair of legs (儿) is bent and twisted under the weight of a king (王) who has two splayed strokes (ハ) for arms — the king is so weak and emaciated he can barely stand, a rickety figure.
reading: The rickety king stumbles and cries out 'ow!' (オウ) as his weak legs give way.

meaning: A pair of legs (儿) with a king (王) on top, but the one (一) leg is crooked — the king is lame and limps.
reading: Ou (オウ) — 'ow' — the lame king says 'ow' as he stumbles on his crooked leg.

meaning: A person with a limp staggers, their legs like a hook stroke (乙) and a hat on top (个) wobbling, while a vertical stroke (｜) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) cross awkwardly — you can't help but feel embarrassed for them.
reading: The limp makes you say 'kai' (カイ) like 'kite' — the person's leg catches like a tangled kite string, dragging them sideways.

meaning: Ten (十) and one (一) are lifted high by two hands (廾) — the hands raise the numbers up, reaching far and high.
reading: ギョウ — 'Gyo' (ギョウ) — like 'gyoza' — you hold a gyoza high above your head, far away, showing it off.

meaning: A vertical stroke, a hook stroke, two, one, day, and a car — the car's tire hits a hook stroke, and the day's heat makes the rubber swell, with a vertical stroke of pressure.
reading: ショウ — 'Show' (ショウ) me the swollen ankle — it's a show of swelling.

meaning: A lid (亠) sits on a dot (丶) over a crooked-big (尢) shape, and a mouth (口) with a little (小) below — you settle into a position, like a lid settling on a pot.
reading: You take your new position and say “シュウ” (like “shoe”) — you’re shoe-ing yourself into the role, fitting right in.

meaning: A vertical stroke (｜) and a dot (丶) sit on a hook stroke (乙) under two short strokes on top (并) and three stacked strokes (ヨ) — this awkward pile makes you limp with embarrassment.
reading: The 'kan' (can) of beans you drop makes you limp and embarrassed — you can't even pick it up.
