meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) sweeps nine (九) things off a hand at the side (扎), and then power (力) hurls them away. The hand at the side is the base, the sweeping stroke is the motion, and power is the force — together they hurl.
reading: ホウ — Picture a baseball pitcher named "Hoe" (ホウ) who hurls the ball so hard it digs a hoe-shaped trench in the mound. Say "Hoe!" as you hurl.

meaning: A stooping figure with a lid on top, and a hand at the side pulling a right hand — you slip out by pulling your hand free from that grip.
reading: バツ — Picture a bad guy (バツ) trying to slip out of a tight spot, but he keeps getting caught — the sound of his escape is 'batsu'.

meaning: A flag (尸) with a dot (丶) on top stands next to a hand at the side (扎) — the hand points at the flag, choosing it from many.
reading: タク — Imagine a hand at the side (扎) tapping a flag (尸) and saying "TAKU!" — that's the one I pick.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) slaps the dry (干) ground with two splayed strokes (ハ) — you attack and impeach the offender.
reading: The attack lands with a 'HOU' — like a 'howl' of protest as you impeach the guilty one.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) pulls back a pelt (皮) to expose what's underneath — opening it up.
reading: The pelt is pulled open to reveal a 'hee' (ヒ) — a high-pitched squeal of surprise at what's exposed.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) grabs a mouth (口) that is shaped like a katakana-mu (厶) — you lift the whole thing up to carry it away.
reading: The sound is タイ — imagine a tired worker saying 'tie' (タイ) as he lifts a heavy load with his hand at the side.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) reaches into a wrapping enclosure (勹) that holds a stop (已) — you're wrapping your arms around someone and holding them still, so you embrace or hug them.
reading: ホウ — Imagine hugging a giant 'hoe' (ホウ) — you wrap your arms around the handle and hold it tight.

meaning: The family name (氏) is written on a hand (扎) that reaches out to touch — the hand resists being pushed back, so it reaches and touches the obstacle.
reading: Picture a hand (扎) with a family name (氏) on it, and the hand is pushing against a wall, saying 'TEI' (like 'tay' in 'stay') — it resists, but the sound is 'tei'.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) swings a large (大) sweeping stroke (ノ) — that's a beat, like whipping something with a big stick.
reading: The sound is チツ — picture a 'cheat' (チツ) who gets beaten for cheating, the whip making a sharp 'chits' sound.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) holds a tree (木) branch with a lid (亠) on top — you rub it to erase the mark, then paint over it with one (一) stroke and two splayed strokes (ハ).
reading: You rub so hard you say 'MATSU!' (マツ) — like a frustrated painter erasing a mistake.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) pulls a vertical stroke (｜) through a day (日) and a rice field (田) — stretching them out long and thin.
reading: The sound is シン — imagine 'shin' (シン) as you stretch your leg, extending your shin bone forward.

meaning: A vertical stroke (｜) presses down on a hand at the side (扎) that is trying to hold up a rice field (田) under a blazing day (日) sun — you push it all down to subdue it.
reading: You push the button with a loud 'OW!' (オウ) as the machine checks your work.

meaning: Under the day (日), a hand (扎) plucks a vertical stroke (｜) from the rice field (田) to extract it.
reading: You pluck and chew (チュウ) the extracted item.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) presses a family name (氏) under a flag (尸) with a hook stroke (乙) — that's how you pucker your lips into a tight smile.
reading: The sound is ビン — think of a 'bin' (ビン) — you press your lips to the rim of a bin to sip, puckering up.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) holds a bow (弓) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) — you sweep it all away, clearing out dust and debris.
reading: The sound is ヒツ — imagine 'hits' (ヒツ) — you sweep so hard the broom 'hits' everything, clearing it out.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) leans on a post made of soil (土) under a lid (亠) with a dot (丶) — that post is a king (王) you prod for support.
reading: The sound is チュ — picture 'chew' (チュ) — you lean on a post while chewing gum, prodding the ground with your foot.

meaning: A hand at the side lifts a day up — you are shouldering the whole day, carrying it on your back.
reading: タン — Imagine a 'tan' (suntan) on the hand at the side as it carries the day — the tan shows the burden of the sun.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) holds an axe (斤) with a dot (丶) on it — the dot is a crack starting to split the axe head apart. So the hand is breaking the axe open.
reading: タク — Imagine a taxi (タク) driver using a crowbar to split apart a stuck door, the axe (斤) lying useless beside him.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) is attached to the mother (母) — the thumb is the 'mother finger' that helps the hand grip, like a mother guiding a child.
reading: ボ — A bow (ボ) is drawn with the thumb, the archer's thumb pressing the string — that thumb is the one that shoots.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) grabs a divining rod (卜) that pokes out of a mouth (口) — you twirl and twist the rod in your fingers to make it point where you want.
reading: The sound is ネン — imagine a ninja (ネン) twirling a stick between their palms, twisting it so fast it hums.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) grabs a stand-up (立) person — that's a kidnap, pulling them up and away, crushing their resistance.
reading: ラツ — A rat (ラツ) in a trap is crushed by a falling stone, and a kidnapper drags the rat away by its tail.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) slaps a person at the side (化) who is holding a measurement (寸) — the slap is a quick strike, measured and precise.
reading: フ — A chef (フ) slaps a fish on the counter to stun it, then strikes it with a cleaver — the slap is the first hit.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) holds a vertical stroke (｜) that stirs a dry (干) pile with two splayed strokes (ハ) and ten (十) grains — mixing everything into a swirl.
reading: The sound is ハン — imagine a hungry (ハン) cook stirring a pot so vigorously that the spoon clangs against the sides, mixing everything together.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) meets a white (白) surface — you clap your hand against something pale and flat, making a beat. The white part is the drum or palm you strike.
reading: ハク — Picture a drummer who HACKS (ハク) at a white drum with his hand, each clap a sharp, rhythmic beat.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) grabs a hat on top (个) that has a dot (丶) and a マ-shaped stroke (マ) — you lift the whole thing up by the hat, hauling it away.
reading: The most common reading is レイ. Imagine a LAYER of hats stacked on your hand — you haul them all at once, saying 'LAY-er' as you lift.

meaning: A hand (手) grabs a woman (女) by the arm, while a right hand (又) also reaches in — you catch and arrest her, holding her with both hands.
reading: You shout 'DA!' (ダ) as you make the arrest — a sharp, commanding sound that stops her in her tracks.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) grabs a mouth (口) and a sword (刀) — that's how you kidnap someone, and also falsify a document.
reading: カイ — The kidnapper yells 'KAI!' (カイ) as he drags the victim away — like a pirate's 'Kai!'

meaning: A hand at the side clamps over a sweet — the sweet tries to speak, but the hand shuts its mouth tight.
reading: カン — Can you keep quiet? The hand over the sweet says 'can' — you can't talk now.

meaning: A gigantic (巨) hand at the side (扎) pushes against a box-on-side enclosure (匚) — it repels the box, refusing to let it in.
reading: キョ — The giant says 'kyo' as he shoves the box away, refusing it.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) pushes a stone (石) out of the mouth (口) of the land — you clear the land, open it up, break it for farming.
reading: タク — You 'tack' (タク) the land with your hand, breaking the stone to open it up.

meaning: A hand at the side pulls out a one, a dot, and a sweeping stroke from the ground — extracting them like a stubborn weed.
reading: バツ — Bats fly out when you pull the plug — the extraction scares them into the night.

meaning: A hand at the side drags a spoon under a roof — the spoon is stuck, so you haul it out slowly, delaying everything.
reading: タ — Ta-da! You finally drag the spoon out from under the roof after a long delay.

meaning: A hand at the side drags a hook stroke and a spoon, while a vertical stroke and a sweeping stroke tie them to 'to be' — the whole mess gets towed along.
reading: タ — Ta-da! The tow truck drags the broken car, hook and spoon rattling behind.

meaning: A short thread (幺) gets twisted by power (力) while a hand at the side (扎) pulls it — the thread becomes crooked and distorted, perverted from its straight path.
reading: The most common reading is オウ. Imagine an OWL with a twisted, crooked neck — it turns its head all the way around, saying 'OWL' as it distorts.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) is wrapped by a wrapping enclosure (勹) that also holds a mouth (口) — the hand is seized and held, so you are arrested and concerned about being stuck.
reading: The police officer shouts 'KOU!' (コウ) as he slaps the handcuffs on the arrested hand at the side.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) holds a vertical stroke (｜) that pokes into a mountain (山) but slips out of an open box enclosure (凵) — the clumsy hand keeps missing, making a bungling mess of the attempt.
reading: セツ — Imagine a clumsy set (セツ sounds like 'setsu' as in 'setsu' meaning 'to set') of tools that keeps falling apart — every time you try to set them up, they tumble down, showing your unskillfulness.

meaning: Two hands (廾) are pushing aside a katakana-mu shape (厶) that blocks a hand at the side (扎) — you risk everything, disregarding the obstacle, and go all out for the goal.
reading: The ヘン reading sounds like 'hen' — picture a farmer throwing a hen into a fire, risking it all for a cooked meal, disregarding the flames.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) beckons, while a mouth (口) calls out and a sword (刀) is held ready — you summon someone over with a gesture.
reading: You beckon with a 'SHOW!' (ショウ) — like showing someone to come closer.

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) over a dry (干) field, with a hand at the side (扎) — you bow low, sweeping your hand down to worship the dry earth.
reading: You pray 'HAI' (ハイ) — like saying 'hi' to the gods, but with a deep bow.

meaning: To worship (拝), place a hand (扎) on a dry (干) one (一) vertical stroke (｜) as a symbol of prayer.
reading: Say 'hai' (ハイ) when you worship.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) holds a table (几) steady while a stooping figure (夂) leans on it — that's the foothold you need to stand firm.
reading: キョ — 'Kyo' is the sound of a crow cawing as it lands on the table for a foothold.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) pushes against the dotted cliff (广), and the katakana-mu shape (厶) rolls away like a boulder, making the cliff widen and extend outward.
reading: A giant hand (扎) grabs the dotted cliff (广) and pulls it apart, shouting 'KA-KU!' as the crack widens — the sound of the rock splitting is 'kaku'.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) grabs a tongue (舌) and ties it with ten (十) knots, while a mouth (口) is shut — fastening and constricting the tongue so it cannot speak.
reading: カツ — You tie the tongue with a "KATSU!" (カツ) — like a karate chop that binds and arrests the movement, a quick "katsu" snap.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) holds a piling (弋) like a mop handle, and you use it to wipe a surface that has been crafted (工) smooth — so you wipe, mop, or swab.
reading: Imagine wiping a table with a cloth that makes a squeaky sound like “shik” (シキ) as it drags across.

meaning: A gentleman (士) with a hand at the side (扎) stands by a mouth (口) — he is tense, about to speak, the moment of crisis is imminent.
reading: The moment is KATSU (カツ) — like a 'KATSU!' shout before a sudden action, the situation is about to break.

meaning: Water (水) rises, and a hand at the side (扎) reaches down — you scoop someone out of the flood, helping them up.
reading: You help with a 'SHOU' (ショウ) — like a 'show' of rescue, pulling them from the water.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) with two splayed strokes (ハ) above, and a vertical stroke (｜) with two (二) and one (一) — you fold your arms into an arch, hands tucked, forming a bridge shape.
reading: You fold your arms in a 'KYOU' (キョウ) — like a 'kyou' (today) pose, standing calmly with arched arms.

meaning: A large hand with two short strokes on top (like knuckles) and a one — that's your fist, clenched tight.
reading: ケン — Ken clenched his fist and punched the air, shouting 'Ken!'

meaning: A hat on top sits on a king, while a hand at the side ties a rope around them both — binding the king's hat fast with a rope.
reading: セン — Imagine a SENator being tied to a chair with a rope, his hat on top and a king watching, as the hand at the side pulls the knot tight.

meaning: A hand at the side arranges a child under a one-stroke line, while a sweeping stroke and a second hand help prepare the scene — making and preparing everything neatly.
reading: ソン — The SON (child) is being prepared by the hand at the side, who sets out a one-stroke line and a sweeping stroke like tools on a table, ready to arrange.

meaning: A hand at the side reaches out as a curving river and an evening sky draw close — the moment of danger is imminent, the water nearly touching the hand.
reading: サツ — Imagine SATSUma (a type of sweet potato) being washed in the curving river at evening, and the hand at the side pulls it out just as the water rises — the flood is imminent.

meaning: An old man with a hand at the side — the old man's hand is raised to beat, that's torture, plain and brutal.
reading: ゴウ — The old man's hand comes down with a loud 'GOW!' (ゴウ) — the sound of the blow echoing in the cell.

meaning: A hand at the side joins two short strokes on top with two hands below, linking them together into one piece — incorporating all parts into a single unit.
reading: ヘイ — Say HEY! to the two hands below as they clap together, joining the two short strokes on top — they link up like friends shaking hands, incorporating each other.

meaning: A hand at the side drags a hook stroke across the day, pulling it along the ground — the day is being towed, twisted and thrown aside.
reading: エイ — Imagine an EEL (エイ) with a hook stroke for a tail, being dragged by a hand at the side across the day — the eel twists and pulls, but the hand tows it along.

meaning: A hand at the side reaches down to pick up a one-yen coin near a mouth on the ground, while a hat on top keeps the sun off — you gather it on foot.
reading: シュウ — Say 'SHOO!' as you shoo away a crow to pick up the coin — the sound is 'shoo' like 'shuu'.

meaning: A hand reaches up to grab a hat on top of a mouth — you catch the hat as it falls, arresting it mid-air.
reading: The police officer shouts 'NA!' (ナ) as they catch the thief by the hand.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) holds a measurement (寸) of soil (土) — you hold it steady, having it in your grip.
reading: JI — Picture a hand at the side holding a giant 'gee' (like a guitar string) made of soil — you hold it, and it hums 'ji' as you grip it.

meaning: A hand at the side hangs a piece of soil from a hook — the soil dangles, suspended by the hand, ready to be placed.
reading: ケイ — A CAKE (ケイ) made of soil is hung by a hand at the side on a hook — the cake sways, and you reach out to take it down.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) holds a spoon (匕) under the day (日) — the spoon points to the sun, showing you exactly where to look.
reading: Your finger says 'SHE (シ)!' — like a teacher shushing a class, pointing at the noisy student to indicate who to blame.

meaning: A hand holds a sword over soil — you carry the sword by hand, keeping it above the dirt so it stays clean.
reading: You carry a heavy sword and say 'KAY' (ケイ) — like 'okay' but with effort.

meaning: A woman under a roof presses down with her hand at the side, holding something steady while she investigates it carefully.
reading: The woman under the roof says 'AN' as she holds the suspect still, like saying 'ANd?' to ask for more info.

meaning: A stooping figure opens its mouth and strikes with a hand at the side — a sudden hit that makes the figure lurch forward.
reading: The strike lands with a sharp 'KAKU' — like the sound of a hard knock on a door, 'kaku-kaku'.

meaning: A lid sits on top, a father watches below, and a hand at the side measures — collating means checking each item against the next.
reading: You collate pages with a 'KOU' sound — like a teacher saying 'KOUnt them again' as you check the list.

meaning: A woman's mouth opens wide as a hand drags her along — she is being pulled by the arm, resisting.
reading: The woman yells 'DA!' (ダ) as she is dragged — like 'duh!' in annoyance.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) with ice (冫) and a pair of legs (儿) — you challenge someone to a race on ice, but your legs are shaky, so you contend for the win.
reading: You challenge someone to a CHO (チョウ) — like a 'chow' dog barking at you to fight.

meaning: A hand at the side pulls open a roof, revealing one sweeping stroke and a hook stroke — the whole thing expands outward like opening a folding fan.
reading: You open it out with a 'TA' — like saying 'TA-da!' as you reveal the expanded shape.

meaning: A hand at the side digs under a roof, scooping out a pair of legs and two splayed strokes — gouging out what's hidden below.
reading: You dig and scoop with an 'ATSU' — like the hot 'ATSU' steam rising from the hole you just dug.

meaning: A hand at the side plucks a little power from a sweeping stroke and a hook stroke — tearing it off with a quick twist.
reading: You pluck it off with a 'MUSHI' — like a bug ('mushi') you pick off a leaf and tear away.

meaning: A hand reaches up under the esteem of two splayed strokes, lifting a plan into action — this is the gesture of raising something, and also the behavior of doing so.
reading: キョ — Picture a giant 'key' (キョ) being raised high by a hand to unlock a project plan, the key itself becoming the symbol of the raised plan.

meaning: A large person with two short strokes on top and a dot, plus a hand at the side — the hand pinches the person between two things.
reading: キョウ — 'KYO' (キョウ) — imagine a 'KYO' (like 'key-oh') pinched between two fingers, stuck in the middle.

meaning: The feathers (羽) are frozen (冫) to a hand at the side (扎), like a ghostly horse chestnut tree in winter — its spiky husk is the hand, the frozen sap the ice, and the leaves the feathers.
reading: The ghost kanji's on-reading is ウ — imagine a ghost saying 'Ooo' as it floats past a frozen horse chestnut tree, its feathers rattling in the wind.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) pushes open a door, and a dart (矢) flies toward the katakana-mu shape (厶) — you approach and draw near to see what happened.
reading: The 乞-shaped part (乞) looks like a hook, and you use it to pull open a door — but the sound is 'ai', like saying 'Aye!' as you approach.

meaning: A hand at the side pushes a home country with three stacked strokes — you move the whole country slightly to one side, shifting it.
reading: You shift the country and say 'DA' (ダ) — like 'done' but short, as the move is quick.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) grabs a person (人) and crushes them into the soil (土) below a vertical stroke (｜) — that’s a sprain and a broken spirit.
reading: ザ — Imagine a loud 'ZAP!' as the sprain hits, the sound of the joint crushing like a electric shock.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) holds a mouth (口) that has a sweeping stroke (ノ) and a dot (丶) stuck in it like fish bones, while the day (日) below shows it's been stuck all day — this is what makes a person unyielding and blunt of speech.
reading: The fish bone stuck in your throat makes you cough "KOFF" — that's the コウ reading.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) shakes a garment (衣) that hangs from a cliff (厂) — the sign of the dragon (辰) waves as the cloth flaps in the wind.
reading: シン — A shin (シン) injury makes you shake your leg violently to wave off the pain.

meaning: A hand (not listed, but implied by the radical 手) — but here, the parts are a sweeping stroke, a little, a divining rod, and a halberd — you sweep your fingers over the little divining rod and halberd, feeling their texture with a gentle touch.
reading: サ — A 'sa' (サ) is the soft sound of fingers sliding over silk as you fondle the fabric.

meaning: Two hands (廾) and a hand at the side (扎) all fiddle with a king (王)'s crown — you play with and handle things you shouldn't.
reading: ロウ — You play with a toy rowboat (ロウ) in a pond, splashing water with your hands.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) holds up a flag (尸) with a barb (亅) on top, and a mouth (口) below — you grip the flagpole with both hands to hold it steady.
reading: You hold the flagpole and say "KYOKU" as you plant it firmly in the ground — sounds like "KYOKU" (like "kyoku" in "kyoku" meaning a tune you hold in your hands).

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) dips into a mouth (口) of liquid, using a hook stroke (乙) and a stop (已) to bale out water, while a comma-design (巴) swirls in the home country (邦) of the cup.
reading: ユウ — You use a ladle to scoop (ユウ) water from a bucket, pouring it out.

meaning: A king (王) takes a long stride (廴) and raises a hand at the side (扎) to bravely volunteer — the king steps forward with a raised hand, volunteering for battle.
reading: チョウ — Picture a brave volunteer shouting 'Chow!' as he charges forward, like a martial artist yelling before a strike. 'Chow' sounds like チョウ.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) rubs a woman (女)'s back with a claw (爪), crumpling her dress as you stroke it.
reading: ダ — You rub a da (ダ) of butter into dough, crumpling it with your hands.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) pulls a saw across a vertical stroke (｜) and one (一) piece of wood, while an excuse (免) with a pair of legs (儿) and a wrapping enclosure (勹) turns the lathe — you saw and grind.
reading: バン — You pull the saw back and forth with a bang (バン) as it cuts the wood.

meaning: A person and a large hand at the side squeeze something between them — the hand at the side jams the object between the person and the large palm, so it gets caught in the middle.
reading: キョウ — Imagine a giant hand at the side squeezing a person between two walls, and the person yells 'KYO!' (like 'kyo' in 'kyoto') as they get caught.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) pushes a sweeping stroke (ノ) and a ten (十) into a day (日) that sits in a rice field (田) — that’s inserting a sword into its sheath.
reading: ソウ — Picture a sword being inserted with a 'SOW' sound, like stitching a seam through cloth.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) covers a mouth (口) that sits above a five (五) and two (二) lines, resisting any sound from escaping.
reading: ゴ — Think of a wrestler saying "Go!" (ゴ) as he resists being pinned, his hand blocking the opponent's mouth.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) reaches into water (水) with a dot (丶) and a one (一) line, pulling out something long, like a long rope or eel.
reading: ク — Picture a long, winding river (ku) where a hand pulls out a long fish, stretching it out.

meaning: A mouth inside a box speaks to a tree, but a hand at the side ties the tree up with rope — the mouth is bound shut, and the tree is trussed into a bundle.
reading: コン — Picture a hand at the side tying a tree into a bundle, and the tree groans 'KON!' (like 'con' in 'congratulate') as the rope tightens.

meaning: A hand at the side with a leg and a stop — you catch the leg to make it stop, capturing it.
reading: ソク — 'Sock!' (ソク) — I caught the thief with a sock to the leg.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) uses a claw (爪) and a measurement (寸) to pluck and gather grains, rubbing and scraping them off the stalk.
reading: ラツ — Picture a chef with a rat (ラツ) that uses its claws to pluck and scrape off leaves from a herb, gathering them in its fingers.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) uses a reap (刈) tool with a mouth (口) and power (力) inside a wrapping enclosure (勹) to handle and dispose of goods, selling them off.
reading: ハツ — Imagine a merchant shouting "Hats off!" (ハツ) as he handles and sells off his entire stock, dealing with each item quickly.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) raises a dry (干) shield under the day (日) sun — you defend against the heat and the enemy.
reading: The guard's shout 'KAN!' echoes as he blocks the blow — like a tin can (カン) being struck.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) reaches up to a little (小) shelf under an esteem (尚) sign — you select the best item and carry it away.
reading: You carefully select a 'sou' (ソウ) — like a tailor picking a 'sew' (ソウ) thread from a spool.

meaning: Soil (土) and a hand at the side (扎) work under the day (日) — you knead the mud into a firm ball, mixing it well.
reading: You knead the dough with a 'netsu' (ネツ) — like a hot 'net' (ネツ) of tangled noodles you must mix through.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) tosses a month (月) of old papers into a mouth (口) of a bin — you throw it all away.
reading: You throw it with an 'en' (エン) — like an 'engine' (エン) that flings the trash far off the deck.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) grips a tusk (牙) while your home country (邦) cheers — you strive to pull it out for the festival.
reading: You strive with a 'yo' (ヨ) — like a 'yodel' (ヨ) you belt out to rally your strength for the tug.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) grabs a dot (丶) from a utilize (用) tool — that's catching or capturing something quick, like snatching a fly out of the air.
reading: ホ — A hunter shouts 'Ho!' (ホ) as he throws a net to catch a rabbit mid-leap.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) pushes a little (小) cart up a stop (止) sign, while a sweeping stroke (ノ) marks the path — you make progress step by step.
reading: You make progress with a 'haku' (ホ) — like a 'hoe' (ホ) that clears the ground, each swing moves you forward.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) grabs a stooping figure (夂) who is leaning on the katakana-mu shape (厶) — you push them forward to get them moving.
reading: Push the button with your thumb — it goes 'SON' like the sound of a spring releasing.

meaning: A hand at the side holds a day, while a right hand searches through a rice field — the hand at the side looks for the day that is lost, locating it among the rows.
reading: To search is 'ソウ' (sou) — imagine a 'sow' (like a pig) rooting around in the rice field, searching for food with its snout.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) grabs a roof (宀) and twists it like a wrist bending, making the evening (夕) seal (卩) pop off — the whole thing comes off and breaks.
reading: The wrist bends so hard it goes 'WAN' — like a bent wire snapping with a 'wan' sound.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) clamps down on gold (金) — you seize and clutch it, arresting the shiny metal.
reading: You clutch the gold so tight it goes 'KIN' — like 'kin' (family) you won't let go of.

meaning: A person raises both hands at the side, lifting a large offering above a one-line altar — you give it up, consecrating it.
reading: The priest hoists the offering and shouts 'HO!' (ホウ) as the crowd bows.

meaning: A hand at the side throws away a hat on top of a mouth that sits on soil — the hand discards the whole pile (hat, mouth, soil) into the trash.
reading: You throw away the hat, and it lands with a 'シャ' (sha) sound — like 'shah!' as it hits the bin.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) twists a door (戸) that has a large (大) one (一) sticking out — you wrench it until the flag (尸) shape bends.
reading: Twist the lid off a jar and it makes a 'REI' sound like a rusty hinge.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) reaches through a gate (門) to stroke whatever is on the other side.
reading: You stroke the gate and it hums 'MON' — like a monk (mon) patting the wood.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) presses down heavily on a person at the side (化) who is under a dotted cliff (广) with a measurement (寸) — squashing them flat.
reading: Press down so hard it goes 'FU' — like 'foo' (a heavy thud).

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) pulls open a mouth (口) that has a day (日) inside, spreading it out like a ten (十) with a sweeping stroke (ノ) — opening wide.
reading: You spread it open and it cracks 'HAI' — like 'hi' (a wide-open greeting).

meaning: A hand at the side sets a flag (尸) on top of a mouth and ten, firmly laying a foundation to install something in place.
reading: キョ — Picture a 'kyo' (キョ) as a giant key that you use to set and install a heavy stone slab into its foundation.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) pushes against a cliff (厂) with soil (土) on top — you put off the collapse and endure the pressure.
reading: You endure the weight and groan 'GAI' — like 'guy' who just keeps going.

meaning: A hand at the side grabs the two short strokes on top and pulls them over the stop, like rolling up a scroll — then you turn the page to the next one.
reading: ケン — Ken rolls up his sleeve and winds the film reel, saying 'Ken, roll it!'

meaning: A hand at the side holds a vertical stroke and a sweeping stroke, using them like a whip to strike down on the two strokes below.
reading: スイ — Swee (スイ) the whip cracks as you strike the drum, 'swee-swee!'

meaning: The head (疋) with three stacked strokes on top moves fast — a hand at the side helps it sprint to victory.
reading: ショウ — Show (ショウ) your speed — you win the race, 'show!'

meaning: A hand at the side presses down on the show (示) with two strokes and a little mark, stamping a seal onto the large paper below.
reading: ナツ — Natsu (ナツ) stamps her summer postcard with a red seal, 'natsu!'

meaning: A hand at the side twists a vertical stroke and a one, while a hat on top covers the heart — you twirl the knob playfully.
reading: ネン — Nen (ネン) twists the dial on the safe, 'nen-nen-nen' as it spins.

meaning: A hand at the side rubs a woman's grain stalk against a tree, crumpling the leaves into a messy ball.
reading: ダ — Da (ダ) rubs the crumpled paper between his palms, 'da-da-da' as it crinkles.

meaning: A person (人) under a lid (亠) reaches out with a hand at the side (扎) to grab ten (十) things at once — you clutch and pull them all up, even if it contradicts logic.
reading: The sound is ソツ — imagine a soldier in a tight spot, clutching his rifle and pulling it up, shouting 'SOOTS!' as he yanks it free from the mud.

meaning: A woman with three stacked strokes perches on a vertical stroke under a one, while a hand at the side steadies her — she stays there to roost.
reading: セイ — Say 'say' (セイ) as you point to the woman perched on the branch, telling her to 'stay' — she says 'say' back.

meaning: An axe and a lack — you lack an axe, so you use a hand at the side to raise and hoist the heavy lid instead.
reading: キン — A 'kin' (キン) is a family member who hoists you up with one hand at the side — like a king lifting a flag.

meaning: A hand at the side holds a divining rod over a mouth under a dotted cliff — you heft it in your palm to weigh its worth.
reading: テン — A 'ten' (テン) — picture ten coins in your palm, hefting them to feel their weight, like a shopkeeper testing a coin.

meaning: A hand at the side holds a towel under a crown, and three stacked strokes are the broom bristles — the hand sweeps the towel and bristles across the floor.
reading: You sweep the floor with a broom, and the bristles go 'ソウ' (so) — like saying 'so, so' as you brush back and forth.

meaning: A hand at the side swings a tome wrapped in an upside-down box with a hat on top, while a barb and two hands hold the ends — you brandish it in a circle.
reading: ロン — 'Ron' (ロン) — imagine Ron Weasley brandishing a tome like a sword, swinging it around his head with two hands.

meaning: A hand at the side and a right hand together collect and gather up the scattered pieces — you pick them up with both hands.
reading: タツ — 'Tatsu' (タツ) — a dragon (tatsu) uses its claws to pick up and collect shiny pebbles from the ground.

meaning: A claw reaches down from a crown to a hand at the side, while another hand (又) holds a brush — this is the act of imparting or granting something, like a teacher giving a brush to a student.
reading: The 'ju' in 'juice' — imagine a teacher granting a cup of juice to a student, imparting refreshment.

meaning: A hand at the side grabs a divining rod and shakes it over a day marker, while a say-mouth chants — the whole scene shakes and moves with frantic energy.
reading: トウ — Imagine a TOE (トウ) shaking violently as it kicks a tin can down the road, the can clattering and moving with every jolt.

meaning: A hand at the side strikes a mouth that is trying to stand up — the blow extracts the words from it, injuring the speaker.
reading: ホウ — Picture a HOE (ホウ) digging into the ground to extract a stubborn root, injuring the soil as it scrapes.

meaning: Your hand (手) is held up like a platform under a crown (冖), showing you rule (掌) what rests in your palm. The mouth (口) below the crown is the command you give while administering.
reading: ショウ — Imagine showing your palm to a crowd and shouting "SHOW!" (ショウ) as you take charge of the stage.

meaning: A hand at the side pulls a large barb that is hooked onto a one-stick — the barb holds back the pull, resisting the tug.
reading: キ — A KEY (キ) is stuck in a lock, and you pull it hard but it holds back, refusing to turn.

meaning: A hand at the side sneaks into an open box enclosure that holds a tin can wrapped in a wrapping enclosure — the hand extracts the can, a pickpocket's move.
reading: トウ — A TOE (トウ) secretly lifts a wallet from a pocket, the pickpocket's toe doing the dirty work.

meaning: A hand at the side grips a mortar that is wrapped in a wrapping enclosure — the hand gathers the contents, then chokes the opening shut.
reading: コウ — A COW (コウ) chokes on a handful of grain, its throat gathering and closing as it struggles.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) pushes away something marked with un- (非) — you repudiate, exclude, and expel it. The hand rejects what is not wanted.
reading: You shout 'high!' (ハイ) as you raise your hand to exclude someone from the group — like a referee ejecting a player.

meaning: A retainer (臣) in a box-on-side enclosure (匚) uses a right hand (又) and a hand (手) to hold firm — the sturdy grip of a loyal retainer.
reading: Picture a sturdy retainer saying 'kan' (カン) as he braces — 'KAN! I won't budge!' — like a solid wall.

meaning: A person at the side carries a stooping figure under their arm, while a lid and a dot sit on top — the side of the body bears the weight, and the hand at the side helps.
reading: エキ — An ECHO (エキ) bounces off the side of a canyon, carrying the sound under its arm as it travels.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) uses a vertical stroke (｜) to dig into a mountain (山) under a flag (尸) that marks the spot, with an open box enclosure (凵) as the hole — that's digging or excavating.
reading: The digging sound is 'kutsu' (クツ) — imagine a pickaxe going 'kutsu, kutsu' as it breaks the mountain rock.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) grabs a barb (亅) and three stacked strokes (ヨ) — you're struggling to pull them apart, striving against the resistance.
reading: Imagine a SOUL (ソウ) wrestling with a barb — the struggle is a battle for your very soul.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) grabs a divining rod (卜) and sticks it into soil (土) to hang a sign. The sign depends on the rod, and you arrive at the spot where it hangs.
reading: Picture a coat hanging on a hook that goes 'kay' (カイ) as it swings — like a creaky hinge.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) smooths out fire (火) — the flames become easy, quiet, and suave as they're pressed flat.
reading: Think of an 'engine' (エン) running smoothly and quietly — no sputtering, just easy motion.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) places a head (疋) under a roof (宀) — that's the law: every head must be sheltered, these are the commandments.
reading: Picture a 'toe' (トウ) tapping impatiently as you read the regulations — the law is long, and your toe counts the seconds.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) snatches a little (小) thing from under a lid (亠) and a mouth (口) — that's pillaging, robbing a tiny treasure.
reading: A thief skims past a RYAKU (リャク) — the sound of his quick grab is 'ryaku-ryaku' as he grazes by.

meaning: A claw reaches down from a tree to grab something, while a hand at the side steadies the branch — you pick or take what you need.
reading: Imagine a 'サイ' (sigh) as you pick a ripe fruit from the tree, letting out a long breath of satisfaction.

meaning: A tree (木) with a crown (冖) on top, and a pair of legs (儿) under it — a hand at the side (扎) gropes under the crown, searching for something hidden in the tree.
reading: タン — 'Tan' (タン) sounds like 'tan' — you search for a tan-colored fruit hidden under the tree's crown, groping with your hand.

meaning: A hand (手) pulls back a cow (牛) from a tin can (缶) with a towel (巾) in an open box enclosure (凵) — you restrain the cow, pulling it back from the can.
reading: Imagine pulling back a cow and it moos 'sei' (セイ) — 'SEI! Stop pulling!' — the sound of restraint.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) holds a month (月) like a lid — that's a quiver, a container with a month-shaped cover for arrows.
reading: A 'hyo' (ヒョウ) — like a 'hi-yo' cowboy yell — as you pull an arrow from the quiver and shoot.

meaning: A woman stands up and reaches out with a hand at the side to touch and adjoin two pieces — she makes contact to connect them.
reading: セツ — Picture a set (セツ) of puzzle pieces that you touch together — they click with a 'set' sound, adjoining perfectly.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) is under a roof (宀), and next to a hole (穴) with a pair of legs (儿) and craft (工) inside. You pull your hand back from the hole, withdrawing it to your side, holding back from reaching in.
reading: コウ — Imagine a 'ko' (child) who is told to 'hold back' from touching a hot stove, and you shout 'KO!' to stop them, pulling your own hand back in sympathy.

meaning: A hand at the side pushes an old bird — you conjecture that the bird is about to fly, so you guess and infer its next move.
reading: スイ — Picture a detective saying 'sweet' (スイ) as he infers the culprit from a clue, like a sweet guess.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) pulls a cover (奄) over a day (日) — the cover conceals the sun, hiding the whole day in shadow.
reading: An 'en' (エン) — like 'envelope' — you cover and conceal the letter inside, hiding it from view.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) pushes a day (日) with a vertical stroke (｜) and two ones (一, 二) off a shelf — you set it aside and suspend it.
reading: ソ — Think of a 'so-so' (ソ) performance that gets suspended — the judge says 'so-so, not good enough' and sets the act aside.

meaning: An ear and a right hand are at the side of a hand at the side — the night watchman cups his ear to listen, then rakes the ground with his hand to keep awake.
reading: ソウ — 'sow' the night watchman's rake, scattering seeds of vigilance in the dark.

meaning: A hand at the side scoops up rice from a wrapping enclosure — you cup your hand to catch the grains, like scooping water.
reading: キク — 'kick' up water with your hand, splashing it as you scoop.

meaning: A hand at the side pokes a barb into a large dot with four dots at the bottom — that's the pricker for a lamp wick, adjusting the flame.
reading: テン — 'ten' tiny pokes to fix the wick, each one a small adjustment.

meaning: A hand at the side lifts a flag over a door with a month inside — you bear the heavy load on your shoulders, like carrying a banner through the gate.
reading: ケン — 'ken' (as in 'ken'nel) — you shoulder a heavy dog kennel, straining under its weight.

meaning: A hand at the side grabs a month and a stop — you oppress and extort, stopping time itself to take by force.
reading: コウ — 'cow' — you seize a cow by force, oppressing it until it stops moving.

meaning: A day (日) shines on a wrapping enclosure (勹) that holds a spoon (匕) — you hoist this wrapped bundle up on a pole to display it for all to see.
reading: ケイ — Think of a 'kay' (ケイ) — like a kayak — you hoist the kayak up onto the roof to display it after a day of paddling.

meaning: A king's hand at the side reaches into a box, grabs the dot inside, and holds it tight — that's a catch or grasp.
reading: You catch the king's crown with a quick 'kak' (カク) — like the sharp click of a lock snapping shut.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) holds a seal (卩) that stamps a hat on top (个) of a mouth (口) — this official mark designates the terraced land along the river.
reading: The terraced fields are so steep that a farmer shouts 'HA-BA!' (ハバ) as he slips down each step.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) uses a right hand (又) to scratch an insect (虫) off its back — that's the motion of raking or combing.
reading: You scratch so hard you make a 'SOU' (ソウ) sound like a cat hissing through its teeth.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) pushes two short strokes on top (并) of a vertical stroke (｜) with a dot (丶) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) — they all collide into a messy pile.
reading: Two carts 'HO-U' (ホウ) into each other — the sound of the crash is a hollow 'hou'.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) holds a pig (豕) under three stacked strokes (ヨ) — this is the subordinate official who helps by managing the imperial pigsty, a lowly but necessary government service rank.
reading: The subordinate official's help is always 'en' route — imagine him rushing to assist, shouting 'EN-route!' as he runs, with the pig trotting behind.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) picks through a tree (木) where a day (日) shines between two splayed strokes (ハ) and a vertical stroke (｜) — you select the best branch by sight, sorting through the leaves.
reading: You 'kan' the options like a scanner — imagine a barcode scanner beeping 'KAN!' each time you select an item from the shelf.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) plucks a string over a divining rod (卜) while an eye (目) watches a shellfish (貝) — the sound of setting up a koto resonates as the player tunes it, checking the tension like a diviner reading shells.
reading: The koto's tuning sound is a sharp 'tei' — imagine the string snapping with a crisp 'TEI!' as you tighten it, making the eye and shellfish jump.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) reaches up to a reap (刈) of month (月) plants, and two short strokes on top (并) show they're all counted — so everything is uniform and complete.
reading: The 'sen' sound is like 'sen' in 'sentence' — imagine a teacher saying, 'All students present, your uniforms are complete — that's a full sen-tence of order!'

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) pulls a month (月) under a hat on top (个) while a reap (刈) cuts nearby — you pull and tease the month like a toy, playing with time itself.
reading: You 'you' the month around like a yo-yo — imagine pulling the string and the month spins, saying 'YOU!' as it bounces back.

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) and a mouth (口) sit on one (一), while two hands (廾) and a hand (手) grind and rub them together — that's research.
reading: You 'KEN' the stone with your hand and two hands, grinding it down to study it.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) measures a large (大) plan under a dotted tent (癶) with two (二) people (人) — this is the category of plans, and the drumstick that beats out the rhythm for the council's decisions.
reading: The drumstick beats a steady 'ki' — imagine a drummer counting 'KI, ki, ki' as he plans the next move under the tent.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) rubs a halberd (矛) against a tree (木) with a マ-shaped stroke (マ) — you massage the wood vigorously, debating whether to polish or sharpen it.
reading: You 'juu' the muscles like a massage therapist — imagine the therapist chanting 'JUU, juu' with each deep rub, working out the knots.

meaning: Under a roof, you see a hand at the side pulling up sleeves next to a day and a say — you roll up your sleeves and stretch out your arms to strike with bare fists.
reading: The sound of the strike is 'sen' — like 'send' — you send your bare fist forward after pulling up your sleeves.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) holds a brush over a rice field (田) with grass on top (艾), sketching the scene into a picture.
reading: The artist's brush goes 'byoo' as it sweeps across the canvas, painting a vivid portrait.

meaning: You see a head (疋) with a hand at the side (扎) — that hand is carrying the head, proposing it forward, taking it along in hand.
reading: You 'TEI' a waiter to come over — 'TEI, TEI!' — as you carry your bag in hand and propose a toast.

meaning: A hand at the side grabs a craft and a mortar — you fabricate a story by mixing crafty lies in a mortar with your hand.
reading: The lie is 'netsu' — like 'nets' — you fabricate a net of falsehoods to catch someone.

meaning: A sweeping stroke, a mortar, a ten, and a hand at the side — you insert the ten into the mortar, sticking it in with your hand.
reading: The sound is 'sou' — like 'sow' — you sow seeds by inserting them into the ground with your hand.

meaning: A pair of legs, two splayed strokes, a box-on-side enclosure, a sweet, and a hand at the side — you roll up sleeves and fight bare fist, your legs braced, your hand ready, ignoring the sweet box.
reading: The fight is 'chin' — like 'chin up' — you chin up and roll up sleeves to fight.

meaning: A mouth, an ear, and a hand at the side — you bow with arms folded, bringing your mouth and ear together to assemble with others.
reading: The bow is 'itsu' — like 'it's you' — you bow and say 'it's you' as you come together.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) raises a day (日) up with a one (一) and a not (勿) — you hoist the sun itself, not letting it fall.
reading: You YO-YO (ヨウ) the flag up and down as you raise it — up, down, up, down.

meaning: A large (大) pair of legs (儿) inside an upside-down box (冂) with a wrapping enclosure (勹) and a hand at the side (扎) — you interchange the contents, changing what's inside.
reading: KAN (カン) — think of a can of paint being swapped for another color, a complete change.

meaning: A one, a hat on top, a mouth, two hands, and a hand at the side — you cover up the mouth with two hands and a hat, taking by force and shutting it.
reading: The cover is 'en' — like 'end' — you cover up to end the matter, shutting it away.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) grabs a woman (女) under a box-on-side enclosure (匚) next to a day (日) — you pull her up and eradicate the weeds from the field.
reading: You pull up the plant with a 'サツ' (satsu) — imagine a police officer (satsu) yanking a weed out of the ground with his bare hand.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) grips the climax (至) of soil (土) — that's a firm grip, like molding sushi or taking a bribe.
reading: You grip the sushi so hard it goes "AKU!" — like "achoo!" but with a hard K.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) touches a mountain (山) that has 'and yet' (而) on top — you feel the mountain's shape and make a conjecture about its height.
reading: You conjecture 'シ' (shi) — picture a detective saying 'shi...' as he strokes his chin, guessing the mountain's secret.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) holds a scratcher made of a vertical stroke (｜) under a lid (亠) with two short strokes (并) inside an upside-down box (冂) with a crown (冖) and a towel (巾) — you scratch your back with this tool.
reading: The scratcher is called 'テイ' (tei) — imagine a tea (tei) ceremony where you use a long scratcher to reach an itch on your back.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) wipes a white (白) surface that has a compare (比) mark on it — you wipe the whiteboard clean to compare notes.
reading: You wipe with a 'カイ' (kai) — picture a 'kayak' (kai) paddle wiping a wet surface dry.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) grabs a tree (木) that has fire (火) and a grain stalk (禾) tangled in its branches — you pinch and pull them all out with that hand.
reading: Imagine a chef pinching a grain stalk (禾) and shouting 'SHOO!' (シュウ) to shoo away a fire (火) that's licking the tree (木).

meaning: A hand (手) grabs a mouth (口) and an ear (耳) together — you grasp them with your hand and pinch them shut.
reading: You 'SHUU' the mouth and ear together with your hand, pinching them into silence.

meaning: A hand (手) lifts up a mouth (口) that sits on a box-on-side enclosure (匚) — you raise it high with your hand.
reading: You 'KAKAGE' the box with your hand — but the sound is 'KEI' as you lift it like a flag.

meaning: A car (車) under a crown (冖) has a hand at the side (扎) — you wave it away, brandishing it like a royal chauffeur dismissing a crowd.
reading: キ — Think of a 'key' (キ) you swing on a ring, brandishing it to unlock a door.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) sorts out one (一) vertical stroke (｜) and a generation (世) of wooden (木) divination stalks, folding them into neat piles.
reading: You fold the stalks and count them with a 'SET-sy' (セツ) motion — like setting a table, each stalk clicks into place.

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) and one (一) line lead to a claw (爪) and a right hand (又) that grab a hand at the side (扎) — that's help and rescue.
reading: エン — Imagine an angel (エン) reaching out a claw to save someone, saying 'I'll help you, en!'

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) lifts a brush (聿) over a long stride (廴) with two (二) and three stacked strokes (ヨ) — you carry the whole setup forward.
reading: ケン — Imagine carrying a heavy brush (聿) and saying 'Ken!' as you strain, like Ken from Street Fighter lifting a weight.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) pokes an ear (耳) that belongs to your home country (邦) — you tease it playfully.
reading: ヤ — Picture teasing someone by saying 'Ya ya ya!' while wiggling your hand (扎) near their ear (耳).

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) pushes a vertical stroke (｜) into a one (一) that sits under an upside-down box (冂) — that’s inserting something into a tight slot.
reading: The sound is ソウ — imagine a “sow” (pig) inserting its snout into a fence gap to root for food.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) grabs a handful of one (一) day (日) tree (木) with an eye (目) on it — you pick up the whole thing with your fingers.
reading: サ — You pick up a handful of sand (サ sounds like 'sa') and let it slip through your fingers.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) holds a spoon (匕) over a month (月) of supplies, while a vertical stroke (｜) and a one (一) form the straps — you carry the whole bundle on your back.
reading: The backpacker says 'HAI!' as he hoists the load onto his back — the sound of effort is 'hai'.

meaning: A dry (干) claw (爪) grabs an open box enclosure (凵) while a hand at the side (扎) pushes — the whole thing swings, shakes, and sways.
reading: Picture a swing set rocking back and forth, and each creak sounds like "YO" (ヨウ) — the swing says "yo-yo-yo" as it moves.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) grabs a yellow (黄) thing inside an upside-down box (冂) with a vertical stroke (｜) and a ten (十) — you pull it out, causing it to come.
reading: The sound is コウ. Imagine a 'ko' (child) pulling a yellow rope out of a box — the rope goes 'ko-ko-ko' as it comes out.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) knocks on a crown (冖) that sits on an old bird (隹) — the bird pecks back, picking out seeds from the ground.
reading: The old bird's knock echoes 'KAKU' — like a quick 'cuckoo' but with a hard K, as in 'KAKU' the knock.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) reaches into a wrapping enclosure (勹) to grab a left hand (屮) — you pluck that hand out like a string from a bundle.
reading: The sound is シュウ — imagine “shoe” — you pluck a shoe off a shelf with one quick tug.

meaning: A shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) and a hand at the side (扎) is trying to grab two splayed strokes (ハ) from your mouth (口) — that's a loss and damage to you.
reading: The 'son' in 'sonar' pings and bounces back, but the damage is done — you hear the loss echo. (ソン)

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) swings at a rice field (田) with a ten (十) and a measurement (寸) — you seize the field and spring upon it, striking hard.
reading: The sound is ハク — think “hack” — you hack at something to seize it, like a hawk’s talon striking.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) touches a mysterious (玄) short thread (幺) under a lid (亠) in a rice field (田) — the thread twitches, causing a cramp or spasm in the hand.
reading: The sound is チク — imagine “chick” — a chick’s leg twitches in a spasm when it’s startled.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) holds a pole made of a direction (方) and a stand up (立) under a crown (冖) with two short strokes on top (并) — you use the pole to beat something, or pole a boat along.
reading: The sound is ホウ — think “hoe” — you beat the ground with a hoe, or use a pole like a hoe to push off.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) grabs a sheep (羊) and two short strokes on top (并) — you braid the wool into a rope, then cut it with a craft (工) knife held by the king (王).
reading: The king (王) says 'サ' as he slices the braid — imagine the sound of scissors going 'sa-sa' through wool.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) scratches an insect (虫) that has a dot (丶) and a right hand (又) — you scratch the itch it causes.
reading: ソウ — Imagine scratching a mosquito bite and saying 'Sow!' (ソウ sounds like 'sow') as you scratch.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) tips a tin can (缶) that has an evening (夕) inside an open box enclosure (凵) — the can wags and swings, spilling the evening light.
reading: The tin can goes 'ヨウ' as it swings — like a yo-yo (ヨウ) on a string, wagging back and forth.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) pounds a bird (鳥) on a mountain (山) — you husk the grain by crushing it with a heavy stone, and the bird's feathers fly off.
reading: The pounding goes 'トウ' — like 'toe' — you use your toe to press the pestle down on the mountain.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) props up an old man (老) who holds a spoon (匕) and a day (日) on soil (土) — the prop keeps him from falling, with a sweeping stroke (ノ) as the brace.
reading: The old man says 'シ' as he leans on the prop — like 'she' — she holds the spoon steady.

meaning: A vertical stroke (｜) pokes into a mortar (臼), while a branch (支) and a right hand (又) reach in, and a hand at the side (扎) with ten (十) fingers digs — all searching and seeking inside the mortar.
reading: You 'so' (ソウ) the search — imagine saying 'so, where is it?' as you rummage through the mortar with both hands.

meaning: A hand at the side clears the tall lid and mouth, clarifying what's inside.
reading: He clears the tall lid with a 'ko' (a child's cry) to see what's inside.

meaning: A hand at the side thrusts two short strokes on top of a month, daubing it with paint.
reading: He thrusts his hand and daubs 'saku' (like 'sock you') onto the month.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) holds a vertical stroke (｜) that pierces through a dot (丶) and a sweeping stroke (ノ), then pushes between two (二) lines and the katakana-mu shape (厶) — all under a day (日). The hand shoves the whole bundle into a tight gap, so you stick it in or insert it.
reading: The hand at the side (扎) jabs a needle into a cushion — the sound is the sharp 'shin' of the needle going in. (シン)

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) grabs a dish (皿) that has one (一) dot (丶) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) on top, plus two splayed strokes (ハ) and two short strokes (并) — the hand clamps down hard, seizing the whole thing.
reading: The hand at the side (扎) seizes a dish (皿) so tightly it makes an 'aku' sound like a gasp of effort. (アク)

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) swings a vertical stroke (｜) like a club into a crowded (込) mouth (口) — the blow lands with a thud, beating and pounding the mouth until it taps out a message.
reading: The hand at the side (扎) beats a drum with a stick — each strike goes 'tai' like the beat of a taiko drum. (タイ)

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) takes a bow (弓) and ice (冫) — the ice makes the bowstring slippery, so the hand winds it around and around, binding and tying the bow tightly.
reading: The hand at the side (扎) ties a knot in a frozen bowstring — the rope creaks 'jaku' as it tightens. (ジャク)

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) presses paper onto a stone with feathers (羽) and a day (日) symbol, using ice (冫) to wet the surface — the hand rubs the paper to trace the inscription underneath.
reading: The hand at the side (扎) rubs the paper in a slow circle — the motion makes a soft 'tou' sound like a brush on stone. (トウ)

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) raises a vertical stroke (｜) like a shield in front of a mouth (口) under a dotted cliff (广) with three stacked strokes (ヨ) — the hand blocks and wards off anything coming at the mouth.
reading: The hand at the side (扎) parries a blow with a shield — the impact rings out 'tou' like a gong. (トウ)

meaning: A boat (舟) with a hand at the side (扎) and a pike (殳) on a table (几) — you use a right hand (又) to carry and transport goods from the boat to the table.
reading: The conveyor belt goes 'ハン' (han) — like 'hand' — you use your hand to move things along.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) helps a person (人) with a hat on top (个) and grass on top (艾) — they all board (搭) a vehicle together.
reading: トウ — “Tow” — the vehicle tows the person aboard.

meaning: A hand at the side reaches into a mortar (臼) with a claw (爪) to take out the contents. The claw pulls out what's stuck inside.
reading: トウ — Imagine a hand at the side pulling a stubborn 'toe' (トウ) out of a mortar, like a toe stuck in a hole.

meaning: An upside-down box and a crown sit on top of a skeleton. The skeleton's hand at the side is digging into the ground, stirring up turbid dirt.
reading: The skeleton's hand at the side digs so hard it makes a hollow 'kotsu' sound as it hits a buried bone.

meaning: A vertical stroke and one sit under a roof, with two and two splayed strokes above a hand — the hand reaches up to take and hoist the roof, pulling it out and shrinking it down.
reading: The sound 'ken' is in 'ken' (as in Ken) — imagine Ken pulling out a stubborn nail with his hand, 'Ken, take it out!'

meaning: A hand at the side presses down with a knuckle onto a dish (皿) to wipe off the water, while a person (人) nearby opens their mouth (口) to immerse it in the dish.
reading: オン — The person (人) says 'on' (オン) as the hand at the side presses the dish down to immerse it.

meaning: A hand at the side thrusts a spear through a door (戸) with a hat on top (个), while a flag (尸) and a mouth (口) come together to assemble the crowd. The one (一) thrust pokes through.
reading: ソウ — The thrust makes a 'sow' (ソウ) sound as it pokes through the door, like a sewing needle.

meaning: An old bird (隹) is perched on a hand at the side (扎), while a sweeping stroke (ノ) and from (乃) hang nearby — you carry the bird along with you, so you're always armed with it.
reading: ケイ — Imagine you're carrying a heavy suitcase (携) and you say 'KAY!' (ケイ) as you strain to lift it.

meaning: A hand at the side smears grass on top (艾) over a tree (木) with a little (小) one (一) hat (个) on it, rubbing and wiping the anointing oil.
reading: タ — The hand at the side smears 'tar' (タ) onto the tree, wiping it all over.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) squeezes a hole (穴) under a roof (宀) — with a vertical stroke (｜) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) pressing down, you wring out every drop.
reading: You squeeze the juice and it goes 'saku' (サク) — like the crack of a ripe fruit being pressed.

meaning: An ear (耳) with ice (冫) and a hand at the side (扎) — the hand takes in the ice to cool the ear, acting as a surrogate for the real ear.
reading: You 'SETSU' (セツ) the ice on your ear — like 'setsu' as in 'set' it down, but with a 'tsu' sound.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) grabs feathers (羽) and a hat on top (个), then wraps them with ice (冫) and three (彡) strands — all twisted into one tight bundle, coiling around itself.
reading: The bundle coils like a 'cue' (ク) — think of a pool cue wrapped in tape, spinning around as you tie it.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) lifts a large (大) mortar (臼) and slams it down — one (一) heavy pound, striking against the ground.
reading: The pound sounds like 'sho' (ショ) — imagine a ram hitting a gong with a loud 'SHO!' echo.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) swings a halberd (戈) inside a box (囗) with a mouth (口) — a sharp slap that boxes the ears, right across the face.
reading: The slap lands with a 'kaku' (カク) — like 'cock' (as in a rooster's peck), a quick, sharp strike.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) pushes away a flag (尸) with two short strokes on top (并) and two hands (廾) — casting off the clutter, arranging the rest with a sweep.
reading: You expel it with a 'hei' (ヘイ) — like 'hay' — tossing a bale of hay out of the barn with a grunt.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) trips over a mysterious (玄) thread (幺) under a lid (亠) with a dot (丶) and ice (冫) — you stumble, fall to the ground, and a sweeping stroke (ノ) marks your tumble.
reading: You fall with a 'shutsu' (シュツ) — like 'shoots' — as in a plant shoots up, but you shoot down to the ground.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) reaches under an upside-down box (冂) with a lid (亠) to pinch off a small stem — like picking a berry from a bush. The two short strokes on top (并) are the leaves you trim away.
reading: テキ — Think of a chef saying "tek-i" (like 'tech') as he pinches a sprig of thyme to pluck the leaves off for a dish.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) spreads out the name of a chinese emperor (禹) under a lid (亠) with a dot (丶) and a sweeping stroke (ノ), inside an upside-down box (冂) with an open box enclosure (凵) and the katakana-mu shape (厶) — casting the news wide, knowing all the details.
reading: You spread the news with a 'chi' (チ) — like 'cheese' — smiling as you tell everyone, 'Say cheese!' for the announcement.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) grabs a rice field (田) and an eye (目) above a shellfish (貝) — you've seen this field so many times you could throw it to the ground and still know it. The hand throws the familiar field down, and the eye + shellfish are the familiar sight you recognize.
reading: The kanji for 'know' is カン — think of a 'con' artist who knows every trick, and you throw him to the ground (摜) because you're familiar with his scams.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) pulls a woman (女) close, while a mouth (口) and a day (日) watch — that's a hug you drag in.
reading: ロウ — You row (ロウ) a boat, then pull your oar in to hug your partner.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) gathers a sweeping stroke (ノ), a mouth (口), a stooping figure (夂), and a heart (心) — all together, that's the general.
reading: ソウ — The general sows (ソウ) seeds of order with his hand, sweeping them into one pile.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) washes a katakana-mu shape (厶) and nothing (无) under a day (日) — that's flooding water to scour clean.
reading: カイ — The kai (カイ) of a harbor floods in, and you scour the deck with your hand.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) seizes a handful from a cliff (厂) where a spoon (匕) and a divining rod (卜) lie, while tiger spots (虍) and an eye (目) watch — grab it fast.
reading: サ — You say 'sah!' (サ) as you snatch a handful of sand from the beach.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) smashes an old bird (隹) against a mountain (山) — break it to bits, crush it flat.
reading: サイ — The scythe (サイ) swings down, crushing the bird and the mountain in one blow.

meaning: A hand (手) rubs against a tree (木) under a dotted cliff (广) that is covered in hemp (麻) — the rough hemp fibers chafe and polish the wood as you grind it smooth.
reading: マ — Picture a masseuse saying 'ma' (マ) softly as she rubs and chafes your sore shoulders with hemp cloth.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) reaches under a dotted cliff (广) to pick up scattered things, while four dots at the bottom (杰) mark the bits gathered.
reading: セキ — Imagine a 'sexy' hand (扎) sweeping up crumbs under a cliff, gathering them all in a pile.

meaning: A hand reaches up through a stand-up spicy nine and a dot, grabbing a serious gift — the hand holds it firmly, showing the intensity of the offering.
reading: The gift is so serious that you must say 'shee' (as in 'sheep') before accepting it — the sound 'shi' is in 'shee'.

meaning: The box-on-side enclosure traps a mouth, but a hand at the side reaches in and lifts it up — you raise the lid, and the same motion makes you tight-fisted, clutching what you found.
reading: Imagine a tight-fisted miser named "Ko" (コウ) who must raise his hand to hail a taxi — he shouts "Ko! Ko!" to lift it up, but never pays the fare.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) spreads out a cloth under a crown (冖) and rain (雨), with a wrapping enclosure (勹) and two (二) lines — all arranged so it feels comfortable and easy.
reading: チョ — 'Cho' (as in 'chop') — you chop down a tree to make a comfortable, easy chair, and the rain stops.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) rolls a rice field (田) with an insect (虫) and a measurement (寸) into a ball, slapping it flat with ten (十) fingers.
reading: タン — A 'tan' (タン) ball of rice is slapped by a hand until it's round and smooth.

meaning: A hand at the side searches through grass on top (艾) to find a large (大) day (日) marker, then imitates and copies the pattern it finds.
reading: モ — The hand at the side feels around and says 'mo' (モ) as it copies the large day marker's shape.

meaning: A hand at the side, a hat on top, and a wrapping enclosure — you trace the pattern under the hat, copying it exactly.
reading: モ — You 'mow' (モ) over the original with your hand, tracing every line to duplicate it.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) rubs feathers (羽) against white (白) cloth with ice (冫) on it, folding the cloth to print a pattern.
reading: ショウ — 'Show' (ショウ) — you rub feathers on cloth to show a print, folding it like a fan.

meaning: A hat on top sits over the katakana-mu shape, while three strokes fall like threads — a delicate hand (at the side) mixes them all together, blending the strands into one cloth.
reading: The delicate hand mixes a bowl of soup, and the chef says "San!" (サン) — as in "sang" — to call for more blending, but the hand is too gentle to stir fast.

meaning: A hand at the side grabs a little show sign and throws it out to the west — the hand at the side strikes the show, pushing it away from the two little marks.
reading: ヒョウ — Picture a hyena (ヒョウ) using its paw to strike and throw out a show sign to the west.

meaning: A car (車) crashes into a hand (手) holding a pike (殳) on a table (几), and a right hand (又) swings to beat and conquer the attacker.
reading: GEKI (ゲキ) — Picture a gecko (geki) on the car’s hood, using its tail to beat the pike-wielding hand away.

meaning: A hand at the side grabs a person with two short strokes on top, who is stuck under a cliff — the hand snaps the protrusion to break them free.
reading: ケツ — You 'ketsu' (ケツ) — like 'get so' — angry, you snap the stick in half, making it protrude at a sharp angle.

meaning: A hand at the side throws away a strike — the strike is discarded, abandoned, left behind in the dust.
reading: ヘツ — You 'hetsu' (ヘツ) — like 'hate it' — so you throw the strike away, discarding it completely.

meaning: A hand at the side reaches into fire under a crown to catch fish — the fire cooks them as you scoop them out.
reading: ロウ — You 'row' (ロウ) a boat slowly, dipping your hand in to catch fish, one by one.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) reaches up to a mouth (口) that is stretched by a measurement (寸) of craft (工) — you pull out a splinter from the mouth with that hand.
reading: Imagine a samurai (サン) pulling out a long hair from his rice bowl with a hand at the side — the hair comes out with a 'sannn' twang.

meaning: A hand at the side props up a crown that sits on an esteem's mouth, while a tusk braces the whole structure from below.
reading: チョウ — Picture a tusk propping up a crown, and the crown says 'chow' (チョウ) like a dog's dinner bell, holding everything steady.

meaning: A hand at the side uses a hand to brace a crown on an esteem's mouth, like pushing up a sagging shelf.
reading: チョウ — The hand at the side shouts 'chow!' (チョウ) as it shoves the crown back up onto the esteem's head.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) throws a strike (攵) at a stooping figure (夂) who is scattering seeds from a month (月) of two hands (廾) — the seeds fly everywhere.
reading: You see a chef scatter (まく) salt with a flick of his wrist — the salt lands with a 'satsu' sound on the counter.

meaning: A hand at the side bends a pair of legs that stand on soil, training them to be lithe like a willow.
reading: トウ — The hand at the side bends the legs into a 'toe' (トウ) touch, showing how flexible they've become.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) takes an axe (斤) to a sweet (甘) block, splitting it into two splayed strokes (ハ) — that's how you rend and tear.
reading: You hear a 'seee' sound as you tear a sheet of paper in half with both hands — the paper rips with a long 'sei' cry.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) holds a measurement (寸) while two short strokes on top (并) press down on a west (酉) jar — you economize by measuring every drop, and you abide by the jar's strict rules.
reading: The son (ソン) is told to economize and comply, so he measures his allowance with a tiny ruler — "son, save it!"

meaning: A dog (犬) bites the evening (夕) air, but a hand at the side (扎) twists it, and four dots at the bottom (杰) scatter like twisted fibers — that's the twist.
reading: You twist the rope and it goes 'nen' like a 'nene' (baby) crying — ネン.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) waves a flag (尸) with a barb (亅) on a door (戸), while a claw (爪) and four dots at the bottom (杰) stay humble — the wave is modest, not aggressive.
reading: The modest wave says "key" (キ) — you gently brandish a key to signal, not to strike.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) thrusts a stand up (立) into a ri (里) — the thrust pierces the rice field's center, stabbing deep.
reading: You thrust a stick into the ground with a "doe" (ドウ) — the doe jumps back, pierced by the sharp poke.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) straightens a large (大) mouth (口) inside an upside-down box (冂) with a sweeping stroke (ノ) — correcting the crooked shape.
reading: The teacher says "kyo" (キョウ) to correct your posture — "kyo, stand straight!"

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) dusts a day (日) and a rice field (田) with ten (十) strokes, while a mouth (口) blows away the dust — the duster cleans every corner.
reading: You dust the shelf with a "tan" (タン) — the duster goes "tan tan" as it taps the wood.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) strikes (攵) the month (月) under a lid (亠) and the katakana-mu shape (厶) — the whole setup is removed and dismantled.
reading: テツ — Think of a 'tetsu' (テツ) ball (like a wrecking ball) that strikes and withdraws everything from the room.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) brushes up under a dotted tent (癶) with two (二) strokes and a pair of legs (儿) — it rejects and excludes the dirt, eliminating it from the surface.
reading: You brush up the dust with a "hatsu" (ハツ) — "hats off" to the brush that eliminates every speck.

meaning: A hand at the side grabs a large old man's day (日) and rips it up, tearing down his say (曰) — the whole scene is hauled away.
reading: シャ — A shark (シャ) with a hand at the side rips up the day's catch, tearing it down and hauling it away.

meaning: A hand at the side pokes at a little person with two short strokes on top and a lid, causing disorder among the large day's plans.
reading: リョウ — A lion (リョウ) with a hand at the side stirs up disorder among the little people, knocking over their lid.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) with four dots at the bottom (杰) strokes the nothingness (無) — the 乞-shaped part (乞) is the gentle curve of the palm smoothing down.
reading: You stroke a cat and it purrs 'bu' like a soft 'boo' — ブ.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) grabs a hook stroke (乙) and pulls up on two (二) — the hook lifts and raises the whole thing open.
reading: You use the hook to pry open a jar, and it makes a sharp "キョウ!" (like "kyo" in "kyoukai") sound as the lid pops.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) scatters rice (米) over a rice field (田) — that's how you plant and sow the seeds.
reading: You 'ha' (ハ) as you toss the rice — a quick breath out with each handful over the field.

meaning: A hand at the side holds a camera, and an ear and a day are in the frame — the right hand presses the button to take a snapshot. The claw-like fingers pinch the moment.
reading: サツ — Think of 'sats' (サツ) as in 'satsuma' — you snap a photo of a satsuma orange, quick and easy, like taking a picture.

meaning: A hand at the side picks out two splayed strokes and a stop (已) from a vertical stroke and two, composing and editing a selection.
reading: セン — A cent (セン) is selected by a hand at the side, which compiles and edits the pile of coins.

meaning: A king (王) with a person (人) and two short strokes on top (并) stands next to a sheep (羊) with a hand at the side (扎) and two (二) large (大) strokes — the king slaps the sheep with his hand, striking it hard.
reading: ボク — Imagine a boxer (ボク) who slaps and hits a punching bag shaped like a sheep, each strike making a loud 'bok' sound.

meaning: A hand at the side presses down on a person wrapped in a wrapping enclosure who lacks gold, pushing them flat.
reading: キン — A king (キン) presses a hand at the side on a person who lacks gold, pushing them down.

meaning: A hand at the side throws a crown onto an esteem (尚) that sees (見) too much, disturbing and confusing the scene.
reading: カク — A cock (カク) with a hand at the side knocks over an esteem's crown, throwing everything into confusion.

meaning: A king (王) is crowded (込) into a corner, and a hand at the side (扎) whips him with a ten (十) and a spicy (辛) stick, while a sheep (羊) stands on soil (土) under a lid (亠) watching — that's a flogging.
reading: The whip cracks 'TATSU!' (タツ) — like 'tats' as in 'tattoo' — 'TATSU, that stings!'

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) grabs a heart (心) and shakes it, while a mouth (口) screams and a halberd (戈) swings — the whole scene moves violently.
reading: The heart is shaken so hard it goes 'KAN!' like a loud gong hitting the ground.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) reaches into an upside-down box (冂) that is crowded (込) with a mouth (口) and a box (囗) — it strikes them all out.
reading: Think of a TA (タ) — a karate chop — the hand at the side (扎) strikes down like a ta-ta-ta beat on a drum.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) picks up a person (人) who wears a hat on top (个) and carries a mouth (口) and a one (一) — it inspects them carefully.
reading: Imagine a REN (レン) — a lens — you pick up a lens to inspect it closely, checking for cracks.

meaning: A lid (亠) over a hand at the side (扎) and an old bird (隹) with a short thread (幺) — you hug the bird to protect it, holding it close with your hand.
reading: You hug so tight you say 'ヨウ' (yo) — like 'yo, hold on' — as you embrace the bird.

meaning: Rain (雨) falls on a rice field (田), and a hand at the side (扎) grinds the wet rice into a mash on a stone.
reading: Think of RAI (ライ) — a rye grain — you grind rye with your hand at the side (扎) to make flour.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) grabs a tiger (虍) that has a cliff (厂) and a divining rod (卜) — it captures the tiger, pulling it from a rice field (田) where a spoon (匕) and power (力) lie.
reading: Imagine a RYO (リョ) — a lion — you capture a lion with your hand at the side (扎), seizing it by the mane.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) acts on its own, ignoring the day (日) and the lid (亠) over the mouth (口) inside a box (囗) with a one (一) — it does what it wants.
reading: Think of SEN (セン) — a cent — you are self-indulgent, spending every cent on yourself, hand at the side (扎) grabbing coins.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) reaches up to a lid (亠) on a stand-up (立) box, but the box is full of spicy (辛) soil (土) — you must select and pick out the good bits from the mess.
reading: タク — Imagine a taxi (タク) driver who has to select the right passenger from a crowd, pointing with his hand at the side.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) holds a sharp stick to pierce the wrapping enclosure (勹) that contains a buy (買) — but an insect (虫) crawls out, so you break through to get it.
reading: サク — The insect pierces a sack (サク) of rice, breaking through the cloth with a sharp poke.

meaning: A car hits an open box enclosure on a table, and a right hand with a pike strikes it — that's the attack, the beat, the hit.
reading: ゲキ — The attack is so fierce it feels like a gecko (ゲキ) slamming its tail against the car.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) holds up a crown (冖) as a shield, while a mouth (口) shouts 'esteem' (尚) — but the rice field (田) is blocked, so you must obstruct the path.
reading: トウ — You throw a towel (トウ) over the crown to obstruct the view, stopping the enemy.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) steers a tree (木) while a mouth (口) and goods (品) are arranged — you maneuver and operate the controls.
reading: Picture a pilot saying 'SOU' (like 'so') as they steer a plane — that's the maneuver sound.

meaning: A hand holds up a wrapping enclosure with a mouth, while grass on top and a strike support it — the hand lifts it all up high.
reading: ケイ — You lift the heavy box up and say 'kay' (ケイ) — like a cheerleader's 'kay!' as she supports the load.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) reaches up to pull a garment (衣) over the head, with a lid (亠) on top and a mouth (口) below — you are putting on armor or clothes.
reading: The sound is 'kan' — imagine a knight putting on armor and saying 'CAN I get this on?' — 'kan' as in 'can'.

meaning: A hat on top (个) sits over an open box enclosure (凵) where a Chinese emperor (禹) is trapped — a hand at the side (扎) grabs him to capture him as a captive.
reading: キン — You capture the emperor and put him in a king's (キン) cage, locking the lid.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) lifts a say (言) and a pair of legs (儿) off a cliff (厂) — but the load is heavy, so you must carry it on your shoulder, bearing the weight.
reading: タン — You carry a heavy tan (タン) barrel on your shoulder, bearing its weight up the hill.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) beats a spicy (辛) chest, while a flag (尸) and a mouth (口) cry out in grief — you're pounding your breast in sorrow.
reading: The sound of beating your breast is a hollow 'HEK' — like 'heck' you say when you're so upset you hit your chest.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) grabs a spicy (辛) mouth (口) and a flag (尸) under a stand-up (立) ten (十) — all torn apart in a struggle, so you tear up the paper.
reading: ハク — Imagine a hawk (ハク) tearing up a fish with its claws, ripping it apart.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) grabs a pig (豕) under tiger spots (虍) on a cliff (厂), using a divining rod (卜) and a spoon (匕) to claim the spot as your base.
reading: You 'KYO' (like 'kyo' in 'kyoto') — you occupy Kyoto, taking it as your base camp.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) pushes aside a family name (氏) that is under a lid (亠) with two hands (廾) and a sword (刀) — all alike (齊) in a crowd, so you shove them out of the way.
reading: セイ — Say 'say' (セイ) as you push aside a curtain to get through a crowd.

meaning: A gentleman (士) uses his hand (扎) to lift a crown (冖) off the climax (至) of a soil (土) mound, while a mouth (口) below cheers — that's lifting and raising.
reading: You lift the crown (冖) high with a 'tie' (タイ) — like tying it to a tall pole to raise it up.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) pulls out an old bird (隹) from three stacked strokes (ヨ) — you excel by selecting it and pulling it out of the pile.
reading: テキ — A tech (テキ) expert pulls out the best component from a machine, excelling in the task.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) pounds a craft (工) with a gentleman (士) using a measurement (寸) and a mouth (口) — you pound it all into a paste.
reading: トウ — A toe (トウ) pounds the ground as you stomp in rhythm.
