meaning: Your hand (扎) and two hands (廾) are at your nose (鼻) — you pinch it to blow out, while your eye (目) and rice field (田) are squeezed shut from the effort.
reading: You blow your nose with a 'koh' (コウ) sound — like a cough that clears the nasal passage.

meaning: A retainer's hand (手) grabs a buy (買) receipt, but a box-on-side enclosure (匚) traps it — you must drive away the retainer to oust the deal.
reading: ラン — A 'run' (ラン) away from the scene is how you drive away the intruder.

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) shows (示) two (二) little (小) marks under a roof (宀), where a hand at the side (扎) and a dotted tent (癶) rub together to grate and scratch the surface.
reading: サツ — Picture a 'satsuma' orange being grated on a grater — the rough skin makes a scratchy, rubbing sound as you grate it.

meaning: A mortar sits on a hand, while two splayed strokes above show a plan being lifted up — you raise the whole project off the ground.
reading: キョ — Imagine a giant 'kyo' (like 'key-oh') being raised high on a hand, a plan written on it, lifted toward the sky.

meaning: A crown sits on a hand at the side, while rain falls through 'and yet' — the rain stains the cloth, dyeing it with wet color.
reading: ジュ — Think of 'juice' (ジュ) spilling from a cup onto fabric, staining it deeply — the juice is the dye.

meaning: A large (大) hand (手) presses a dog (犬) under a cliff (厂) — you tuck it in, stowing it away with your finger.
reading: ヨウ — 'Yo!' (ヨウ) you shout as you tuck the dog into a fold.

meaning: A head (疋) with a dart (矢) and a spoon (匕) is held by a hand at the side (扎), while a マ-shaped stroke (マ) and the 乞-shaped part (乞) hover above — this whole weird setup mimics a person you're aiming at, like a target dummy you imitate or nominate for a role.
reading: The reading is ギ. Imagine a GI (as in 'GI Joe') who mimics every move you make, aiming a dart at a target — the GI's imitation is so perfect you nominate him for the mimicry award.

meaning: A right hand and a hand at the side grab grass on top, while an old bird flies into the trap — you seize the bird with the snare.
reading: ワク — 'Waku' sounds like 'wack-you' — you wack the trap shut, catching the bird with a snap.

meaning: A hand at the side pushes back a shellfish, an eye, and a little roof — you reject the whole pile, shoving it away from the door.
reading: ヒン — 'Hin' like 'hint' — you give a cold hint to push people back, a sharp 'hin' of dismissal.

meaning: A hand at the side twists a barb under a roof, while a heart sits on a dish — determined, you wring the water out with a pinch.
reading: ドウ — 'Dou' like 'dough' — you twist and wring the dough with your hands, determined to shape it.

meaning: A hand at the side lays down a mouth, a gate, and a stooping figure — you put the whole scene down gently on the ground.
reading: カク — 'Kaku' like 'cackle' — you lay down the heavy load and let out a 'kaku' of relief.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) throws a large (大) west (酉) bottle at home country (邦) — you hit it and resign from the game.
reading: テキ — 'Tech' (テキ) you hit the target with a tech gadget, then resign.

meaning: A dotted cliff (广) with a yellow (黄) rice field (田) — a hand at the side (扎) pulls the field wider, broadening the land.
reading: カク — 'Cock' (カク) the rooster's crow expands the morning — broaden your ears.

meaning: Reap (刈) bamboo (竹) with a hand at the side (扎) — you straighten the arrow shaft by the month (月) light.
reading: セン — 'Sen' (セン) the arrow flies straight as a senator's line.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) picks up a page (頁) with a shellfish (貝) and an eye (目) — gather it all into your lap.
reading: ケツ — 'Kets' (ケツ) — you pick up the 'kets' (like a cat's 'kets' — butt) and hold it in your lap.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) pushes open a door made of month (月) and buy (買) — the katakana-mu shape (厶) is the door handle you shove aside.
reading: The hand at the side (扎) shoves the door open with a loud 'HAI!' (like a karate shout).

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) grabs a woman (女) by the rice field (田) and strikes (攵) her — she shakes and trembles, and the day (日) and vertical stroke (｜) are the quivering lines around her.
reading: The woman shakes so hard her rice field (田) rattles — 'SOU' (like 'sow' seeds scattering in the quake).

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) tickles a short thread (幺) under a white (白) tree (木) — the ice (冫) makes the tickle feel cold and funny.
reading: Tickle the tree (木) until it laughs — 'RYAKU' (like 'laugh' but with a tickle in the throat).

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) throws a stooping figure (夂) into a crown (冖) over a white (白) heart (心) — the oneself (自) is confused, and the one (一) line is the chaos that disturbs it all.
reading: The stooping figure (夂) stumbles into the crown (冖) and cries 'JOU!' (like 'jolt' — a sudden disturbance).

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) picks out from a crowded (込) upside-down box (冂) — the lid (亠) and two short strokes (并) are the discarded bits, while the ten (十) and mouth (口) and stand up (立) and drip (滴) are the selected ones.
reading: The hand picks out the drip (滴) from the box — 'TEKI' (like 'tick' — a precise selection).

meaning: Two hands (one large, one small) grab a tree with two splayed strokes, while a mix of branches and a one-stroke hook help you climb the cliff.
reading: ハン — You climb the tree using a HANG glider (ハン) that you strap to your back, but you still have to scale by hand.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) spreads tiger spots (虍) over a cliff (厂) — the heart (心) and rice field (田) are vented out, while the divining rod (卜) and spoon (匕) set forth the order.
reading: The tiger spots (虍) spread over the cliff (厂) — 'CHO' (like 'chore' — you spread out the work).

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) reaches out to gather shellfish (貝) and an eye (目) watches as two splayed strokes (ハ) and a person (人) under a lid (亠) over large (大) soil (土) all come together, with two (二) of everything piling up.
reading: サン — Imagine a sun (サン) that gathers all the shellfish and people together at sunset, pulling them into one glowing pile.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) makes a beckoning motion toward an old bird (隹) that sits under a crown (冖) while rain (雨) falls, and a person at the side (化) urges it forward with a dot (丶) and a vertical stroke (｜).
reading: カク — Picture a quacking duck (カク) that you beckon and urge with your hand, the duck waddling toward you through the rain.

meaning: A hand at the side pulls a dragon toward a month and a stand-up figure — you collect everything together, even a dragon, into one place.
reading: ロウ — You use a ROW (ロウ) boat to collect all the dragons from the river, bringing them together on the shore.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) pushes against a gate (門) with two short strokes on top (并) — the gate won't open, so you are obstructed and barred from passing.
reading: Imagine a huge gate (門) that is blocked by a giant RANch (ラン) — the ranch fence bars the way, and you cannot get through.

meaning: A hand at the side grabs a woman's eye, but two splayed strokes on top show she opposes — she runs counter to the grab.
reading: エイ — The woman shouts 'EIGH!' (like 'hey' but with a long A) as she opposes the hand.

meaning: A hand at the side steals a garment from a lid, while two short strokes on top and a mouth chase away the thief — the garment is stolen, then the thief is chased away.
reading: ジョウ — The thief says 'JOE!' (like the name) as he steals the garment and runs.

meaning: A hand at the side gives a helping hand to a person with a pair of legs, a wrapping enclosure, a spoon, and a compare — the excuse is that they need support.
reading: セン — The hand at the side says 'SEN!' (like 'send') to send help to the person.

meaning: A rat sits in a mortar under a roof, but a hand at the side (扎) is throwing it out — the rat must hurry, so the hand urges it on with a toss.
reading: The rat is thrown out with a loud 'SAN!' as it lands in the sand — think of 'sand' (サン) flying as you hurl it.

meaning: An old bird (隹) with a hand at the side (扎) carries a bag in its beak, walking over a mountain (山) — it brings the bag along, armed with it.
reading: The old bird carries the bag with a 'KEI' — like a key (ケイ) jingling in the bag as it walks.

meaning: An ear (耳) with a hand at the side (扎) acts as a surrogate — the hand takes over for the ear, doing its job in addition.
reading: セツ — Think of a 'set' (セツ) of surrogate ears — you grab a spare ear with your hand to act in addition to your own.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) grabs a buy (買) bag full of thread (糸) and an old bird (隹) — you split the bag open and rub the contents to choose the best thread, rending the bag in the process.
reading: The sound is 'ra' — like when you 'raw' a seam apart with your hands, rending the fabric with a rough 'ra' sound.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) piles up soil (土) and shellfish (貝) under a sweeping stroke (ノ) and two splayed strokes (ハ), with a pair of legs (儿) standing on top. The eye (目) watches the hoard grow.
reading: You 'san' (like 'sahn') the coins — imagine counting your hoard and saying 'san, san, san' as you stack each shellfish.

meaning: A hand pulls a short thread that twists around a little thread, and a say-word gets tangled — the whole thing is crooked and bent, like a knot that won't straighten.
reading: The bent thread reminds you of a 'REN' — like a 'wrench' (レンチ) that's bent and crooked.

meaning: A hand at the side (扎) opens a well (井) with grass on top (艾), and an old bird (隹) sits on the two (二) lines. The bird spreads its wings to broaden the space.
reading: You 'tan' (like 'tahn') the mat — imagine unrolling it with a 'TAN!' sound, the bird hopping off as it opens wide.

meaning: A hand at the side blocks a crown, while two short strokes on top and a mouth shout 'esteem' — but a ri and black four dots at the bottom hold it back, obstructing everything.
reading: You shout 'TOU!' — like 'TOU' in 'tough' — as you resist and stop the obstacle.

meaning: A hand at the side stirs a mortar, and an eye sees the mess — the see-part watches as everything gets thrown into confusion, like mixing a pot too hard.
reading: You cry 'KAKU!' — like 'KAKU' in 'cactus' — as the disturbance pokes you and makes you jump.

meaning: A right hand grabs an old bird's eye, while another hand at the side snatches it away — you abduct the bird, taking it off in a flash.
reading: You snatch it with a 'KAKU!' — like the sharp 'KAKU' of a crow's caw as it's taken.

meaning: A retainer's hand at the side grabs a see-ing eye and the 乞-shaped part — you hold all of it firmly in your grip.
reading: You RUN (ラン) to grab the falling scroll before it hits the ground.

meaning: A hand at the side pushes a vertical stroke through a crown, two mouths, and a garment — fending off the attacker with a stab.
reading: You DOUGH (ドウ) the enemy's chest with a quick stab, then push him away.

meaning: A right hand (又) holds up a ten (十) — the branch of a tree that supports the whole, or a hand that sustains a load.
reading: The シ reading sounds like 'she' — picture a she-branch supporting a heavy ten-pound weight, saying 'she can hold it!'

meaning: A vertical stroke leans against a divining rod and a right hand, but the hand is holding it unevenly, so the whole thing tilts up on one side — that's 'up, uneven'.
reading: キ — A key (キ) is unevenly balanced on a table, one end up, one end down.

meaning: A folding chair radical — the top part is like the back of a chair, and the bottom is the strike — imagine hitting the chair to fold it shut.
reading: The 'hoku' in 'Hokkaido' — picture a folding chair in Hokkaido being struck by a snowball, making a 'HOKU' thud.

meaning: This variant of the folding chair radical — the '乞-shaped part' (乞) is the chair's frame, and the strike hits it to fold it up.
reading: The 'hoku' in 'hokum' — imagine a folding chair made of '乞' parts being struck, and a magician says 'HOKU' to make it vanish.

meaning: A vertical stroke (｜) and the 乞-shaped part (乞) are gathered up by a strike (攵) — collecting them as income.
reading: シュウ — Imagine a cashier saying "SHOO" (シュウ) as they sweep coins into the till — that's your income.

meaning: The 乞-shaped part (乞) is struck (攵) to test and examine it — like tapping a wall to check its strength.
reading: You 'KOH' on the wall to examine it, listening for hollow spots.

meaning: A vertical stroke (｜) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) form a path, and the 乞-shaped part (乞) sits like a resting person, while strike (攵) taps gently. This is a relaxed, at-ease place where nothing is struck hard.
reading: ユウ — You are at ease in a yurt (ユウ), a cozy place where you relax.

meaning: You stop (已) the old way, then strike (攵) it with a change — that's reformation.
reading: You 'kai' the old habit — like saying 'kai' (as in 'kite') to cut it away with a strike.

meaning: The craft (工) is being hit by a strike (攵) — that's an aggression, an attack. The 乞-shaped part (乞) is the attacker's arm reaching out to criticize and polish the craft.
reading: The attack is so loud it sounds like a 'KO' (コウ) — imagine a giant 'KO' punch landing on the craft, then the strike (攵) keeps criticizing it.

meaning: Direction (方) plus strike (攵) — you strike toward a direction to set free, to release the arrow, to fire it.
reading: You release it 'HO' (like 'hoe') — you hoe the ground to set the seeds free — ホウ.

meaning: A government is built on a stop sign (止) that holds up a one (一) — but a strike (攵) from a 乞-shaped part (乞) knocks it down, showing how politics is a messy fight over control.
reading: セイ — Imagine a politician shouting 'SAY!' (セイ) at a crowd, but a strike from a whip makes him stumble — that's the sound of government.

meaning: A family name (氏) under a flag (尸) with a hook stroke (乙) and one (一) line, all struck (攵) — this is the strong, robust ancestor who led the clan, vigorous even in death.
reading: The on-reading ビン sounds like 'bin' — picture a robust warrior lifting a heavy bin over his head, his family name stitched on his flag, striking it with a stick.

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) over a hook stroke (乙) and a flag (尸), all struck (攵) — you put forth effort to strike that flag down, but the hook keeps pulling you back, so you try again.
reading: The on-reading ブ (from ブツ) — imagine a 'boo' sound as you put forth effort to push a heavy boulder, but it rolls back with a 'boo' from the ghost inside.

meaning: The mouth (口) and ten (十) form an old well, and next to it a strike (攵) hits the ground — this is the reason an old well collapsed, by happenstance, not intention. The strike is the accidental cause.
reading: コ — A koala (コ) sits by the old well, and the reason it's there is pure happenstance — it wandered in by accident.

meaning: A father (父) puts a lid (亠) on a strike (攵) — the result is that the 乞-shaped part (乞) finally works, giving the effect you wanted.
reading: The effect of the strike is a loud 'KOU' — like a gong hitting after the blow.

meaning: You strike (攵) the rice (米) with a gentle hand — the grains settle down, pacified and soothed into stillness.
reading: To pacify, you hum a soft 'MI' — like a mother's soothing murmur.

meaning: A dry (干) little (小) hat on top (个) is struck (攵) by one (一) — the blow makes the hat fall off, and you must express what happened.
reading: You 'JO' (ジョ) down the story in a journal, jotting each event with a quick stroke.

meaning: The mother (母) is quick to strike (攵) — she's alert and agile, always ready to swat a fly. The do not (毋) part is just the mother's face, and the strike is her hand.
reading: You're 'BIN' — like a 'bin' (trash can) that tips over quickly when touched — that's cleverness and agility.

meaning: Water (水) with a dot (丶) splashes as a strike (攵) hits the 乞-shaped part (乞) — you rescue someone from drowning.
reading: You shout 'KYUU!' as you throw a lifebuoy — 'KYUU' is the sound of the rescue whistle.

meaning: A mouth (口) inside a five (五) is struck (攵) by one (一) and two (二) — the gavel hits the block to silence the mouth.
reading: The judge bangs the gavel and shouts 'GYO!' (ギョ) to stop the noise.

meaning: A vertical stroke (｜) through a mouth (口) and two splayed strokes (ハ) on a tree (木) is struck (攵) by the 乞-shaped part (乞) — this is the emperor's decree carved into wood.
reading: The decree is read aloud with a sharp 'CHOKU' (チョク) — like a chop of the imperial axe.

meaning: A soil mound with a lid and two lines on top, but a strike hits it — you play on the mound, then get proud when you win.
reading: GOW — a proud goat (GOW) butts the soil mound with its horns, then plays a game of tag.

meaning: A shellfish with an eye gets struck by two splayed strokes and the 乞-shaped part — the shellfish is defeated, its shell cracked in reversal.
reading: ハイ — Imagine a high (ハイ) five that misses — your hand slaps air, and you feel the sting of defeat.

meaning: A dry little hat on top of a one, with a strike — you express your story by striking the dry ground with a stick, narrating each step.
reading: JOE — Joe (JO) stands on a dry hill and strikes a pose to express his feelings to the crowd.

meaning: The old man (老) strikes (攵) the child (子) with a 乞-shaped part (乞) — he teaches the child the doctrine through discipline.
reading: The teacher says 'KYO-ko!' as she strikes the desk — the sound echoes in the classroom.

meaning: The esteem part is wrapped in a towel, but a strike from the 乞-shaped part and an upside-down box has torn the towel — it's worn-out and defeated.
reading: ヘイ — 'Hey!' (ヘイ) you shout as the worn-out towel falls apart under the strike.

meaning: A mouth speaks with esteem, but the strike and the 乞-shaped part push the upside-down box open wide — the space becomes high, flat, and spacious.
reading: ショウ — 'Show' (ショウ) me the broad, high hall — it's spacious enough for a show.

meaning: A divining rod and a right hand together weigh something — the hand holds the rod to measure, but the result is so uneven it cuts the measurement short, and you come uninvited to check.
reading: タツ — 'Tats' (タツ) — you weigh a tatami mat with a divining rod, but it's cut short.

meaning: The ear strikes the 乞-shaped part — that takes daring. A bold ear dares to strike the begging shape.
reading: カン — The daring knight kicks a can down the road, brave and bold.

meaning: A month (月) and two (二) with a 乞-shaped part (乞) are struck (攵) by two hands (廾) — the strike scatters the pieces. The hands throw, the strike breaks, and everything disperses.
reading: サン — "Sun" (サン) — the sun scatters its rays everywhere, and you spend (散) your time in its light.

meaning: A child (子) sits under a lid (亠) while a strike (攵) hits the 乞-shaped part (乞) — the kindliness of the strike is that it only taps, not hits hard, so the child stays industrious.
reading: トン — Imagine a heavy 'ton' of bricks falling gently on the 乞-shaped part (乞) — the soft thud is the sound of kind industry.

meaning: A barb, a divining rod, a right hand, a mouth, and a large part — the hand uses the barb like chopsticks to pick up a thing from the mouth, pinching it with the rod.
reading: キ — A key (キ) is pinched between chopsticks (the barb and rod) — you pick it up with a 'key' click.

meaning: A strike (攵) hits a direction (方) marker on a day (日) that is white (白) with heat, producing the sound of an ancient musical instrument.
reading: The strike (攵) makes a 'seku' sound like a sharp 'SEC-ond' beat on the instrument. (uses セク)

meaning: A wrapping enclosure (勹) holds a mouth (口) that is struck (攵) by grass on top (艾) and the 乞-shaped part (乞) — this mix of elements inspires awe and respect.
reading: Imagine a respectful bow while saying "KEI" (ケイ) — like a polite "kei" from a servant to a lord, full of honor.

meaning: A woman (女) counts grains of rice (米) with a strike (攵) from a stooping figure (夂) who begs (乞) for the exact number — fate is in the count.
reading: The number is SUU (スウ) — picture a sushi chef (suu) rapidly counting out rice grains for each roll, his hands a blur of numbers.

meaning: A mouth under a lid on an upside-down box, with a tall strike on top — the strike hits the tall box, making the mouth rattle as you beat it.
reading: コウ — Imagine a kōan (コウ) riddle: you strike a tall box with a stick, and the sound is the answer.

meaning: To organize, you strike (攵) the stop (止) sign with a one (一) and a mouth (口) to make a neat row, then place a tree (木) on top — everything in its proper order.
reading: セイ — Say 'say' as you arrange books on a shelf — 'セイ, that's the right spot' — the strike (攵) helps you tune each item.

meaning: The enemy stands up (立) under a lid (亠) inside an upside-down box (冂), holding a mouth (口) and ten (十) with two short strokes on top (并), while a strike (攵) from a drip (滴) and the 乞-shaped part (乞) attack — that's your foe.
reading: テキ — The enemy throws a 'teki' (テキ) — a sticky, dripping tar ball — at you.

meaning: Spread out a ten (十) and a rice field (田) with a direction (方) and a dot (丶), then strike (攵) the 乞-shaped part (乞) to pave the ground — that's how you promulgate a plan.
reading: フ — You 'fu' (フ) — like 'foo' — spread a futon on the floor to sit and sleep.

meaning: A woman (女) is counting on her fingers, but a strike (攵) from a vertical stroke (｜) and a one (一) breaks her focus, while a mouth (口) begs (乞) for the final number — this is the number and its fate.
reading: The number of times you say 'sue' (スウ) to a lawyer is your fate — imagine shouting 'sue!' as you count each finger.

meaning: A box-on-side enclosure (匚) holds a divining rod (卜) and a right hand (又) that beats a mouth (口) — you expel the mouth from the box by driving it away.
reading: To expel someone, you 'coo' (ク) at them like a pigeon until they leave — imagine cooing to shoo away a pigeon from your porch.

meaning: A right hand (又) ties a large (大) mouth (口) inside an upside-down box (冂) with a sweeping stroke (ノ) — binding it shut.
reading: You 'KYO' (like 'kyo' in 'kyoto') — you bind the box with a 'kyo' knot, tight and secure.

meaning: A dry (干) field of soil (土) with two short strokes on top (并) gets struck (攵) by a buyer (買) who is weary of it — the strike makes you dislike the whole deal.
reading: The buyer (買) says "エキ" (eki) like "echo" — the strike (攵) echoes in your ears, making you weary of the sound.

meaning: A person (人) with a hat on top (个) and a mouth (口) is struck (攵) by a beggar (乞) — the strike tightens the person's stiffened posture.
reading: The beggar (乞) cries "レン" (ren) like "wren" — a small bird that stiffens its body when frightened.

meaning: A towel (巾) and a little (小) thing fall under esteem (尚) as two short strokes on top (并) strike (攵) with a spoon (匕) in an upside-down box (冂) at evening (夕), causing a violent death.
reading: ヘイ — Say 'hey!' (ヘイ) as you strike down the enemy with a spoon, killing them in a violent fall.

meaning: A crown sits on top of a divining rod and a right hand, while three stacked strokes mix with a child below — the child is taught by the mix of signs.
reading: ガク — The child learns 'GAKU' (like 'gaku' in 'gakusei' — student) from the crown and rod.

meaning: A person's style or art is like a cross of lines — the top is a マ-shaped stroke (マ) over a one (一) and a barb (亅) — a written sentence with a hook to catch your eye.
reading: The ブン reading sounds like 'boon' — picture a literature book that is a boon to your studies, full of sentences and art.

meaning: A child (子) sits under a sentence (文) written on a board. The child studies the sentence to gain learning and knowledge.
reading: ガク — The child goes to school and shouts "Gak!" (ガク) when the bell rings, excited to learn.

meaning: A vertical stroke (｜) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) cross over a sentence (文), while two hands (廾) hold it steady below. The hands adjust the sentence so all lines are equal and alike.
reading: The two hands (廾) carefully SEI-ze (セイ) the crooked sentence — making it perfectly aligned.

meaning: A stop sign, a sentence, and a piling — the sentence is stopped by the piling, but the pattern of strokes is beautiful, a harmony of appearance.
reading: ヒン — 'Hin' (ヒン) — the beautiful sentence is 'hin' (a sound of admiration) as you see the harmony.

meaning: An adjusted (斉) room with a sentence (文) written on the wall, two hands (廾) washing a show (示) of offerings — this is purification and worship.
reading: サイ — In the purification room, you say 'サイ' (sigh) as you cleanse yourself, the sound of relief.

meaning: A sentence (文) that is un- (非) plain — it's beautifully patterned, like a woven tapestry of words.
reading: The pattern is so fine it makes you say 'HI' (as in 'high' art) — picture a gallery owner gasping 'HI! That's beautiful!'

meaning: A king writes a sentence, but the ink splatters — leaving spots and patches all over the page.
reading: The spots are like a 'han' (ハン) — a stamp that leaves uneven marks on paper.

meaning: A tome (冊) with a door (戸) and a flag (尸) shows a variegated pattern of one (一) vertical stroke (｜), a dot (丶), a sweeping stroke (ノ), and a barb (亅) inside an upside-down box (冂), held by two hands (廾).
reading: The variegated pattern is like a 'han' (ハン) — think of a 'HAN-dkerchief' with stripes and marbles.

meaning: A gate (門) with two short strokes on top (并) and a tree (木) inside, plus a mouth (口) and a dot (丶) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) — all painted in multicolored patterns on the gate.
reading: The multicolored gate shines 'RAN' (like 'run' but with an 'a') — you run through the rainbow gate.

meaning: The dot is the ladle's scoop, and the cross is the handle — this is the sake dipper, also used to measure ten sho, and it points to the Big Dipper in the sky.
reading: You 'TO' (like 'toe') the dipper through the sake barrel, dipping it in and out with a rhythmic 'toe-toe' splash.

meaning: A big dipper (斗) scoops up rice (米) — that's the material you pay a fee for.
reading: You pay the fee with a 'RYO' (リョウ) — like a ryo, the old Japanese gold coin.

meaning: An angle and a big dipper — you measure a unit of volume by tilting the dipper at an angle to pour out about 180 liters.
reading: KOKU — a cook (KOKU) uses a big dipper to measure rice, filling it to the brim for a feast.

meaning: A grain stalk leans against a big dipper, while a hat on top and a one tilt it further — everything is diagonal and slanting.
reading: シャ — Imagine a 'sha' (シャ) as a sharp 'shard' of glass that lies at a slanting angle on the ground.

meaning: A crown (冖) sits on a mouth (口) that pours into a big dipper (斗) — this small jade wine cup is shaped like a crowned dipper with a lip.
reading: You sip from the cup and go 'KA!' (カ) — it's so small, one gulp is all it holds.

meaning: You dip water (く.む) from a sweet (甘) well using a big dipper (斗) that has a pair of legs (儿) standing in a box-on-side enclosure (匚).
reading: The big dipper (斗) dips with a 'shin' (シン) — imagine a 'SHIN-ing dipper scooping water.

meaning: A vertical stroke and one line cross the big dipper, while a month and utilize sit below — you measure the month by using the big dipper as a ruler, with the vertical stroke marking the level.
reading: カク — Picture a cock (カク) strutting with a measuring stick, checking the month's length with a big dipper.

meaning: Ten big dippers spin around a day, with a hat on top — you go around and rule by spinning the dippers, each one administering a different hour of the day.
reading: アツ — Imagine a hot (アツ) summer day: you spin ten big dippers to fan yourself while ruling over the crowd.

meaning: An axe — the top is the blade, the bottom is the handle, and it's also a weight (1.32 lb) and a counter for loaves of bread.
reading: The 'kin' in 'king' — picture a king using an axe (斤) to chop a loaf of bread, weighing it to exactly 1.32 lb.

meaning: An axe with a dot on top — the dot is the unwanted thing, and the axe chops it away, rejecting and retreating it.
reading: The axe swings and says “SEKI” — like “seki” (a Japanese word for a barrier) — it rejects the dot, pushing it back.

meaning: Father (父) holds an axe (斤) — he's the one who chops wood with the hatchet.
reading: The フ reading sounds like 'foo' — imagine father saying 'foo!' as he swings the axe, missing the log and hitting the ground.

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) and an axe (斤) cut into a stone (石) with a mouth (口) — the stone screams as the axe chops it, like cutting a sword from rock.
reading: The on-reading シャク sounds like 'shack' — picture a swordsman cutting a stone shack in half with one axe blow, the stone mouth yelling 'shack!' as it splits.

meaning: An axe cuts through a car, beheading it—a violent kill.
reading: The axe swings with a 'zan' (ザン) sound, slicing the car in two.

meaning: An axe (斤) cuts through a pile of rice (米) with a vertical stroke (｜) and a one (一) — the cut severs the rice, so you decline the offer and refuse to continue.
reading: The axe falls with a 'DAN' (like 'dan' in 'dance') — you sever the rice and decline the dance invitation, cutting it off cleanly.

meaning: An axe (斤) chops through two (二) day (日) and say (曰) tablets — cutting them off cleanly with one swing.
reading: The axe comes down with a 'SAK' (サク) — like a sharp crack splitting the wood.

meaning: A sweet (甘) axe (斤) with two splayed strokes (ハ) — this is the axe that cuts 'this' thing here, pointing at it with its blade.
reading: You point at 'this' sweet (甘) thing and say 'SHE' (シ) — like 'she' is right here, not there.

meaning: A lid sits on a stand-up, and a spicy axe cuts a tree — the axe is new, so it cuts the tree fresh.
reading: The axe's 'SHIN' (shiny) blade reflects the new light — 'SHIN'.

meaning: An axe (斤) chops a left-side kata (爿) that has a mouth (口) and a vertical stroke (｜) and a one (一) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) — cutting it all to pieces.
reading: You 'TAKU' (like 'tack' + 'oo') — you tack the wood down, then hack it with the axe.

meaning: An evening (夕) axe (斤) chops rice (米) into dancing (舛) pieces — the sound of water flowing among rocks is the rhythm of the dance.
reading: The dancing (舛) rice (米) flows with a "リン" (rin) like "ring" — the water rings as it hits the rocks.

meaning: An axe (斤) strikes (攵) a piece of wood — you cut it to pieces, hack, chop, and carve ornaments from the splinters.
reading: No reading given — but the axe (斤) goes "chop" — remember the action, not the sound.

meaning: An axe (斤) cuts through a short thread (幺) and a vertical stroke (｜), severing it completely, interrupting the flow.
reading: ダン — Imagine a 'dan' (ダン) of a drumbeat that suddenly stops when the axe severs the thread, cutting off the sound.

meaning: A vertical stroke, two, a crown, ten mouths, and a hand at the side — all under a dotted cliff — you cut through them with a single chop.
reading: You CHOP (チョク) the wood so hard it splits — but here it's just 'cut'.

meaning: A person standing on a direction signpost — the top dot is the person's head, the horizontal line is their outstretched arm pointing, and the bottom hook is the signpost's base. That person is pointing you toward a direction.
reading: ホウ — Imagine a loudspeaker blaring "HO!" as it broadcasts a direction to a crowd, the sound bouncing off the signpost.

meaning: A direction (方) is marked by a hat on top (个) — the hat points to where something is 'at' or 'in' that direction.
reading: オ — Think of 'oh!' (オ) — you point in a direction and say 'Oh, it's over there!' — that's where it is.

meaning: The sweeping stroke (ノ) sweeps over the direction (方) of a to-be (也) person, and you give them alms with your two hands (廾) — actually, the bottom is 乞, so: the sweeping stroke (ノ) points in the direction (方) of a beggar (乞) — you give alms to that beggar.
reading: The sound is シ (shi) — imagine a 'she' (she) who gives alms to every beggar she sees, saying 'she gives, she gives.'

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) and one (一) line, a barb (亅) and a direction (方) — this is a flag that swims freely in the wind, roving wherever the direction points, like a fish with a barbed tail.
reading: The on-reading ヨウ sounds like 'yo' — imagine a swimmer yelling 'Yo!' as he roves freely across a lake, his direction flag flapping behind him.

meaning: Two short strokes on top (并) sit beside a direction (方) — this is the right-hand side of a character, standing at the same time as the left.
reading: The RHS of the character points in a 'BOU' direction — like a bow aiming to the side.

meaning: A flag (尸) with a sweeping stroke (ノ) and an axe (斤) hangs from a direction (方) pole — the one (一) at the top marks it as a banner.
reading: The flag waves with a 'KI' — like the key that unlocks the pole's secret.

meaning: A direction (方) sign made of woollen cloth hangs from an upside-down box (冂) frame, with a 乞-shaped part (乞) as the dangling fringe — this is the woollen cloth itself.
reading: The woollen cloth is sold by the yard, and the merchant shouts 'SEN!' (セン) as he cuts it — 'sen' sounds like 'send' (as in 'send the cloth').

meaning: A direction (方) pole has fur (毛) tied on top, and a 乞-shaped part (乞) hangs below — that fur tassel is on a flag, and the same fur covers a long-haired cow, and an old man's beard is like that fur.
reading: The old man with the long fur beard says 'BOW!' (ボウ) like a bow-legged cowboy — 'bow' is the sound of the tassel swinging.

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) and a direction (方) lead you to the 乞-shaped part (乞) — you beg for directions as you travel on a trip.
reading: You travel on a 'RYO'ad — the road you take, sounding like 'リョ'.

meaning: A dry (干) pole, a tin can (缶) tied to it, a towel (巾) flapping, all held by a direction (方) sign, with an open box enclosure (凵) at the base and a 乞-shaped part (乞) as the tail — this is the flag itself.
reading: The flag flaps with a 'HAI!' (ハイ) sound as it waves — like a sailor shouting 'hi!' to the wind.

meaning: A vertical stroke, a sweeping stroke, a hook, a lid, a katakana-mu, and a stream — the fringes of pearls hang like a stream from the crown, with a hook to hold them.
reading: RYUU — a dragon (RYUU) wears a crown with pearl fringes that sway like a stream as it flies.

meaning: One, a vertical stroke, a dot, ten, a direction, and a day — you announce to the day by pointing in a direction with a ten-stroke banner.
reading: FU — a fan (FU) is waved to announce the start of a festival, with a banner pointing in the direction of the sun.

meaning: The head (疋) is spinning around the direction (方) marker, while the 乞-shaped part (乞) hangs on — everything is in rotation, going around and around.
reading: A centrifuge spins so fast it makes you say 'SEN-sational!' — the whole machine rotates around you.

meaning: Life and a direction with a 乞-shaped part — a flag that praises life, waving in the direction of the wind, with a hook to hold it.
reading: SEI — a saint (SEI) waves a flag to praise life, and the flag points in the direction of the heavens.

meaning: A flag (尸) on a pole (方) with a spoon (匕) tied to it, fluttering in the wind — the romantic image of a banner waving at a festival.
reading: The flag flutters with a soft 'ji' sound as it catches the breeze — think of a gentle 'jee' from the wind.

meaning: A 'direction' (the clan's banner) plus a 'dart' (their weapon) and the '乞-shaped part' (the family's mark) — together they form the tribe that follows that banner.
reading: ゾク — Say 'zoku' — imagine a tribe of 'zoku' warriors who all carry darts and march in one direction, chanting 'ZOKU! ZOKU!'

meaning: A direction (方) pole with a dot (丶) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) on top, held by a pair of legs (儿) over ice (冫) — an embroidered pennant flutters in the cold wind.
reading: The pennant flaps with a 'CHOU' (チョウ) sound — like a flag whipping in a strong gust over the ice.

meaning: A stream (川) of flags (方) hangs from a lid (亠) with a katakana-mu shape (厶) and a 乞-shaped part (乞), each flag counted as a streamer.
reading: Counting flags, you say 'ryuu' (リュウ) — like 'RYU' (dragon) flying with many flag-streamers.

meaning: A sweeping stroke and a barb lean on a large mouth, while a direction waves — the large mouth sways in the direction of the sweeping stroke, charming and tender.
reading: イ — Picture an eel (イ) that sways romantically in the water, its body bending like a sweeping stroke toward a large mouth.

meaning: A sweet (甘) flag with two splayed strokes (ハ) on top, held up by a direction (方) pole, and the 乞-shaped part (乞) flutters at the side — it's a banner waving in the wind.
reading: The flag's 'ki' (キ) sound — imagine a flag that says 'key' on it, and you use that key to unlock a secret banner.

meaning: A lid (亠) covers two short strokes on top (并) and a halberd (戈) — the direction (方) of the day (日) is marked by a standing (立) flag that fastens the pennon.
reading: The flag (旘) waves with a "シ" (shi) like "she" — she fastens the pennon to the pole.

meaning: A direction (方) banner waves over a rice field (田) with rice (米) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) — it's a pennant fluttering in the breeze.
reading: The banner flaps 'HAN' (like 'han' in 'hand') — you hold the banner in your hand.

meaning: A rice field with rice and a direction, plus the 乞-shaped part — this flag waves in the wind, marking the field's edge.
reading: The flag flaps with a 'HAN' sound as it snaps in the breeze.

meaning: A military flag has a vertical pole (｜) with a sweeping cloth (ノ) and two splayed tips (ハ) at the end, three stacked stripes (ヨ) of color, and shows the direction (方) of the wind.
reading: "Yo" like "yo-yo" — picture a soldier tossing a yo-yo shaped like a flag.

meaning: A table (几) with nothing on it, and a right hand (又) sweeping across it to show that nothing is there — the state of not existing.
reading: The sound is ブ (bu). Imagine a ghost saying 'Boo!' — but it's a ghost of nothing, so it's just a faint 'bu' with no body behind it.

meaning: A person has swallowed something wrong — the 'nothing' radical (无) is turned sideways, and the mouth is open, choking and sobbing with no air.
reading: The choking person lets out a weak 'kee' sound, like a squeaky sob — think of a kitten's cry 'ki' stuck in the throat.

meaning: The tusk (牙) has already pierced through the northeast (艮) corner of the calendar — this event happened long ago, so it's already done.
reading: キ — Picture a key (キ) that has already turned in the lock, unlocking a door that was long ago sealed.

meaning: The square is the sun itself — a bright disk with a horizontal line across it, like the horizon. See the sun rising over the horizon, marking the start of a day.
reading: Imagine a giant sun wearing a tiny hat, saying 'NEE-chee' as it bows — the sound of 'ニチ' is like 'knee-chee', and the sun's rays are like knees bending.

meaning: The sun (日) rises above the horizon line (一) — that flat line is the ground, and the sun peeks over it, bringing daybreak.
reading: At dawn, the alarm goes 'TAN!' — like a drumbeat 'tan' that wakes you up.

meaning: A vertical stroke (｜) cuts through a day (日) — that day is now old, gone, part of old times. The stroke marks the boundary between the old day and the new one.
reading: キュウ — Say 'cue you' — like a queue of old friends from old times, each one cues you to remember the former days.

meaning: A day and a spoon — you taste the day's soup with a spoon, and it's delicious, showing its purport.
reading: The delicious taste makes you say 'shi' (she) — she cooks with such relish.

meaning: The ten sits on top of the day. Ten o'clock is early — the day has barely started, so you're fast to get going.
reading: ソウ — Imagine 'sow' (ソウ) — you sow seeds early in the morning, before the day heats up.

meaning: A day inside a wrapping enclosure marks a ten-day period — the season when that product is fresh.
reading: The ten-day season is 'jun' (June) — June is the prime ten-day period for strawberries.

meaning: The day (日) is rising above the nine (九) hills — that's the morning sun peeking over the horizon.
reading: A kyoku (キョク) player drums at dawn, but the rising sun (旭) makes him squint — 'kyoku' sounds like 'kyoku' in 'kyoku' (a Japanese music genre).

meaning: The sun (日) is under a dry (干) line, and a one (一) and ten (十) mark the time. As the sun sets, the dry day turns to dusk.
reading: カン — At dusk, the sky turns a deep orange, like a can (カン) of soda reflecting the sunset.

meaning: The sun (日) beats down on dry (干) ground. The dry sun causes a drought, with no rain in sight.
reading: カン — The drought is so bad you can only find water in a can (カン), and even that is dry.

meaning: The sun (日) rises over a dry (干) field, with a barb (亅) and two (二) lines marking the early hour. The dry land is lit by the dawn.
reading: ク — At dawn, the rooster goes "Coo-coo" (クク), waking you to the first light.

meaning: A lid (亠) sits on a mountain (山), and a vertical stroke (｜) pierces through it into the day (日) below — this marks the time, season, era, and age as the sun moves.
reading: The ジ reading sounds like 'gee' — picture an old clock saying 'gee, time flies' as the mountain shadow moves across the day.

meaning: The king (王) stands in the bright day (日) — his reign is flourishing and vigorous, full of beauty and success.
reading: The king shouts 'OU!' (オウ) as he raises his sword to the sun — a triumphant cry of flourishing power.

meaning: The day (日) is wrapped in a sentence (文) — that's the autumn sky, where the light writes a story across the heavens.
reading: The ビン reading sounds like 'bin' — imagine throwing a bin into the autumn sky, and it floats there, catching the orange light.

meaning: The day (日) is covered by a sentence (文) that is soft and smooth — this makes the character gentle and affable, like a calm, kind word.
reading: The ビン reading sounds like 'bin' — picture a gentle person handing you a bin full of soft pillows, smiling affably.

meaning: A dot (丶) and a one (一) sit under a wrapping enclosure (勹) that holds a two (二) — all above the day (日), this is sunlight breaking through, used in a personal name.
reading: The イン reading sounds like 'in' — imagine sunlight streaming 'in' through a window, warming a baby named with this character.

meaning: The day rises above the seal, lifting it up — a rising motion.
reading: Imagine a seal stamping a rising sun, and the sun shouts 'KOH!' as it pops up.

meaning: A person (人) leans under a cliff (厂) as the day (日) slides down behind it — the sun is going down.
reading: ショク — The sun's decline is like a shock (ショク) of cold air at sunset.

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) and a right hand (又) stretch out wide under the day (日) — everything is big and expansive.
reading: ハン — A big hand (ハン) reaches out to grab the whole sky.

meaning: Under the DAY, a group of COMPARE-like insects (like ants) are all descendants of one elder brother — they all come from the same queen.
reading: コン — Imagine a CON (convict) elder brother sitting on a log, surrounded by his insect descendants, all bowing to him.

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) rises up like a sunbeam from the day (日), while two hands (廾) lift a ten (十) — all together they rise up into the sky.
reading: The sun rises with a 'SHOW!' (ショウ) as it climbs above the horizon.

meaning: The direction (方) of the day (日) is upward — bright dawn appears where the sun first shows its face.
reading: ホウ — At dawn, the sun says 'ho!' (ホウ) as it pops over the horizon.

meaning: A large day with a one and a two stretched across it — the vast, big sky.
reading: The big sky is so wide you say 'KOH!' in awe, like a deep breath of open air.

meaning: Two days stacked on top of each other — the sun shines down twice as bright, making everything prosperous and clear. The lower day is the ground, the upper day is the sky, both glowing.
reading: ショウ — Imagine a bright, prosperous festival where a SHOW (ショウ) of fireworks lights up two days in a row, each burst clearer than the last.

meaning: The month (月) and the day (日) together — both shine bright, lighting up the sky. The month and day are both bright lights.
reading: メイ — The bright month and day together shout 'MEI!' (like 'may') — a brilliant light that says 'may I shine?'

meaning: The family name is written on the day, but the day is dark — evening falls.
reading: In the dark evening, you call 'KON!' for your family name to come home.

meaning: A hat on top (个) sits over the day (日), and a dot (丶) marks the spot — the day is so bright that even the hat casts a sharp, clear shadow.
reading: The bright day makes you squint and say 'kin' — like the sharp 'kin' of a bell ringing in clear light.

meaning: A day (日) with a sweeping stroke (ノ) and a 'not' (勿) wrapped in a wrapping enclosure (勹) — it's easy because you don't have to work hard, just a simple sweep.
reading: エキ — Think of an easy test where the answer is 'EASY' (エキ) — you just write 'EKI' on the paper and it's done.

meaning: A vertical stroke (｜) and one (一) and two (二) sit above a day (日). These stacked lines are like old calendar marks — counting days long past, once upon a time.
reading: You flip back to an old diary page and see 'SEK-ki' (セキ) written — a nostalgic sound from antiquity.

meaning: The axe (斤) chops the day (日) open — dawn splits the darkness, revealing the early morning.
reading: At dawn, the axe (斤) hits the day (日) with a 'kin' — like the crisp sound of metal striking wood at first light.

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) over one (一) line, then a day (日) wrapped in a not (勿) with a wrapping enclosure (勹) — the sun is open, but not fully, like a day half-wrapped in clouds.
reading: The on-reading ヨウ sounds like 'yo' — picture the sun saying 'Yo!' as it opens up from behind a cloud, its rays spreading like a wrapping enclosure.

meaning: A stooping figure (夂) uses a divining rod (卜) to point at the day (日) and say (曰) "you and me, we two" — a dual pronoun for the pair of us.
reading: The sun (日) says (曰) "サン" like the English "sun" — and this is a dual pronoun, so think of the sun and moon as "we two" shining together.

meaning: A person (人) stands under an upside-down box (冂) with a one (一) on top, and the day (日) shines through — bright, luminous, and clear.
reading: The bright day (日) makes you say "ヘイ!" like "hey!" — you squint and shout because it's so luminous.

meaning: Life (生) and day (日) combine: a star is a spot of light that lives in the day sky too, like a dot or mark on the sun.
reading: The sound is セイ — say 'say!' as you point at a bright star in the night sky, a spot of light.

meaning: The sun (日) shines on a large (大) surface under a crown (冖), and a sweeping stroke (ノ) of light reflects back at you — that's a reflection.
reading: エイ — Imagine a movie projector showing a film, and the screen says 'A' (エイ) — the projection is the reflection of light.

meaning: A mysterious (玄) short thread (幺) hangs from a lid (亠) over the day (日), stretching it out — a long day, extended and relaxed.
reading: The long day (日) feels like "ケン" — think of Ken who takes a long, relaxed nap under the mysterious thread.

meaning: The day (日) is wearing a hat on top (个) and a マ-shaped stroke (マ) like a bright crown — that's sunshine pouring down from above.
reading: レイ — Imagine a sunny day where a **ray** of light (レイ sounds like 'ray') shoots straight down from the マ-shaped stroke onto the day (日).

meaning: A person (人) stands under a large (大) day (日) with one (一) and two (二) lines of soil (土) — that’s springtime, when the soil warms and the day grows large.
reading: Picture a spring day where you shout “SHOON!” (シュン) as you jump into a puddle — “shoon” rhymes with “moon” and contains the sound “shun” (シュン).

meaning: A tree (木) with two splayed strokes (ハ) and a lid (亠) covers the day (日) — dark and foolish, because you can't see clearly under the tree's shadow.
reading: In the dark (日 hidden), you feel "マイ" like "my" — "my" foolish mistake, stumbling in the gloom.

meaning: A vertical stroke (｜) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) cross over the day (日) — that's the previous day, yesterday, already gone.
reading: サク — Imagine 'sack' (like a burlap sack) filled with yesterday's leftovers, thrown out the door.

meaning: Two hands (廾) lift a katakana-mu shape (厶) up to the day (日) — delighted, pleased, as if offering something joyful to the sun.
reading: The delighted hands (廾) clap "ヘン" like "hen" — a happy hen clucking with joy in the daylight.

meaning: The sun (日) is wrapped in a warm blanket (勹), and it opens its mouth (口) to breathe out gentle heat — that's warm.
reading: The sun's warm breath makes a 'ku' sound like a soft coo — 'ク' (ku) as in 'coo'.

meaning: At dusk, a flag (尸) hangs limp over a family name (氏) written on the ground, while the sun (日) sinks below the horizon — all is dark and confused.
reading: At dusk, you feel 'kon' — like 'con' in 'confused' — as the world gets dark and stupid.

meaning: A mouth (口) and a sword (刀) next to a day (日) — the day shines so bright that even the sword's edge glitters and the mouth opens in awe.
reading: ショウ — Show (ショウ) off the bright shining day — it's so bright you want to show it to everyone.

meaning: The day sun shines down on a head that is bent in respect — this is exactly right, this is justice.
reading: Imagine a judge saying 'Zeh!' (ゼ) as she stamps 'just so' on a verdict, the head bowing in agreement.

meaning: The sun (日) stops (止) right above a line (一) — this is 'this' thing, right here, like a summer marker.
reading: This is 'ze' — like 'ze' in 'zero' — the point where summer starts and stops.

meaning: The sun (日) stands up (立) tall — its light is so bright and dazzling it blinds you.
reading: The bright light makes you go 'iku' — like 'eek!' — as you shield your eyes.

meaning: A large (大) dart (矢) with a sweeping stroke (ノ) points at the sun (日) as it tilts down in the west — the declining sun.
reading: The sun tilts with a 'tetsu' — like 'tetsu' in 'tetsudo' (iron road) — as it falls toward the horizon.

meaning: The sun (日) is sealed (卩) into a tiny cluster — those are the Pleiades, a small bright group of stars.
reading: The Pleiades shine like a 'subaru' — the car brand's logo is six stars — 'すばる' (subaru).

meaning: A day passes under a flag, and a spoon is laid beside it — the two sides have become intimate enough to share a meal, reconciling their differences.
reading: Imagine a spoon and a flag both stuck in the same day's calendar page, and you say 'jitsu' (like 'jeets') as you pull them out — they've become so close they come out together.

meaning: Water (水) flows over a day (日) that has a dot (丶) on top — the water reflects the long, clear daylight, stretching the day out endlessly.
reading: チョウ — Picture a 'choir' (チョウ) singing all day long — their voices carry through the long, clear daylight.

meaning: A day (日) inside a say (曰) box, with a dish (皿) below — you put the prisoner's food in the dish, and the say-box tells you when to feed them each day.
reading: オン — Think of an 'on' (オン) switch — you turn it on to feed the prisoner, and the dish fills with food.

meaning: The day (日) is so bright it shines like a glorious sun — no parts needed, just pure brilliance filling the sky.
reading: ヘイ — Imagine a 'hey' (ヘイ) shout of awe — you look up at the brilliant, glorious day and say 'hey, that's bright!'

meaning: The day is split by a flag (尸) with a dot (丶) on top, marking the exact middle — that's daytime, noon.
reading: At noon, you chew (チュウ) on your lunch slowly, like a cow chewing cud.

meaning: The day stretches out under a dotted cliff, and the katakana-mu shape floats in the empty sky — the view is wide and empty.
reading: You stand under the dotted cliff and see the wide empty land, and you say 'kou' (like 'co-') as in 'co-wide' — the space is so vast it's just 'kou'.

meaning: The day (日) starts with a pair of legs (儿) stepping over ice (冫) — this is a proper name for someone who rises early, like the morning sun.
reading: The proper name is 'Chō' (チョウ) — imagine a butterfly (chō) fluttering over the ice at dawn.

meaning: The day (日) is measured by a measurement (寸) of soil (土) falling through an hourglass — that's time, hour by hour.
reading: The clock says 'ジ' (ji) — imagine a big clock that goes 'ji-ji-ji' as the hands move, like a ticking sound.

meaning: One (一) day (日) you hold esteem (尚) high and stand on a pair of legs (儿) — the light is so clear you can see everything.
reading: The clear light makes you shout 'KOH' (like 'co' in 'code') — 'KOH, I can see clearly now!'

meaning: The day is held up by a pair of legs under an esteem-worthy roof, showing everything clearly in the light.
reading: The clear light makes a 'ko' sound like a crow's call at dawn.

meaning: One (一) day (日) of sun — the light of the sun dries things out, so this means 'light of the sun' and 'to dry in the sun'.
reading: The sun's light is so strong it makes you squint and say 'KEN!' (ケン) — like 'ken' as in 'ken' (know) the sun is hot.

meaning: Under the day, two ones and a katakana-mu shape stack up like a ladder — you climb them to advance upward toward the sun.
reading: Shin (as in 'shin' guard) — you advance by kicking a shin guard up the ladder of ones and mu shapes.

meaning: One (一) day (日) you take a step forward — that's the advance, moving from today into tomorrow.
reading: You advance so fast you leave a 'SHIN' (shin) — like kicking your shin against a rock as you rush ahead.

meaning: The day (日) is inside an upside-down box (冂) with a mouth (口) below — at noon, the sun is trapped in a box, and the mouth calls out for the moment to pass.
reading: Shō (as in 'show') — at noon, the sun puts on a show inside the upside-down box, with the mouth as the audience.

meaning: Under a roof (宀), a woman (女) watches the day (日) — she stays quiet and late, waiting for the sun to set.
reading: An (as in 'an' as in 'an apple') — the woman under the roof says 'an' softly, quiet and late, as the sun sets.

meaning: The sun (日) beats down from the west (西) — you bleach and expose cloth by airing it out in that western sun.
reading: Sai (as in 'sigh') — you sigh as you bleach the cloth, hanging it west to dry in the sun.

meaning: A day (日) with a hat on top (个) and a mouth (口) below, all under a dot (丶) — the first pale light before the sun fully rises, pre-dawn.
reading: In the pre-dawn, you hear a distant 'kan' — like a temple bell calling the morning.

meaning: The day (日) is wrapped in a flag (尸) and a spoon (匕) — as the flag droops at night, it's late and evening falls.
reading: At night, you say 'ban' — like the sound of a gong closing the day.

meaning: The day (日) has eyes (目) that see (見) — when the sun's rays peek through, that's sunlight appearing.
reading: Sunlight breaks through with a 'ken' — like a camera lens clicking open to capture the light.

meaning: A day (日) with a bow (弓) and two short strokes (并) on top — the bow is drawn to shoot an insect, but it's just a harmless bug on a sunny day.
reading: The insect buzzes with a 'kon' — like a small drumbeat in the grass.

meaning: A day (日) with a brush (聿) and a one (一) stroke — the brush paints the daylight across the sky, marking the daytime.
reading: In the middle of the day, you hear 'chuu' — like the long, drawn-out sound of a noon bell.

meaning: A sweeping stroke sweeps over a one and a towel, all under the day — the towel is hung out to dry in the sun, so the day dries it out completely.
reading: キ — The day (日) is so hot it makes a key (キ) melt, drying out everything it touches.

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) cuts across the day (日) while a halberd (戈) stands by — the sky is clear, so the sun's light is sharp and unobstructed.
reading: Sei (as in 'say') — you say 'sei' clearly, like the clear day with the halberd cutting through the haze.

meaning: A vertical stroke, a dot, and ten sit above a month, and the day is beside a utilize. In the late afternoon, you utilize the last hour of daylight to finish ten tasks.
reading: In the late afternoon, you 'ho' (ホ) — like 'hoe' — the soil, but here the parts are a vertical stroke, dot, ten, month, and utilize, all under the day.

meaning: An axe and a hand at the side are under the day. The day's light is so bright it shines like an axe blade, and the hand at the side shields your eyes.
reading: The star's light is 'se' (セイ) — imagine saying 'say' as you point at the shining stars, with the axe and hand at the side under the day.

meaning: A mouth and a day meet — when you speak clearly in the daylight, your words are clear and bright.
reading: ゴ — In the clear light, you say 'go' (ゴ) to the darkness, making everything clear.

meaning: The day shines over a place with a one, a vertical stroke, a dot, and a ten — this is the bright province of Anhui, where the sun is strong.
reading: カン — The province is so bright you need a can (カン) of sunscreen to stay safe under the day.

meaning: The day (日) is hidden behind a mother (母) who says 'do not' (毋) and a 乞-shaped part (乞) — the day disappears into darkness, and the month's end is dark.
reading: Kai (as in 'kite') — the dark day disappears like a kite lost in the night sky, with the mother saying 'do not' fly it.

meaning: A sweeping stroke over a mouth and soil, all under the day — the pure bright sun dries the soil, making it clean and bright.
reading: コウ — The bright sun makes the soil glow like a ko (コウ) — a small, pure light in the field.

meaning: The sign of the dragon (辰) is wrapped in a garment (衣) that flaps in the day (日) — that's how you know it's early morning, when the dragon's robe catches the first light.
reading: シン — Imagine a 'shin' (shin bone) poking out of the garment at dawn, glowing in the morning light.

meaning: The day (日) is wrapped in an excuse (免) — the excuse has a pair of legs (儿) and a wrapping enclosure (勹) — and as the excuse runs off, nightfall (晩) arrives.
reading: バン — Picture a “ban” (like a ban on daylight) — the sun is banned, and night falls.

meaning: A lid sits on top of a person who is ten days old, and the day itself is the first birthday — the child has just completed one full turn of the sun.
reading: サイ — Imagine a child's first birthday cake with a big 'サイ' (sigh) written on it, and everyone lets out a relieved sigh that the year is done.

meaning: A vertical stroke (｜) and two (二) lines sit above a day (日), with two short strokes on top (并) — the sun shines widely, universally, over everything. The strokes spread out like rays.
reading: フ — "Foo" (フ) — think of "foo" as a universal placeholder — this kanji means universal, so it's the "foo" of all things.

meaning: A lid (亠) covers a little (小) day (日) with a mouth (口) below — picture a small sun (day) under a lid, with a mouth open in awe at the scenery. That's the view you see.
reading: You look at the scenery and say 'KEI' (ケイ) — like 'kay' as in 'okay, that's a nice view,' a calm acknowledgment.

meaning: An axe (斤) chops a tree (木) into clear, split planks under the bright day (日) — the grain becomes clearly visible.
reading: セキ — Picture a clear glass of 'セキ' (sake) — the liquid is so transparent you can see the tree rings at the bottom of the glass.

meaning: The axe (斤) has chopped down the tree (木), and now the day (日) is clear and fair — you can see everything white and bright, and you can discriminate every branch on the ground.
reading: The clear day lets you see a 'sexy' (セキ) landscape — everything is fair and white in the sun.

meaning: The day (日) is clear after the blue (青) sky shows through, with the soil (土) and two (二) clouds parting under a lid (亠) — the month (月) feels bright and clear.
reading: セイ — Imagine saying "SAY" to the clear sky: "Say, what a clear day!" The sound 'se-i' is in 'say' (pronounced 'sei').

meaning: Three days (日) stacked and side by side — each one a facet of a crystal, sparkling as light hits from every angle, clear as three suns.
reading: The crystal sparkles with a 'shou' (ショウ) — like 'show' — as it catches the light and puts on a little display.

meaning: The day (日) is measured by a stooping figure (夂) who uses a divining rod (卜) and a mouth (口) to mark the shadows of sun on a sundial — this is time itself.
reading: キ — Imagine a key (キ) that you turn to set the sundial's shadow, marking the time of day.

meaning: A dart (矢) of knowledge flies from the mouth (口) into the day (日) — that's wisdom and intellect.
reading: The wise one says "CHI" — like "cheese!" — as the dart of knowledge hits the day.

meaning: Put a lid (亠) over the little (小) clothes, and let the day (日) shine through the mouth (口) of the drying rack — you air dry them in the sun.
reading: You 'ryo' (リョウ) the laundry — like 'rio' in Rio de Janeiro, where the sun always dries things fast.

meaning: Ten (十) rays of day (日) rise over a pair of legs (儿) and two hands (廾) — at daybreak, the sun's first light stretches out like limbs.
reading: ギョウ — At dawn, a rooster cries 'gyo' (ギョウ) — a sharp, clear call that breaks the night.

meaning: The day (日) is un- (非) — it is separated from the sun, so this ghost kanji is a lonely, disconnected day.
reading: The separated day feels like a 'hi' (ヒ) — a sigh of loneliness, as the sun leaves.

meaning: Warm weather comes when the day (日) is under a roof (宀) with two (二) lines of heat and one (一) sun, making it cozy.
reading: The warm weather makes you say 'ken' (ケン) — like 'KEN' (a warm, sunny day in a cabin).

meaning: The day (日) is free because a right hand (又) is resting — no work, just spare time.
reading: When you have spare time, you say 'ka' (カ) as in 'car' — you drive your car to relax on your day off.

meaning: A halo or corona forms around the day (日) when a crown (冖) covers a car (車) — the light fades (ぼか.す) into a ring.
reading: The halo fades with an 'un' (ウン) — like 'UN' (a soft, blurry 'un' of light around the sun).

meaning: A car (車) is parked under a crown (冖) that floats above a day (日) — the whole scene is so bright that the car's metal reflects the light, making it shine.
reading: The shine is so strong it feels like a key (キ) turning in a lock — click, and the light floods out.

meaning: A family name (氏) is written on a flag (尸) that gets struck (攵) by the day (日) — the flag stays strong and robust through all that abuse.
reading: ビン — Imagine a strong, tough wrestler named 'Bin' (ビン) who can't be knocked down, even when the day (日) strikes (攵) him with a flag (尸).

meaning: A large (大) dotted tent (癶) is set up far from the day (日) — so the tent is in opposition, distant and separated from the sun's light.
reading: ケイ — Picture a 'K' (ケイ) shaped crack in the ground that separates you from the day (日) — you're distant, in opposition, on the other side.

meaning: A person (人) wrapped in a wrapping enclosure (勹) under the day (日) gets too hot — that's sun-stroke, collapsing from the heat.
reading: エツ — 'Etsu' (エツ) sounds like 'etch' — imagine etching a line in the sand with your finger as you faint from sun-stroke, the day (日) beating down.

meaning: The day (日) is under a crown (冖) and grass on top (艾), with a large (大) person (人) inside an upside-down box (冂) — the sun begins to decline, and the person's reflection is cast in the water.
reading: The declining sun makes the water 'ei' (エイ) — like 'aye' (a pirate's 'aye') as you see your reflection in the sea.

meaning: The tanned leather (韋) is held up to the day (日) with a mouth (口) open in awe — the bright shining of the sun makes the leather glow.
reading: イ — Say 'ee' (イ) like a squeal of delight when you see the sun's bright shining — 'Ee! It's so bright!'

meaning: The old man (老) sits under the day (日) — the summer heat (暑) makes him sweat and fan himself.
reading: ショ — Say “show” — the old man shows you how hot it is by wiping his brow.

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) and one (一) line form a claw (爪) that holds the day (日) — the claw's warmth radiates like a sun-heated hand.
reading: ダン — Think of a warm DANce floor — the heat from the day (日) makes you feel cozy and warm.

meaning: The sound (音) of the day (日) is hidden behind a stand up (立) — when the sun stands up, the sound fades into darkness and shade.
reading: アン — In the dark (暗), you can't see, so you say 'AHN?' (アン) to ask where the light went.

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) and a one (一) sit above the day (日), while a wrapping enclosure (勹) holds a 'not' (勿) — at sunrise, the sun rises over the horizon, not yet fully wrapped in light.
reading: ヨウ — 'Yo' (ヨウ) like 'yo!' — at sunrise you shout 'Yo! The sun is up!' as the day (日) peeks over the horizon.

meaning: A day under a crown with two splayed strokes and a lid — the crown covers the day, making it dark, as the two splayed strokes block the light.
reading: メイ — Imagine a may (メイ) day that suddenly goes dark when a crown-shaped cloud covers the sun.

meaning: The tall (高) day (日) under an upside-down box (冂) with a lid (亠) and a mouth (口) — the sun rises high and bright, so the day is at daybreak, brilliant and clear.
reading: At daybreak, the sun is so bright it feels like a KO-wboy (コウ) squinting into the light — the KO of コウ is the sharp, clear ring of dawn.

meaning: A vertical stroke and one line stretch through a day, a rice field, and a 'not' — the day stretches out long, not ending.
reading: You stretch your arms wide and say 'CHOU' (チョウ) — like 'chow' for a long, lazy meal that stretches on.

meaning: A day (日) is marked under a cliff (厂) where hemp (麻) hangs from a dotted cliff (广) over a tree (木) — this is the calendar that tracks the days.
reading: You flip the calendar page and it makes a 'レキ' sound like a quick 'rek' of a clock ticking.

meaning: An axe (斤) cutting a car (車) in half on a day (日) — that's only temporary, a while, a moment, but it feels like a long time.
reading: ザン — The axe makes a "ZAN!" (ザン) sound as it slices the car, and you wait a long moment for the pieces to fall.

meaning: The large (大) day (日) is covered by grass on top (艾) — as evening falls, the grass shadows the sun, ending the season's light.
reading: ボ — Imagine a 'bo' (ボ) — a bow — at twilight, the sun sets like a bowstring releasing, ending the day's livelihood.

meaning: A day (日) spent with a mouth (口) under grass on top (艾) and a stone (石) — you get intimate and close, approaching each other in a hidden grassy spot.
reading: On a close day, you 'jitsu' (ジツ) your way into someone's heart — imagine saying 'jitsu' as you lean in for a hug.

meaning: The sun (日) blazes down on water (水) in a well (井) — suddenly it boils over, a violent outburst of steam and bubbles that raves and frets against the lid.
reading: A BOA constrictor (ボウ) bursts out of the well in a rage, thrashing and hissing — that's the outburst you can't ignore.

meaning: A day (日) with a ten (十) and a large (大) leather (革) sheet held by two hands (廾) — you dry the leather by exposing it to the sun, and a mouth (口) cries out for water.
reading: To dry something, you 'kan' (カン) it — imagine a can of sun-dried tomatoes, each one a dry 'kan' in the heat.

meaning: The large (大) sun (日) pushes aside a little (小) lid (亠) and two short strokes on top (并) of clouds, making the sky clear.
reading: Imagine a clear sky where you can see a row (ryou) of birds flying in formation.

meaning: An old bird flies into a crowded day — the sun rises and the bird's shadow is cast, marking the start of a new day.
reading: The sunrise is so bright it feels like a 'sen' (セン) — a coin — glowing in the sky.

meaning: A day (日) under a lid (亠) with a mouth (口) and a little (小) — the little mouth opens wide, and the day is bright, clear, and shining.
reading: The bright sky makes you 'kei' (ケイ) with joy — imagine saying 'kei!' as you squint at the sun.

meaning: A towel hangs over an esteem-worthy box, with two short strokes and a strike on top — the setting sun is being struck down by the day's end, wrapped in a towel to cool it.
reading: The setting sun looks like a 'pet' (ヘツ) being put to bed, wrapped in a towel.

meaning: A child opens its mouth under a lid, while a strike hits the sun's rays — the sunrise is so strong it wakes the child with a shout.
reading: The sun's rays at dawn sound like a 'ton' (トン) — a drumbeat — waking everyone up.

meaning: A day (日) with two short strokes on top (并) under a crown (冖), a gentleman (士) and beans (豆) — the beans and gentleman are hidden by a stormy, cloudy mist, making everything dim.
reading: The stormy sky makes you say 'ei' (エイ) like a groan — imagine 'ei...' as the clouds roll in and dim the day.

meaning: A spoon and nothing sit next to a white day, with one line reaching toward the northeast — the day extends its reach to include everything, and along with it, all things are connected.
reading: The day reaches out and says 'ki' (キ) — like a key — unlocking all connections.

meaning: A day (日) where grass on top (艾) grows over a vertical stroke (｜) and two horizontal lines (一, 二) — the grass is flourishing, and the day shines with life.
reading: The flourishing shine makes you say 'YO! (ヨウ) look at that glow!' — the YO of ヨウ is the exclamation you make when the light bursts through.

meaning: A lid covers two short strokes, and a strike hits the day — the calendar is marked by strikes on each day, recording the era.
reading: The calendar pages flip with a 'reki' (レキ) — like a 'reck' (wreck) — as time crashes forward.

meaning: Rain (雨) falls on two (二) days (日) with a katakana-mu shape (厶) — the sky clouds up, giving cloudy weather.
reading: The clouds say "DON" (ドン) — like a heavy drum "DON" as they roll in and block the sun.

meaning: The day (日) stands up (立) in the ri (里) fields, but the sun is still below the horizon — it's twilight just before sunrise.
reading: The on-reading トウ sounds like 'toe' — imagine stubbing your toe in the dark twilight before sunrise.

meaning: The soil (土) and day (日) are under a pair of legs (儿) — dawn is when you stand on the earth and start the day.
reading: The on-reading キョウ sounds like 'kyo' as in 'Kyoto' — picture dawn breaking over Kyoto's temples.

meaning: A dot (丶) and a spoon (匕) sit under a katakana-mu shape (厶) with a short thread (幺) — the home country (邦) of the day (日) is white (白) and once upon a time, it was a period of time.
reading: The white (白) day (日) once upon a time had a "キョウ" (kyou) like "kyoto" — the old capital of home country (邦).

meaning: A heart is hidden under a crown, with a claw and a day above, and a stooping figure below — all blurred together, so the heart's shape is not clear. The whole scene is dark and indistinct.
reading: The 'eye' in the middle of the kanji is like a dim eye that can't see clearly — say 'eye' and it's 'アイ' (ai), as in 'I can't see in the dark.'

meaning: The day (日) breaks as an old man (老) buys (買) the first light — dawn arrives when the old man's purchase of the sun's rays is complete.
reading: ショ — At dawn, a 'show' (ショ) begins — the sun rises like a spotlight, revealing the daybreak stage.

meaning: A day under a crown, with grass on top and a pig below — the pig's shadow makes the daylight dim, so everything is darkness.
reading: モウ — 'Mow' (モウ) the grass, but the pig's darkness makes it hard to see what you're cutting.

meaning: A day (日) with a sweeping stroke (ノ) and two short strokes on top (并) shows four dots at the bottom (杰) like a car (車) driving into twilight, the sun setting.
reading: クン — The twilight 'coon' (クン) — a raccoon — sits on a car at sunset, watching the sky darken.

meaning: Three stacked strokes sit above a day, and an old bird perches on the day — this bird marks each day of the week by its song.
reading: ヨウ — Say 'yo!' (ヨウ) to the old bird each morning — it sings a different tune for each weekday, and you greet it with a cheerful 'yo!'.

meaning: A vertical stroke holds up a one, but water and day are both under a two splayed strokes — imagine hanging wet laundry out on a line under the sun, the water dripping and the day's light bleaching the cloth white.
reading: The sun bleaches everything to a pale 'BAKU' — like a loud, sudden 'BAKU!' sound as the fabric snaps in the wind.

meaning: Under a dotted cliff, a yellow rice field stretches wide, with a day and two splayed strokes on top — the field is so vast it feels worthless, empty, and open to the sky.
reading: The wide, empty field echoes with a long 'KOU' — like a hollow call across the barren land.

meaning: The sun is a king (王) of the day (日) who wears a sheep (羊) as a hat with two short strokes (并) on top, and carries a barb (亅) and a halberd (戈) as weapons.
reading: "Gi" like "gee" — you say "Gee, that sun is hot!" as it shines.

meaning: At twilight, a one (一) horizontal line is the horizon, with a vertical stroke (｜) and a hook (乙) of a dragon (竜) standing up (立) in a rice field (田) between day (日) and month (月) — all vague and dim.
reading: "Row" — row a boat in the dim twilight, but you can't see clearly.

meaning: A vertical stroke (｜) pierces a garment (衣) under a lid (亠) and a day (日) — that day is earlier, before the garment was torn, so it's the former time.
reading: ノウ — Imagine 'now' (ノウ) is the present, but this hook shows a 'no' (ノウ) — a big 'no' sign over the earlier day, marking it as before.

meaning: A deer (鹿) stands on a dotted cliff (广) under the day (日) sun, while a spoon (匕) and compare (比) mark the spot where you spread cloth to dry — the whole scene is exposed to the sun.
reading: The sun is so strong it makes the deer's antlers sizzle — 'sa-i' (サイ) like the hiss of hot air.

meaning: A day (日) that is squashed and flat — like a record of what was said on that day. It's the reason or pretext given for something, a historical 'say'.
reading: The sound is エツ (etsu). Picture a person saying 'Et tu?' — accusing a friend of betrayal, using a pretext as their reason.

meaning: A vertical stroke pierces the day, bending it into a crooked shape — that's how you get a bend, and also a melody that twists and turns.
reading: Imagine a DJ spinning a record that gets bent, and the crowd shouts 'KYOKU!' as the music warps.

meaning: A day (日) is hooked by a hook stroke (乙) — you pull and tug it along, like dragging a heavy sun across the sky.
reading: エイ — Imagine saying "AYE" (エイ) as you tug a rope — "Aye, pull!" — that's the jerk motion.

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) over a one (一) and a day (日) inside a rice field (田) — as the day grows late, the field watch continues, and you sit up through the night.
reading: コウ — Picture a 'cow' (コウ) that refuses to sleep, standing in the rice field at night, keeping watch as the hours grow late.

meaning: A piling (弋) is being dragged along by a say (曰) — the say is tied to the piling and pulls it, trailing behind like a heavy load.
reading: The piling is towed by a giant 'eel' (エイ) that wraps around it and drags it through the mud.

meaning: A day, a spoon, a flag, and a say — all wrapped in a wrapping enclosure — you ask 'why' are these things bundled together?
reading: You see the wrapped bundle and ask 'katsu' (like 'cat's zoo') — 'why is a cat's zoo in there?' — the 'katsu' sound is your 'why'.

meaning: A day (日) under a brush (聿) — you spend the day with the brush, writing.
reading: ショ — Picture a writer shouting “SHOW!” as they hold up their finished page — the brush writes a showpiece. “Show” sounds like ショ.

meaning: A vertical stroke (｜) and a one (一) stand before a day (日) — this is the office where officials track the day's work, and comrades gather.
reading: The official's office is full of 'sou' (ソウ) — imagine a 'soul' (sou) signing papers at the desk.

meaning: The day (日) is long and wide, and you buy (買) something with a right hand (又) — the scene stretches out beautifully and broadly.
reading: マン — 'Man' (マン) spreads his arms wide to show how vast and beautiful the view is.

meaning: A rice field (田) under the day (日) has two short strokes on top (并) — those strokes mark a time that was once, before, formerly, when the field was different.
reading: ソウ — Think 'so-oh' (ソウ) — 'so, oh, that was once before' — like a sigh remembering a former time.

meaning: The day (日) is covered by two splayed strokes (ハ) like a lid — this was once before, formerly, a day that has already passed.
reading: You've seen this day 'so' (ソウ) many times — like 'so' in 'so long ago' — it was once, before.

meaning: A person (人) and a large (大) thing under two (二) and a day (日) with a lid (亠) — you exchange the old lid for a new one, substituting it after a day's work.
reading: タイ — 'Tie' (タイ) — you tie a new string to replace the old one, exchanging it.

meaning: The ear (耳) is the most sensitive part — it catches the utmost sound, while the sun (日) and a right hand (又) reach for the extreme edge of the day.
reading: Think of a contest where the winner is the 'sai' — like 'sai' in 'sai-lor' — the most extreme sailor who sails the farthest.

meaning: A pair of legs (儿) stands under an upside-down box (冂) that holds a mouth (口) and a box (囗) — but the mouth is silent and the box is empty. This odd, uncertain setup makes you think: 'if, supposing, nevertheless' — all words of doubt and condition.
reading: Imagine a person saying 'if' while shrugging — the sound is 'so' (as in 'so what?'). The hook: 'SO, supposing it rains, we stay inside.'

meaning: A hat on top (个) sits over a buy (買) sign, and the day (日) is the meeting time — people gather for a party or association to buy and meet under that hat.
reading: カイ — 'Kai' (カイ) sounds like 'kite' — imagine a kite flying over a meeting (party) where everyone gathers to buy things, the day (日) bright above.

meaning: A person (人) wrapped in a wrapping enclosure (勹) with a katakana-mu shape (厶) on top of soil (土) under a day (日) — the brave one stands firm on the ground, facing the sun, unshaken.
reading: The brave one leaps over the soil with a 'KETSU! (ケツ)' — like a warrior's battle cry, short and sharp, the KETSU of ケツ is the sound of courage.

meaning: This is a crescent moon with a line across it, like a window showing the moon at night. The shape is the moon itself, hanging in the sky.
reading: Imagine a moon made of cheese, and a mouse takes a bite — it squeaks 'GETS' as it nibbles. 'ゲツ' sounds like 'gets', and the moon is what the mouse gets.

meaning: A sweeping stroke cuts across the one and the month. The month has the stroke — it possesses it, like a calendar that has all the days.
reading: ユウ — Say 'you' (ユウ) — you have the month in your hand, so you possess it.

meaning: Two months (月) side by side — like two friends who have spent many months together, so they are companions.
reading: You call your friend 'HO-U' (ホウ) — like 'ho!' to get their attention across the street.

meaning: A right hand (又) pulls a seal (卩) off a month (月) — the seal is like a label on clothing, and you obey the rules of what to wear, so this is clothing and also obeying.
reading: フク — Picture a 'fuku' (フク) — a fluffy coat — you put it on and it makes you feel like a 'fuku' (good luck) charm, so you wear it and obey the dress code.

meaning: A vertical stroke cuts through the month, and a mountain rises beside it — the thin sliver of a new moon is like a mountain peak barely visible in the dark month sky.
reading: ヒ — The new moon is so thin it's just a 'hee' of light, like a tiny whisper of a crescent.

meaning: A dot and a sweeping stroke sit on a pair of legs, all under an ice-cold month. The month is being sacrificed — it's frozen, offered up on those legs.
reading: The month is being sacrificed with a loud 'chō' — like a chef's knife chopping through ice, 'chōp'.

meaning: The month begins with two short strokes on top of a left hand — that first day is a conjunction, when the moon and sun align in the north sky.
reading: On the first day of the month, you 'sak' open a calendar — the sound of tearing paper is 'saku'.
