meaning: A mouth, a dart, and the 乞-shaped part all sit on a tree — this kokuji tree is so distinctive that you can name it just by its odd parts, like a nagī tree.
reading: なぎ — The evergreen tree sways in the wind, and the sound it makes is 'なぎ' (nah-gee) — like a gentle 'naggy' whisper from the leaves.

meaning: A large tree with two short strokes on top and a power underneath — imagine a giant wickerwork basket woven from the tree's branches, with the two strokes as the basket's lid handles and the power as the strong base.
reading: ケン — Ken the basket weaver sits on a wickerwork stool, saying 'Ken!' as he snaps a twig.

meaning: A dotted cliff shelters a person at the side who uses a measurement to mark a tree — this is the camphor tree, whose wood is measured for building.
reading: たぶ — 'Tabu' the camphor tree has a tab (like a label) on its trunk, and you tap it with a finger.

meaning: A vertical stroke and a one sit on top of two short strokes, all next to a tree — this is the Poona tree, a place name in India where such trees line the road.
reading: ポン — 'Pon!' goes the sound as you pop a bubble under the Poona tree.

meaning: A tree that grows near your home country, with ears of coconut leaves — that's the coconut tree.
reading: ヤ — Say 'Yah!' (ヤ) as you spot a coconut tree on the beach.

meaning: A tree with a rice field and a garment wrapped around it — the garment is the pivot that lets the door turn.
reading: ワイ — The door pivots with a 'why' (ワイ) sound as it swings.

meaning: A tree struck by a pike on a table, and a right hand grabs the fir branch.
reading: タン — The fir tree goes 'tan' (タン) when you chop it with a pike.

meaning: A tree with a vertical stroke and a right hand — the hand drives the stake (くい) into the ground, and the pompelmoose fruit hangs from the tree.
reading: The stake is hammered with a 'KA' (カ) sound — like the 'ca' in 'car'.

meaning: A tree with a pair of legs stepping into an open box enclosure, while a stooping figure bends over — that's the hemp palm, its fronds drooping like the stooping figure.
reading: The hemp palm's fronds rustle with a 'SHU' (シュ) sound — like 'shoo' as you wave them away.

meaning: A tree (木) with a hook stroke (乙) and a spoon (匕) hanging from it, plus a direction (方) marker — it's a rack for hanging clothes, where you hook and spoon your garments onto the tree branch.
reading: The rack is in the shape of the letter 'I' (イ) — imagine a coat rack that looks like a giant capital I, with hooks on both sides.

meaning: A sweet (甘) tree (木) with a pair of legs (儿) standing inside a box-on-side enclosure (匚) — this cypress tree grows in a fenced-off sweet-smelling grove, its wood used for sacred boxes.
reading: The cypress wood is so fine it's used for a 'jin' (ジン) — imagine a shrine (jinja) built entirely from this cypress, with the sweet smell filling the air.

meaning: A tree (木) with three stacked strokes (ヨ) on top of a pig (豕) — the pig is walking on the rafters of a porch, balancing on the three stacked beams.
reading: The rafter is so long it reaches to 'ten' (テン) — picture a rafter stretching ten meters across the porch, with a pig trotting along it.

meaning: A tree (木) with two (二) branches and a day (日) on top — a large (大) person (人) stands under it, picking a camellia flower.
reading: The camellia blooms in 'CHIN' (chin) — like a 'chin' (as in 'chin up') — the flower lifts your spirits when you see it.

meaning: A tree (木) with a day (日) and an eye (目) — you hew the tree while keeping an eye on the day's work, then tie the logs into a raft.
reading: You hew the tree and make a raft to sail to 'sa' (サ) — imagine shouting 'Sa!' as you push the raft off the shore, the eye watching the day's progress.

meaning: A tree (木) with a one (一) and a mouth (口) inside a rice field (田) — the guard stands by the tree at the field's edge, shouting one command through his mouth to protect the rice.
reading: The guard shouts 'fuku' (フク) — imagine him yelling 'Fuku!' as a warning, his mouth wide open in the rice field.

meaning: A tree (木) stands by a day (日) marked with 'not' (勿) — the willow tree does not lose its leaves on that day, it just sways.
reading: The willow's branches wave like a 'YŌ' (yo) — as in 'yo-yo' — swinging up and down in the wind.

meaning: A tree (木) with a crown (冖) and a car (車) — the peg is driven into the tree to hold the car's rope, with a crown-shaped cap on top of the peg.
reading: The peg is so strong it can hold a 'kon' (コン) — imagine a giant peg made of concrete (konkurīto) that anchors the car.

meaning: A tree (木) that stands on a table (几) in the wind (風), with an insect (虫) clinging to it — the maple's leaves flutter like insect wings in the breeze.
reading: The wind (風) blows a 'foo' (フウ) sound through the maple leaves — imagine the tree humming 'foo-oo' as the wind passes.

meaning: A large (大) wedge of wood (木) with soil (土) packed around it, struck by a sword (刀) under a lid (亠) with two (二) marks — the wedge splits the log.
reading: You 'ketsu' (ケツ) the wedge into the crack with a sharp blow — the sound of the sword hitting wood is 'ketsu-ketsu'.

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) over one (一) month (月) of craft (工) in a tree (木) — the shape you get is an ellipse, stretched and rounded.
reading: The ellipse is 'da' (ダ) — like 'dah' as you draw a long, flat oval.

meaning: A tree (木) with a vertical stroke (｜) and two (二) marks, stretched (廴) across a door, with three stacked strokes (ヨ) and a brush (聿) — the bolt bars the door.
reading: The bolt 'ken' (ケン) clicks shut — imagine the metal bar sliding with a firm 'ken' sound as it locks.

meaning: A halberd (矛) stuck into a tree (木) — the tree grows lush (楙) around the weapon, sprouting thick green leaves.
reading: The lush growth goes 'bou' (ボウ) — like a 'bow' of a plant bending under its own weight, heavy and green.

meaning: A head (疋) on a tree (木) — you whip the tree with a cane, and the head-shaped branch bends under the strike.
reading: The whip cracks 'so' (ソ) — a sharp 'so' sound as the cane slices through air and hits the wood.

meaning: A tree (木) with ten (十) mouths (口) and grass on top (艾) — the plant is coarse and crude, rough to the touch like dry grass.
reading: The coarse bark feels 'ko' (コ) — like a rough 'ko-ko' scrape against your hand as you touch the plant.

meaning: A month (月) of growth, then a mouth (口) bites into a ten (十) times bitter bark, while a tree (木) stands tall — this is the pepper tree, whose fruit stings like a bite.
reading: The pepper's heat makes you shout "KO!" as you drop it — like a karate chop to the tongue.

meaning: A tree (木) with a lid (亠) on top, and under it two splayed strokes (ハ) and a towel (巾) — the Japanese bead tree, whose seeds look like beads strung on a towel.
reading: レン — Picture a row of bead-tree seeds being strung like a "レン" (ren, as in "wren") — a small bird pecking at the beads.

meaning: A tree (木) that grows at the corner (protrusion) where a buy (買) sign meets a direction (方) — the corner of a building juts out like a tree branch.
reading: リョウ — Imagine a corner so sharp it makes you yell "リョウ!" (like "ryo!" as in "ryo-ken") — a martial arts shout at the corner.

meaning: A tree (木) with an upside-down box (冂) on top, holding two short strokes (并) and a dry (干) ten (十) — this is the camphor tree, whose wood is so sturdy it's used for boxes and beams.
reading: ナン — Nan the carpenter carves a camphor wood box, and as he works he hums "Nan, nan, nan" to the rhythm of his chisel.

meaning: A tree (木) with a hat on top (个) and a one (一) under it, next to a reap (刈) and a month (月) — the elm, whose leaves are reaped like grain.
reading: ユ — Picture an elm tree with a "ユ" (yu, as in "you") — you see the tree and say "you!" as you recognize it.

meaning: A tree (木) with two short strokes on top (并) growing next to a west (酉) marker — this is the oak that marks the western edge of the forest.
reading: The oak's acorns are a favorite of the wild boar — hear its grunt 'nara' (なら) as it roots under the tree.

meaning: A tree (木) with an eye (目) and a flag (尸) and a vertical stroke (｜) — the cross-beam above a gate, where a flag hangs and an eye looks out.
reading: ビ — Imagine a gate's cross-beam with a "ビ" (bi, as in "bee") — a bee buzzing right under the beam.

meaning: A tree (木) with a claw (爪) and a right hand (又) and a two (二) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) — a last for making shoes, shaped like a claw that turns wood on a lathe.
reading: ケン — Picture a shoe last being turned on a lathe — the wood spins and you say "ケン!" (ken, as in "ken" — a spinning top).

meaning: A tree (木) with a roof (宀) over a day (日) that says (曰) something — this is the wooden form you slide into a shoe to shape it, like a little house for the foot.
reading: The shoe last is turned on a lathe — think of a woodworker shouting 'KEN!' as the spinning wood flies off.

meaning: A tree (木) with an eye (目) and a shellfish (貝) on a divining rod (卜) — this hardwood is so strong it supports posts, like a tree that holds up a whole structure.
reading: The hardwood posts are so sturdy they can hold up a 'TEI' (tea) house — imagine a giant tea cup resting on these posts.

meaning: A tree (木) with a person at the side (化) and a dot (丶) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) — this is just a plain tree, nothing special, just standing there.
reading: The tree is so ordinary you just say 'HEN' (like 'hen' in 'henhouse') — it's just a tree, not a fancy one.

meaning: A tree (木) that has been cut into a flat dish for a generation (世) — this lacquered dish is made from wood, polished and shiny.
reading: You serve 'CHA' (tea) on this lacquered dish — imagine a tea ceremony where the dish is the star.

meaning: A tree (木) with a mouth (口) and an ear (耳) — this oar is like a long wooden ear that listens to the water, and you scull with it by moving your mouth to shout commands.
reading: The sculling oar makes a 'SHU' sound as it cuts through water — like 'shush' but with a 'u' — you shush the waves.

meaning: A tree (木) with a person (人) wrapped in a wrapping enclosure (勹) and a day (日) — this wooden tablet is a signpost, with a person wrapped up in it, pointing the way.
reading: The signpost has a 'KETSU' (like 'kets' in 'ketchup') — imagine a signpost made of a giant ketchup bottle, pointing the way.

meaning: A vertical stroke and a one stand over a king, who is under a tree — a sheep comes with a plow (耒) to start the business of farming, but the king's vocation is to perform arts on the tree.
reading: The sheep's 'GYO' (go) sound as it plows the field is the business — 'GYO'.

meaning: An old man (老) sits under a tree (木) by a day (日) marker, peeling bark from a paper mulberry to make paper.
reading: The paper mulberry's bark is chewed like 'cho' (チョ) gum by the old man.

meaning: A shield (楯) is a wooden (木) board with an eye (目) slit, held by a ten (十) grip, leaning against a cliff (厂) with an axe (斤) nearby.
reading: The shield's owner shouts 'June!' (ジュン) as he raises it against the rain of arrows.

meaning: A large person stands under a tree, holding a mortar — this is a tree so sturdy and old that it feels like a living tool, a tree that could grind grain. Picture the mortar wedged in the branches, the person reaching up to it, the tree as the workshop.
reading: The reading is ユ. Imagine a 'ユ' (yu) as a 'you' — you are the person under the tree, and you say 'YOU, this tree is my mortar-tree!' — the sound 'yu' is in 'you' exactly.

meaning: A sweet (甘) tree (木) bears plums (楳) — the fruit's sweetness is the tree's gift.
reading: The plum is baked into a 'bye' (バイ) — a sweet pie with a stone inside.

meaning: A tree (木) branch is carved into an ornamental hairpin, topped with a lid (亠) and a crown (冖), with a towel (巾) and two short strokes (并) as decoration, standing up (立) in the hair.
reading: The hairpin is so fancy it's a 'tei' (テイ) — a tiara for the hair.

meaning: A mouth (口) and a right hand (又) reach for a tree (木) with one (一) line marking the very top—that is the extreme pole you must climb to.
reading: キョク — Think of 'kyoku' (曲) as a song that reaches its extreme high note, so high it feels like a pole.

meaning: A tree (木) with white (白) bark and compare (比) marks is the model for square character style — correctness in every stroke.
reading: The calligrapher writes 'kai' (カイ) — like 'kite' — in perfect square style, straight as a kite's frame.

meaning: A tree (木) that has a grain stalk (禾) growing from it, with fire (火) burning at the base — this is the Japanese catalpa, whose wood is used for making fires and whose leaves feed silkworms.
reading: The catalpa's leaves rustle with a long 'shuuu' sound as the wind blows through them — like a soft 'shoo' from a distant crowd.

meaning: A tree (木) that holds up a roof — imagine a pillar made of wood, with a dish (皿) balanced on top and a right hand (又) gripping it, while a sweeping stroke (ノ) and 'from' (乃) mark the grain. The pillar is the tree that supports everything.
reading: エイ — Picture a pillar that says 'AY' (like 'hey' without the h) as you lean on it — it creaks 'ay-ee' under the weight of the roof.

meaning: A woman climbs up a high building made of rice and wood — she stands at the watchtower, looking out over the fields, the tall structure rising above the trees.
reading: The watchtower is so tall you must 'row' (ロウ) a boat to see the top — picture rowing a boat far out to sea to view the high building on the shore.

meaning: White music notes float over a tree, with ice cooling the air — that's comfort and ease.
reading: You listen to GAKU (ガク) — like 'gock' the sound of a drum, making music.

meaning: A wooden (木) container that holds water (水) that has been purified to a white (白) clarity — this is the kokuji for a water-pouring vessel, used in tea ceremonies.
reading: You pour the water and it splashes with a 'han-zoh' sound — like the name 'Hans' followed by a soft 'zoh' as the water hits the bowl.

meaning: A tree (木) that grows under a roof (宀) with a climax (至) of needles, rooted in soil (土) and shaped like the katakana-mu (厶) — this is the needle juniper, a hardy evergreen.
reading: The juniper's needles are so sharp they make you say 'moo-roh' in pain — like a cow's 'moo' followed by a low 'roh'.

meaning: A tree (木) with a tusk (牙) stuck in its bark, and a northeast (艮) marker carved beside it — this gives you the rough outline of the forest, not the details.
reading: You roughly guess the tree's age by its rings — 'GUY' (ガイ) the forester squints and says, 'That's about 50 years, give or take.'

meaning: A vertical stroke stands like a sacred pole in the day, next to a tree, while a salute and a rice field below show this is a holy Shinto tree where people bow and offer rice.
reading: The sacred tree sways in the wind, and you say 'sah-kah-kee' (さかき) as you watch its leaves rustle — imagine a priest chanting 'sah' while a key (kaki) hangs from a branch.

meaning: A tree (木) with an eye (目) on oneself (自) — the lotus tree's bark has patterns that look like staring eyes, and a stooping figure (夂) leans against it.
reading: The hackberry tree's bark is so smooth you can see your own face — 'KA' (カ) like 'car' mirror reflecting yourself.

meaning: A tree (木) that has been stripped of its bark and left to dry in the sun — the day (日) shines on the bare wood, while the measurement (寸) marks its length and the rice field (田) is where it lies stacked, with a dot (丶) of sap still oozing from the cut end.
reading: The reading is フ (fu). Imagine a lumberjack shouting 'Foo!' as he heaves a heavy unbarked log onto a pile — the sound 'foo' is exactly the reading.

meaning: A tree (木) that stands in your home country (邦) with a northeast (艮) orientation — this is the betel palm, whose trunk leans toward the northeast in its native land.
reading: The betel palm's fronds sway and whisper 'low' — like saying 'low' as you duck under its hanging leaves.

meaning: A tree (木) with a hole (穴) and a roof (宀) over a valley (谷) with a mouth (口) and two splayed strokes (ハ) and a hat on top (个) — the evergreen mulberry grows by the valley, its leaves like a roof over the hole.
reading: The evergreen mulberry sways in the valley, and you say 'YO! (ヨウ)' as you see it — the YO of ヨウ is the same as the shine of the leaves.

meaning: A gentleman (士) sits at a table (几) under a crown (冖) with a one (一) on top, while a right hand (又) holds a pike (殳) to beat the tree (木) — the bark is used to make paper mulberry.
reading: The paper mulberry bark is soaked in a big pot of 'koku' (コク) — imagine a giant 'coke' (コーク) bottle made of bark, fizzing with pulp.

meaning: A retainer (臣) uses a dart (矢) to measure a large (大) wooden (木) board inside a box-on-side enclosure (匚), with a sweeping stroke (ノ) marking the line — that's the carpenter's square.
reading: The carpenter's square is called 'ku' (ク) — imagine a 'coo' (クー) of a pigeon as it pecks at the right angle of the square.

meaning: A grain stalk (禾) grows next to a person (人) under a one (一) and two (二) trees (木), but the trees are actually hazelnut trees, so the whole scene is a hazelnut grove.
reading: シン — Imagine a hazelnut shell cracking with a loud 'SHIN' as you step on it, and the sound echoes through the grove.

meaning: A direction (方) sign made of wood (木) with two short strokes on top (并) and a lid (亠) under a crown (冖) — that's the name plate on a boat, and also the rudder that steers it.
reading: ボウ — The rudder hits a buoy (ボウ) with a loud "BOW!" every time you turn.

meaning: A lid (亠) covers a crown (冖) under the day (日), and two splayed strokes (ハ) spread out like branches from the tree (木) — this is a type of tree.
reading: The tree's name sounds like 'bei' (ベイ) — picture a 'bay' (ベイ) tree growing by the shore, its leaves shaped like little bays.

meaning: A pair of legs (儿) stands on a one (一) under a crown (冖) and day (日), while esteem (尚) holds up the tree (木) — this is a screen, like a wooden room divider.
reading: The screen is 'kou' (コウ) — imagine a 'koala' (コアラ) hiding behind a wooden screen, peeking out with its nose.

meaning: A hat on top (个) sits on a ten (十) and a mouth (口) under the day (日), while the tree (木) provides the trunk — that's the main support.
reading: The trunk is 'kan' (カン) — imagine a 'can' (カン) of paint strapped to the tree trunk, supporting it like a prop.

meaning: The tree (木) has a box-on-side enclosure (匚) around its trunk, and inside that box is the un- (非) part, marking it as a special, protected tree — the Japanese nutmeg plum-yew.
reading: The tree (木) is so special it gets a box-on-side enclosure (匚) — think of a 'hee' (ヒ) sound of surprise when you see it, like 'hee, that's a rare tree!'

meaning: Under a roof (宀), a tree (木) is squeezed by two splayed strokes (ハ) and a pair of legs (儿) — this is the extractor of juices, pressing the wood.
reading: The juice extractor goes 'sah' (サ) as it crushes — like the sound of a press releasing steam.

meaning: A ten (十) piece of wood (木) fits into an old bird (隹) shaped notch — that's the mortise and tenon joint.
reading: The joint fits with a 'shun' (シュン) — like the quick snap of wood locking into place.

meaning: A kiosk with a measurement (寸) of wood (木) and an eye (目) for viewing — this is a pavilion built for looking out.
reading: The pavilion's roof is 'sha' (シャ) — like the 'shah' of a king who surveys his garden from it.

meaning: A crown (冖) over a tree (木) with fire (火) at its base — the tree flourishes and brings honour, glowing with prosperity.
reading: The flourishing tree glows with 'ei' (エイ) — like the 'ay' in 'day' when the sun shines on its glory.

meaning: A tree (木) with a lid (亠) and a garment (衣) draped over it — this is the rafter that holds up the roof like a cloth.
reading: The rafter bends with a 'sui' (スイ) — like the 'swee' of wind passing through the eaves.

meaning: A quince is a fruit that grows on a tree (木) near a dish (皿) that sits in the sun (日) — imagine the quince ripening on a branch overhanging a sunny dish on a table.
reading: The quince is so sour it makes you say 'otsu!' (オツ) — like a sudden 'ouch' when you bite it.

meaning: A tree stands by a rice field where a sword cuts a katakana-mu shape — the seeds inside the fruit spill out like red gems, a pomegranate.
reading: ざくろ — The pomegranate's skin cracks with a 'zaku' sound, and the seeds roll out like a 'ro' of red beads.

meaning: An old bird perches on a crown that sits on a tree — this tree is a footbridge, and the bird collects a toll from anyone who crosses.
reading: カク — The toll collector shouts 'Kak!' to stop you, like a sharp 'cack' of a crow demanding payment.

meaning: A tree with feathers and ice on its branches — you sit on it as a chair, but it's so cold and feathery it feels like a frozen bird's nest.
reading: トウ — You sit on the chair and say 'Toe!' because a splinter jabs your toe — 'tou' like 'toe'.

meaning: A tree holds a dish with soil and a katakana-mu shape — this dish is a wine glass, filled with earthy, muddy wine.
reading: コウ — You raise the wine glass and say 'Kou!' as a toast, like 'cow' but with a long 'o' — 'kou'.

meaning: A skeleton's month (mouth) is under a crown on a tree — you chop the tree into chips, and each chip is a tiny bone from the skeleton's mouth.
reading: コツ — The chip of wood is as hard as a bone — 'kotsu' sounds like 'cots' (small beds), but imagine a bone 'cots' against the tree.

meaning: A tree (木) with a mouth (口) that eats beans (豆) from a mountain (山), while two short strokes on top (并) mark the spot — this odd tree is an alder.
reading: The alder's bark is so rough it makes you say 'gai' (ガイ) — like a guy scraping his hand on it.

meaning: A tall (高) tree (木) under a lid (亠) inside an upside-down box (冂) — the tree is sealed off, so it dies (vegetation).
reading: The dying tree goes 'koh' (コウ) — like a cough from a withered plant.

meaning: A boat (舟) on a tree (木) with a pike (殳) and a table (几) and a right hand (又) — the hand uses the pike to carve the boat into a tub.
reading: You fill the tub with water and it goes 'han' (ハン) — like a hand splashing in it.

meaning: A tree (木) with a shellfish (貝) and an eye (目) on top, plus two splayed strokes (ハ) and a vertical stroke (｜) and one (一) — the eye sees a twig, and the shellfish is a pine cone on a Chinese black pine.
reading: The twig snaps with a 'ten' (テン) — like a tense string breaking.

meaning: A month (月) with two short strokes on top (并) and a tree (木) and a left hand (屮) — the hand grabs the tree and turns it into a halberd, sharpened over a month.
reading: The halberd thrust makes a 'saku' (サク) sound — like a quick 'sack' of air.

meaning: A tree (木) stands inside an upside-down box (冂) with a one (一) and a ten (十) — the tree's posture and stance are built strong, like a frame or scaffold.
reading: You 'KO' on the tree trunk to test its build — a solid 'KO' sound means it's well-constructed.

meaning: A vertical stroke (｜) pokes through a crowded (込) mouth (口) into a tree (木) — that's a hammer or mallet driving a nail into wood.
reading: The mallet goes 'tsui' (ツイ) as it hits the wood — like 'tsu-ee' with a sharp thud.

meaning: A tree (木) with a hat on top (个) is held by a mouth (口) that shouts, and a one (一) is the spear's shaft—so the whole thing is a spear, lance, or javelin.
reading: ソウ — You throw the spear and it flies with a 'SOW' (like 'sow' seeds) sound, and it lands in a tree (木).

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) over a king (王) and craft (工) with two short strokes on top (并) and a tree (木) and a sheep (羊) — the sheep stands on the raft made of the tree, while the king cuts it slantwise.
reading: The raft floats with a 'sa' (サ) — like a soft 'sah' of water.

meaning: A ghost (鬼) with a spoon (匕) and a katakana-mu shape (厶) sits in a rice field (田), while a tree (木) grows from its head — this odd tree is the Japanese pagoda tree.
reading: The ghost (鬼) in the field shouts 'KAI!' as it swings a spoon (匕) at the tree (木).

meaning: A tree (木) with a craft (工) lever sticking out, and on top sits a shellfish (貝) with one big eye (目) and two splayed strokes (ハ) as feelers — that lever is what you pull.
reading: You pull the lever (槓) and shout 'KO!' as the shellfish (貝) pops up from the craft (工) box.

meaning: A king (王) stands by water (水) with two short strokes (并) on a tree (木), while a sheep (羊) watches — this shows the way or manner of things.
reading: ヨウ — Imagine a 'yo-yo' (ヨウ) spinning in a certain manner, showing the way it moves — that's the situation.

meaning: A tree (木) with an eye (目) on top, and a ten (十) with two splayed strokes (ハ) above that — like a decorated evergreen branch with a pattern of needles and a knot that looks like an eye.
reading: The evergreen's twig is so sharp it could poke a 'teen' (テン) — imagine a teenager yelping as a twig pricks their finger.

meaning: A tree (木) grows on a mountain (山), and a bird (鳥) perches on it — this is the oak tree used for mooring poles, a name-only kanji.
reading: The bird (鳥) on the oak tree chirps 'KASHI!' as it pecks the bark.

meaning: A tree (木) stands up (立) like a dragon (竜) — but it's just a cage, a ghost kanji that never really existed.
reading: The dragon (竜) in the cage roars 'ROU!' but the tree (木) bars hold it in.

meaning: A tree that has been cut and joined with a wedge — the ice (冫) on the day (日) under a sweeping stroke (ノ) is pressed into the white (白) wood, and feathers (羽) are stuck in the joint to seal it. This hard wood is used for making strong wedges.
reading: The hard wood is so tough that it takes a 'shoo' (シュウ) — like shooing away a bird that pecks at the wedge — to break it apart.

meaning: A coffin is a box made of tree (木) wood, with a lid (亠) on top and a vertical stroke (｜) for the side, and three stacked strokes (ヨ) for the base — all nailed shut with one (一) final board.
reading: The coffin is carried out with a sad 'ei' (エイ) — like the long 'ey' sound of a mourner's wail as the procession moves.

meaning: A printed book is made by carving a tree (木) block with an axe (斤), then rolling a car (車) over it to press the ink onto paper — the car leaves the printed page.
reading: The printed book is so old that it smells of 'zan' (ザン) — like the 'zan' in 'zanzibar' where ancient scrolls were once traded.

meaning: The outer box for a coffin is a big tree (木) case, with a lid (亠) on top, a mouth (口) for the opening, a child (子) placed inside, and the whole thing is like a home country (邦) for the dead — a protective shell.
reading: The outer box is so large it takes a 'kaku' (カク) — like 'cuckoo' — to echo inside when you knock on it.

meaning: A tree (木) with a pair of legs (儿) and a spoon (匕) — the legs walk around the tree, giving a general, approximate view of it.
reading: You say 'GAI' as you give a general glance at the tree (木) with legs (儿) — it's roughly a tree.

meaning: Generally, approximately — this is a tree (木) that has been cut down and its outline is only roughly sketched, with no fine details, just the general shape of the branches and trunk.
reading: The general idea is 'gai' (ガイ) — like 'guy' — you only get the gist of the guy, not his exact features.

meaning: A hearse is a car (車) made of tree (木) wood, with ten (十) wheels, a measurement (寸) of space for the coffin, an insect (虫) crawling on the side, and a rice field (田) in the back — all held together with a katakana-mu (厶) latch.
reading: The hearse drives slowly with a 'tan' (タン) — like the 'tan' in 'tank' — heavy and rumbling as it carries the dead.

meaning: A maple tree (木) with little (小) leaves that look like divining rods (卜) — the branches are armed with a halberd (戈) to guard the sap.
reading: The maple's red leaves rustle with a 'seki' (セキ) sound in the autumn wind.

meaning: Firewood for sacrifice — a tree (木) with four dots (杰) at the bottom, and west (酉) on top, like wood stacked for a ritual fire, with the dots representing sparks and the west direction where the sun sets, ready for burning.
reading: The sound is ユウ (yuu) — imagine a 'you' (yuu) who is the one lighting the sacrificial fire, saying 'you, you, you' as you toss each log on.

meaning: An oak tree grows where an ANGLE meets a BIG DIPPER, and the TREE itself is shaped like a dipper handle — a sturdy oak for making dippers.
reading: コク — The oak's acorn goes 'kok' when it hits the ground, like a hard 'cock' sound.

meaning: A LEFT-SIDE KATA board with a TREE handle, a DOT of pitch, an EVENING glow, and a MEASURE of rope — that's your oar for rowing at dusk.
reading: ショウ — 'Show' me how you pull the oar — 'shō' the stroke!

meaning: A WELL SWEEP is a TREE pole with a BIG DIPPER bucket, a WHITE rope, and a TEN-foot counterweight — all balanced to lift water.
reading: コウ — The sweep goes 'ko' up and 'ko' down, like a cow's 'moo' but with a 'k' — 'kō'.

meaning: A person (人) with large (大) eyes (見) stands under a tree (木) — this is the Zelkova tree, known for its tall, straight trunk. The one (一) and two (二) marks on the trunk are the tree's growth rings.
reading: The Zelkova tree is called 'TSUKI' — like 'tsuki' (moon) — imagine the moon shining through its branches at night. (Reading: キ, but the hook uses the kun つき)

meaning: A tree (木) with a vertical stroke (｜) and a one (一) on top of a day (日) — that's the wooden vat where the day's brew sits.
reading: The vat is so big, you need a 'SOH' (ソウ) — like a slow 'so' — to stir it all day.

meaning: To PASTE WALL WITH DIRT, you use a TREE trowel, a RIGHT HAND to press, a DAY of drying, and a BUY of fresh mud — then smooth it again.
reading: バン — 'Ban' the dirt onto the wall with a flat slap — 'ban'!

meaning: A tree (木) with soil (土) packed around its base, topped by two (二) blades of grass (艾) and a mouth (口) — this is the rose of Sharon, a hardy shrub that grows in poor soil and is often trimmed into hedges.
reading: The rose of Sharon blooms in the KINdergarten garden — picture a child pointing at the pink flower and shouting 'KIN!'

meaning: A large (大) tree (木) with a mortar (臼) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) leaning against it, plus a dot (丶) and two (二) marks — this is a stake driven into the ground, the center of an affair or matter.
reading: You TOE the stake into the ground with your boot — 'TOE' for the sound of the stake hitting the dirt.

meaning: On top, a white thread hangs over a tree. The white thread is a string for a musical instrument, and the tree is the wood used to make it. This combination suggests the joy of making music, and the comfort it brings.
reading: Imagine a concert hall where the orchestra plays so beautifully that the audience feels total comfort and relaxation — they all say "ga-ku" (like "gah-koo") as they sink into their seats. The sound of the music is "gaku".

meaning: A tree (木) with two short strokes on top (并) and a head (疋) that stops (彳) — this is a fir, its pointed top like a head that stops growing upward, staying evergreen.
reading: The fir tree's branches show you the SHO (ショウ) — picture a show of Christmas trees, all firs, lined up for display.

meaning: A large (大) tree (木) with to mix with (爻) branches — this is a cage or fence, made by weaving branches together to enclose a pen.
reading: The cage is HANd-made — picture a farmer's HANd weaving the fence around the pen.

meaning: A tree (木) has been crowded (込) into a pipe, and you utilize (用) it to channel water — the tree trunk is hollowed out to make a gutter or downspout.
reading: トウ — Imagine a downspout pouring water onto a TOE (トウ) that's sticking out from under the house.

meaning: A tree (木) with a shellfish (貝) and an eye (目) under two splayed strokes (ハ) in a rice field (田) — this is a grove, where many trees stand like eyes watching over the field.
reading: The grove is KANnected — picture trees in a row, their roots KANnected underground, forming a single grove.

meaning: A little thread (幺) hangs from a tree (木) over a rice field (田), and more thread (糸) is woven into a flat mat — that’s a sedan chair carried over snow, or the snowshoes themselves.
reading: The sedan sways as porters chant “ルイ” (rui) — like “rui” in “ruin” — but they don’t fall, they glide.

meaning: A dot (丶) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) sit above a sword (刀) that cuts through water at the side (汁) — all resting on a tree (木) that spans a gap, forming a bridge or a beam.
reading: The beam groans “リョウ” (ryou) — like “leo” in “Leonardo” — as it holds up the roof.

meaning: Under a roof (宀), a heart (心) and a dot (丶) rest on a mountain (ノ + 山) — and this tree (木) is placed on graves, its branches a quiet offering.
reading: The branches whisper “ミツ” (mitsu) — like “mits” in “mitts” — as they’re laid down in silence.

meaning: A vertical stroke (｜) and a one (一) form a post, a mouth (口) shouts from the top, and a woman (女) stands below — all built into a tree (木) that rises as a tower or turret.
reading: The tower bell rings “ロウ” (rou) — like “row” in “rowboat” — echoing from the high lookout.

meaning: Esteem (尚) is built on a rice field (田) with a curving river (巛) flowing through — and a tree (木) above holds a nest, where you dip up water and scoop it out.
reading: You scoop up the river with a “ソウ” (sou) — like “sow” in “sow seeds” — and the nest empties out.

meaning: A person (人) is wrapped in a wrapping enclosure (勹), their mouth (口) open in lack (欠) — and this tree (木) is just a low shrub, not enough to hide behind.
reading: The shrub rustles “ソク” (soku) — like “sock” in “sock” — as the person crouches, lacking cover.

meaning: A tree (木) that stands in the rain (雨) with two (二) branches wrapped in a wrapping enclosure (勹) — this odd tree is the Japanese bead tree, known for its bitter, bead-like seeds.
reading: The bead tree’s seeds rattle like a tiny 'cho' (as in 'chop') when you shake the dried branches in the rain.

meaning: A tree shows two small marks under the west — this is the signpost, the seal, the mark you see.
reading: The signpost points with a 'ヒョウ' (hyou) — like 'hio' — a shout of 'hi-yo!' to mark the spot.

meaning: A tree (木) with a dotted cliff (广) and a deer (鹿) standing on a spoon (匕) — the deer turns the tree’s trunk like a pulley, winding a rope around the wheel.
reading: The pulley squeaks 'roku-roku' as the deer winds the rope around the wooden wheel.

meaning: A tree (木) with feathers (羽) and a hat on top (个) — the hat droops, and the feathers bend and entwine, while ice (冫) and three (彡) streaks show the undulating curve.
reading: The drooping branch makes a 'kyuu' sound as it bends under the weight of the icy feathers.

meaning: A tree (木) with a box-on-side enclosure (匚) holding goods (品) and a mouth (口) — the goods are stacked around the tree’s pivot, and the mouth is the door’s hinge.
reading: The door’s pivot turns with a 'suu' — like the soft 'sue' of a sliding door in an old house.

meaning: A tree (木) that stands up (立) tall, with a sound (音) like ten (十) drums beating under the day (日) sun — this is the camphor tree, known for its fragrant wood.
reading: The camphor tree’s scent makes you say “SHOW!” (ショウ) as you point at it — like a magician revealing a prize.

meaning: A tree (木) with one (一) vertical stroke (｜) entering (入) an upside-down box (冂) and an open box enclosure (凵) — the tree oozes gum, sticky like elm sap, from the cracks in the boxes.
reading: The gum drips with a 'bon' — like a soft 'bong' of a hollow elm trunk when tapped.

meaning: A large (大) tree (木) with grass on top (艾) stands by a day (日) — you copy its shape exactly, like tracing a shadow at noon to make an imitation.
reading: モ — Think of a mock-up model (モ) made of cardboard — a copy of the real thing, but not the real thing.

meaning: A tree (木) with a bird (鳥) and four dots at the bottom (杰) — the bird perches on the vine that wraps the tree, its four claw marks dotting the bark.
reading: The bird sings 'to' — a short 'toe' — as it hops along the vine.

meaning: A king (王) stands by water (水) under a tree (木), with two short strokes on top (并) and a sheep (羊) nearby, all marked by a dot (丶) — this is the proper way, the manner of a noble situation.
reading: The king's manner is so refined that he says 'ヨウ' (yo) as he bows, like 'yo' in 'yoga' — a calm, formal greeting.

meaning: The old bird sits on the tree, holding a dart and a 乞-shaped part — this is the bird's authority to rule the forest. The tree gives it power, the dart gives it rights.
reading: ケン — Ken (like the doll) sits on the tree with the old bird, and everyone must obey his authority.

meaning: A vertical stroke (｜) runs sideways through a yellow (黄) rice field (田) with two (二) day (日) marks, two splayed strokes (ハ) on a tree (木), and two hands (廾) pushing it all horizontal.
reading: OU (オウ) — Say “owe” (ou) as you owe someone for tilting the whole yellow field sideways — the width of the debt is huge.

meaning: A retainer (臣) plants his right hand (又) into the soil (土) beside a tree (木) — the evergreen oak that grows only where loyal hands have worked the ground.
reading: The evergreen oak's bark is so hard you need a KASHI (かし) knife to carve it — say "KASHI-knife" as you chop.

meaning: A tree (木) with fire (火) on the west (西) side — this kokuji is a type of tree that burns well, named 'hokusō'.
reading: The fire (火) on the west (西) side of the tree (木) crackles 'HOKUSO!' as it catches.

meaning: A tree (木) with two (二) piling (弋) branches — the jujube fruit piles up like stones on the branches.
reading: The on-reading ジ sounds like 'gee' (as in 'gee whiz') — say 'gee, that's a jujube!'

meaning: A tall tree — imagine a wooden trunk so high it scrapes the sky, with branches like arms reaching up, but no other parts needed to see its height.
reading: The tree is so tall you have to say 'jun' (like 'June' in 'June bug') just to reach the first branch.

meaning: A tree (木) with four dots (杰) and an old bird (隹) — the lumberjack's axe scatters the bird as he chops.
reading: The on-reading ショウ sounds like 'show' — imagine a lumberjack show where he chops logs.

meaning: A tree (木) with a knot — the knot looks like an ear (耳) that has been squeezed by a right hand (又) under a day (日) of pressure, creating a twisted grain.
reading: サイ — Imagine a saw (sounds like 'sigh') cutting into a knotty wood, and the saw blade gets stuck in the knot, making a 'sai-sai' sound as it vibrates.

meaning: A tree with two short strokes on top (并) and a sheep (羊) grazing beneath it — the sheep strips the bark off the tree, leaving the rough outer layer exposed.
reading: Imagine a BOK (ボク) — a boxer — punching a tree so hard the bark flies off in chunks.

meaning: A tree (木) with two short strokes on top (并) stands by a mouth (口) that measures (寸) the soil (土) and beans (豆) — this is timber, trees, wood, and establishing a grove.
reading: Picture a giant tree that says 'JU' (like 'Jew' but with a soft J) as it grows — it's the timber you establish.

meaning: A tree (木) with grass on top (艾) and a vertical stroke (｜) — the birch tree's white bark has a single dark vertical line, like a grass blade stuck on.
reading: The birch bark peels like a 'KA' (カ) — 'car' — door being stripped of its paint.

meaning: A tree (木) with a measurement (寸) on top, a west (酉) side, and two short strokes (并) — this is a barrel, measured and marked for its contents.
reading: The barrel rolls down the hill with a deep 'SON' — imagine a heavy oak cask thudding 'SON' as it bumps over roots.

meaning: A tree (木) with a halberd (戈) stuck in its trunk, and a head (疋) resting on the ground in its shade — the shade is so deep it feels like a shelter.
reading: Say 'ETSU' (エツ) — like 'etch' — you etch your name into the tree trunk, but the shade keeps you cool while you work.

meaning: A tree (木) cut into planks, with a mouth (口) and a day (日) carved on the side, and a rice field (田) below — the planks are shaped into a coffin for a farmer.
reading: Think of a SEN (セン) — a 'sen' is a coin — you pay a coin to the carpenter who builds the coffin.

meaning: A tree (木) with an ear (耳) listening, while a strike (攵) hits the 乞-shaped part (乞) — the tree bears olives, which are pressed (struck) for oil.
reading: Imagine a KAN (カン) — a can — of olives rolling off the tree and hitting your ear.

meaning: A tree (木) with nothingness (無) on top — the tree is bare, no leaves, just a beech tree with four dots (杰) at the bottom like fallen nuts.
reading: Say 'BO' (ボ) — like 'bow' — you bow to the beech tree, but it has no leaves to bow back.

meaning: A tree (木) with nothingness (無) above it and a dish (皿) below — the tree grows nothing, the dish is empty, so there is 'without' or 'none'.
reading: Think of 'BU' (ブ) — like 'boo' — you say 'boo' to the empty tree, and it gives you nothing in return.

meaning: The fur (毛) is wrapped around the tree (木) to make a sled that slides over snow, and the same fur-and-wood frame straps onto your boots as snowshoes.
reading: キョウ — A sled driver shouts "KYO!" to his horse as they race down the snowy hill.

meaning: The soil (土) on the riverbank holds a tree (木) that you've carved into an oar, and a pair of legs (儿) stand in the boat, ready to paddle.
reading: ドウ — You row the boat with a "DOUGH"-shaped paddle, kneading the water like bread.

meaning: A tree and a mouth sit inside an upside-down box, with a sweeping stroke on top — that's the bridge you cross, made of wood and echoing voices.
reading: You walk across the bridge and shout 'KYO!' — the sound bounces off the upside-down box and the tree, like a kyo-kyo echo.

meaning: A crown (冖) sits on a mouth (口) that blows air into a sack made of tree (木) and stone (石) — the sack opens at both ends, like a bellows for a forge.
reading: タク — You "TACK" the sack shut at both ends with a needle and thread, but the wind still leaks out.

meaning: A tree (木) under a crown (冖) with the katakana-mu shape (厶) and rain (雨) falling on it, while two short strokes (并) and a vertical stroke (｜) mark the grain — these are the wood streaks on the tree's surface.
reading: The wood streaks look like a map of clouds, and you say 'un' as in 'under' — the streaks are under the rain (雨), and 'un' sounds like 'under' without the 'der'.

meaning: A crown (冖) and a mouth (口) sit on a tree (木) that has a tusk (牙) sticking out — you use this as a prop to shore up the leaning tree.
reading: トウ — You "TOW" the prop into place with a rope, pulling it tight against the tree.

meaning: A mouth (口) and a halberd (矛) over a tree (木), with a pair of legs (儿) under an upside-down box (冂) — this is a mandarin orange, a fruit guarded by a warrior's spear.
reading: The orange bursts with a sharp 'KITSU' — imagine biting into it and the juice squirts 'KITSU' into your eye, making you blink.

meaning: The dotted tent (癶) covers a tree (木) that grows beans (豆) with two short strokes (并) on top — these are bitter oranges, not sweet ones.
reading: トウ — You "TOW" the bitter orange in a net behind your boat, but it's too sour to eat.

meaning: A tree (木) that has been cut short by a lack (欠) of a person (人) with a wrapping enclosure (勹) and a cliff (厂) — the left hand (屮) holds the post, but the top is a blunt stake driven into the ground.
reading: ケツ — Imagine a wooden post that says 'kets' as it's hammered — like the sound of a stake hitting hard earth, 'ketsu'.

meaning: A tree (木) with a dot (丶) and a short thread (幺) tangled around a halberd (戈) — this is the loom, a wooden machine that weaves threads into cloth.
reading: キ — Imagine a key (ki) turning a loom's wheel — the mechanism clicks and the machine starts weaving.

meaning: A tree (木) that grows near a pig (豕) with a wrapping enclosure (勹) around its mouth (口) — the pig eats the fallen horse chestnuts under the tree.
reading: ショウ — Picture a horse chestnut that shouts 'show!' as it bursts open from its spiky shell, revealing the shiny nut.

meaning: A tree (木) that is shaped like a thousand (阡) craft (工) projects — a month (月) of work, with a sweeping stroke (ノ) and a one (一) — all stretched into an oval, elliptical form.
reading: ダ — Imagine an ellipse that is 'da' flat — like a squashed ball that goes 'da' when it hits the ground.

meaning: A tree (木) with a heart (心) at its center — the stamen is the heart of the flower, hanging down from the tree.
reading: ズイ — The stamen is 'zui' — think of 'zui' as the buzz of a bee that lands right on the stamen to collect pollen.

meaning: A tree (木) that is used as a pole to stand up (立) a ri (里) — a long pole to measure or support a village's flag.
reading: トウ — The pole goes 'tou' as it taps the ground — like a blind person's cane tapping 'tou, tou'.

meaning: A tree (木) with a hut built on top — the hut has a mouth (口) for a door, a day (日) for a window, and two short strokes on top (并) for a roof, with a vertical stroke (｜) as the center post.
reading: ソウ — The hut is 'sou' — imagine a small hut that says 'sou' as the wind blows through its cracks, a lonely sound.

meaning: A tree (木) lies flat under two short strokes on top (并) — the tree is not standing but stretched out across the ground, so you see it as horizontal and lateral.
reading: Imagine a wide, horizontal river crossing an 'owe' (オウ) — you owe someone a boat ride across it, and the boat moves sideways, not up.

meaning: A tree (木) is cut into planks, and next to it a cliff (厂) holds a mouth (口) and a measurement (寸) — you measure the planks to build a cabinet with a door that opens like a mouth, and beans (豆) are stored inside on shelves.
reading: In the cupboard, you store a 'shoe' (シュウ) — but it's a giant shoe, and you have to shove it in sideways, making the whole cabinet wobble.

meaning: A tree (木) stands near a gentleman (士) who counts ten (十) beans (豆) with his mouth (口) — this tree is the Japanese storax, a tree that grows in a gentleman's garden, used in names of places.
reading: The storax tree's sap smells like 'key' (キ) — you use a key to unlock a box of resin, and the key is sticky with it.

meaning: A tree (木) with a day (日) carved into its trunk — the grain runs so straight that the sun's light follows the lines like a ruler, showing straight grain.
reading: The straight grain is 'masa' (まさ) — you say 'masa, masa' as you run your finger along the perfectly straight lines, like a mantra of straightness.

meaning: A rice field (田) sits under a lid (亠) on top of a tree (木) — this is the oak, a tree so sturdy it holds up the field above it.
reading: The oak's branches are so strong they can hold a whole 'kyo' (キョウ) — like a giant 'kyo' (as in 'kyoto') — in their arms.

meaning: A tree grows under a lid, with a mouth and a day inside — this is the cedar or sandalwood tree, its wood used for incense and fine boxes.
reading: ダン — The sandalwood smells like a 'dance' (ダン) hall full of incense.

meaning: A tree with a grain stalk and a box under a lid — the grain stalk is the bole, and the box is the cross-beam, all combed around the ship's hatches.
reading: リン — 'Ring' (リン) the bell on the ship's cross-beam to signal the hatch is secure.

meaning: A written appeal is struck onto a tree with a strike, using white paper and a direction arrow, while the 乞-shaped part is the signature — this is a manifesto.
reading: ケキ — The manifesto is so forceful it makes you 'kek' (like a cough) when you read it aloud.

meaning: An old bird sits on a tree, but a vertical stroke and a barb pierce the tree from above — like a wooden rammer pounding down. The bird is startled, and the place is a mess.
reading: The rammer goes 'swish' as it swings down — 'スイ' (sui) sounds like 'swish' with a soft 's'.

meaning: A tree with a king's ear and a mouth — the king's ear hears the willow's rustle, and the mouth names the tamarisk by the riverbank.
reading: テイ — 'Tay' (テイ) like 'tea' — the tamarisk grows by the tea house, its willow branches swaying.

meaning: A tree (木) that stands up (立) tall, with its heart (心) hidden inside, listening to the sound (音) of the day (日) — this is the ilex, a sturdy evergreen oak.
reading: The ilex tree's bark is so tough it makes an 'oku' (オク) sound when you knock on it, like a hollow 'ok' echo.

meaning: A tree (木) with a lid (亠) on top, under which sits an upside-down box (冂) holding a katakana-mu shape (厶) — this odd fruit-bearing tree is named after the Chinese emperor (禹) who first grew apples.
reading: The apple falls with a 'gon' (ゴン) thud on the ground, a heavy sound that echoes in the orchard.

meaning: The eaves are the part of a house that says (言) 'stay dry' to the rain, jutting out from the tree (木) beams, with a pair of legs (儿) standing on a cliff (厂) — the edge of the roof.
reading: The eaves drip with a steady 'en' (エン) sound as rain falls off them, like a soft 'en-en' rhythm.

meaning: A shelf is a wooden (木) frame that holds things, like a crosspiece that spans between two supports — picture a sturdy plank of tree (木) laid flat to make a shelf.
reading: The shelf creaks under weight with a low 'tou' (トウ) groan, like a heavy 'tow' of a load.

meaning: The cork tree has a trunk (木) that stands up (立) with a mouth (口) and ten (十) branches, all covered in spicy (辛) bitter bark, and a flag (尸) waving from the top — this is the Amur cork tree.
reading: The cork tree's bark is so bitter it makes you say 'haku' (ハク) — like a sharp 'hack' cough from the taste.

meaning: A tree with a hat on top (个) stands next to a day (日) and a buy (買) sign — this is the Japanese cypress, a wood so fine it's bought for shrines, with a single (一) straight trunk.
reading: The cypress tree is so tall it pokes a hole in the sky — 'kai' as in 'kite' caught on its top branch.

meaning: An oar is a long piece of tree (木) with a halberd (戈) blade at one end and an ear (耳) shaped handle at the other, plus a mouth (口) to shout commands — you row with it.
reading: The oar slices the water with a 'shuu' (シュウ) swoosh, a quick 'shoo' sound as it moves.

meaning: A tree with a cow's horn-shaped branch, wrapped in a sword-like leaf, standing under a month of moonlight — this is the oak, sturdy and familiar.
reading: The oak's bark feels like a rough 'kai' (カイ) — imagine a kayak paddle made of oak, hitting the water with a solid 'kai' sound.

meaning: A small evergreen shrub with two splayed strokes for leaves, an eye-like berry, and a west-facing shell-shaped flower — all growing from a tree.
reading: The shrub's tiny leaves whisper 'ka' (カ) as the wind blows — like a quiet 'ka' from a cat's mouth.

meaning: A tree (木) is bent, but a wrapping enclosure (勹) holds it while a strike (攵) hits it, and grass on top (艾) and the 乞-shaped part (乞) pull it — you straighten a bow by force, then place it on a lamp stand made of the same wood.
reading: You 'kay' (ケイ) the bow — like saying 'okay' to the bow as you straighten it, then you set the lamp on the stand and say 'kay, it's straight now.'

meaning: A person with a hat on top checks a tree, using one hand to examine each branch — this is the act of checking and examining.
reading: You check every leaf with a 'ken' (ケン) — like a ken (sword) poking each branch to test it.

meaning: A tree with a box of soil on top, and a person standing inside the box — that's the mast of a ship, rooted in the deck.
reading: The mast sways with a 'sho' (ショウ) — imagine a showman balancing on the mast, shouting 'sho!' to the crowd below.

meaning: A white tree with ice on its branches — this oak is so hard it's used for charcoal, burning cold and white.
reading: The charcoal crackles with a 'reki' (レキ) — like a 'rekki' (reckless) fire that burns too fast.

meaning: A tree with a roof over a little show, with two dots and an evening sky — this is the sassafras, a tree that shows off its flowers.
reading: The sassafras smells like 'satsu' (サツ) — imagine a 'satsuma' orange tree, but this one is sassafras.

meaning: A tree with a crown on top, grass on top of that, and a pig underneath — the pig is hiding under the lemon tree's dense leaves, but you can see its snout poking through the grass.
reading: モウ — 'Mow' the grass under the lemon tree, but the pig says 'mow' as it chews the fallen lemons.

meaning: A tree (木) with a mouth (口) and craft (工) under a gentleman (士) holding a measurement (寸) becomes a foolish stump, ignorant and unmoving.
reading: トウ — Imagine a 'toe' (トウ) stubbing against a wooden stump, and you feel foolish for not seeing it.

meaning: A gentleman sits at a table made of soil and wood, with a crown on top and a mouth below, while the katakana-mu shape holds the climax of the meal.
reading: タイ — Imagine a table set for a grand feast, and the host shouts 'TAI!' (like 'tie') to call everyone to sit down.

meaning: A betel-nut palm grows under a roof, with a sweeping stroke and two splayed strokes as leaves, while a shellfish and an eye watch over the little tree.
reading: ビン — Picture a betel-nut palm in a bin (ビン) that you carry to the market, the nuts rattling inside.

meaning: A tree with grass on top and an old bird perched on a right hand, all standing on a cliff — this is the tree that grows there.
reading: カク — The old bird squawks 'KAKU!' (like 'cackle') as it lands on the tree, startling the hand.

meaning: A lemon tree grows under a roof, with a barb and a dish below, while a heart and a buy sign hang from the branches, and one little leaf flutters.
reading: ネイ — The lemon is so sour that you say 'NEI!' (like 'nay') and refuse to eat it, even though it's on the dish.

meaning: A tree stands beside a dish, but a retainer and two are trapped inside — the retainer is locked in a wooden pen, the dish as his only bowl, the two bars of the cell keeping him in.
reading: The jail cell clangs shut with a 'KAN' — the metallic sound of the lock hitting the wooden frame.

meaning: A grassy plant with fibres for cloth grows as a tree, with a crown on top and fire at the base, burning the fibres to make thread.
reading: ケイ — The fibres are twisted into rope, and you shout 'KEI!' (like 'kay') to the weaver, asking for more.

meaning: A mulberry tree grows on a cliff, with a dot and a large dog under it, while the day and month pass and the dog eats the berries.
reading: エン — The mulberry tree is in a garden (エン), and the dog digs around its roots every day.

meaning: Under a roof (宀), a heart (心) and an insect (虫) sit on a tree (木) with a dot (丶) above — this is the star anise, whose seed pod looks like a tiny insect heart under a roof, and the dot is the aromatic oil drop.
reading: The star anise smells like 'mitts' of cinnamon — imagine a giant hand wearing a mitten (ミツ) crushing the anise pods on a tree.

meaning: An old bird (隹) with three stacked strokes (ヨ) as its wing sits on a tree (木) — that bird is using a tree branch as an oar to paddle across a lake.
reading: You 'tow' (トウ) the boat with this oar — picture towing a heavy log (the oar) behind a rowboat, the rope straining.

meaning: A box-on-side enclosure (匚) holds a shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) on it, and a tree (木) is stuffed inside, with a vertical stroke (｜) poking out — it's a sturdy chest or coffer.
reading: Imagine a giant key (キ) unlocking a wooden chest (櫃) — the key turns with a loud 'ki' click.

meaning: A tree (木) with a table (几) on top, and on that table sit beans (豆) under a dotted tent (癶) with two short strokes (并) — this is a bench, where you sit like a tent over your beans, and the table is the seat.
reading: You 'tow' (トウ) the bench across the floor — picture dragging a heavy wooden stool, its legs scraping like a tow rope.

meaning: A tree holds a one, a crown, a stooping figure, a heart, an eye, and oneself — the hoe's handle is the tree, and the curved blade (the stooping figure) digs into the soil, while the eye and heart watch the work, and oneself is the farmer.
reading: The hoe scrapes the ground with a soft 'YUU' — like a long, slow sigh of effort as you pull it through the dirt.

meaning: A tree is topped with a rice field — the decorated wine cask is a wooden barrel with a wide, flat top like a field, and the sword hilt is also carved from that same wood, both ornate and heavy.
reading: The cask is rolled with a deep 'RAI' — like the rumble of a heavy barrel across a wooden floor.

meaning: A tree stands under a fish, a rice field, a day, and four dots at the bottom — the tower is built of wood, with a fish-shaped weathervane on top, and the oar is also made from that tree, its blade like a fish tail, with four dots of water dripping off.
reading: The oar strokes the water with a rhythmic 'RO' — like the low, steady chant of a rower.

meaning: A tree (木) stands by a gate (門) with a mouth (口) carved into it, and a sweeping stroke (ノ) marks the spot — this is the quince tree, known for its gnarled, gate-like branches.
reading: The quince's fruit is so tart it makes you say 'ロ' (ro) — like a surprised 'roh!' — as you bite into it. (Reading: ロ)

meaning: A bamboo (竹) tool with a seal (卩) and a northeast (艮) corner, plus a tree (木) — this is the comb, used to part hair like a well (井) divides land.
reading: The comb's teeth are so fine they make a 'shitsu' (シツ) sound — like 'shitsu' (as in 'shitsu' — a Japanese room) where you comb your hair before entering.

meaning: A stooping figure bends under a crown, holding a divining rod and a mouth, while a tree grows from the top — this odd bundle is a quiver, a case for arrows slung over the shoulder.
reading: The sound is コウ — imagine a quiver full of arrows that you 'ko' (like 'caw') at a crow, but the crow is perched on the tree on top of the quiver, cawing back at you.

meaning: A gentleman (士) with a pair of legs (儿) and two splayed strokes (ハ) opens a wooden (木) chest, but inside is an eye (目) and a shellfish (貝) — he must buy (買) the whole cabinet to get the treasure.
reading: The cabinet is so heavy you need a 'トク' (toku) — like 'toku' (特) meaning special — but here it's just a big wooden box that says 'tok, tok' when you knock. (Reading: トク)

meaning: A pig (豕) with a short thread (幺) and three stacked strokes (ヨ) climbs a little (小) lemon tree (木), tangling its thread in the branches — that's the kind of lemon tree that grows wild.
reading: The lemon's sour juice makes you pucker and say 'エン' (en) — like 'en' in 'envy' — as you watch the pig struggle. (Reading: エン)

meaning: A white (白) tree (木) with a short thread (幺) hanging from it — this oak is so pale it looks bleached, perfect for making charcoal.
reading: The charcoal burns with a 'レキ' (reki) — like 'rekishi' (history) — but here it's just a crackling 'rek, rek' sound as the oak turns to embers. (Reading: レキ)

meaning: An old man (老) stands under an oak tree (木) on a day (日) and says (言) that the soil (土) has a sweeping stroke (ノ) of fertility.
reading: "Show" — the old man shows off his oak tree to everyone.

meaning: On a cliff (厂) with tiger spots (虍), a wax tree (木) is tapped using a divining rod (卜) and a spoon (匕) to collect wax in a dish (皿) from a rice field (田).
reading: "Low" — the wax tree grows low on the cliff, easy to reach.

meaning: A cliff (厂) shelters a stop (止) sign made of wood (木) — the horse barn's manger is a wooden trough that stops the horse's feed from spilling.
reading: The horse in the barn chews its fodder with a loud 'レキ' (rekki) crunch — imagine the sound of a horse biting into a hard wooden trough.

meaning: A coffin (this kanji) is a tree (木) that has been cut down, with a pair of legs (儿) standing on it, and an eye (目) looking up from inside, while a little (小) stand (立) holds the lid — all under a one (一) flat top.
reading: シン — The coffin is so shiny it makes you SHIN (シン) — like a new car, but for the dead.

meaning: Yeast sprouts from a tree (木) like a left hand (屮) reaching up, with a mouth (口) and a ten (十) on a stand (立), all under a spicy (辛) burst of fermentation.
reading: ゲツ — The yeast makes a GETSU (ゲツ) — like a 'get it?' joke, but it's the alcohol talking.

meaning: A cage is a tree (木) with bars, and an upside-down box (冂) over it, with a vertical stroke (｜) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) as the lock — but no parts given for the rest, so imagine the whole thing as a wooden pen.
reading: ロウ — The cage is so old it's a ROW (ロウ) of rusty bars, like a prison lineup.

meaning: Rain (雨) falls through a mouth (口) and a tree (木) — the latticework of the window lets the rain in, with the tree's branches forming the pattern.
reading: レイ — Picture a 'ray' (レイ) of light shining through the latticework, each square letting a ray pass.

meaning: A woman (女) under a tree (木) sees shellfish (貝) and an eye (目) with two splayed strokes (ハ) — the cherry blossoms fall like shells, and she watches them with her eye.
reading: オウ — Say 'oh!' (オウ) as you see the cherry tree — the woman gasps 'oh' at the sight of the blossoms.

meaning: The craft of shaping wood by heat: imagine a tree trunk clamped under a claw, with a heart-shaped flame bending it over a thousand-degree fire, while a vertical stroke of steam rises.
reading: The wood is bent into an 'in' curve — think of a bentwood chair that says 'IN' as you sit in it.

meaning: A sandalwood tree with a comet tail: the tree's trunk is wrapped in a spoon-like bark, and a pair of legs dangle from a comet that has a mouth and a compare-marked tail.
reading: The comet's sandalwood tail smells like 'san' — as in 'sandalwood' (sounds like 'san' + 'dal').

meaning: A vertical stroke splits the gate, and inside you see a day, a tree, and a rice field arranged in a column — this is the handrail-like blank space in a newspaper column.
reading: You grab the handrail of a LAN (ラン) — imagine a long LAN cable wrapped around the rail, and you pull it to scroll down the column.

meaning: A keyaki tree with esteem: the tree's branches are held up by a hand, and its leaves are two splayed strokes, showing the tree's honored status.
reading: The keyaki tree is so tall you need a 'kyo' (like 'key-oh') to climb it.

meaning: Authority is a tree with an old bird perched on top, holding a ten in its beak, while a mouth below declares the law — the bird's power is absolute.
reading: The old bird's authority is 'ken' — it can 'ken' (like 'can') do anything.

meaning: A horse-chestnut tree (木) grows near an old bird (隹) that perches on a branch, while a short thread (幺) and buy (買) hang from the leaves — you buy the nuts from this tree.
reading: The horse-chestnut falls with a 'ra' (ラ) sound onto the ground, like a rattle rolling away.

meaning: A beam (木) stretches across a dotted cliff (广), held up by a deer (鹿) and a spoon (匕) — the compare (比) shows how straight and strong the beam is.
reading: The beam is so long it reaches from 'rei' (レイ) to the next house — like a railway tie.

meaning: People gather (gather) around a tree (木) where a pair of legs (儿) stand on soil (土), an eye (目) watches a shellfish (貝) — all together under a sweeping stroke (ノ) and two splayed strokes (ハ).
reading: They gather to share a 'san' (サン) — like a sandwich passed around the group.

meaning: A chinaberry tree (木) is round and harmonious, with little (小) threads (糸) and say (言) wrapped around it — the tree's fruit is round and the people talk peacefully beneath it.
reading: The round fruit rolls 'ran' (ラン) down the hill — like a run-away ball.

meaning: A retainer sees a tree with two short strokes on top, and the 乞-shaped part hangs from a branch — that's the Chinese olive tree, where the retainer picks the fruit.
reading: The olive tree is so tall you need a 'ran' (run) to climb it — you run 'ran' up the trunk to get the olives.

meaning: Two hands grip a month, a tree, rain, and leather — all tied to a knife handle with a hilt, ready to swing.
reading: You grab the HILT and say 'HAH!' (ハ) as you pull the blade free.

meaning: A buy sign hangs on a tree, but the northeast wind blows, and a measurement of gloom covers everything — the tree is heavy with melancholy, and the flag-like leaves droop.
reading: When you feel 'utsu' (depression), you sit under the tree and say 'oo-tsu' — a long sigh that sounds like the wind in the gloomy branches.

meaning: The rain falls through the craft-made lattice of a window, and the crown above the mouth and the two people below are all framed by the vertical stroke and the one — this is the sill and lintel.
reading: レイ — The rain on the window sill makes a 'lay' (レイ) of water, like a thin layer on the lattice.

meaning: The old bird sits on the tree, and the grass on top and the ten below are all part of the keyaki — a zelkova tree that grows tall with a see-through canopy.
reading: つき — The keyaki tree's bark is as smooth as a 'tsuki' (つき) moon, glowing in the night.

meaning: A person (人) is wrapped in a wrapping enclosure (勹) that is open at the bottom — they are missing something, leaving a gap. That gap is the lack.
reading: ケツ — Imagine a person yawning (欠) so hard they fall into a kettle (ケツ) of hot water, and the steam escapes through the gap in their mouth.

meaning: Ice (冫) melts and drips onto a lack (欠) — the lack of ice creates a sequence, as each drop follows the next in order.
reading: ジ — Picture a JI (ジ) — a small gear — turning in sequence, each tooth following the next, powered by melting ice.

meaning: An axe (斤) chops wood, but you lack (欠) the strength — yet you take pleasure in the effort, rejoicing in each swing.
reading: You rejoice with a 'KIN' (キン) — like a 'king' laughing heartily in his court, pleased with his realm.

meaning: A person (人) wrapped in a wrapping enclosure (勹) holds a divining rod (卜) and lacks (欠) certainty, so they ask a question with a final particle. The one (一) and barb (亅) show the rising tone of the question.
reading: The particle sounds like 'yo' — imagine saying 'yo?' with a shrug, like 'yo, really?' The reading is 'ヨ' (yo), a short questioning sound.

meaning: A box-on-side enclosure holds a sweeping stroke and a dot, but lacks a person — that's Europe, far away and empty of familiar faces.
reading: オウ — Say 'Ow!' as you stub your toe on the box-on-side enclosure — that's the sound of Europe's surprise.

meaning: A person with a wrapping enclosure around a mouth that lacks — you blow air through a gap, smiling as you breathe out.
reading: You blow a soft 'ku' — like a gentle 'coo' from a dove, a breath of air.

meaning: A lid over a person wrapped in a wrapping enclosure, with a short thread and a lack — a cough bursts out from that trapped, lacking breath.
reading: A cough sounds like 'kai' (カイ) — as in 'kite' caught in your throat, you hack it out.

meaning: A valley (谷) with a hat on top (个) and two splayed strokes (ハ) below, next to a mouth (口) that lacks (欠) — the mouth longs for what the valley hides, a greedy passion.
reading: ヨク — 'Yok' (ヨク) sounds like 'yolk' — you crave the golden yolk of an egg, your mouth watering with longing.

meaning: A large (大) person (人) wrapped in a wrapping enclosure (勹) holds a dart (矢) and a lack (欠) — to treat someone well, you wrap them in friendship, but you lack the dart to hurt them, so you detain them kindly.
reading: You treat the guest so well that they 'can' (カン) stay forever — like a can of preserved friendship.

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) over one (一) and a towel (巾) with a lack (欠) — the towel is soaked with tears because you lack comfort, so you cry into it.
reading: You cry so hard that your breath goes 'kee' (キ) — like a high-pitched sob that sounds like a key turning in a lock.

meaning: A dart (矢) with a katakana-mu shape (厶) and a lack (欠) — the dart misses its target (厶) and you lack a hit, so you let out an exclamation of surprise or frustration.
reading: The exclamation 'ai' (アイ) — like saying 'I!' when you're startled, or 'eye' when you see something shocking.

meaning: A large mouth with a barb and a one, plus a lack — you prick up your ears (the barb) to hear what the mouth lacks, because it's whispering.
reading: イ — 'Ee!' you squeak, pricking up your ears to hear the faint sound.

meaning: The sweet (甘) part is missing (欠) from the two splayed strokes (ハ) — that lack of sweetness is a deceit, a cheat that hides the truth.
reading: A GI (ギ) — like a 'gee' (as in 'gee, that's a lie!') — the cheat says 'gee' when caught, and the sound is GI.

meaning: A person wrapped in a wrapping enclosure, with fire and a lack — suddenly the fire flares up, and the person is gone (lack) in an abrupt whoosh.
reading: クツ — 'Kutsu!' the sudden sound of a firework bursting, like a shoe (kutsu) stomping on the ground.

meaning: Gold is rare, but when you lack it, you still respect the king who has it — you revere his wealth and power.
reading: You 'kin' (キン) your head in respect — a deep bow to the gold-laden ruler.

meaning: A gentleman shows a little lack of two things — but his goodwill makes up for it. The gentleman's friendly article is signed with a lack of formality.
reading: カン — A can of goodwill is passed around at the friendship meeting, everyone takes a sip.

meaning: A person (人) under a wrapping enclosure (勹) looks into a mortar (臼) that lacks (欠) any grain — they feel discontented and gloomy.
reading: The gloomy person says 'TAN!' as they kick the empty mortar — like a sad 'tango' with no partner.

meaning: You use a mortar (臼) to crush grain, then a lack (欠) of water makes you sip (すす.る) — you slurp up the last drops with a sweeping stroke (ノ) of your tongue, and a ten (十) marks the spot where you finish.
reading: You slurp loudly, making a 'soh' sound as you suck the liquid through your teeth — like a quick 'so' followed by a breathy 'h'.

meaning: A person (人) wraps a day (日) in a wrapping enclosure (勹), but then a lack (欠) of sound (音) makes them stand up (立) — they admire the silence and gladly accept it.
reading: The sound of a bell going 'KIN' makes you gladly admire it, like a temple gong you willingly listen to.

meaning: A day (日) wrapped in a wrapping enclosure (勹) is hit by a lack (欠) — the spoon (匕) is gone, so you're exhausted and out of energy, and you stop (やめる).
reading: You're so exhausted you 'KET' down on the floor, like a puppet with its strings cut.

meaning: The three stacked strokes (ヨ) and two short strokes (并) sit on top of a lack (欠) — imagine a shelf with only a few items left, showing a shortage.
reading: When you feel the lack, you say 'KEN' (ケン) — like 'can't' without the 't', as in 'I ken't find enough'.

meaning: A tall (高) person (人) inside an upside-down box (冂) with a wrapping enclosure (勹) and a mouth (口) — all under a lid (亠) — lets out a hot sigh that rises up.
reading: The sigh rises up with a 'KYO' (キョウ) — like 'kyo' in 'kyoto' where the hot air goes up.

meaning: A mouth (口) opens wide, a barb (亅) hooks the tune, and a lack (欠) of words is filled by one (一) long note — that's how you sing a song.
reading: カ — Picture a singer belting out 'KAH!' as the opening syllable of a powerful song, mouth wide open.

meaning: A large (大) person with a mouth (口) under grass (艾) and a one (一) and two (二) — the mouth lets out a lament, while the large one grieves.
reading: The grief makes you 'TAN' (タン) — like 'tan' in 'tantrum', a loud lament.

meaning: A box-on-side enclosure (匚) holds goods (品) and a mouth (口), but a lack (欠) of air makes it cough — that's Europe, a place of many nations packed together, each with its own voice.
reading: Europe's sound is a big 'オウ' (ou) — like 'oh' you say when you see the Eiffel Tower, a long, impressed 'oh'.

meaning: An old bird (隹) with a dart (矢) in its beak, begging (乞) for a lack (欠) of sorrow — that's pure delight and joy.
reading: カン — The bird's joyful song sounds like "KAN! KAN!" as it dances around a can (カン) of happiness.

meaning: A tiger spots (虍) a lack (欠) of air, and under a cliff (厂) a divining rod (卜) and a spoon (匕) are crossed with two short strokes on top (并) — the tiger cries because it can't breathe, so it sobs.
reading: You cry 'kyo' (キョ) — like a kitten's 'meow' but sadder, 'kyo-kyo' as you sob into a tissue, and the sound is a choked cry.

meaning: Feathers, lack, mouth, a hat on top, and ice come together: the hat on top presses down on the feathers, the lack of air makes the mouth gasp, and ice forms as they all meet and are put away in a cold storage.
reading: The sound is 'kyuu' — imagine a cat saying 'kyuu' as it sucks in air, pulling feathers and ice together into a box to store them.

meaning: A person with a hat on top, a mouth, and a lack — the person tightens the hat strap because the mouth (of the bag) lacks closure, so they pull it tight.
reading: レン — 'Ren' the rope tight around the bag's mouth, like a sailor named Ren hauling in a line.

meaning: A mortar with two splayed strokes on top, and a lack below — the mortar is empty (lack), so you ask 'is that all?' with a questioning particle.
reading: ヨ — 'Yo!' you shout to ask if the mortar is empty — 'Yo, is that all?'

meaning: A person (人) with a wrapping enclosure (勹) holds a right hand (又) to a mouth (口) that lacks (欠) a cup — so they sip directly from the west (酉) jar, sucking the drink out.
reading: You sip so loudly it sounds like 'セツ' (setsu) — like 'setsu' in 'setsumei' (explanation) — but here it's just the slurp of a thirsty person. (Reading: セツ)

meaning: Delight is an old bird with a lack of worry: it sings from a tree, its mouth open in joy, while a ten and grass on top celebrate the moment.
reading: The bird's joy makes it 'kan' — it 'can' (like 'kan') sing all day.

meaning: A foot (the top part) comes down hard on the ground (the bottom line) — that's the universal sign to stop, like a red light in kanji form.
reading: You shout 'shi!' to stop a horse — a sharp, short 'shi' that halts everything.

meaning: One (一) stops (止) at the line — that's the correct, righteous place to halt, no further.
reading: セイ — 'Say' (セイ) the correct answer out loud — you're stating what's right.

meaning: A stop (止) sign and a spoon (匕) — this is the one right here, the current thing you're pointing at with the spoon, stopping your attention on it.
reading: You point with the spoon and say 'shi' — like 'this' but shorter, 'shi' (シ) is the sound of pointing at 'this'.

meaning: A step is a small movement — the top part looks like a foot (the 止 shape, but here simplified) and the bottom is a sweeping stroke (ノ) over a one (一). You take a step, then a pace, then walk on.
reading: The reading 'ホ' (ho) sounds like 'hoe' — picture a farmer taking a step while holding a hoe, then walking a stroll with it. 'Ho, ho, ho' as he paces.

meaning: A stop (止) sign is piling (弋) up weapons — the warrior stops the piling of arms, but still carries the spear of chivalry.
reading: The warrior shouts 'bu' (ブ) — like a battle cry 'bu-bu' as he charges into the fray.

meaning: A ten (十) crosses a right hand (又) that holds a branch (支), and a stop (止) sign stands at the fork — you must stop and choose which road to take.
reading: At the fork, you 'kee'p your hand (又) steady — 'ki' (キ) as you decide which branch to follow.

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) sweeps over a stop (止) sign, but a little (小) person keeps walking past it — that's a step, and you count each one.
reading: ホ — Imagine walking and counting steps, but each step lands on a big 'HO' (as in 'hoe') lying on the ground, and you step on it with a crunch.

meaning: A vertical stroke (｜) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) lean on a one (一) that sits on a stop (止), with a dot (丶) thrown off — the whole thing is bent and warped, the dot falls away from the straight line.
reading: The metal bar warps into a 'ワイ' (why) shape — you ask 'why is it bent like that?'

meaning: A stop (止) sign blocks the rice (米) inside an open box enclosure (凵) — like teeth stopping food from escaping your mouth.
reading: You see a tooth in a cogwheel — it goes 'SHI' as it turns, like the sound of a gear slipping.

meaning: A sweeping stroke (the year's end) stops at a little halberd — each year you get older, and each occasion is a chance to stop and reflect.
reading: You say 'SAI' as you count your age on your fingers — each year is a new SAI (サイ) of life.

meaning: A stop (止) sign on a cliff (厂) under a dotted cliff (广) with hemp (麻) growing over a tree (木) — the layers of growth and stops mark the passage of time, like rings in a tree trunk.
reading: レキ — Picture a clock's second hand ticking "レキ, レキ, レキ" as it moves across the face, marking each moment of history.

meaning: The bare bone (歹) of time, with a vertical stroke (｜) and two splayed strokes (ハ) marking days, plus a mouth (口) and a crown (冖) — all these parts take place in the past, forming history.
reading: Think of a 'reki' (レキ) — like a 'record' — where the bare bone and crown mark the past events that have taken place.

meaning: Three stacked strokes (ヨ) on top, a towel (巾) and a mouth (口) below, with a stop (止) at the bottom, all under a crown (冖) — the procession arrives home, stopping at the gate.
reading: The homecoming parade ends with a 'kae' (かえ) — like a frog's 'ribbit' but with a 'k' — as the traveler returns.

meaning: A bare bone (歹) sticking out of the ground — it's a sign of death, something bad and wrong, left to rot.
reading: The sound is ガツ (gatsu). Imagine a hungry dog gnawing on a bare bone, growling 'gatsu, gatsu' as it chews.

meaning: A pair of legs (儿) under a dot (丶) and a vertical stroke (｜) — but the top is broken and jagged, like a vicious, depraved creature with a twisted spine.
reading: No reading given — so just see the vicious creature's jagged teeth, and remember it's 'bad' by its ugly shape.

meaning: A bare bone (歹) lies under a one (一) and an evening (夕) sky — the evening of life, when death comes.
reading: The bare bone (歹) is a shi-ny skeleton — it says 'shi' as it rattles. (シ, kun し.ぬ)

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) and a wrapping enclosure (勹) trap a bare bone (歹) with a 'not' (勿) sign — this is drowning, where the water wraps around you and you cannot escape.
reading: A drowning person goes 'bo'tsu, bo'tsu' as they sink — 'bo' (ボツ) like the bubbling sound of water closing over the bone.

meaning: A bare bone (歹) is wrapped in a wrapping enclosure (勹) while a right hand (又) reaches out — but it's too late, the hand can't save the bone, so it dies.
reading: The hand (又) waves goodbye as the bone dies — 'bo' (ボツ) like the final 'bo' of a funeral bell.

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) and a large (大) figure stand over a bare bone (歹) — this is dying young, the large figure cut down before its time.
reading: A young person dies 'yo'ung — 'yo' (ヨウ) as in 'yo'uth, cut short by the bare bone.

meaning: A sweeping stroke cuts down a person, and the deceased falls into the grave — that's death.
reading: ボツ — A boat (ボツ) sinks, and everyone on board dies in the cold water.

meaning: A bare bone with a one-eyed gaze — death comes when the eye stops seeing, the bone left alone.
reading: Death is a soft 'so' — like a sigh 'soh' as life leaves the body.

meaning: A bare bone under a large upside-down box with a crown — calamity falls from above, trapping you in misfortune.
reading: Disaster strikes with a loud 'ou' — like 'ow!' when you stub your toe, a cry of pain.

meaning: A bare bone (歹) lies under a hat on top (个), with three (彡) lines of dust falling from it — the bone is completely gone, all that's left is dust.
reading: Imagine a TENnis ball hitting the bare bone and shattering it into three pieces — completely destroyed.

meaning: A bare bone (歹) sits next to a mouth (口) with a katakana-mu (厶) inside it — the mouth is almost empty, just a tiny bit left.
reading: The mouth says 'TAI' (like 'tie') — it's almost tied shut, only a tiny gap remains.

meaning: A bare bone (歹) next to a day (日) wrapped in a wrapping enclosure (勹) — following a leader to death, even the bone is wrapped in loyalty.
reading: ジュン — JUNE (ジュン) — in June, the martyr's bones are buried with full honors, a solemn ceremony.
