reading: The disease spreads so rapidly that you shout 'SHITSU!' (シツ) as the dart hits the carbuncle.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) sits under two hands (廾) holding a bow (弓) — the sweat and friction of gripping the bow gives you a prickly heat rash.
reading: ヒ — Picture a 'hee' (as in 'heat') sound: the rash itches so you go 'hee-hee' while scratching.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) grows on the back of a mouth (口) wrapped in a wrapping enclosure (勹) — the weight makes you crouch into a hunchback.
reading: ク — You 'coo' (ク) like a pigeon as you crouch low, unable to straighten your spine.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) pokes out of a mouth (口) that holds a divining rod (卜) — the rod predicts a fever that comes and goes, chronic malaria.
reading: セン — The malaria sends you to 'send' (セン) for a doctor every time it returns.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) with a mouth (口) and power (力) — the mouth bites and the power pulls, drying the wound into a hard scab.
reading: カ — The scab feels like a 'car' (カ) door slammed on your skin — dry and rough.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) under a lid (亠) with a short thread (幺) and mysterious (玄) energy — the mysterious tension twists your muscles into cramps.
reading: ゲン — The cramps make you 'gen' (ゲン) in pain, like a groan from deep in your gut.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) with a one (一), a vertical stroke (｜), and a sweeping stroke (ノ) — the strokes spread out like swollen sores on the neck.
reading: サ — The swellings look like a 'saw' (サ) blade cutting jagged lines under the skin.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) sits under an upside-down box (冂) with a person (人) and a one (一) — the person is ill, sick, trapped by the disease.
reading: The sick person groans 'byou' (ビョウ) — like 'bio' in 'biology' — as the carbuncle swells under the box.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) makes you stop (止) — the one (一) symptom is that you can't move, showing the illness.
reading: ショウ — 'Show' (ショウ) your symptoms to the doctor — the carbuncle is the sign of the illness.

meaning: A king with a hat on top sits by a carbuncle — the hat is a bandage, and the king’s presence helps the carbuncle heal.
reading: セン — The king sends a cent (セン) to buy medicine, and the carbuncle heals.

meaning: An upside-down box with a one inside, and a mouth — the box is a body, the one is a pain point, and the mouth cries out in ache.
reading: トウ — The mouth shouts 'toe!' (トウ) as the pain hits the one inside the box.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) sits on a large (大) person (人) who is leaning on a bow (弓) — the wound from battle is an injury.
reading: The injured soldier says 'イ' (ee) as he touches the wound — like a sharp 'ee' of pain.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) under a month (月) with a sweeping stroke (ノ) and one (一) — the bruise looks like a dark crescent moon on the skin.
reading: The bruise is 'イ' (ee) — you see it and go 'ee, that's a nasty contusion'.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) on a sheep (羊) with a king (王) and two short strokes (并) — the sheep scratches itself because it's itchy.
reading: You say 'ヨウ' (yo) — 'yo, stop scratching, it's itchy!'

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) on the soil (土) where a measurement (寸) is taken — sitting on the ground gives you piles.
reading: The pain makes you say 'ヂ' (ji) — like 'jeez, my piles hurt'.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) leaves a scar on the northeast (艮) side of your foot — that permanent mark or footprint left behind.
reading: Kon (コン) — the mark is a 'con' (like a con artist's fake footprint) — you see the print and know someone was here.

meaning: A carbuncle on the skin, with a one and a sweeping stroke and a 'do not' — the mother says 'do not touch' — you're ill from the carbuncle.
reading: My ill — 'my' as in 'my pain' — the carbuncle is mine, and I'm ill.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) on your face, and next to it a mouth (口) that has beans (豆) stuck in its teeth — the whole thing is a pox outbreak.
reading: トウ — Imagine a pox-covered warrior shouting 'TOW!' as he charges into battle, his mouth full of beans.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) on your leg makes you twist like a curving river (巛) while you try to work (工) — that's the cramp.
reading: ケイ — You cramp up and yell 'KAY!' (like 'okay' but strained) as you try to keep working at your craft.

meaning: A 'carbuncle' (疔) on your 'utilize' (用) hand — every time you try to use it, you feel a sharp 'pain' or 'hurt', and the 'マ-shaped stroke' (マ) marks the spot where it throbs.
reading: ツウ — Say 'too' (ツウ) — as in 'too much!' — when you stub your toe and feel that sharp pain, it's just too much to bear.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) on your scalp, and above it a table (几) with a grain stalk (禾) on it — the grain falls off, leaving a scabby bald head.
reading: トク — You're so bald and scabby that you say 'TOOK' (like 'took off') all your hair — the grain stalk took it away.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) in your chest, with a vertical stroke (｜) and a dot (丶) stuck in a mouth (口) that has a one (一) across it — everything is blocked, causing constipation.
reading: ヒ — You feel a 'HEE' (like a wheeze) of pressure in your chest, blocked by that carbuncle.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) on your leg, and below it a pair of legs (儿) with two splayed strokes (ハ) and a katakana-mu shape (厶) — a stooping figure (夂) bends over in aching pain.
reading: サン — The aching limbs make you say 'SUN' (like the sun) — you feel burned out and sore all over.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) on your belly, with a vertical stroke (｜) and a dot (丶) on a one (一) that sits above a month (月) — the disease spreads through your body over a month.
reading: ホ — You groan 'HO' (like 'ho ho' but weak) as the ailment drags on for a month.

meaning: A grain stalk (禾) is reaped (刈) but then a carbuncle (疔) appears — that’s diarrhea, a sudden messy problem.
reading: You rush to the toilet with a “ri” (like “ree” in “reel”) — the carbuncle makes you groan.

meaning: A gentleman's heart is marked by a carbuncle — but instead of a sore, it's a permanent birthmark or mole on the skin.
reading: シ — A 'she' (シ) has a birthmark shaped like a tiny ship on her cheek, and everyone calls it her 'she-mark'.

meaning: A person stands on soil, but a carbuncle swells up on their neck — that's the lymph gland swelling.
reading: サ — 'Sah!' you say, wincing as you touch the swollen lymph gland — it stings like a 'saber' cut.

meaning: A sweeping stroke drips little water drops onto a carbuncle — that's the cholera rash, spreading with colic pain.
reading: サ — 'Sah!' the patient groans, clutching their belly from colic, as the cholera rash spreads like sand.

meaning: A right hand grabs a carbuncle and squeezes it — all the fat drains out, making you get thin.
reading: ソウ — 'Sow' the seeds of weight loss — each day you get thinner, like a 'soul' fading away.

meaning: A carbuncle that has grown so long it stretches the belly skin tight — the belly is swelled and inflated like a drum.
reading: チョウ — Imagine a long (長) carbuncle on your belly that makes you shout 'CHOW!' (as in 'chow down') because you feel bloated and swollen.

meaning: A carbuncle under a roof, with a mouth and a vertical stroke — the sick person lies under the roof, too weak to speak, only a vertical groan escapes the mouth.
reading: カン — Picture a sick person under a roof who can only say 'KAHN' (like a weak cough) — that's the sound of being sick.

meaning: A carbuncle next to fire — the heat of the fire makes you cough up thick sputum and phlegm.
reading: タン — The phlegm lands with a 'TAN' (like a coin dropping into a metal cup) — that's the sound of sputum hitting the spittoon.

meaning: A carbuncle that is 'un-' (非) comfortable — it's a heat rash or prickly heat, with ulcers that itch and burn.
reading: ヒ — Say 'HEE!' (like a sharp hiss) when the prickly heat stings — that's the sound of the rash.

meaning: A carbuncle with a tree and a pair of legs — the tree's branches are like numb legs, and the measles make you paralyzed and unable to walk.
reading: マ — Imagine a 'MA' (like 'ma' as in mother) who has measles and can't move her legs — she just lies there saying 'ma... ma...'.

meaning: A carbuncle next to a tree — the tree's bark is rough and scaly, like the painful sores of gonorrhea.
reading: リン — The tree rings (リン, like 'ring') are the shape of the infection's circular sores — remember 'ring' for gonorrhea.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) on the mouth (口) makes you drool, and you shoot a dart (矢) at the 乞-shaped part (乞) — that's just stupid and foolish behavior.
reading: Calling someone foolish is like saying 'チ' (chi) — a short, dismissive 'chi' sound, like a tsk of annoyance.

meaning: Two hands (廾) are pressing down on a rice field (田) that has a carbuncle (疔) growing in it — the whole field goes numb and paralyzed from the infection.
reading: The farmer's hands are numb, so he can't feel the 'hee' (ヒ) of the horse — he just stands there saying 'hee' as the horse steps on his foot.

meaning: A ten (十) is stuck in the rice field (田) next to a carbuncle (疔) — the wound makes the whole area go palsied and numb, like a dead limb.
reading: The palsy makes you say 'hee' (ヒ) like a horse whinnying — you can't control your muscles, only that sound.

meaning: A mouth (口) is trapped inside a box (囗) with a ten (十) and a carbuncle (疔) — the chronic illness keeps you sealed in, unable to escape the pain.
reading: The chronic illness is like a 'ko' (コ) — a cold that never leaves, you keep coughing 'ko, ko' every winter.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) sits under a barb (亅) and a thousand (阡) with a one (一) and a mouth (口) — the chronic illness is a thousand tiny wounds that never heal.
reading: The chronic illness makes you groan 'ah' (ア) every time you move — a long, drawn-out 'ah' of pain.

meaning: A grain stalk (禾) falls on a woman (女) who has a carbuncle (疔) — her muscles atrophy and go numb from the shock and the wound.
reading: The atrophy makes you feel like 'ee' (イ) — a long, weak 'ee' as your strength drains away.

meaning: A dot (丶) falls from a hat (个) onto a direction (方) where a carbuncle (疔) is — the blood pools into a hematoma, a dark bruise that won't move.
reading: The hematoma is a 'yo' (ヨ) — like a yo-yo, the blood goes out and then comes back, stuck in one spot.

meaning: A carbuncle sits under a lid, with a person and ten more people all exhausted from tending it — the whole group takes sick from the strain.
reading: スイ — Imagine a sick person saying 'swee' as they collapse, like a long, weak 'sweeze' of fatigue.

meaning: A carbuncle grows on the throat, and a vertical stroke pierces it — the person becomes dumb, unable to speak a single word.
reading: ア — Picture a mute person opening their mouth to say 'ah' but only a silent 'a' comes out, stuck like the carbuncle.

meaning: A carbuncle on a pig's foot, with a dot of frost on top — the pig gets sores from cold, shivering in the snow.
reading: ショク — The pig's frozen foot goes 'shock' as it hits ice, a sudden jolt of cold pain.

meaning: A prolonged fever that makes you see a large sword (刀) and a dart (矢) stuck in a carbuncle (疔) on your skin, while a vertical stroke (｜) and a one (一) mark the days of sickness.
reading: The fever makes you 'ケイ' — imagine a kayak (ケイ) paddling through a swamp of fever, with the carbuncle (疔) as the boat.

meaning: You have a carbuncle (疔) that you need to reap (刈) over a month (月). After that, put a hat (个) on your head to show you're one (一) with health – you've recovered.
reading: Say 'You' as you imagine yourself recovering from the carbuncle – the sound 'yu' is like 'you'.

meaning: A person at the side (化) has a large (大) carbuncle (疔) that is a wart. He tries to remove it with a dart (矢), but only makes a sweeping stroke (ノ) and a ユ-shaped mark, and it remains one (一) big wart.
reading: The reading コウ sounds like 'ko' in 'koala' – picture a koala with warts all over its nose.

meaning: Insanity and headache come from a wind (風) that blows through a carbuncle (疔) into your head, with an insect (虫) buzzing inside and a table (几) shaking from the storm.
reading: The headache makes you feel 'フウ' — like 'foo' (フウ) a wind gust, as the insect (虫) flies out of the carbuncle (疔).

meaning: Severe, poisonous skin diseases — you reap (刈) the carbuncle (疔) with a mouth (口) that bites, and a tree (木) grows thorns that scratch the itch, making it dangerous.
reading: The itch is so severe you shout 'ラツ' — like 'rats' (ラツ) biting your skin, with the carbuncle (疔) as the wound.

meaning: A swelling or tumor — a carbuncle (疔) with a wrapping enclosure (勹) around it, a day (日) of heat, and a sweeping stroke (ノ) that pushes it up, while a one (一) marks the lump.
reading: The tumor swells like 'ヨウ' — imagine 'yo' (ヨウ) a big yolk (卵) growing under the skin, with the carbuncle (疔) as the core.

meaning: An old man (老) is so ill that he can't even move his legs (ノ) — he just lies in the soil (土) under the hot day (日) sun, and the carbuncle (疔) on his back throbs.
reading: ト — Think of a 'toe' (ト) that is so ill it turns black and falls off, like a carbuncle on your foot.

meaning: A large (大) pair of legs (儿) with two splayed strokes (ハ) are wrapped in a wrapping enclosure (勹) inside an upside-down box (冂) — the whole body is paralyzed, numb, and the carbuncle (疔) spreads.
reading: タン — Imagine a 'tan' (タン) line on your arm where the paralysis stops — the skin is numb and pale there.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) sits under an upside-down box (冂) that traps a right hand (又) and a mouth (口) — the body's lower pipes are blocked, causing a disease of the bowels and wheezing like asthma.
reading: The sick man's breath comes in short 'kah' gasps — imagine him coughing 'kah-kah' as the carbuncle presses on his gut.

meaning: The sound (音) of your voice is trapped under a stand up (立) — you try to speak but only a day (日) of silence comes out, and the carbuncle (疔) blocks your throat.
reading: イン — Imagine an 'inn' (イン) where the mute guest can't call for help — only silent gestures.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) that tunnels through the skin like a small tube — the sore leaks and forms a fistula, an ulcer that won't heal.
reading: ロウ — Think of a 'low' (ロウ) point in the ground where a sewer pipe leaks — that's the fistula draining.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) is covered in an insect (虫) that bites with a right hand (又) and a dot (丶) of poison — the whole thing makes you itch.
reading: ソウ — Imagine the itch is so bad you shout "SOW!" (like throwing seeds) at the insect, but it keeps biting.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) grows inside your nose, and you see it with your own eye (目) — it's a polypus, a fleshy growth that feels like a second heart (心) beating in your face.
reading: ショク — The polypus makes you feel like you're at a "SHOCK" concert, the bass vibrating in your nose.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) makes you neglect your duties — you just lie there, a vertical stroke (｜) of pain, a sweeping stroke (ノ) of weakness, while your wallet (買) sits unused, useless.
reading: カン — The pain is so bad you can't even "CAN" (カン) open a can of soup — you just stare at it.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) is so bad you bury it — you dig a hole in the soil (土) with a large (大) shovel, and a person (人) helps you lower it into the ground.
reading: エイ — You say "AYE" (エイ) as you heave the dirt over the buried carbuncle, like a sailor's chant.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) sits on a dish (皿) under the hot day (日) sun — the heat breeds a contagious disease that spreads through the village.
reading: オン — The disease is "ON" (オン) everyone — it's on your skin, on your clothes, on everything.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) on your month (月) of illness makes you get thin — you see two (二) ribs sticking out, and a person (人) looks like a skeleton.
reading: セキ — You're so thin you can "SEC" (セキ) through the gaps between your ribs — like a security check that sees everything.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) sits under a flag (尸) with a hat on top (个), and a mouth (口) is open in pain — this is a wound that has become a boil, and if it gets worse, it turns into syphilis.
reading: The wound is so deep you can see the SOW (ソウ) — a female pig — lying in it, oozing pus.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) on a boat (舟) gets hit by a pike (殳) held by a right hand (又) on a table (几) — the healing leaves a permanent scar.
reading: The scar is from a HAN (ハン) — like Han Solo — who got burned and now has a mark on his face.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) grows in a rice field (田), and a sword (刀) slices it open, but the katakana-mu shape (厶) of pus still swells up — that's the lump.
reading: The lump is so big it feels like a 'ryu' (dragon) under the skin, ready to burst — リュウ.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) with a king (王) and a craft (工) on top, plus two short strokes (并) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) over one (一) — the disease is so bad that only a king's craft can help you recover from it, but it also spreads as an epidemic.
reading: You recover when you say 'SAH' (サ) — like a sigh of relief — after the fever breaks.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) sits in a mortar (臼) with a branch (支) and a right hand (又) holding a ten (十) — the illness makes you so thin that your bones stick out like a branch, and you look emaciated and lean.
reading: You are so thin you can see your SOW (ソウ) — the pig — ribs through your skin.

meaning: A tiger spots (虍) pattern on the skin, a divining rod (卜) shakes, a spoon (匕) rattles, and a cliff (厂) looms — the ague brings chills and fever, with a carbuncle (疔) as the source.
reading: ギャク — Imagine 'gyaku' (ギャク) meaning 'reverse' — the fever reverses hot and cold, like a yo-yo.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) on a head with a hat (个) and a mouth (口) — the disease makes you mad, so you scream and foam at the mouth.
reading: You go MAD and start TEN (テン) — like a ten-ton weight — crashing around the room.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) with grass on top (艾) and a hat (个) over a mouth (口) — the grass hides the pimples on your face, but they still itch and pop.
reading: The pimples are so big they look like a TOW (トウ) — a rope — wrapped around your nose.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) on the west (西) side of your hand, with a little (小) show (示) of pus — that's a whitlow, a painful infection at the nail edge.
reading: The whitlow makes you cry 'HYOW!' (ヒョウ) as it throbs — imagine a loud, high-pitched 'hyow' of pain.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) in a rice field (田) where a short thread (幺) and a thread (糸) hang from a little (小) tree — the swollen neck glands feel like knotted threads under your skin.
reading: The swollen glands make your neck feel like it's wrapped in a 'rui' (ルイ) of rope — imagine a heavy rope necklace called 'rui'.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) on a person (人) who stops (彳, 止) mid-step — the child's spasms and convulsions from indigestion make them jerk and stop, jerk and stop.
reading: The child's convulsions make them shout 'SHO!' (ショウ) with each jerk — imagine a sharp 'sho' sound with every spasm.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) under a hat (个) with a sweeping stroke (ノ), ice (冫), three (彡) feathers (羽) — after healing, the wound reforms into smooth, feather-like skin.
reading: The healing feels like a gentle 'chuu' (チュウ) — imagine a soft kiss (chuu) on the wound, and it reforms.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) that makes a sound (音) from a day (日) of standing (立) in a swamp — the miasma rises like a poisonous fog that you hear hissing.
reading: The miasma smells like 'sho' (ショウ) — imagine a swamp gas that makes you say 'sho' as you gag.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) with a dot (丶) and two (二) evening (夕) marks, plus a little (小) show (示) — the wasting disease drains you, leaving only a small show of life.
reading: The wasting disease makes you sigh 'sai' (サイ) — imagine a long, tired 'sai' as you waste away.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) on the leg (肉) makes you enter (入) a state of lameness, and your hands lose power (力) — but the upside-down box (冂) over your mouth (口) traps your cries.
reading: The lame man's leg is caught in a KAR (car) door, and he can't pull it out — 'KAR' as in カ.

meaning: A flag (尸) hangs over a carbuncle (疔) that leaks like rain (雨) — the sore drips down, forming a tumor and an anal fistula.
reading: The fistula leaks 'loo' (ルー) like a toilet, and the sore 'roh' (ロー) like a crow's call — the hook uses the 'ル' sound.

meaning: A vertical stroke (｜) pokes a one (一) into a mouth (口) that spits out a woman (女) who has a carbuncle (疔) — the hole left behind is a fistula.
reading: The fistula makes a 'loo' (ルー) sound when air escapes, like a tiny flute — the hook uses the 'ル' sound.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) on a large (大) area, with grass on top (艾) and a day (日) of suffering — this is sickness and distress.
reading: The sick man's distress is so BAD, he says 'BAKU' (バク) — like 'back' but with a 'u'.

meaning: A carbuncle on a rice field turns everything yellow — that's the yellow sickness, jaundice.
reading: コウ — Imagine a cow (コウ) with yellow skin, mooing weakly in a rice field, struck by jaundice.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) on a large (大) day (日) with two short strokes on top (并) — the doctor must 'heal' and 'cure' this sore.
reading: The carbuncle (疔) is healed by a 'ryo' (リョウ) — 'ryo' as in 'ryokan' (a healing inn).

meaning: A stooping figure (夂) with a thousand (阡) lives (生) but one (一) carbuncle (疔) causes weakness and urine retention.
reading: Picture a weak fighter named Ryu (リュウ) who can't move because of urine retention.

meaning: A carbuncle under a crown, with fire and power — the heat and strain cause a rash, pain, and total debilitation.
reading: ロウ — Think of a low (ロウ) burning fire under a crown — it scorches the skin, causing a painful rash.

meaning: A carbuncle at the gate, with day and month — the long wait makes you bitter, hot-tempered, and irritable, even causing fits.
reading: カン — A can (カン) of hot peppers sits at the gate — one bite makes you bitter and twitchy.

meaning: A dotted tent with two splayed strokes and a pair of legs — but a carbuncle cripples you, so you can't walk — chronic illness.
reading: ハイ — Say 'hi' (ハイ) to the crippled legs — they can't carry you anymore, a chronic failure.

meaning: A carbuncle on a rice field, with ten mouths and a day — the dry heat makes everyone hate bitterly, and the field is drought-stricken.
reading: タン — A tan (タン) dry patch on the rice field — the drought makes you hate the sun, and you rest (やす.む) in the shade.

meaning: A dot (丶) on a hat (个) covers a katakana-mu (厶) that sits on a thousand (阡) — but a carbuncle (疔) grows on the heart, hidden under the one (一) — that's the disease of the heart.
reading: The heart disease makes you 'in' (イン) like a sigh, and the pain is 'on' (オン) like a switch — the hook uses the 'イン' sound.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) grows on the mountain (山) of the body, and goods (品) spill from the mouth (口) — this is cancer, the evil that spreads and consumes.
reading: The cancer is a 'gan' (ガン) — like a gang of cells that take over the body, a 'gan' (as in 'gangster') that won't leave.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) on the heart (心) is being reaped (刈) by a month (月) of rest, with a hat on top (个) to keep the head cool — that's healing.
reading: The doctor says 'YOU' (ユ) will heal if you rest — imagine the doctor pointing at you and saying 'YOU, heal!'

meaning: A lid covers a short thread, but a carbuncle (a boil) grows on it, and an old bird perches nearby — this disease makes you lose your sense of smell, so you can't even smell the bird's stink.
reading: ヨウ — You lose your sense of smell, so you can't smell the 'YO-gurt' (ヨウ) that's gone bad on the table — you only see the mold.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) on a flag (尸) that stands up (立) with a spicy (辛) mouth (口) and ten (十) — that's a bad mannerism, like picking at a sore.
reading: Your habit is to say 'HEKI' (ヘキ) — imagine a person with a tic who always sneezes 'heki!' at the worst moments.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) sits under grass on top (艾) while a rice field (田) is infected — the whole area is a contagious disease that spreads like a curse from an ancient emperor (禹).
reading: The disease makes you cry 'rai' (like 'rye' bread, but with a long 'a') — the reading is ライ.

meaning: A carbuncle sits on a mortar, and a rat is gnawing at it — this illness makes you feel as sick and miserable as a rat trapped in a mortar, unable to escape.
reading: ショ — The rat in the mortar squeaks 'SHOW!' (ショ) as it's crushed — that's the sound of being ill.

meaning: Two splayed strokes on a flag, a pike, a carbuncle, a table, and a right hand — this skin disease leaves white patches like a piebald cat, and the patches look like the splayed strokes on a flag.
reading: デン — The white patches on your skin look like 'DEN-tures' (デン) — fake teeth that are unnaturally white and patchy.

meaning: A carbuncle with a tome, an eye, oneself, and two hands, all under an upside-down box and a barb — the carbuncle is so shrivelled up that the hands can't even hold it, it's dried up and vexed.
reading: ハツ — The shrivelled fruit goes 'hats' when you squeeze it — like a tiny, dry 'hats' of air escaping.

meaning: A carbuncle with a head, a dart, a spoon, and the 乞-shaped part — the foolish person lets a dart and spoon poke at their head, not even noticing the carbuncle.
reading: チ — The foolish one says 'chee' when you point at the dart in their head — 'chee' as in a silly, childish sound.

meaning: A carbuncle on the skin, with a king eating sheep and two short strokes on top — the itch makes you want to scratch until the sheep runs away.
reading: The itch makes you yell 'YO!' as you scratch — a sharp 'YO' of irritation.

meaning: A carbuncle with a spoon, a seal, a katakana-mu shape, a day, white, and bamboo — a pimple that boils up like a sealed bamboo shoot, sore to the touch.
reading: The pimple pops with a 'SETSU' sound — like a tiny bamboo joint snapping under pressure.

meaning: A carbuncle with one mountain, a stop, a strike, and a king — the bowel obstruction is a hard lump that stops the flow, like a mountain blocking a path.
reading: The lump feels like a 'CHŌ' block — a heavy, stuck 'CHŌ' in the gut.

meaning: A carbuncle sits under a cliff, with a stop sign and a tree — the swollen neck glands press against the stop, making you halt in pain.
reading: レキ — Think 'レキ' (like 'reck' in 'reckless') — the reckless swelling on your neck makes you reckless with fear, but the sound is 'レキ'.

meaning: Rain falls on a carbuncle, and an old bird perches on it — the heatstroke makes the carbuncle throb under the hot rain.
reading: The heatstroke makes you KAKU (as in 'cuckoo') — you feel crazy and dizzy in the sun.

meaning: A carbuncle with a shellfish, an eye, two splayed strokes, a mouth, a page, and a tree — leprosy makes your skin fall off like pages from a book.
reading: ライ — 'ライ' sounds like 'lie' — the leprosy makes you tell a 'lie' about your health, but the rash on the page reveals the truth.

meaning: A carbuncle with a grain stalk, shellfish, eye, two splayed strokes, soil, two, and a lid — the spasms make you clutch your stomach like a lid over a pot.
reading: しゃく — 'しゃく' sounds like 'shack' — the spasms shake you like you're in a 'shack' during an earthquake, rattling your bones.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) on a sheep (羊) that swims with a fish (魚) in a rice field (田) — the ringworm spreads in rings, and the king (王) watches the itchy sheep scratch against the field's four dots (杰).
reading: セン — Say 'sen' (セン) — imagine a centipede crawling in a ring on your skin, causing ringworm — the centipede's name is Sen.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) on a woman's (女) neck, with an eye (目) and a shellfish (貝) stuck inside — the swelling is a goitre, a lump that bulges like a shell.
reading: The goitre makes her neck swell like a **yo-yo** (ヨウ) — it bobs up and down when she swallows.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) with a craft (工) and three stacked strokes (ヨ) — the rash itches, and you crave (addiction) to scratch it, but a thousand (阡) hearts (心) and a claw (爪) hold back — the habit is hard to break.
reading: イン — Imagine an inn (イン) where you get a rash from the bedbugs — you crave the scratch, but the innkeeper says 'no scratching here' — the addiction to scratching is your 'inn' habit.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) sits on an eye (目) and an old bird (隹) — the bird is so thin and emaciated that its eye looks like a sore, and it's too worn out to fly away.
reading: The emaciated old bird is so weak it can only say 'coo' (ク) softly, like a tired pigeon.

meaning: A carbuncle (疔) grows where a curving river (巛) meets a comma-design (巴) under an old bird (隹) — the bird's mouth (口) is swollen with a boil, a painful carbuncle.
reading: The boil throbs with a 'yo' (ヨウ) sound, like a groan echoing from the swollen mouth.

meaning: Paralysis — a carbuncle (疔) strikes a body that has two hands (廾) and an old bird (隹) trapped under leather (革), with a mouth (口) and a large (大) frame, plus a dot (丶), a sweeping stroke (ノ), two (二), and ten (十). The carbuncle makes the limbs go numb, so the hands and bird can't move.
reading: タン — The paralyzed person can only say "tan" (タン) weakly, like a single dull thud, as they try to move but can't.

meaning: Insanity — a carbuncle (疔) on the head makes the eye (目) see a page (頁) full of shellfish (貝) and ten (十) with two splayed strokes (ハ) and a mouth (口) — all jumbled, driving the person mad.
reading: テン — The insane person counts "ten, ten, ten" (テン) over and over, staring at the shellfish on the page, unable to stop.

meaning: Picture a tent with legs spread wide, its two feet planted on the ground like a dotted pattern of footprints. The sweeping strokes on top are the tent's poles, and the dots below are the pegs holding it down.
reading: ハツ — Imagine a tent that 'hatches' open like an egg, cracking its shell with a loud 'hatsu' sound as campers pop out.

meaning: A large 'two' sits under a dotted tent, with a 'one' below — this odd stack marks the 10th calendar sign, a special day in the old cycle.
reading: The 10th sign is a key (キ) date on the calendar — you turn the key to unlock the next cycle.

meaning: A dotted tent (癶) sits on two (二) legs (儿) — the tent is packed up and ready to depart, discharging its contents as it goes.
reading: ハツ — Picture a dotted tent that suddenly 'hatches' (ハツ) open like an egg, and a bird flies out — that's the departure and discharge.

meaning: Two short strokes on top (并) sit above a dotted tent (癶) and beans (口? no, 豆) — you climb up the tent's pole to reach the beans on the shelf.
reading: You 'toe' (トウ) your way up the mountain, step by step.

meaning: A dotted tent on a table, a bow, and a pike with a right hand — the signal to depart and start from the camp, publishing the order.
reading: ハツ — 'Hats off!' — the departure begins, and you throw your hat in the air as the journey starts.

meaning: A day is covered by a lid, and the light that seeps out from under the lid is pure white. The day is hidden, but its whiteness shines through.
reading: ハク — Imagine a 'hack' (like a taxi hack) that is painted entirely white, driving through a bright day, its white paint blinding you.

meaning: A white (白) one (一) is placed on top of a white (白) base — together they form a big white block that stands for a hundred of something.
reading: Imagine a huge white (白) block labeled 'HYAKU' (ヒャク) — you need a hundred of these blocks to build a wall.

meaning: A white spoon sits on a pile of fragrant grain, the steam rising like a ghostly white veil.
reading: The fragrant steam smells like a 'cue' (キュウ) — as in barbecue — rising from the grain.

meaning: Ten days of black clothes — the police runners wore black, and the ten marks their long shifts under the white sun.
reading: The runners' black clothes make them look like 'sow' (ソウ) — a black pig — scurrying through the streets.

meaning: A white face on a pair of legs — the countenance is what you see when the body walks toward you.
reading: The countenance is like a 'bow' (ボウ) — you bow to show your face politely.

meaning: A white (白) dot (丶) inside a wrapping enclosure (勹) — that dot is the bull's eye, the target you aim at, the object of your focus.
reading: The target is 'teki' (テキ) — imagine a 'tech' arrow hitting the bull's eye with a sharp 'TEKI' sound.

meaning: White (白) and compare (比) — when you compare all the white things, you see they're all the same, so 'all' of them are included.
reading: You look at the crowd and say 'kai' (カイ) — like 'kite' but you're flying it over everyone, seeing all of them at once.

meaning: A king (王) above white (白) — the emperor is the white-robed king who rules over all.
reading: コウ — The emperor's crown (コウ) is a golden ring of light, like a halo (コウ) above his head.

meaning: A white thing on a cliff, and a right hand reaching up — the hand pulls you home, arriving at last, leading to a result.
reading: You come home and the key (キ) fits the lock — 'ki' as in 'key' — and the door opens to your arrival.

meaning: A large white bird perches on a ten-marked high bank, looking down at the river — that's the high land along a river.
reading: コウ — Imagine a 'ko' sound: a crow (カラス) says 'ko-ko' as it flies over the high riverbank, and you shout 'コウ!' to it.

meaning: White (白) under a father (父) with a lid (亠) — the moon's white light shines through the father's open lid, making everything bright and white.
reading: The shining white light is 'コウ' (kou) — like 'ko' as in 'glow' but with a 'u' — 'kou, it's so bright'.

meaning: Ten (十) white (白) things sit on two (二) strokes — this is a swampy shore in the fifth month, where white herons stand in pairs on the muddy bank.
reading: In the fifth month, the swamp sounds like 'コウ (kou)' — imagine a frog croaking 'kou, kou' from the shore.

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) over a mouth (口) and soil (土) forms a bright white (白) moon — so white it's clear and shining.
reading: The 'kou' sound is like 'coal' — think of white-hot coal (コウ) glowing so clearly it lights up the night.

meaning: Two white legs under a roof, with a beginning — that's the morning star Venus, shining over the place name皖.
reading: カン — 'Can' you see Venus? It's the 'can' of light in the dawn sky, marking the place.

meaning: An axe chops a white tree, and the fresh wood underneath is clear and pale — the skin is clear and white like that cut surface.
reading: シャク — The axe makes a 'shack' sound as it splits the white wood, revealing the clear grain.

meaning: The white part on top is a snowy mountain, and below it the beans and mouth are frozen solid — everything is white and cold.
reading: The white snow makes you say 'gai' (ガイ) as you gasp in the cold air.

meaning: Under the lid and upside-down box, the tall sun (day) shines on white — that's bright, clear, pure white.
reading: The tall white tower glows with a 'kou' (コウ) light, like a lighthouse beam.

meaning: The king stands on one leg under the esteem, and his white crown shines — he is luminous and hoary.
reading: The king's white robe makes a 'kou' (コウ) sound as it swishes, bright as a royal banner.

meaning: The white sun (day) under the lid and upside-down box is so brilliant it lights up everything.
reading: The brilliant white light makes you shout 'kou' (コウ) — like a bright 'ko' beam.

meaning: A bright white sun (日) shines over a large (大) field with grass on top (艾) — the brilliance is so strong it whitens everything.
reading: The bright light makes you say 'goh' (ゴウ) in awe, like a gasp of wonder — the hook uses the 'ゴウ' sound.

meaning: A white (白) belly over a rice (米) field, with a day (日) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) on top — the person is so corpulent that their white skin is stretched grey and shiny.
reading: The corpulent man's belly goes 'ha' as he pants — the reading is ハ.

meaning: A white (白) sun (日) with a vertical stroke (｜) and a dot (丶) above, plus two (二) ice (冫) strokes — the bright light makes everything clear and brilliant, like looking at oneself (自) in a mirror.
reading: The brilliant light makes you shout 'kou!' (like 'cow' but with a long 'o') — the reading is コウ.

meaning: A strike hits a direction, and the day is white — this is the bright white of a clear sky, so bright you can see every direction clearly, like a white day with no clouds.
reading: キョウ — The bright white light makes you squint and say 'KYO-w!' (キョウ) — like 'kyow' from the glare.

meaning: A white (白) claw (爪) grabs a buy (買) tag, but the day (日) is so bright and clean that the measurement (寸) on the tag is clear — the katakana-mu (厶) shape is washed white, everything is pure and bright.
reading: The bright white light makes everything 'shaku' (シャク) — like a clean, sharp 'shock' of clarity.

meaning: A right hand (又) peels back the skin or pelt of an animal, holding the hide like a leather sheet.
reading: ヒ — Picture a HE (ヒ) — a male deer — whose pelt is being pulled off by a right hand, leaving raw hide.

meaning: A pimple is a small bump on the pelt, wrapped by the skin — the right hand squeezes it, but the stop sign says don't.
reading: The pimple pops with a 'hō' (ホウ) — like 'hoe' — as you dig it out of the skin.

meaning: A pelt (皮) is gripped by a right hand (又) while a pair of legs (儿) kicks and a katakana-mu shape (厶) twists — the stooping figure (夂) bends over, and the whole scene leaves the skin with wrinkles, cracking, and creases.
reading: The skin cracks like a dry riverbed in the sun — think of a shriveled 'shun' (シュン) of a peach left out too long.

meaning: A pelt (皮) stretched over a rough surface, like a drum (鼓) with no skin — the texture is rough and cracked, so you remember it as rough skin.
reading: The rough skin feels like a 'サ' (sa) — imagine sandpaper scraping your arm with a harsh 'sa-sa-sa' sound.

meaning: A drum (鼓) with a pelt (皮) stretched tight, but a gentleman (士) beats it with a right hand (又) holding a branch (支) — the drum is beaten to rouse people.
reading: The drum goes 'コ' (ko) — imagine a big 'ko' sound echoing as the drum is struck, like 'KO!' in a boxing match.

meaning: A car (車) with a crown (冖) on top, and a pelt (皮) underneath — the pelt has cracks from the car's weight, like skin cracks in winter.
reading: The skin cracks make a 'クン' (kun) sound — imagine a 'クン' as a dog whining over its cracked paws.

meaning: Same as 皸 — a car (車) with a crown (冖) presses on a pelt (皮), causing rough cracks, but here the pelt is even more worn, like old leather.
reading: The cracks go 'キン' (kin) — imagine a 'キン' as the sharp ping of ice cracking on a frozen pelt.

meaning: The pelt on the left is held by a right hand, and the wrapping enclosure squeezes it — making wrinkles and folds.
reading: The wrinkled pelt makes a 'shuu' (シュウ) sound as you fold it, like shuffling paper.

meaning: A lid sits on a box, and under it a day and a branch are pressed by a right hand — the skin flakes off like dry scurf from that squeezed surface.
reading: テン — Imagine a 'ten' (テン)nis ball bouncing on a patch of scurf, and each bounce flicks off more flakes.

meaning: A dish is a flat plate — imagine it as a simple, round surface, like a plate you put food on, with no parts to confuse you.
reading: ベイ — Say "bay" — picture a dish full of bay leaves, a helping of herbs on a plate.

meaning: A dish with a barb and two — the barb hooks the two sides of the dish, making a deep bowl for offerings.
reading: You fill the bowl with 'oo' (ウ) — a long, hollow sound as you pour water into it.

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) and one (一) sit above a dish (皿) — this is a shallow cup or glass, like a sake cup that holds just a little.
reading: You raise the glass to say 'hai!' (ハイ) — a toast where the cup clinks and you shout 'hai!' before drinking.

meaning: A vertical stroke goes into a mouth, and that mouth sits on a dish — a small cup or bowl, just big enough for a sip.
reading: The small cup is so tiny you say 'CHOO' (チュウ) like a little mouse sip — 'choo' as in 'choo-choo' but short.

meaning: A dish (皿) sits on a table (几) with two splayed strokes (ハ) on top, like a tray holding offerings during the Lantern Festival — so this is a basin/tray.
reading: The festival tray is called a 'bon' — imagine a big bass drum (ボン) being carried on the tray during the parade.

meaning: A sweeping stroke and a 'one' on a dish, plus a right hand — the hand fills the dish to fullness, enough to satisfy.
reading: You fill the dish until it's full, and you say 'AY' (エイ) like a satisfied sigh — 'ay' as in 'say' but with a long 'a'.

meaning: One (一) dish (皿) with two splayed strokes (ハ) and two short strokes on top (并) — the extra strokes are the profit piled onto the dish, a benefit added to what you already have.
reading: The EGG (エキ) in the dish is the profit — you gain an extra egg for your breakfast.

meaning: A bowl with a seal on the rim, filled with evening rice — the dish is deep enough to hold a cup of soup.
reading: This bowl is a 'wan' (ワン) — like 'one' — the one dish you always use.

meaning: A dish with soil and a katakana-mu shape on top — they all come together under a cover, meeting in one place.
reading: コウ — Picture a 'ko' sound: a koala (コアラ) sits on a dish, and all its friends come together to cover it with soil, saying 'コウ, コウ!'

meaning: A large mouth of a dish — this cup is so abundant it overflows, a pot that holds more than you'd think.
reading: The abundant cup goes 'ō' (オウ) — like 'oh' — as you see how much it holds.

meaning: A dish (皿) with a mouth (口) and a hat on top (个) plus one (一) — the covered utensil has a lid that fits over the dish like a hat.
reading: You open the covered box and say 'コウ' (kou) — 'kou, what's in this box?'

meaning: A one (一) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) sit above fire (火), all resting on a dish (皿). The dish is a helmet bowl, and the fire inside heats it like a metal basin for forging.
reading: カイ — The helmet is a 'kai' (like a kayak paddle) — you wear it while paddling through fire, and the dish catches the sparks.

meaning: A king (王) places a dish (皿) on top of a sheep (羊) — the dish is the lid covering the sheep, and the two short strokes (并) on top are the handle of the lid.
reading: The lid goes on with a loud GAI (ガイ) — like a heavy metal gate slamming shut over the dish.

meaning: Ice (冫) melts into water that drips into a dish (皿), but you lack (欠) it — so you steal the dish. The thief takes what you don't have.
reading: A thief sneaks in and says 'toe' (トウ) as he tiptoes — like 'toe' as in the foot part, stepping quietly to rob.

meaning: A dot (丶) sits on a ten (十) above a month (月) — that's the square outside — and the whole thing rests on a dish (皿), which is round inside, making a basket for boiled grain in State worship.
reading: The priest 'foo' (フ) — like a chef saying 'foo' — carefully places the grain basket on the altar.

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) cuts a halberd (戈) across a dish (皿) — the dish overflows with food, making the household boom and prosper.
reading: セイ — Say 'say' (セイ) as you pile food high on a dish — the feast makes everyone say 'more!' and the business prospers.

meaning: Water at the side (汁) spills from a dish (皿) as a lack (欠) of care — that's the thief's sloppy grab, stealing the offering.
reading: The thief 'toe' (トウ) — imagine a big toe sneaking out of a sandal to hook the dish away.

meaning: A halberd rests on a dish — the dish is a shallow sake cup, ready to be filled for a warrior's toast.
reading: サン — The halberd clinks against the dish with a 'san' ring, like a bell for a toast.

meaning: A month (月) and a day (日) are placed on a dish (皿) — that's the oath of alliance, sworn over time and light.
reading: Mei — imagine two leaders swearing an oath over a dish, saying 'Mei' (like 'may') as they seal the alliance for a month and a day.

meaning: Three stacked strokes (ヨ) pour a dish (皿) of liquid, while a brush (聿) writes until the ink is gone — you exhaust every drop, using it all up.
reading: You use up everything, and say 'ジン' (jin) — imagine a genie (jin) who exhausts all his wishes in one go.

meaning: A retainer (臣) with a dish (皿) and two (二) splayed strokes (ハ) above — this is the official who oversees the ritual offerings, watching over the dish to ensure everything is done correctly.
reading: カン — Picture a KAN of soup (a big metal pot) being overseen by the retainer, who watches the dish (皿) to make sure the soup doesn't boil over.

meaning: A boat (舟) carries a dish (皿) on a table (几), while a pike (殳) and a right hand (又) hold it steady — this is a tray or platter for serving.
reading: Picture a big banquet (バン) where a boat-shaped tray is passed around — the tray is the 盤, and the banquet is full of praise for the food.

meaning: A mortar sits on a dish, and water pours over it — you wash your hands in this tub, catching the water in the dish below.
reading: The kanji looks like a tub with water — imagine a big 'kan' (can) used as a washbasin, filled with water.

meaning: A hat on top covers a one-dot mark, and a west-facing mortar sits on a dish — that's the lid of a cauldron, sealing the pot below.
reading: アン — The lid clamps down with an 'unh' sound as it seals the cauldron tight.

meaning: A tiger spots (虍) sit on a cliff (厂) above a dish (皿) with a rice field (田) and a divining rod (卜) and a spoon (匕) — a simple hut where a tiger lives, with a dish for food.
reading: The hut is a 'ro' (ロ) — picture a low, round hut with a 'ro' (like a row of stones) as its foundation.

meaning: Water at the side (汁) pours into a dish (皿) while a wrapping enclosure (勹) holds a day (日) and a one (一) — the heat melts the metal, and you are charmed by the flowing liquid.
reading: The melted metal flows 'tou' (like 'toe' but with a 'u' sound) — the reading is トウ.

meaning: A retainer (臣) sits by a box-on-side enclosure (匚) holding dry (干) goods, but a dish (皿) with a mouth (口) and ten (十) marks shows this is a place for leisure — a salt pit where workers take breaks and drink.
reading: The salt pit is so deep you can hear a 'ko' echo from the bottom — like a crow's 'caw' (コ) bouncing off the walls.

meaning: A single eye drawn as a vertical rectangle with a pupil line — this is the eye itself, and by extension, a look or insight.
reading: Picture an eye that says 'MOKE' (モク) like a gentle 'moke' sound as it blinks slowly.

meaning: A barb (亅) and two (二) lines sit above an eye — the eye is forced wide open by the barb, staring in astonishment.
reading: ク — A cow says “moo” but this eye says “ku!” — imagine a shocked eye popping open with a “ku!” sound as you see a giant cow.

meaning: The deceased (亡) person's eye (目) is covered by a lid (亠) — they are blind, unable to see.
reading: A blind man named Mo (モウ) stumbles into a moat (モウ) — 'mou'!

meaning: Ten (十) eyes (目) and a vertical stroke (｜) plus one (一) — all lined up straight, so you can fix things directly.
reading: You fix it 'CHO' (like 'chop') — a straight chop cuts through the problem — チョク.

meaning: A tree (木) and an eye (目) look at each other — the tree sees the eye, and the eye sees the tree, so they are mutual, together, each other.
reading: ソウ — Imagine two trees (木) and an eye (目) all singing 'sow' (ソウ) together — they are mutual partners in a chorus.

meaning: The eye is heavy, and the open box enclosure is like a little bed you sink into. The barracks nearby are quiet, so you nod off — that's a doze.
reading: シュン — You 'shoon' off to sleep, like a quick nap that's over before you know it.

meaning: The eye stares hard, and the one line below is like a furrowed brow. The wrapping enclosure holds in all your effort — you glare at your work and toil on.
reading: ケイ — You give a sharp 'kay' (like 'kay?') glare at someone who's slacking, then go back to toiling.

meaning: The eye looks out, and the two splayed strokes are like two hands reaching forward. The sword is sheathed — you're not fighting, just gazing and hoping for something to come.
reading: ハン — You 'han' (like 'hand') over your hope, gazing at the horizon for a sign.

meaning: An eye peeks through a ten-shaped slit in a shield, while an axe and a cliff guard the back — the shield is both a defense and a pretext to hide behind.
reading: ジュン — Picture a soldier shouting 'JUN!' as he raises his shield, the axe bouncing off with a dull 'jun' thud.

meaning: A little eye (小 + 目) sits under a sweeping stroke (ノ) that acts like a lid — this is the government ministry's seal, which also tells you to conserve resources and omit what's unnecessary.
reading: The ministry official says 'SHOW' (セイ) you the budget cuts — he literally shows you what to omit.

meaning: The eye is on the side, and the mountain is in the way — you can't look straight, so you glance askance. The one line and the barb are like a crooked fence you peek around.
reading: ベン — You 'ben' your head sideways to get that askance look, like a bird checking for danger.

meaning: The eye looks through the direction marker, but everything is blurry — you can't tell which way is which. It's all indistinct, like a foggy path.
reading: ホウ — You 'how' (like 'how?') can you see anything? It's so indistinct you can't even guess the direction.

meaning: The eye is squeezed, and the little stroke on top is like a tiny squint. The sweeping stroke below is a thin slit — you see only a minute sliver of the world.
reading: ビョウ — You 'byo' (like 'bio') — a tiny, squinting look at something microscopic, so small it's almost nothing.

meaning: The eye is under a crown, but the crooked-big part below is what it watches — the eye is fixed on that twisted, large shape, so you watch intently.
reading: A tiger (タン) crouches low, its eye locked on prey — the sound of its low growl is 'tan-tan-tan' as it watches intently.

meaning: An eyebrow sits above the eye (目) under a flag (尸) with a vertical stroke (｜) – the flag is the brow line.
reading: ビ sounds like 'bee' – a bee landed on your eyebrow.

meaning: The eye sees a hook stroke and a sweeping stroke tangled with a one — everything looks blurry and dim, so the eye can't see clearly.
reading: You feel 'bow' (ボウ) — like a dim-sighted old man who bumps into a bow (弓) because he can't see it clearly.

meaning: A hand shades one eye above a two-eyed face — you watch over the scene from above.
reading: A guard shouts 'KAN!' (カン) as he sees a thief — he watches over the gate with a hand over his eye.

meaning: A little eye (小 + 目) is the prefecture's symbol — it watches over the whole region from above, like a tiny lookout.
reading: The prefecture's governor is a KEN (ケン) doll — think of a Barbie KEN standing on a map, pointing at his territory.

meaning: Show the eye the two little marks — that's how you inspect and observe what's written on the tablet.
reading: You 'shi' (シ) — like 'she' — looks at the eye to see what's shown.

meaning: A hat on top presses down on an eye, while three lines of tears are held back — the eye shows restraint, not letting them fall.
reading: シン — Imagine a 'shin' guard placed over your eye to restrain a kick, the hat on top keeping it in place.

meaning: The katakana-mu shape is a person staring, with a mouth open in awe — the eye is fixed, gazing at something far away.
reading: チ — A 'chee' (cheese) photo moment: you gaze at the camera, mouth saying 'chee' while your eye stays locked.

meaning: Life (生) is seen through an eye (目) that is diseased — a fault in the eye brings crime and disease of vision.
reading: セイ — 'Say' (セイ) — you say 'say' when you see a fault in your eye, like a doctor diagnosing a disease.

meaning: The eye is under a tree, but the tree's two splayed strokes and the vertical stroke block the light, making everything dark.
reading: In the dark, you bump into a 'my' (マイ) — imagine saying 'my!' as you stumble in the gloom.

meaning: Two splayed strokes sit above an eye, and a spoon rests below — the truth is what you see clearly, not what the spoon stirs up.
reading: The truth is 'shin' (シン) — like a shin bone, bare and real, no lies covering it.

meaning: One ten under two splayed strokes, with an eye below — the eye sees the true reality, not the illusion, the real form of things.
reading: シン — Picture a 'shin' (シン) — the shin bone is the true, real part of the leg you see when you look closely, the reality beneath the skin.

meaning: Your eye (目) is closed, and a flag (尸) waves over your family name (氏) — you are so sleepy you can't even read your own name, so you sleep (and maybe die) right there.
reading: ミン — The sleepy person mumbles 'MIN' (like 'min' in 'minimum') as they drift off, unable to keep their eye open.

meaning: An eye (目) under a seal (卩) and evening (夕) — the eye has no brightness, like a sealed jar in the dark evening.
reading: ワン — 'Wan' (ワン) — a dog's 'wan' bark in the evening, but the eye is dull and sees no light.

meaning: The eye glances at a spoon and a flag — the spoon is the quick glance, the flag marks the spot you keep returning to.
reading: A quick glance at the flag makes you say 'kei' (ケイ) — like 'kay' as in 'okay, I see it.'

meaning: The eye (目) stops (止) at the outer corner, where a spoon (匕) pokes out — that's the outside corner of the eye.
reading: You see the corner of the eye and think 'SEH' (セ) — like saying 'saw' with a lisp, as you squint to see it.

meaning: The eye (目) stops (止) at the corner, and a spoon (匕) digs into the socket — that's the corner of the eye and the socket around it.
reading: The corner of the eye is where you feel a sharp 'SEH' (セ) — like a splinter of glass cutting the socket.

meaning: The eye (目) is under a lid (亠) with a sweeping stroke (ノ) and a hook stroke (乙) — a quick blink that winks, closing and opening the eye in a flash.
reading: ソウ — Imagine a 'sow' (pig) winking at you with one eye, the wink being the 眨 action.

meaning: A mysterious (玄) eye (目) under a lid (亠) with a short thread (幺) — the eye spins with mystery, making you feel faint and dizzy.
reading: ゲン — 'Gen' (like 'genie') spins your head with a dizzying magical swirl, making you faint.

meaning: An eye (目) with rice (米) stuck in it — the rice blinds you, so you can't see clearly.
reading: You're blinded by rice and stumble, saying 'MAI' (マイ) — like 'my eye!' in pain.

meaning: A wrapping enclosure (勹) wraps around the day (日), and an eye (目) watches — you're dazzled by the bright day, and you signal with your eyes to shade it.
reading: ケン — The dazzled eye blinks 'ken' (like a kendo mask) — the bright day makes you squint like a fighter.

meaning: The evening (夕) has fallen, and your eye (目) is covered with a film — you can't see clearly, everything is dim and diseased.
reading: The eye (目) is so dim you see only a 'she' (シ) — like a ghostly 'she' in the fog.

meaning: The eye (目) sits inside a box-on-side enclosure (匚) that is guarded by a king (王) — that bony rim is the eye socket, the edge of the eyelid.
reading: The king (王) in the box (匚) shouts 'KYO!' (キョウ) as he pokes your eye socket.

meaning: A person (人) with two short strokes on top (并) and a large (大) heart looks at your eye (目) — they turn back to gaze at you with affection.
reading: The person turns back and says 'Ken!' (ケン) — like calling a beloved dog's name, full of fondness.

meaning: A cow (牛) has a katakana-mu shape (厶) floating in its eye (目) — that dark spot is the pupil, the very center of the gaze.
reading: The cow's pupil is a 'bow' (ボウ) — like a tiny bow in the eye, ready to shoot a glance.

meaning: Two splayed strokes (ハ) and two short strokes on top (并) sit above a large (大) eye (目) — that's the pupil, the dark window in the middle.
reading: The pupil is a tiny 'chin' (チン) — like a chin in the eye, jutting out to see.

meaning: To stare, you use your eye (目) while standing on a pair of legs (儿) on a block of ice (冫) — you're frozen in place, just watching.
reading: You 'CHO' — like 'chow' — as you stare at a bowl of food, your eyes fixed on the meal while your legs stand on ice.

meaning: The eye (目) is the part that looks northeast (艮) — the eyeball itself, the round thing that rolls in your socket.
reading: The eyeball is a 'gan' (ガン) — imagine a cannon (gan) shooting an eyeball out of its socket, rolling toward the northeast.

meaning: A dot (丶) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) cross over the eye (目) — that's a sly glance, an ogle from the corner of the eye.
reading: The ogle is a 'baku' (バク) — like a dream-eating baku peeking at you with one eye.

meaning: A vertical stroke and a sweeping stroke cross over a person, and then a person at the side and a person under a mouth (the 買 part) all crowd together — this is a mass of people, a multitude.
reading: Imagine a huge crowd all shouting 'SHOE!' as they stampede through a shoe store — the sound 'shu' is in 'SHOE'.

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) over a king (王) with two short strokes on top (并) and an eye (目) — the sheep (羊) arrives wearing its wool, and you wear it too.
reading: You arrive at the door and ring the bell — "CHAKU!" like a clock ticking — チャク.

meaning: A one (一) and a ten (十) form a dry (干) pole, and under a day (日) an eye (目) stares — the eye is so big it fills the whole scene, big-eyed.
reading: The big eye glares like a 'kan' (カン) — think of a tin can with a huge painted eye on it.

meaning: Two (二) legs (儿) stand under a roof (宀) at the beginning (元) — and an eye (目) looks out, bright and clear from that sheltered spot.
reading: The bright eye shines like a 'wan' (ワン) — a dog's bright eye in a bowl, saying 'wan!'

meaning: A vertical stroke (｜) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) cross a bow (弓), and two short strokes on top (并) sit above an eye (目) — the eye glances sideways, looking askance at the odd shape.
reading: You 'day' (ダイ) — like 'die' — but you only glance sideways, not straight on, because you're too shy to look directly.

meaning: A mouth (口) is open next to a month (月) while an eye (目) watches sideways — you're glancing at someone from the corner of your eye, not staring straight.
reading: The eye (目) gives a sly 'en' glance, like saying 'en?' to ask 'what?' while looking askance.

meaning: A pair of legs (儿) trembles under a see (見) that is also an eye (目) — you're looking at something scary, so you're over-cautious and fearful.
reading: You 'ken' your eyes shut in fear, like 'ken' in 'kennel' where a scared dog hides.

meaning: An eye (目) under a towel (巾) that's inside an upside-down box (冂) with a one (一), a vertical stroke (｜), a dot (丶), and a sweeping stroke (ノ) — you're peeking out from under a cloth, longing to see something far away.
reading: You 'kee' (key) your eye to the keyhole, gazing longingly through it.

meaning: A tree (木) is trapped in a box (囗) while an eye (目) watches — the tree is tired and sleepy, just like you when you're stuck in a boring room.
reading: You 'konk' out (fall asleep) — the tree in the box goes 'konk' as it nods off.

meaning: An eye watches a fire flicker — the glance is quick, a peep at the glittering flames that shine and dance.
reading: セン — The eye darts to the fire with a 'sen' — like a quick 'sensor' detecting the glow.

meaning: A stooping figure (夂) stands on soil (土) under two splayed strokes (ハ), staring straight ahead with a wide eye (目) — they are so focused they don't move, just stare straight ahead.
reading: The stooping figure stares straight ahead at a giant 'cho' (チョウ) — like a choo-choo train — and won't look away until it passes.

meaning: The eye (目) is wrapped in a circle of soil (土) and a stooping figure (夂) — the whole shape is round, and the eye stares roundly at everything around it.
reading: The round eye stares at a 'rin' (リン) — a ring — and the ring is perfectly round, just like the eye's stare.

meaning: A cliff (厂) drops down to soil (土), and an eye (目) at the edge glares angrily at the drop — the glare is sharp like the cliff's edge.
reading: The angry glare hits you like a 'gai' (ガイ) — a guy who just stepped on a nail — his face is all glare.

meaning: The eye (目) looks at a blue (青) lid (亠) over two (二) lines of soil (土) — the pupil is the dark center of the eye, like the blue iris around it.
reading: The pupil is so clear you can see a 'sei' (セイ) — a 'say' — like a wise saying written in the blue of the eye.

meaning: A claw (爪) pulls up a barb (亅) from three stacked strokes (ヨ) — the eye (目) opens wide in surprise, staring at the claw's action.
reading: The eye opens wide and stares at a 'sei' (セイ) — a 'sail' — that suddenly unfurls, making the eye open and stare.

meaning: A person (人) stands by a tree (木), and the eye (目) squints at them from the side — a sidelong glance, not a full look.
reading: The sidelong glance is a 'rai' (ライ) — like a 'rye' field — you squint sideways at the tall rye stalks.

meaning: A lid sits on top of a person, who holds up ten eyes — all of them clear and bright, so you can see through them perfectly. This is the state of being clear-eyed.
reading: スイ — Imagine a clear-eyed sushi chef (スイ) who can spot a single grain of rice from across the room.

meaning: A large seal stamps a document with two short strokes, while an eye watches over it — this is the act of caring for and loving what you oversee.
reading: ケン — Picture a caring guardian named Ken (ケン) who lovingly watches over a child with his big eye.

meaning: An eye (目) with a vertical stroke (｜), a sweeping stroke (ノ), and a one (一) — the eye droops, heavy with drowsiness, about to close.
reading: You feel 'SUI' — a soft, sinking sigh as your eyelids fall, like the whisper of 'sweet' sleep.

meaning: An old bird perches on an eye, staring straight ahead without blinking — the bird is uninhibited, and the eye is wide open, gazing at you.
reading: キ — The old bird says "キー!" as it stares, a sharp cry that cuts through the silence.

meaning: A little (小) divining rod (卜) in a right hand (又) points at an eye (目) — the coach commands and urges you to look and lead.
reading: Toku — imagine a coach shouting 'Toku!' (like 'talk to') at you, pointing with a rod at your eye to get you moving.

meaning: A rice field sits on top of an eye, with ten stalks growing from it — you glare at the field because someone trampled it, and your eye narrows in anger.
reading: ヘイ — You glare at the hay (ヘイ) stack that fell on your rice field, your eye burning with rage.

meaning: Soil (土) and an eye (目) sit on a pair of legs (儿) — when people are intimate and friendly, they stand close together, looking into each other's eyes on the same ground.
reading: ボク — Boku the friend gives you a warm hug, and you say "Boku, you're so friendly!" as you feel the harmony between you.

meaning: A mortar sits on an eye, and a pair of legs kicks it — the eye scowls at the legs, glaring with authority and power.
reading: ゲイ — The scowling eye is a gay (ゲイ) detective who glares at suspects with absolute authority.

meaning: A dry soil mound with two short strokes on top, under a lid, and a buy sign — an eye spies on the whole scene from above, watching the transaction.
reading: エキ — The spy uses an echo (エキ) device to listen in on the secret buy deal, his eye glued to the scene.

meaning: A vertical stroke (｜) pierces three stacked strokes (ヨ) that run (走) over soil (土) and an eye (目) — the eye's lashes are like tiny strokes brushing over the dirt below.
reading: Imagine a show (ショウ) where the eyelashes are so long they sweep the stage floor like brooms.

meaning: A tree (木) with a claw (爪) over an eye (目) — the tree is watching you, so you must notice it and pay attention to it.
reading: The tree (木) with the claw (爪) and eye (目) is a 'サイ' (sai) — like a 'サイ' (sai) the weapon, which you must notice and pay attention to in a fight.

meaning: An old man (老) with a day (日) in his eye (目) — he looks at the sun all day, so he sees clearly, but only if he looks directly.
reading: You look at it and say 'ト' (to) — imagine pointing at something and saying 'to' as in 'to look at that!'

meaning: A large eye stares out from under a one-stroke lid, with a dot and a sweeping stroke crossing it — this is the stare of someone who is lost or separated, looking hard for a way back.
reading: The stare is so intense it makes you say 'ケイ' (like 'kay?') as if asking 'are you looking at me?'

meaning: A lid (亠) on top of ten (十) spicy (辛) soil (土) buys (買) an eye (目) that stands up (立) — that's your testicles.
reading: The testicles are like an eye (目) wearing kohl (コウ) makeup.

meaning: A crown covers a hat, and under that an eye looks through two splayed strokes and a divining rod — this is the sharp, imperial intelligence that sees through everything.
reading: The imperial eye is so bright it shines like 'エイ' (like 'A' in 'ace') — the ace of all seers.

meaning: A マ-shaped stroke sits on a halberd, and a strike hits the eye — the eye is so blurred and nearsighted it can only look closely, seeing dim shapes.
reading: You squint so hard you mumble 'ボツ' (like 'bots' — small, blurry dots) — everything looks like tiny bots.

meaning: Grass on top grows over a rice field, and an eye below takes aim — you focus your eye through the grass to aim at a target in the field.
reading: You take aim and whisper 'ビョウ' (like 'byo' — the sound of a bowstring) — then release.

meaning: The eye under the ten and two splayed strokes is wide open — that's the look of being angry.
reading: When angry, you 'shin' (シン) — like a sharp 'shin' kick of frustration.

meaning: The katakana-mu shape sits on soil, holding a dish under an eye — the eye is so heavy it droops onto the dish, and you doze off right there.
reading: Imagine a sleepy crow (コウ) perched on a dish, its eye closing as it coos 'kooo' — the sound of dozing off.

meaning: A blind eye has no pupil — the mortar grinds away the eye's center, leaving only a branch and a right hand groping in the dark.
reading: ソウ — A 'sow' (pig) is blind, bumping into the mortar with its eye closed.

meaning: A mouth under a lid and a roof, with two lines over an eye — the eye is covered by the roof and lid, so it's blind or one-eyed.
reading: A blind pirate shouts 'KATSU!' (カツ) as he bumps into a wall, his one eye squeezed shut.

meaning: The day (日) is covered by a lid (亠) and a crown (冖), while two splayed strokes (ハ) pull the eye (目) shut. That’s closing your eyes to sleep — everything dark and covered.
reading: You 'mei' (メイ) your eyes shut — like 'may' I sleep now?

meaning: A cataract clouds the eye — a stand-up day and a sound (like a bell) are blurred behind a film, seen through the eye's lens.
reading: ショウ — 'Show' — the cataract makes the world a blurry show, like looking through frosted glass.

meaning: A film over the eye — a dart, a pike, and a large hand with a sweeping stroke all press down on the eye, while a box-on-side enclosure holds the blur.
reading: エイ — 'Aye' — you squint and say 'aye' but can't see clearly through the film.

meaning: Deception — an eye peeks through an upside-down box, while an open box enclosure hides the truth, and a vertical stroke with one enter slips past the eye.
reading: マン — 'Man' — the man lies, covering his eye with a box to deceive you.

meaning: A squinting eye (目) under a west (西) sun, with a little (小) show (示) of two (二) fingers — you glare sideways, searching for something in the glare.
reading: ヒョウ — Picture a 'hyo' (like a sneeze) as you squint and glare at a bright light, the sound escaping your lips while your eyes stay narrowed.

meaning: Your eye (目) is wide open, staring at a mouth (口) that is held up by esteem (尚) — but the soil (土) under it is covered by a crown (冖), so you stare intently, amazed.
reading: ドウ — Imagine a 'dough' (ドウ) ball rolling toward you, and you stare at it so intently your eyes go wide, unable to look away.

meaning: Your eye (目) is under a crown (冖) and grass on top (艾), like a buy (買) that's hidden — your eyesight is obscured, and you feel ashamed because you can't see clearly.
reading: ボウ — Picture a 'bow' (ボウ) of grass covering your eyes, making everything blurry — you feel ashamed and can't see, like a blindfolded archer.

meaning: An eye (目) with a sweeping stroke (ノ) and a day (日) inside a wrapping enclosure (勹) — the eyelid twitches uncontrollably, like a muscle spasm under the skin.
reading: The twitch makes you blink 'jun' (like 'June' but shorter) — the reading is ジュン.

meaning: A vertical stroke strikes the towel of esteem, but the eye (under the upside-down box) only gets a quick glance — you barely see it before the strike moves on.
reading: ベツ — Picture a quick glance at a BET (ベツ) — you only see the letters 'bet' for a split second before the towel covers them.

meaning: The eye is on the left, and on the right the old bird sits on four dots at the bottom — you glance at the bird's nest of dots, just a quick look, not a stare.
reading: The old bird (隹) says 'ショウ' — imagine it shouting 'SHOW!' as you glance at it, like a bird showing off its feathers.

meaning: The eye is fixed on the gate (門) — you watch carefully through the gate, staring at what's beyond, not letting it out of sight.
reading: No reading given — use the meaning hook: your eye is glued to the gate, so you 'focus on' it, like a guard watching a gate.

meaning: The eye stares at a mouth (口) that sits on beans (豆) with two short strokes on top (并) — you stare so hard at that bean-mouth that your eye bulges.
reading: The beans (豆) make you think of 'トウ' — imagine a bean that says 'TOH!' as you stare at it, like a magic bean that shouts.

meaning: A cow's eye (目) is covered by a claw (爪) that flicks open and shut, while dancing (舛) legs move in the evening (夕) under a crown (冖) — that's the blink of an eye, a twinkle.
reading: In a blink, a 'SHUN' (like 'shun' in 'shun the light') — you shun the bright flash by blinking quickly.

meaning: The eye is under the little (小) and day (日), with two short strokes (并) on top — the day is clear and bright, so your eye sees everything clearly, no fog.
reading: The day (日) is clear, and you say 'リョウ' — imagine a clear day where you can see a 'RYO' (a Japanese inn) far away, perfectly visible.

meaning: An eye peeks through the gap in the gate, while a month passes — you spy on someone for a whole month, using a sideways glance through the slats.
reading: カン — picture a 'can' (tin can) with a tiny hole, and you peep through it to spy on someone — the sound 'kan' is in 'can'.

meaning: An ear, an eye, and a strike — you strike a pose on a high place, using your ear and eye to look down and see everything below, like a hawk from above.
reading: カン — imagine a 'can' (tin can) used as a periscope — you look through it to see far away, and the sound 'kan' is in 'can'.

meaning: An eye looks at a ri (village) where a stand up is planted — the pupil reflects the whole scene.
reading: ドウ — 'Doe' (a deer) has a big pupil in its eye, and you see a ri in it.

meaning: In the evening, an eye stares at rice grains scattered on a dancing floor — the eye is fixed, unblinking, watching every grain.
reading: The eye stares so hard it makes a 'リン' (ring) of tension around the pupil — like a bell ringing in your head as you stare.

meaning: A vertical stroke and one shellfish sit above a mouth, all under an eye — the eye sees everything, from the single shellfish to the open mouth below.
reading: The eye sees everything, so it says 'キ' (key) — it holds the key to all knowledge, unlocking every secret in sight.

meaning: A heart (心) hides under a crown (冖) while a claw (爪) covers an eye (目) — the stooping figure (夂) can't see clearly, so everything stays hidden and unclear.
reading: The hidden thing is 'ai' — like saying 'I' (アイ) but you can't see who it is.

meaning: A say-word is spoken from a cliff, and a pair of legs under a wrapping enclosure look at the eye — they look at the speaker.
reading: セン — A 'sen' (セン)ator on a cliff looks down at the crowd, making a speech — everyone looks at him.

meaning: A person with a hat on top has a mouth and an eye, but two short strokes on top of a one — the eyelids close over the eye.
reading: ケン — A 'ken' (ケン)do fighter blinks — his eyelids close fast as he blocks a strike.

meaning: A gentleman (士) beats a drum (鼓) with a branch (支) and a right hand (又), but the blind person (目) can't see it — only hears the sound, with beans (豆) and two short strokes (并) nearby.
reading: The blind person says 'ko' (コ) — like a knock on the drum, 'ko-ko'.

meaning: An old bird with two big eyes (目) stares at you — this is the face of a surname that looks like it's watching you, startled. The two 目 are the bird's wide-open eyes, and the 隹 is the bird itself.
reading: The old bird's eyes go 'ク' (coo) — like a pigeon's soft call, 'coo-coo' — as it watches you.

meaning: A pig (豕) is hidden under grass on top (艾) and a crown (冖) — but your eye (目) can't see it clearly, so you are blind to what's underneath.
reading: You're blind, so you feel your way with a 'モウ' (mow) — like mowing grass blindly, you just swing and hope.

meaning: A roof over an eye that is glaring at a shellfish — the shellfish is so annoying that the eye opens wide with anger, giving an angry glare.
reading: ヒン — Picture a HINd (hind legs of a deer) kicking up dust as it glares angrily at you, its eyes wide open.

meaning: A right hand grabs an old bird's eyes — surprise and confusion make you look around wildly, eyes darting like a startled bird.
reading: You go 'KAKU' in shock — a sharp, startled 'KAKU' as the bird flies off.

meaning: Tiger spots on a cliff above a rice field — the pupil of the eye is like a dark spot in the field, and you see it clearly from the cliff.
reading: ロ — Imagine a LO (low) spot in the rice field where the pupil of an eye is visible — you see it from the cliff.

meaning: See, witness, inspect — an eye (目) looks closely at a short thread (幺) and a thread (糸) wrapped around a little (小) object, while a say (言) records what is seen. The eye inspects every detail of the threads and the spoken words.
reading: バン — Imagine a witness in a courtroom saying "ban!" (バン) as they point at the threads, having inspected them carefully to give testimony.

meaning: Three vertical strokes (｜) rise like tall grass, each topped with an eye (目) and a ten (十) crossbar — imagine a field of luxuriant, overgrown stalks so thick you can't see through them.
reading: The stalks are so thick they block the road, and you shout 'CHOKE!' (チョク) as you push through the greenery.

meaning: To view — you strike the gate with your eye, and through the gap you see an ear listening, while the ユ-shaped stroke is the crack you peek through.
reading: カン — You KANnot see clearly, so you squint through the gate crack to get a better view.

meaning: An eye looks at a buy sign, but a wrapping enclosure and a flag hide it — you must look intently to see what's inside the wrapped package.
reading: You stare so hard your eye goes 'shoku' — like a shock 'shoku' when you finally see what's inside.

meaning: A halberd is a weapon shaped like a マ-shaped stroke (マ) — the blade curves like that stroke, ready for battle.
reading: ム — Picture a festival float carrying a giant halberd, and the crowd shouts "MOO!" like cows, because the float is pulled by oxen.

meaning: A halberd holds a hat on top, and under that hat is a マ-shaped stroke and a one — the halberd stands tall with pride, and you respect its strength.
reading: The king (キン) wears a hat on his halberd — he is proud and demands respect, so you bow to the 'kin' of the king.

meaning: A halberd (矛) pierces a mouth (口) inside an upside-down box (冂) with a マ-shaped stroke (マ) and two splayed strokes (ハ) — you bore a hole with an awl, making something bright and charming.
reading: You 'itsu' (it's) a bright idea to bore with an awl — 'itsu' sounds like 'it's' as in 'it's sharp!'

meaning: A halberd (矛) with a month (月) and esteem (尚) — the 8-foot lance is so long it's like a month's worth of halberd, and you esteem it highly.
reading: You 'saku' (sock) someone with the 8-foot lance — 'saku' sounds like 'sock' as in punch.

meaning: A large (大) sweeping stroke (ノ) is the arrow's shaft, and the one (一) line is the bowstring drawn back — the whole thing is a dart or arrow ready to fly.
reading: The arrow's tip is a sharp シ (shi) — imagine a snake's tongue hissing 'shi' as the dart zips past.

meaning: A dart flies past the katakana-mu shape and the 乞-shaped hook — the sentence particle ends the thought with a sharp stop.
reading: The dart's flight ends with an 'ee' (イ) sound — a squeak as it hits the target.

meaning: A mouth shoots a dart at the 乞-shaped part — that's how wisdom pierces through ignorance.
reading: A CHEEKY (チ) wise mouth shoots a dart that lands with a 'chi' sound into the 乞-shaped target.

meaning: A vertical stroke joins a bow and a dart, and the 乞-shaped part is the feather — you feather an arrow by fitting that 乞-shaped piece onto the shaft.
reading: You 'shin' (シン) the arrow — like shining the feather to make it sleek, as you fit the 乞-shaped feather onto the dart.

meaning: A gigantic dart (矢) is held by a gigantic (巨) hand, but the 乞-shaped part (乞) bends it into a perfect right angle — this is the carpenter's square.
reading: The carpenter's square is used to measure a 'coo' (ク) — like a pigeon's coo as it walks along the straight edge.

meaning: A person with a sweeping stroke and one is under a large soil mound, and a dart points down — everything is compressed, making the person a dwarf.
reading: サ — A dwarf sits on a 'サ' (sah) — like a tiny 'sah' (saw) that cuts low to the ground, only reaching a dwarf's height.

meaning: A dart (矢) with two short strokes on top (并) hits a bean (豆) near a mouth (口) — the dart is short, so it's a fault, a defect in aim.
reading: TAN (タン) — a short 'tan' line on a ruler, marking brevity.

meaning: A grain stalk (禾) next to a woman (女) who is shooting a dart (矢) at a 乞-shaped part (乞) — the dart makes the woman low and short, so she can't reach the stalk.
reading: The woman (女) is so low and short that she says 'ワイ' (wai) — like 'ワイ' (wai) as in 'wai-wai' (noisy, short bursts of sound) — as she tries to shoot the dart (矢).

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) and a mouth (口) shout at a dart (矢) stuck in an upside-down box (冂) — a large (大) hand pulls it straight, like the 乞-shaped part (乞) bending it back to correct it.
reading: You 'kyo' (like 'key-oh') the bent dart back into line — the sound of metal straightening with a sharp 'kyo'.

meaning: A dart with a sweeping stroke and two short strokes on top, plus a large day and a mouth — the arrow has a silk cord attached, ready to be shot from a bow.
reading: The arrow's cord makes a 'ソウ' (sow) sound as it slices the air — like sewing a stitch through the sky.

meaning: An old bird uses a dart and a right hand to measure a large grass-covered cliff — this is the standard for measuring everything.
reading: ワク — Picture a WACK (wak) — a sharp hit with a dart that sets the standard for how long things should be.

meaning: A mouth at the base of a cliff — the stone is what the mouth is pressed against, tasting the hard, silent ground.
reading: Say 'seki' — like 'sexy' but with a hard 'k' — picture a stone statue that is oddly attractive, winking at you from a garden.

meaning: A stone (石) with a barb (亅) and a mouth (口) tied to a one (一) — the anchor's hook bites into the seabed, and the mouth-shaped ring holds the rope.
reading: Picture the anchor's ring as a mouth that shouts 'tei!' (like 'tay') to the sailor — that's the テイ reading.

meaning: A dry stone (石) sits on a cliff, with a mouth (口) and ten (十) marks carved into it, showing the rock face is old and weathered.
reading: カン — Picture a can (カン) of soda balanced on the edge of a rocky cliff, about to fall.

meaning: A stone (石) with a hook stroke (乙) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) stuck in it, like a pickaxe, while a mouth (口) and one (一) show you're too busy to talk — you just slave away.
reading: コツ — Imagine you're so busy toiling that you hit your head on a rock and hear a 'kotsu' (コツ) sound — the sound of bone on stone.
