meaning: A vertical stroke pierces the say box, then a tree falls on a come plow, and two splayed strokes scatter — this is the messy condolence message you write when words fail.
reading: ルイ — The mourner leaves a 'rue-ee' (rue + ee) note on the grave, feeling rueful for the dead.

meaning: A sweeping stroke cuts the cow's head, then a vertical stroke and two lines trap the say box under a tree — this is the death penalty, a harsh sentence spoken over the condemned.
reading: チュウ — The executioner says 'chew' (チュウ) on the criminal's last meal before the blade falls.

meaning: A box-on-side enclosure holds a king, but the say box on top is full of lies — the king is trapped in a swindle, and his words are all fake.
reading: キョウ — The swindler shouts 'kyo!' (キョウ) like a fake karate yell, but it's just a lie to distract you.

meaning: A person uses a large say (言) to wrap themselves in a two-part enclosure (勹) of self-praise — that's the boast.
reading: The boastful person shouts 'KO!' (コ) as they puff out their chest, like a crowing rooster.

meaning: Esteem (尚) and two short strokes on top (并) sit above a say (言) and one (一) — when you speak with esteem, you earn praise and honor.
reading: ヨ — You receive a trophy for your honor (誉) and shout 'YO!' (ヨ) in triumph.

meaning: A gentleman (士) with a heart (心) writes down what he says (言) — this becomes a document or record (誌) of his thoughts.
reading: シ — 'She' — she writes a magazine (誌) about her life, and you read 'she' stories.

meaning: A say (言) with a heart (心) and a sword (刀) and a dot (丶) — you speak with your heart and a sharp blade of truth, and you acknowledge what you witness.
reading: You recognize it and say 'NIN' — imagine a ninja (nin) who witnesses a secret and acknowledges it with a nod, his sword dotting the air.

meaning: The king (王) speaks (言) to commit a crime (犯), coaxing you into a trap with sweet words — that's cheating.
reading: The king (王) coaxes you with a 'kyo' (キョウ) sound, like a sly 'kyo-kyo' laugh before the crime.

meaning: A large dart (矢) pierces the say (言) block, and the katakana-mu shape (厶) under a one (一) crown (冖) makes the speaker cry out in confirmation — like 'eh?' — as the dart lands.
reading: The reading is あ (a). Imagine someone saying 'ah!' in surprise as the dart hits the say-block — that sharp 'ah' is the exclamation of confirmation.

meaning: You raise an axe (斤) and put your hand at the side (扎) while saying (言) a solemn promise — that's a vow (誓).
reading: You 'SEI' (セイ) the deal with a handshake after swearing the vow.

meaning: A long stride (廴) over a stop (止) while saying (言) something — that's the moment of nativity, when a baby takes its first step and declares its arrival.
reading: タン — Imagine a birthday cake with a TAN (タン) colored frosting, and the baby's first cry is a loud "TAN!" as it's born.

meaning: A crown (冖) over ten (十) and a child (子) who speaks (言) — the child is obstinate and disorderly, refusing to obey the crown.
reading: The child's obstinate cry is 'hotsu' (ホツ) — like a hot 'hotsu' tantrum.

meaning: From (乃) a grain stalk (禾) and a say (言) — you say words to lead someone from the field, enticing them with a promise of food.
reading: ユウ — Picture a 'you' (ユウ) — you are the one who tempts a friend with a sweet 'you want some?' — leading them away.

meaning: The month (月) of esteem (尚) speaks (言) — but instead of praise, it censures and blames you for your faults.
reading: The blame comes with a 'sho' (ショウ) — like a sharp 'sho!' of disapproval.

meaning: A say (言) part next to a mouth (口) that speaks five (五) different languages — that's how you get word, speech, and language.
reading: You hear someone say 'GO!' and they start speaking a new language — that's the sound of language.

meaning: A person (ノ) speaks (言) with a halberd (戈) at their side, ready to defend their words — this is sincerity, and also a warning to others.
reading: The セイ reading sounds like 'say' — imagine someone who says (セイ) their words with total sincerity, as if every 'say' is a solemn promise.

meaning: Two hands (廾) hold a halberd (戈) while speaking (言) — they admonish and warn you to stop before you get hurt.
reading: The warning is a 'kai' (カイ) — like a 'kai!' shout to stop.

meaning: A craft (工) person (人) speaks (言) — but the craft is a lie, slandering you with false words.
reading: The slander is a 'fu' (フ) — like a 'foo!' of false accusation.

meaning: Say with a mouth and two splayed strokes — the mouth makes a wrong statement, a mistake in speech.
reading: ゴ — 'Go' sounds like 'go' — you go the wrong way, making a mistake.

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) cuts through the say (言) and the mouth (口) on top of soil (土) — the emperor's words are so heavy they press down into the earth, giving instructions to all below.
reading: The emperor's instructions are a loud 'KO' (コウ) — imagine a giant crow (ko) perched on the soil, squawking orders to the people.

meaning: The say (言) part is paired with utilize (用) — you utilize your mouth to recite and chant, like a monk using a prayer wheel.
reading: Chanting 'SHOW' (ショウ) — picture a monk on stage showing off his recitation skills to a crowd, each word a dramatic show.

meaning: A dot (丶) on ten (十) months (月) of say (言) — the admonishment is so huge it takes ten months to speak, and the dot is the final heavy point.
reading: The huge admonishment is a 'HO' (ホ) — imagine a giant ho (hoe) digging a massive hole in the ground while the speaker yells at you.

meaning: The say (言) part meets mother (母) and do not (毋) — the mother says 'do not' and the 乞-shaped part (乞) begs you to listen, so she instructs you.
reading: Instructing with a 'KAI' (カイ) — picture a mother teaching a child to tie a kite (kai) string, giving clear instructions.

meaning: Two say (言) parts face each other — two mouths arguing, each one saying something, so they quarrel and wrangle.
reading: The quarrel is a 'KEI' (ケイ) — imagine two people fighting over a key (kei), each yanking it and shouting.

meaning: You say something with your mouth, but then add two short strokes on top and a pair of legs to run away—that's just a rumor or an unproven opinion.
reading: Imagine you're explaining a theory, and you say 'set' as in a tennis set—the match is over, your opinion is final.

meaning: A gentleman (士) with a pair of legs (儿) sits under a crown (冖) and uses his mouth (口) to say (言) the words — that's reading aloud to the king.
reading: ドク — Imagine a doctor (ドク) reading a prescription out loud to a patient, slowly and clearly.

meaning: An old bird (隹) perches on a say (言) — the bird says something, and you ask 'who' is speaking?
reading: スイ — Imagine a 'sweet' (スイ) old bird who asks 'who?' in a sugary voice.

meaning: A section (課) of a department is like a chapter in a book — you say (言) what's in it, and it's laid out in a rice field (田) with a tree (木) marking the boundary.
reading: カ — Imagine a teacher saying (言) "KA!" as she points to the next chapter (課) in the textbook, like a sharp bark to get the class's attention.

meaning: A person (人) under a lid (亠) with ten (十) sayings (言) — you interrogate them harshly, berating and vilifying them for every word.
reading: You berate someone with a 'sui' (スイ) — like the sound of a sword swishing 'sui-sui' as you cut down their excuses.

meaning: Your say (言) is un- (非) kind — you use it to ridicule and slander others.
reading: The 'ヒ' sound is like 'he' — picture a 'he' who slanders you with his words.

meaning: Under a roof (宀), an eye (目) and a person (人) with one (一) say (言) — friendship grows when you look each other in the eye and speak honestly.
reading: Friendship is a 'gi' (ギ) — like the 'gi' in 'gift', a present you give to a close friend.

meaning: Inside the gate, two people are speaking so softly and respectfully that their words barely pass through the slats — the gate muffles their gentle voices.
reading: A respectful person at the gate hums a soft 'gin' (like a quiet guitar string plucked once) — the sound is polite, not loud.

meaning: Say (言) something with a mouth (口) and soil (土) inside an upside-down box (冂) — you tune the sound until it's just right, like adjusting a musical key.
reading: Imagine a conductor saying 'CHOU' (チョウ) — like 'chow' — as he tunes the orchestra to the perfect pitch.

meaning: A woman kneels by the mortar, grinding rice with her words — she pounds out flattery like she's making a paste, smoothing every edge to please you.
reading: The flatterer says 'ten' (like a perfect score) to everyone — 'You're a ten! You're a ten!' — but it's all empty praise.

meaning: A lid sits on a child's mouth, and the child keeps saying the same thing over and over — so tedious.
reading: A monk named Shun (シュン) drones on and on, repeating his sermon until everyone is bored stiff — that's tedious.

meaning: A vertical stroke splits two splayed strokes above a say — the crooked lines cross the words, twisting them into a cheat, a lie that bends the truth.
reading: The cheat whispers 'key' (like a skeleton key) — he uses a false key to unlock your trust and steal your words.

meaning: Fire (火) next to say (言) — when people talk, the words heat up like fire, so they discuss and talk passionately.
reading: ダン — Dan (like a dance) — the fire and say parts dance together as people discuss, moving back and forth in conversation.

meaning: A woman leans on a grain stalk under a tree, but the sweeping stroke pushes the blame onto the rice — she passes the buck to the harvest, not herself.
reading: The blame-shifter says 'ee' (like a sheep's bleat) — 'Ee, it wasn't me, it was the grain!' — a weak, evasive sound.

meaning: A wrapping enclosure holds rice, and the say investigates — the judge wraps up the rice grains one by one, examining each to make a judicial inquiry.
reading: The investigator says 'kiku' (like 'chrysanthemum' but short) — he sniffs out the truth like a flower, 'kiku, kiku' — probing each petal.

meaning: A month (月) of saying (言) blue (青) words under a lid (亠) on soil (土) with two (二) — you solicit and invite people to come ask for more.
reading: SEI (セイ) — Imagine a “say” (sei) button on a microphone — you press it to solicit and invite the crowd to ask questions.

meaning: You say (言) with a vertical stroke (｜) through a tree (木) in a rice field (田) — that’s admonishing someone, cutting through their excuse like a sharp stick.
reading: You “KAHN” (カン) your fist on the table to get their attention — a firm, short admonishment.

meaning: A quarrel erupts when three stacked strokes (ヨ) of a claw (爪) grab a barb (亅) and pull it across the say (言) — each side claims the barb is theirs.
reading: The quarrel is so loud it sounds like 'sow' (ソウ) — two pigs fighting over a trough, each squealing 'sow!'

meaning: The say on the left is consulting the ear on the right, while a right hand (又) below the ear holds a scroll of advice. To consult is to speak into someone's ear and then write down what they say.
reading: The consultant says 'SHU' as in 'shush' — he puts a finger to his lips to quiet the room before he speaks. (Reading: シュ)

meaning: A fault is when the say (言) part of you slips under a lid (亠) that hides a claw (爪) and a barb (亅) — the hidden sharpness is the mistake.
reading: The fault is a 'ken' (ケン) — like a broken 'ken' (sword) that snaps in your hand, a clear flaw.

meaning: Slander is gossip that drips from the say (言) like a dot (丶) of poison, then a pig (豕) wallows in it — spreading the rumor through the mud.
reading: The gossip is 'taku' (タク) — like a 'tack' (タク) that sticks to the pig's hide, hard to pull off.

meaning: To understand reality, you put a lid (亠) on the little (小) mouth (口) that talks too much, and let the say (言) speak the truth — that's the fact.
reading: You appreciate the fact with a 'ryo' (リョウ) — like 'rio' (リオ) in Rio de Janeiro, where the reality is bright and clear.

meaning: To intimidate, you place tiger spots (虍) on a table (几) with a spoon (匕) and a divining rod (卜) under a cliff (厂) — then you say (言) a scary shout that makes them jump.
reading: The intimidation is a 'ko' (コウ) — like a 'caw' (コウ) of a crow that startles you from the cliff.

meaning: A tome (冊) with a hat on top (个) sits on two hands (廾), while a vertical stroke and one line cross over the say (言) — this is a formal argument written down and presented.
reading: ロン — Ron (like Ron from Harry Potter) holds up the tome and argues loudly with the say part, making his discourse heard.

meaning: To consult carefully, you put a hat on top (个) of a heart (心) and a dot (丶) on the say (言) — you speak with a one (一) focused mind, counseling gently.
reading: The counsel is 'shin' (シン) — like 'shin' (shin) of a leg, you bend it to listen carefully, not break it.

meaning: A command is spoken from under a roof (宀) to a head (疋) — the say (言) part shows it's a verbal order, and the head is the one who must obey.
reading: ジョウ — Imagine a general shouting 'JOE!' as a command, and the soldier's head (疋) snaps to attention under the roof (宀).

meaning: A person (人) stands by a mortar (臼) under the day (日) sky, but the words they say (言) are not honest — they are flattery, bending truth to please.
reading: Imagine a flatterer saying 'ユ' (you) are wonderful, over and over, like a sycophant repeating 'you, you, you' — the sound of the flattery itself.

meaning: Say words under a tree, and a generation of spies listens in — they're reconnoitering.
reading: The spy whispers 'chō' like 'cho' in 'chocolate' — a secret agent's favorite treat.

meaning: A head (疋) with a month (月) of study, and the words (言) that come out show knowledge — but if twisted, that same head and month can produce treachery.
reading: Think of a scholar who says 'ショ' (show) me your knowledge — the sound of showing off what you know, which can turn to treachery.

meaning: A door (戸) with a tome (冊) behind a flag (尸), and two hands (廾) hold these up while a vertical stroke (｜) and one (一) mark the page — all to say (言) glib, flattering words.
reading: Picture a glib salesman saying 'ヘン' (hen) — like 'hen' as in a chicken, but here it's the smooth, clucking sound of flattery that gets you to buy.

meaning: A day (日) and a head (疋) together — you use your head to examine (say, 言) what happened that day, and if you do it honestly, you consider it truly.
reading: Imagine examining a case and saying 'シ' (she) did it — the sound of pointing out the truth after careful consideration.

meaning: Under a roof (宀), two (二) days (日) pass with one (一) noisy argument — the words (言) are so loud you forget what was said, just the noise remains.
reading: The noise is so loud you shout 'ケン' (ken) — like 'can' you be quiet? The sound of forgetting in the clamor.

meaning: A dish (皿) with two splayed strokes (ハ) and one (一) line, wrapped in a wrapping enclosure (勹) — these are the symbols of a life, and the words (言) spoken after death give the posthumous name.
reading: After death, they say 'シ' (she) is gone — the sound of the final name given, like a sigh 'shi' for the departed.

meaning: The car (車) is wearing a crown (冖) and speaking (言) nonsense — a joke or jest that's just colloquial chatter.
reading: コン — Imagine a comedian telling a joke to a crowd, and they all shout 'KON! KON!' like a drumbeat of laughter.

meaning: A 'say' part with a 'mouth' (口) that has a 'two' (二) and a 'wrapping enclosure' (勹) around it — imagine a mouth wrapped in a tight band, speaking out boldly, telling the truth despite the pressure.
reading: The truth-teller shouts 'ガク' (gaku) — like a 'gack' of surprise when the truth hits hard.

meaning: Say the truth under a crown, with a towel and stand up — you see clearly, then abandon the fight.
reading: You give up with a sigh 'tei' like 'tay' in 'stay' — 'stay' no more, you quit.

meaning: A 'say' part with 'white' (白) and 'compare' (比) — imagine comparing two white notes on a scale, making them blend into a harmonious sound.
reading: The harmony sounds like 'カイ' (kai) — like a 'kite' flying smoothly in the wind, all parts in balance.

meaning: A 'say' part with a 'mouth' (口) and a 'buy' (買) that has a 'vertical stroke' (｜) and a 'tree' (木) — imagine buying a tree with a stake, then using your mouth to gently admonish someone not to cut it down.
reading: The admonishment is a firm 'カン' (kan) — like a 'can' of warning you shake before opening.

meaning: A 'say' part with a 'dot' (丶), a 'sweeping stroke' (ノ), a 'crooked-big' (尢), a 'reasonable' (尤), a 'grain stalk' (禾), and a 'tree' (木) — imagine opening a grain sack with a crooked stick, explaining how to begin the harvest.
reading: To open and explain, you say 'ケイ' (kei) — like 'kay' as in 'okay, let's begin'.

meaning: A say (言) part stands over a reap (刈) and a month (月) with a hat on top (个) and a one (一) — you rebuke someone by reaping their bad words with a sharp warning.
reading: You 'you' (ユ) at someone to rebuke them — like saying 'You!' sharply to a child who misbehaves.

meaning: You say (言) with your mouth (口) but also with ice (冫) — like asking a cold, formal question to a consultant, you consult with someone to get their opinion.
reading: シ (shi) — imagine a SHEEP (shi) that you consult with about which pasture to graze; you ask the sheep "shi?" and it nods.

meaning: A say (言) wraps around tanned leather (韋) with a mouth (口) — you must not speak the posthumous name aloud, only whisper it into the leather-bound book.
reading: The sound is 'ki' — imagine a 'key' (ki) that locks the tomb where the real name is kept, and you must never use that key to speak it.

meaning: A 'say' part with a 'sound' (音) that has a 'day' (日) and a 'stand up' (立) — imagine standing up all day, reciting the sound of a poem from memory without looking.
reading: You memorize it by heart, chanting 'アン' (an) — like 'ahn' as in a monk's meditative hum.

meaning: A mouth (口) under a cliff (厂) with a halberd (戈) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) all speak (言) together — they are in harmony, in agreement.
reading: The general's halberd (戈) points at the map, and he says 'KAN' (カン) to signal the troops are in harmony — like a command that unites them.

meaning: An upside-down box (冂) with ten (十) and dry (干) inside, plus two short strokes (并) on top — all under say (言) — you mutter these parts to yourself.
reading: You mutter 'NAN' (ナン) as you count the ten (十) dry sticks inside the box, a low grumble under your breath.

meaning: A pair of legs (儿) and two splayed strokes (ハ) sit inside a box-on-side enclosure (匚), with a vertical stroke (｜) and one (一) — all under say (言) — this is a sincere, faithful promise.
reading: The sincere person swears 'SHIN' (シン) with a hand on the box (匚), like a solemn oath that rings true.

meaning: An insect (虫) sits on a table (几) inside the wind (風), and you say (言) a hint about it — you satirize the bug's laziness.
reading: The wind (風) blows 'FUU' (フウ) as you whisper a hint about the insect on the table — a soft, satirical breeze.

meaning: The old man says many things to the day, and his words pile up — various, several, all together.
reading: Many things said together sound like 'ショ' (sho) — as in 'show' — a show of many voices.

meaning: Two short strokes (并) on top of a lid (亠), with a barb (亅) and three (彡) strokes, plus stand up (立) — all under say (言) — this is a proverb that stands up to be repeated.
reading: The old proverb says 'GEN' (ゲン) — like a wise elder who stands up (立) and speaks a timeless saying.

meaning: A claw (爪) grabs two (二) things, then a right hand (又) takes them — all under say (言) — you forget the lie you told with that hand.
reading: The claw (爪) snatches the lie and you forget it — 'KEN' (ケン) — like a quick trick that slips your mind.

meaning: A mouth (口) under a lid (亠) with a say (言) and grass on top (艾) — the grass nods in the wind, giving its silent consent to the words spoken below.
reading: ダク — Picture a duck (ダク) nodding its head in agreement, its beak saying 'yes' to every proposal.

meaning: You say (言) sweet (甘) words to a tree (木) to trick it into giving you fruit — that's a conspiring plan. The plan is hidden in the sweet talk, like a cheat.
reading: The plan is a 'BOW' (ボウ) — you bow down to hide your sneaky scheme, like a conspirator bowing in secret.

meaning: A person with a say (言) stands under the day (日) sky, wrapped in a wrapping enclosure (勹) holding a spoon (匕) — this is a formal audience with the king, where you speak only when permitted.
reading: エツ — Imagine the king's audience hall has an 'ets' (エツ) — a tiny elevator ('etsu') that only goes up to the throne. You ride the 'etsu' to have your audience.

meaning: The 'say' radical on the left, and on the right a 'month' over a 'rice field' — imagine someone saying that the origin of this rice field goes back a month, told as an oral history.
reading: The 'イ' reading sounds like 'ee' — picture a historian saying 'ee, let me tell you the origin of this field' as they point with a finger.

meaning: A vertical stroke and one line cross a month, and below that, two lines and a large say — this is a mimeograph, copying words onto paper.
reading: トウ — You mimeograph a 'toe' (トウ) print onto the page.

meaning: Say with a left hand and a wrapping enclosure — you play with words, quip, and talk nonsense, wrapping your hand around the sounds.
reading: ソウ — 'Sow' — you sow nonsense like seeds, scattering quips all over the field.

meaning: Say with a door, a flag, ice, a dot, a sweeping stroke, and feathers — you beguile and cajole by fluttering feathers behind a door, cooling the mark with ice.
reading: セン — 'Sen' (as in 'senior') — a senior cajoles you with sweet words, and you fall for it.

meaning: Under a roof, a vertical stroke and one horizontal line with two splayed strokes block your 'say' — you stutter when trying to speak frankly.
reading: Ken stutters under the roof, unable to get the words out.

meaning: A vertical stroke and sweeping stroke form a hook, then a lid over a stream of grass on top of the deceased — all that 'say' is a lie.
reading: Kou lied about the stream of grass on the deceased's grave.

meaning: Your 'say' with a mouth, a barb, and a single note — that's a poem you sing or recite.
reading: Ka, like a carol, you sing with your mouth and a barbed note.

meaning: Say (言) a crowded (込) rice (米) — the words pile up like grains, forming a riddle that traps your mind in a crowded puzzle.
reading: The riddle whispers 'NAZO' — imagine a shadowy figure in a rice field, leaning close to your ear and hissing 'NAZO... NAZO...' as you try to guess.

meaning: A sweeping stroke covers your 'say', and a dish with a heart and a dot stays still — everything is quiet.
reading: Hitsu keeps quiet after being hit on the head with a dish.

meaning: A large claw grabs a short thread while you 'say' something — that's shame and disgrace.
reading: Kei feels shame when his large claw snags the short thread.

meaning: A 'say' radical plus a 'tiger spots' over a 'box-on-side enclosure' with a 'cliff' and a 'divining rod' and a 'spoon' — imagine a tiger playing a prank, using a spoon to flick a divining rod out of a box on a cliff, all while saying something cheeky.
reading: The 'ギャク' reading sounds like 'gya-ku' — picture a jester saying 'gya-ku!' as he sports with a tiger, making it jump back in surprise.

meaning: A stooping figure in a rice field says something, then stands on a pair of legs — he arises.
reading: Shoku arises from the rice field after a shock of realization.

meaning: A person's words (言) are like a lid (亠) placed on a stand (立) with a direction (方) and two short strokes (并) — they cover the truth and point blame sideways, so you slander and criticize.
reading: ボウ — Imagine a bow (ボウ) shooting arrows of harsh words at someone's reputation, each arrow a slanderous remark.

meaning: Three stacked strokes (ヨ) and two short strokes on top (并) sit above a say (言) — a humble person speaks with few words, lowering themselves like a retainer bowing.
reading: ケン — Imagine a 'ken' (ken-do master) who bows modestly after every match, never boasting — he is self-effacing even when he wins.

meaning: Words (言) on a dish (皿) with two short strokes (并) — like a nameplate on a memorial dish, given to honor the dead, but here it's the sound of laughter echoing at a feast.
reading: エキ — Picture a person laughing so hard they spill a dish (皿) of 'eki' (エキ) — like 'echo' of laughter bouncing off walls.

meaning: The say part on the left is speaking, and the right side is an upside-down box with a one and a ten inside. Imagine someone giving a lecture while standing on a box, holding up a 'one' and a 'ten' to show the audience.
reading: The lecturer says 'KOH' (コウ) as in 'coyote' — a coyote is giving the lecture, howling 'KOH-oh-oh' to the crowd.

meaning: A say (言) part stands next to somebody (身) who is measured (寸) — you see the person bowing so low their body becomes a ruler, and the words (言) spill out as they apologize and thank you for your patience.
reading: シャ — You apologize with a 'sha' (シャ) — imagine a 'shark' (シャーク) in a suit, bowing and saying 'sha, sha, sha' as it refunds your money for a bad meal.

meaning: A claw (爪) and a mortar (臼) sit under words (言) — the claw stirs doubt in the mortar, so you suspect and are uncertain, and you flatter to hide it.
reading: トウ — Imagine a flatterer bowing low, saying 'toe' (トウ) — like touching your toes to show excessive respect, which makes you doubt their sincerity.

meaning: Words (言) pour from a tin can (缶) at evening (夕) into an open box enclosure (凵) — that's a chant or folksong sung in the open air as the sun sets.
reading: ヨウ — Picture a singer in a Noh play chanting 'yo-ho' (ヨウ) like a sailor's call, echoing in the evening air.

meaning: A dry mouth sings words that come out of an open box enclosure — this is the song or noh chanting that fills the space.
reading: The singer's voice goes 'YO' — like 'yo!' — as they chant the ballad, echoing in the open box.

meaning: A gentleman (士) under a flag (尸) holds a pike (殳) on a table (几) with a right hand (又) — he says (言) something, but you only hear a coughing (謦) sound.
reading: ケイ — You cough 'KEI!' (ケイ) to clear your throat before speaking.

meaning: Words (言) are placed on a large (大) day (日) with grass on top (艾) — you plan and deliberate under the open sky, like a council meeting on a grassy hill.
reading: ボ — Imagine a planner drawing a map on a large (大) board, saying 'bo' (ボ) as in 'board' — the board where you deliberate your next move.

meaning: Say (言) a crime — a ten (十) mouth (口) with two short strokes on top (并) stands up (立) under a lid (亠) in an upside-down box (冂) — like a drip (滴) of blame falling on you.
reading: タク — You are 'tacked' (タク) with a crime, pinned to the wall by accusation.

meaning: Feathers (羽) say (言) a mistake — a hat on top (个) with ice (冫) and three (彡) strokes — the feathers are tangled, so the words come out wrong.
reading: ビュウ — A 'view' (ビュウ) that is wrong — you look at the map but see the wrong path.

meaning: A one (一) with two short strokes on top (并) and a sword (刀) that reaps (刈) the month (月) — say (言) something shallow, like cutting grass too close to the ground.
reading: セン — A 'sen' (セン) coin is shallow — it has no depth, just like this stupid remark.

meaning: Say something with your mouth, and put it in a box-on-side enclosure filled with goods — you declare and extol it loudly for all to hear.
reading: You 'owe' (オウ) it to the crowd to extol the hero's deeds — your voice rings out like a public announcement.

meaning: A gentleman (士) strikes (攵) a direction (方) with his words (言), making a huge slanderous noise that shakes the soil (土) beneath him.
reading: ギョウ — Imagine a giant (ギョウ) monster slandering a city, its huge voice making the ground shake like a 'gyo' (ギョ) from a sumo wrestler's stomp.

meaning: Say words over soil, with grass on top and a mouth below, plus two — you must be discreet and reverent when speaking of the earth.
reading: キン — A discreet servant says 'Kin' (like 'kin' family) humbly, with a mouth full of soil.

meaning: Tiger spots (虍) on a cliff (厂) — a person with a barb (亅) and a spoon (匕) and two short strokes (并) shouts (よ.ぶ) to mourn, calling out to invoke spirits, all while saying (言) with a divining rod (卜) and a sweeping stroke (ノ).
reading: The shout "コ" (ko) echoes like a crow's caw from the cliff as you invoke the dead.

meaning: You say (言) something about a day (日) when you buy (買) something with a right hand (又) — but you despise the item, so you mock it with a sneer.
reading: You despise the cheap toy, muttering "マン" (man) like a grumpy "man" who hates shopping.

meaning: A vertical stroke (｜) and one (一) cross over words (言) with grass on top (艾) — the noise of many voices tangled in grass, like a crowded field of chatter.
reading: カ — Picture a noisy crowd shouting 'ka-ka-ka' (カ) like crows in a field, the sound of chaos and clamor.

meaning: A say (言) part is next to a stop (止) that has a sword (刀) and a dot (丶) on top. The words wriggle like a snake — the stop tries to halt them, but the sword cuts the stop, and the dot is a wriggling worm that escapes.
reading: The reading is シュウ. Imagine 'shoo' — you say 'shoo!' to a wriggling worm, but it keeps wriggling, so you shout 'shoo-oo!' The sound 'shuu' is in 'shoo'.

meaning: A say (言) part is under a lid (亠) that has two short strokes (并) on top, and below that a gentleman (士) holds beans (豆) and a mouth (口) — but the mouth is also a ten (十). The gentleman screams because the beans are too hot, and the mouth opens wide to let out a scream.
reading: The reading is キ. Imagine 'key' — you scream 'key!' when you see a giant key, and the scream is a high-pitched 'kee' sound.

meaning: A say (言) part is next to a lid (亠) that covers a mouth (口) and a child (子), and a strike (攵) hits the child. You dislike this — the strike makes you feel dislike, and you say 'no' with your mouth, but the lid covers it, so you just frown.
reading: The reading is タイ. Imagine 'tie' — you dislike wearing a tight tie, and you say 'tie? No!' The sound 'tai' is in 'tie'.

meaning: The dotted tent (癶) covers a pile of beans (豆) with two short strokes on top (并), all guarded by a mouth (口) that speaks (言) — this is the official proof, the certificate that vouches for what is said.
reading: The certificate is shown to the judge, who says 'SHOW it to me' — ショウ.

meaning: A sweeping stroke (ノ) over a claw (爪) and four dots at the bottom (杰) — this odd shape sits next to say (言), and the way you say it is twisted, an accent or dialect that sounds wrong to outsiders.
reading: The accent makes you say 'KA?' like a confused crow — カ.

meaning: A person at the side (化) stands under a dotted cliff (广), shouting words (言) at an old bird (隹) perched above — the bird answers back with a squawk.
reading: The old bird (隹) says 'ヨウ' — like 'yo!' — as it answers you from the cliff.

meaning: A mouth (口) with a halberd (矛) and a pair of legs (儿) inside an upside-down box (冂) — this whole trap is described by say (言), and it's a lie meant to deceive you.
reading: The deceiver says 'KETSU!' as he snaps the box shut — ケツ.

meaning: A dot (丶) on a short thread (幺) hangs from a halberd (戈) with a sweeping stroke (ノ) — this weapon is pointed at say (言), and the words are slander, cutting down the speaker.
reading: The slanderer whispers 'KI' like a snake hissing before it strikes — キ.

meaning: A vertical stroke (｜) and two (二) splayed strokes (ハ) sit above a stop (已) — this structure is built next to say (言), and you compose it carefully to eulogize the dead.
reading: You write the eulogy and say 'SEN' as you set the stone — セン.

meaning: A say balloon over a day that has nothing in it — the speaker says empty words about someone, so it's slander.
reading: Imagine a slanderer named 'Shin' (シン) who whispers lies into a microphone shaped like a day (日) with nothing (无) inside.

meaning: A sound (音) comes from a say (言) that stands up (立) like a day (日) marker — this is how you discriminate and know things, by distinguishing the sound of each word.
reading: Imagine a SHI-ki (シキ) — a shikigami (paper spirit) that can discriminate between truth and lies by writing down what it hears.

meaning: Four dots at the bottom (杰) support an old bird (隹) — this bird sits on a tower, and from there it shouts down with say (言), scolding the people below.
reading: The bird on the tower cries 'SHOW!' to scold the crowd — ショウ.

meaning: A 'say' (言) part is wrapped around a 'west' (西) 'day' (日) and a 'say' (曰) inside, like a long spoken tale told over many days. The 'ten' (十) at the bottom is the tenth retelling of the same story.
reading: タン — Imagine a 'tan' line on your arm from telling a long story in the sun all day. The 'tan' is the mark of the talk.

meaning: A 'person' (人) under a 'lid' (亠) with 'two' (二) 'large' (大) 'day' (日) marks — this person hides behind a lid, spreading false words (言) about someone else. The slander is a big lie told on two days.
reading: シン — Think of a 'shin' (shin bone) being kicked when you slander someone — the false accusation hurts like a kick to the shin.

meaning: A vertical stroke and two short strokes on top sit above a say, with a day and another one below — imagine a musical score where the say is the lyrics, the day is the time signature, and the two short strokes are the notes on the staff.
reading: The score is so full of notes it feels like a 'foo' (フ) — picture a musician shouting 'Foo!' as they flip through the pages.

meaning: Goods (品) are piled up, and a mouth (口) on a tree (木) shouts — the tree's mouth is noisy, so you shout over the goods.
reading: ソウ — Imagine a 'SOW' (like a pig, ソウ) squealing loudly from the tree — that's the noisy shout.

meaning: A say (言) with a mouth (口) and a strike (攵) from a stooping figure (夂) under grass (艾) — that's an admonishment, a commandment to stop.
reading: The commandment is 'kei' — like 'kay' — 'kay, listen up!' — the teacher strikes the desk to get attention.

meaning: A person's 'say' (言) is trapped under a 'cliff' (厂) with a 'wrapping enclosure' (勹) on top, and a pair of 'legs' (儿) dangling below — they're babbling deliriously, unable to escape the fever dream.
reading: The delirious patient keeps repeating 'TOU' (トウ) — like a broken record saying 'tou, tou, tou' — as the nurse tries to calm them.

meaning: A 'say' (言) next to a 'mouth' (口) that opens under a 'flag' (尸) — the flag waves over a 'stand up' (立) figure holding 'ten' (十) 'spicy' (辛) peppers, illustrating a vivid comparison to make a point clear.
reading: To 'illustrate' (譬), the teacher says 'HI' (ヒ) — like 'he' pointing at a chart — 'see, this is how it works!'

meaning: A 'say' (言) that uses a 'mortar' (臼) to grind up a 'craft' (工) — then a 'pike' (殳) stabs the result, while a 'right hand' (又) on a 'table' (几) scatters the dust — that's slander, destroying someone's work with words.
reading: The slanderer whispers 'KI' (キ) — like a key turning in a lock — to secretly defame a rival's name.

meaning: The 'say' part on the left is talking, while the right side has a 'lid' over 'ten' 'spicy' 'soil' and 'buy' — you're decoding a spicy message from a foreign land, translating it into your own words.
reading: Imagine a yak (ヤク) chewing on a scroll, translating it into a different language as it chews.

meaning: The say part on the left, and on the right a sheep with a halberd and a barb, plus two short strokes on top — a debate where a sheep argues with a halberd, and the king listens with a hand raised.
reading: ギ — In the deliberation, a 'gee' (ギ) — like a horse's neigh — interrupts the meeting, and everyone debates whether to let the horse speak.

meaning: A 'king' with a 'sheep' on top and 'say' below — the king speaks kindly, and the sheep is gentle, so this is a virtuous, good ruler.
reading: A zen (ゼン) monk sits peacefully, saying only good things, radiating virtue.

meaning: A garment (衣) under a lid (亠) with say (言) — you defer and turn over the garment to someone else, conveying it with words.
reading: ジョウ — Imagine a JOY-ful ceremony where you say (言) 'I defer to you' and hand over a garment (衣) — the turnover is a joyful transfer of ownership.

meaning: A vertical stroke (｜) and one (一) mouth (口) crowded (込) into a say — you're scolding someone so much they're crowded in a corner, that's reproach.
reading: Picture a stern boss saying 'Ken!' (ケン) as he points a vertical stroke at a crowded mouth — that's the reproach.

meaning: A right hand holds a grass on top over an old bird, while say (言) shouts warnings — you must safeguard the bird from harm.
reading: ゴ — Imagine a GO-kart driver safeguarding a precious old bird by shouting 'GO!' through a megaphone (言) as he steers with his right hand.

meaning: A gentleman (士) with a measurement (寸) and craft (工) uses his mouth (口) to say (言) lies — that's deceive and cheat, and the hurried bustling comes from his frantic gestures.
reading: A cheating gentleman shouts 'Choo!' (チュウ) as he rushes around with a measuring tape, bustling and deceiving.

meaning: A lid (亠) and crown (冖) cover a pig (豕) that opens its mouth (口) to say (言) — the pig roars so loudly it terrifies, and the swiftness is the pig dashing away.
reading: The pig roars 'Koh!' (コウ) so loudly that the lid and crown fly off, and it swiftly runs away.

meaning: A dot (丶) and sweeping stroke (ノ) in a box-on-side enclosure (匚) hold a buy (買) and a retainer (臣) who says (言) — you supervise the retainer's purchases in the box, confining the government office.
reading: The supervisor says 'Kan!' (カン) as he watches the retainer buy things inside the box-on-side enclosure.

meaning: A 'mortar' and 'two splayed strokes' sit above 'say' — you grind your words in a mortar, and what comes out is praise that spreads your fame.
reading: You yell 'Yo!' (ヨ) to the crowd, and they cheer your reputation and praise.

meaning: A shallow (冫) person with two short strokes on top (并) and a reaping (刈) mouth that says (言) foolish things, while feathers (羽) and a month (月) float in an upside-down box (冂) — all showing how stupid and shallow the talk is.
reading: Picture a shallow puddle that is only a SENtimeter (セン) deep, and a stupid person trying to reap (刈) it with a scythe — that's how shallow and foolish they are.

meaning: A gentleman with a pair of legs in a box sees a shellfish with an eye, and he says the words out loud to read and study them.
reading: ドク — A doc (ドク) reads a book to study, and you pronounce the words.

meaning: Say (言) a drip (滴) of blame to punish someone.
reading: To punish (讁), you tack (タク) a note of blame onto their door.

meaning: A person (人) with a large (大) mouth (口) speaks (言) praise, while two splayed strokes (ハ) above an eye (目) and a shellfish (貝) below show the title on a picture being admired. The lid (亠) and two (二) strokes frame the honor.
reading: You say 'SAN!' as you clap for the artist — the praise sounds like a cheerful 'SAN-kyu!' (thank you) to the painter.

meaning: Under a roof (宀), say (言) the details of rice (米) fields (田) with a sweeping stroke (ノ) to know in detail.
reading: Know in detail every part of your shin (シン) bone.

meaning: Say (言) with a strike (攵) — you strike the words, and the threads (糸) and little (小) threads (幺) get tangled, causing a change that's strange.
reading: A change is 'hen' (ヘン) — think of a hen that suddenly changes color, from white to strange purple, right in front of you.

meaning: A dragon (竜) stands up (立) and says (言) with a hook (乙) — the dragon's words make you fear and envy, and it talks too much (loquacious).
reading: The dragon's fear-inducing talk is a 'sho' (ショウ) — like a 'show' of terror, where the dragon gives a long, loquacious speech that scares everyone.

meaning: A banquet (讌) — you say (言) with a mouth (口) while a left-side kata (爿) holds a spoon (匕) and four dots (杰) of food on a dish (皿) — all for the feast.
reading: The banquet is an 'en' (エン) — think of an 'en' (like 'en' in 'enjoy') — you enjoy the banquet, eating and talking with a mouth full of food.

meaning: A mouth (口) speaks honest speech to a king (王), and the king's say (言) is recorded — that's honest speech.
reading: The king's honest speech is so loud it echoes like a 'gaku' (ガク) — imagine a royal decree booming 'GAKU!' across the hall.

meaning: An old bird (隹) perches on your say (言) — it's your enemy, mocking your words, and you seek revenge.
reading: Your enemy's revenge is a 'shuu' (シュウ) — like a hawk's shriek 'SHUU!' as it dives at your head.

meaning: An old bird (隹) sits on your say (言) — it's the same enemy, and you plot revenge by trapping it under your words.
reading: Revenge comes with a 'shuu' (シュウ) — the sound of the bird's wings as it flees, 'SHUU!' into the night.

meaning: Say with a mouth, compare with legs and a wrapping enclosure — defamation is when you wrap your words around someone to compare them badly.
reading: The defamation makes you 'zan' (ザン) — like a zany rumor that stings.

meaning: A person in a garment (衣) under a lid (亠) stands at a gate (門) with a mouth (口) and a say (言) — they speak one word (一) and then step back, yielding the way. The vertical stroke (｜) is the line they won't cross, allowing others to pass.
reading: The judge says 'JOE' (ジョウ) as he lets the crowd through the gate — 'Joe, you may yield now.'

meaning: A person stands at the gate (門) and uses their mouth (口) to say (言) false things about a tree (木) with two short strokes on top (并) — that's slander.
reading: ラン — Imagine a person at the gate (門) shouting 'RAN!' as they falsely accuse someone, the sound echoing like a loud 'ran' through the courtyard.

meaning: A person (人) holds a halberd (戈) over a leek (韭) while saying (言) a prophecy — the leek's green shoots are the omen, and the halberd points to the future they predict.
reading: The omen whispers 'SHIN' (シン) — like a 'shin'ing light that reveals what's to come.

meaning: An old bird (隹) sits on grass on top (艾) of ten (十) mouths (口) all saying (言) at once — the bird squawks over the noisy crowd, making a disputatious racket.
reading: The noise is so loud it 'KAN' (カン) be heard — like a 'can' of rattling pebbles shaken hard.

meaning: A sweeping stroke of praise from the say, over soil, with a pair of legs, a shellfish, and an eye — the picture title is applauded by all who see it.
reading: The crowd gives a 'san' — like 'sang' a song of praise, the chorus sings 'San! San!' as the picture is unveiled.

meaning: A mouth (口) speaks (言) with esteem (尚) and four dots (杰) of passion below — this is counsel given boldly, speaking out with righteous words.
reading: You give advice with a loud "TOH!" (トウ) — like a town crier (トウ) shouting from a tower, making everyone hear your counsel.

meaning: A dog (犬) with tiger spots (虍) stands by a tripod (鬲) while a mouth (口) speaks (言) — the judge decides the verdict by examining the evidence in the pot.
reading: The judge bangs a gavel and says "GETSU!" (ゲツ) — like "get" the verdict — as the dog (犬) and tripod (鬲) settle the case.

meaning: A gentleman (士) with two splayed strokes (ハ) over an eye (目) is buying (買) a shellfish (貝) to say (言) evil words — that's slander.
reading: トク — Imagine a TOKU-sin (tokusatsu) villain slandering the hero with evil words on TV.

meaning: A mouth (口) with two splayed strokes (ハ) and a hat on top (个) — the valley opens like a mouth, with two streams spreading out below the hat-like peak.
reading: KOKU (コク) — a kokutsu (cave) in the valley echoes with the sound of two streams.

meaning: A tusk (牙) and a mouth (口) sit above a valley (谷) with two splayed strokes (ハ) and a hat on top (个) — the tusk's echo bounces off the valley walls, and the tree spirit lives in that echo, so it means tree spirit (the echo of the forest).
reading: The tree spirit's echo in the valley (谷) sounds like 'ko' (コ) — the reading is コ.

meaning: A one (一) with a dot (丶) sits under a hat on top (个) with two splayed strokes (ハ) above a mouth (口) in a valley (谷) — the valley's mouth is a huge opening.
reading: The opening is a 'KAN' (カン) — picture a giant can (kan) in the valley, its open top like a huge mouth.

meaning: A valley with a stream at the bottom — the mouth of the valley opens wide, and inside you see a large claw (爪) scratching the soil, while a hat (个) and a short thread (幺) hang from the cliffs above.
reading: ケイ — Imagine a valley where a giant key (ケイ) unlocks the stream, letting the water flow out.

meaning: An empty room — under a roof (宀) with a lid (亠) and two splayed strokes (ハ), the soil (土) is bare, and the valley (谷) inside is hollow, with only a mouth (口) and a hat (个) left.
reading: カツ — Picture a karate chop (カツ) that slices through the empty room, leaving it completely hollow.

meaning: A mouth with two short strokes on top — like a tiny bean with a sprout, or a midget's mouth with a mustache.
reading: トウ — A toe (トウ) steps on a bean, squashing it flat like a midget.

meaning: Two short strokes on top of a craft-made beans container, with a mouth opening at the side — this is the small kidney bean, packed tight in its pod.
reading: Imagine a small kidney bean shouting "KOH!" as it pops out of its pod, like a tiny green superhero landing.

meaning: A mountain of beans stacked on a mouth, with two short strokes on top — you're so surprised you nearly choke on your beans, exclaiming in shock.
reading: Picture someone gasping "KAI!" as a mountain of beans tumbles into their open mouth — surprise makes them shout it.

meaning: Beans sit under a branch, with a right hand and a mouth nearby — fermented beans are stirred by hand and tasted by mouth, stored in a jar with two short strokes on top.
reading: The sound is 'shi' — imagine a chef saying 'shi-shi' as he tastes the salty fermented beans, puckering his lips.

meaning: A vertical stroke, one mouth, beans, day, and two short strokes (chopsticks) — a bountiful feast.
reading: Ho! The beans are bountiful and rich.

meaning: A dot sits on two short strokes on top, then a mouth and evening share a line, and beans are below — this is the ceremonial vessel, a tall stand for offering beans at dusk.
reading: トウ — The priest lifts the vessel and says 'toe' (トウ) as he places it on the altar, toe-tapping in rhythm.

meaning: A pea is a bean (豆) that sits in a mouth (口) under a roof (宀), with two short strokes (并) and an evening (夕) seal (卩) — like a tiny green sphere sealed in a pod.
reading: エン — Imagine 'EN' (エン) the pea, rolling out of a mouth (口) at evening (夕) and getting sealed (卩) in a bean (豆) pod.

meaning: A 'retainer' standing upright on 'beans', with 'two short strokes on top' and a 'right hand' — imagine a retainer balancing beans vertically on his head, using his hand to steady them, like a child trying to stand tall.
reading: The 'ジュ' reading sounds like 'ju' (as in 'juice') — picture a vertical child holding a juice box straight up, saying 'ju!' as he stands at attention.

meaning: Half-grown beans — the beans (豆) are still small, with a vertical stroke (｜) and a dot (丶) on top, and a sweeping stroke (ノ) plus three stacked strokes (ヨ) showing they haven't fully sprouted, while two short strokes (并) mark the early stage.
reading: カン — A can (カン) of half-grown beans sits on the shelf, still too young to eat.

meaning: A mountain (山) of beans (豆) sits in an open box enclosure (凵) with two short strokes (并) on top, and mouths (口) open wide — the harvest is bountiful, rich, and excellent.
reading: The bountiful feast makes you shout "ホウ" (hō) like "ho!" as you see the overflowing pile.

meaning: A large (大) dish (皿) of beans (豆) sits on a mountain (山) with two short strokes (并) on top — the sight is so beautiful and plump it captivates everyone.
reading: She is "EN" (エン)chanting — imagine a beautiful woman with plump cheeks, and you say "EN!" as she walks by.

meaning: The beans on the dish are plump and voluptuous, with soil and mountain piled high, and the two short strokes on top and the katakana-mu shape add a beautiful, rich color.
reading: エン — The beautiful woman's plump cheeks are 'en' (エン) like a round yen coin, shiny and full.

meaning: A pig with a snout — the top is a lid, the middle is an upside-down box, and the bottom legs are like a towel's fringe. It's the pig radical, snuffling in the mud.
reading: The pig says 'shi' (シ) — like 'she' — as in 'she' is a pig, oinking in the sty.

meaning: A pig with a pair of legs and one sweeping stroke on top, all crammed under a wrapping enclosure — the pig's grunting and stomping makes a clamour.
reading: Hear the pig's loud "KA!" as it kicks its legs against the enclosure — a sharp, noisy clamour that echoes.

meaning: A pig is trapped in an open box enclosure, with a hook stroke and a sweeping stroke on top — this small pig is still in its pen, not yet grown.
reading: The sound is 'ton' — imagine a tiny piglet that goes 'ton ton' as it trots on the wooden floor of its pen.

meaning: A pig (豕) under the month (月) — think of a pig that has been fattened up over a month, ready to become pork.
reading: The pig says 'ton' as it rolls in the mud — imagine a heavy 'ton' sound as it flops down.

meaning: A pig is marked with a comma-design and a stop — the sow is the one who stops and stays, her curly tail like a comma, heavy with young.
reading: The sound is 'ha' — imagine a farmer pointing at the sow and saying 'HA! That's the mother pig!'

meaning: A pig (豕) is wrapped in a wrapping enclosure (勹) with a mouth (口) and a one (一) on top — imagine a giant elephant wrapped in a blanket, with its trunk (mouth) and a single tusk (one) sticking out. That's the elephant, and we imitate its shape.
reading: The elephant's trunk sprays water like a ZO (ゾウ) — think of a zoo (ゾウ) where the elephant is the main attraction, spraying visitors.

meaning: The person (人) puts two short strokes on top (并) of the pig (豕) to mark it as their own, raising it as a domestic animal.
reading: The farmer raises pigs in a KENnel (ケン) — a small shelter for domestic animals.

meaning: One and a sweeping stroke cross a dry field, then two lines and ten hold the pig — this is a pig of 3 years, old and tough, marked by the dry earth it rooted in.
reading: ケン — The old pig is 'ken' (ケン) as in 'kennel' — it's been in the kennel for three years.

meaning: A wild boar (pig) with tiger spots on its back, standing on a cliff, fights with a divining rod and a spoon — this is a scene of battle.
reading: キョ — Imagine a wild boar shouting 'KYO!' as it charges, knocking over a giant spoon and divining rod on the cliff.

meaning: A pig with a towel draped over its back, standing under an upside-down box, with a dot and a sweeping stroke marking its snout — this is a large hog, bigger than a normal pig.
reading: The pig is so big it says 'kee' (like 'key') to unlock the barn door, but it's too fat to fit through.

meaning: A mouth under a lid, under a crown, over a pig — the crowned pig is overpowering and great, excelling above all.
reading: ゴウ — 'Gou' sounds like 'gow' — a powerful bear growls 'gow' as it overpowers.

meaning: A 'wrapping enclosure' with a 'vertical stroke' and a 'halberd' and a 'barb' over a 'pig' with a 'マ-shaped stroke' — imagine a pig wrapped in a blanket, leaning back with a halberd resting nearby, totally relaxed and at ease.
reading: The 'ヨ' reading sounds like 'yo' — picture the relaxed pig saying 'yo, I'm comfortable' as it lounges in its enclosure.

meaning: A 'day' over an 'old man' on the left, and a 'pig' on the right — imagine an old man watching a pig all day, and the pig is so fat it looks like a hog, not a wild boar.
reading: The 'チョ' reading sounds like 'cho' (as in 'chop') — picture a chef chopping a hog into pork chops, saying 'cho!' with each swing.

meaning: A 'pig' on the right, and on the left a 'one' over a 'mouth' with a 'right hand' and a 'vertical stroke' — imagine a male pig with a single tusk (the vertical stroke) sticking out of its mouth, and a hand pointing at it to show it's the boar.
reading: The 'カ' reading sounds like 'ka' (as in 'car') — picture a boar charging at a car, its tusk scraping the paint with a 'ka-ka-ka' sound.

meaning: An ancient state — a mountain (山) rises over a pig (豕), marking the border of a Zhou dynasty territory.
reading: ヒン — A pin (ヒン) on a map marks the location of this ancient state, stuck right into the mountain.

meaning: A pig (豕) with a person (人) and a stop (彳) and another stop (止) — the young pig is stopped by the person's feet, so it stays small and squealing.
reading: The young pig's squeal sounds like "ソウ" (sō) — "so" small, so cute.

meaning: A 'pig' with 'grass on top' and an 'eye' — the pig is castrated, so it's calm and just eats grass, staring at you with a dull eye.
reading: The castrated pig goes 'fun' (フン) — a snort of relief, no more piglets.

meaning: A snake with no legs — the top is a hook stroke, the body is a long insect-like coil, and the bottom is a clawed dog's paw. It's the legless insect or badger radical.
reading: The snake hisses 'tai' (タイ) — like 'tie' — as in you must tie it up before it slithers away.

meaning: A snake (豸) with a dot and a wrapping enclosure — see a leopard's spotted coat as a snake wrapping around its body, with a dot marking each spot, and the enclosure being the leopard's powerful jaw.
reading: ヒョウ — Say 'hyo!' (ヒョウ) as a leopard leaps out of the bushes, its spots flashing like a sudden burst of snow (hyo is like 'hyo' in 'hyow!').

meaning: A snake (豸) with a sweeping stroke, one, and a barb — imagine a jackal with a snake's body, using a barbed tail to sweep through the grass, hunting like a wild dog.
reading: サイ — Picture a 'sigh' (サイ) from a jackal as it howls at the moon, its long snout letting out a mournful 'sai' sound.

meaning: A snake (豸) with one, ten, and dry — see a wild dog (like a dhole) locked in a prison cell, its snake-like body coiled around a dry wooden bar (ten and one forming a cage).
reading: カン — Imagine a 'can' (カン) of food being thrown into a prison cell, where a wild dog (豻) snarls and claws at the bars, making a clanging 'kan' sound.

meaning: A snake body is paired with compare — this brave heraldic beast is like a snake but compared to it, more fierce and noble, shown on shields.
reading: The sound is 'hi' — imagine a heraldic beast that roars 'HI-YA!' as it charges into battle, brave and bold.

meaning: A snake (豸) wraps around a mouth (口) that holds a sword (刀) — this fierce little creature is a marten, known for its sharp bite and sleek fur.
reading: The marten's fur is so fine it's used for a cho (チョウ) — imagine a chef's chopping knife (cho) made of sable fur, slicing through the air.

meaning: A brave heraldic beast — a snake with a person at the side and a tree growing from its back, standing guard like a statue.
reading: キュウ — The beast lets out a proud 'KYUU!' cry, echoing through the tree as the person at the side salutes.

meaning: A small badger — a snake curled around a single day marker, peeking out from under a one-stroke roof, like a tiny burrow.
reading: カン — The badger hides in a can ('KAN') of porcupine quills, with the day marker as its lid.

meaning: A badger — a snake with a mouth and a stooping figure, shuffling along like a clumsy, grumpy badger.
reading: カク — The badger cracks a nut ('KAKU') with its mouth, while the stooping figure watches.

meaning: Barbarians — a snake with a white patch, like a foreign tribe's banner, marching into unknown lands.
reading: ハク — The barbarians shout 'HAKU!' as they raise a white flag, the snake coiling around it.

meaning: A white face with a pair of legs, but the body is a snake — this odd form is the appearance or countenance you see from a distance.
reading: The snake's form is so weird it makes you say 'bow' (like taking a bow) in surprise — that's its appearance.

meaning: A snake wrapped around a ri (a village unit) — this fox-like animal slinks through the fields, not quite a fox, not quite a dog.
reading: The animal says 'ri' (like 'ree') as it runs — that's the sound of its fox-like yelp.

meaning: A wild beast with a mortar (臼) for a head and a pair of legs (儿) standing on a snake (豸) — this is a lion-like creature, a wild beast or wild horse.
reading: ゲイ — The lion roars 'gei' (ゲイ) — like the English 'gay' but with a growl. Picture a lion saying 'gei-gei' as it pounces.

meaning: A snake (豸) slithers through a rice field (田) with grass on top (艾) — that's a cat hunting in the tall grass.
reading: The cat's meow sounds like 'byoo' — imagine a cat saying 'BYOO!' as it pounces.

meaning: A brave heraldic beast — a snake (豸) with a box (囗) on its head, and a compare (比) sign on its side, stands fierce and ready for battle.
reading: ヒ — The beast roars 'hee' (ヒ) as it charges, its heraldic crest shining.

meaning: A tapir — a snake (豸) with a large (大) day (日) on its back, and grass (艾) growing from its head, munching quietly in the meadow.
reading: バク — The tapir backs (バク) away slowly when startled, its nose twitching.

meaning: A snake (豸) with grass on top (艾) and an old bird (隹) perched on a mouth (口) — this odd creature is a badger that digs through grass and bird nests.
reading: The badger's home is a 'kan' (カン) — like a tin can (kan) it lives in, a metal can buried in the grass.

meaning: A snake (豸) with an old bird (隹) on its head, and a right hand (又) holding an eye (目) — this giant ape watches everything, using its hand to shield its eye.
reading: The ape goes "KYAKU!" (キャク) — like a quick "cackle" — as it swings through trees, making a sharp, loud call.

meaning: The eye (目) sits on top of two splayed strokes (ハ) like the hinge of a shell, and the whole shape is a shellfish with its shell open.
reading: The sound is バイ (bai) — imagine a shellfish saying 'bye' (バイ) as it waves its shell and closes up.

meaning: A shellfish (貝) sits under a lid (亠), watched by an eye (目) with two splayed strokes (ハ) and a divining rod (卜) — this is the upright, constant one who never strays from righteousness.
reading: The upright judge says 'TEI' as he stamps the verdict — firm and unchanging, like a steady beat.

meaning: Defeat (負) is like a shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) and two legs (ハ) wrapped (勹) up and helpless.
reading: You say 'Fu' (フ) when you are defeated.

meaning: A shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) and two splayed strokes (ハ) sits on a one (一) with a barb (亅) — that shellfish holds your money, your wealth, like a treasure chest.
reading: ザイ — 'Zai' (ザイ) — 'Zai' the pirate shouts, as he grabs the shellfish full of gold coins.

meaning: A shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) and two splayed strokes (ハ) is carried by a craft (工) — that's the tribute you send to the lord, counted shell by shell.
reading: The tribute is “kou” — picture a worker shouting “KOU! KOU!” as he hauls the heavy shellfish up the hill.

meaning: A vertical stroke pierces a hook stroke, then two splayed strokes and a spoon sit on top of a classical 'to be' — all stacked over an eye and a shellfish. This layered pile of parts is a series of steps or strata, each grade resting on the one below.
reading: The 'イ' reading sounds like 'ee' — imagine a shellfish saying 'ee' as it climbs each step of a steep staircase, one grade at a time.

meaning: A shellfish (貝) is split by a sword (刀) into two splayed strokes (ハ) — the shell is broken, and the eye (目) sees only scraps. That's poverty: even the shell is worthless.
reading: Poverty makes you say 'ヒン' — like 'hin' in 'hint' — you only have a hint of money, not enough.

meaning: A person at the side transforms into a shellfish, but the shellfish is actually a container of goods — freight and property.
reading: The goods are loaded onto a cart that goes 'ka-chunk' over every bump.

meaning: A shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) and two splayed strokes (ハ) is held by a right hand (又) near a cliff (厂) — you sell the shellfish at a market stall by the cliff.
reading: The vendor shouts 'han!' (ハン) as he slaps a fish on the counter to sell it — a sharp, quick sound.

meaning: A shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) under a hat (个) on top of a one (一) — this greedy creature covets everything it sees, even wearing a hat to look richer.
reading: タン — Imagine a greedy person shouting 'TAN-trum!' when they don't get what they covet.

meaning: A mother (母) says 'do not' (毋) — but you pierce through with a shellfish (貝) and an eye (目) on a two splayed strokes (ハ) — that's to pierce and penetrate.
reading: カン — Imagine a 'can' (カン) opener piercing through a metal can, the sharp point going straight in.

meaning: A shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) stares at you from under a lid (亠) on two (二) legs of soil (土), and the two splayed strokes (ハ) are its accusing arms pointing at you — it blames you.
reading: The shellfish's eye (目) is a 'seki' (セキ) — like a security camera lens that catches you in the act, so you get blamed.

meaning: A shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) under a hat (个), but instead of a one, it's pressed under a cliff (厂) and a ten (十) — the hard material of the shell is the substance beneath the surface.
reading: シツ — Picture a scientist testing the material's substance and saying 'SHITSU!' (like 'chew' but with 'shitsu') as it resists.

meaning: A shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) under a hat (个), and a piling (弋) stuck into it — this is the second shellfish you've collected, marked with a piling to count it.
reading: ニ — Say 'NI-ce!' as you count the second shellfish you've piled up.

meaning: A shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) and two splayed strokes (ハ) sits under a roof (宀) with a barb (亅) and a one (一) — this is where you store your savings safely.
reading: Picture a piggy bank shaped like a shellfish (貝) that says "CHO" (チョ) every time you drop a coin in — a cheerful "cho" of saving.

meaning: You see a shellfish and an eye, but to get what you want, you must splay your strokes (ハ) across a generation (世) — you obtain it through persistence.
reading: もらう — You 'morrow' (borrow) from tomorrow to get what you need today — you obtain it now.

meaning: Treasure and assets — a shellfish with an eye, a stop sign, and two splayed strokes, all guarded by a spoon, like a hoard in a vault.
reading: シ — The treasure is sealed with a 'SHI!' (shh!) — the eye and stop sign tell you to be quiet and not touch the shellfish.

meaning: A shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) and two splayed strokes (ハ) sits under a piling (弋) and two (二) — this is the formal way to write 'two' in banking, so the extra parts are like security guards.
reading: You see two (ニ) coins stacked on a shellfish — the second coin is a 'ni' (ニ) — just say 'ni' as you count the pair.

meaning: A vertical stroke (｜) and one (一) shellfish (貝) under an eye (目) with two splayed strokes (ハ) and a mouth (口) — this precious shell is so valued you keep it in a glass case, watching it.
reading: キ — A 'key' (キ) to a treasure chest — that key is precious and valuable.

meaning: A shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) under a hat (个), but a sweeping stroke (ノ) and a hook (乙) and a lid (亠) are pressing it down — you degrade it by piling junk on top.
reading: ヘン — Imagine a critic saying 'HEN!' (like 'hen' in 'hen-pecked') as they belittle the shellfish's worth.

meaning: A shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) on top and two splayed strokes (ハ) underneath — you use your eye to inspect the shellfish before you buy it.
reading: The buyer says 'bye' (バイ) to their money as they hand it over.

meaning: A person at the side (化) hands over a shellfish (貝) as a loan, but keeps an eye (目) on it — that's lending.
reading: The person at the side (化) says "TAI" as they hand over the shellfish — like saying "TAI-ke it, but pay me back!"

meaning: A pair of legs (儿) carries a shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) and two splayed strokes (ハ) past a mouth (口) — this is a grand gesture of giving, like a royal bestowal.
reading: The giver shouts 'kyo!' (キョウ) as he tosses the shellfish — imagine a loud 'kyo' echoing as the gift flies from his legs.

meaning: A vertical stroke (｜) pokes through a shellfish (貝) while an eye (目) watches two splayed strokes (ハ) and a bow (弓) — all this costs money and gets spent.
reading: You spend so much that your wallet goes "HI-sss" like a deflating balloon — ヒ.

meaning: A shellfish with an eye (貝+目) sits on a divining rod (卜) inside a mouth (口) — you stick it all together with paste.
reading: はる — You 'hurl' the paste onto the paper, then stick it — that's how you apply it.

meaning: A shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) and two splayed strokes (ハ) is left behind next to a mouth (口) and a katakana-mu shape (厶) — this is a gift you leave for someone, like a parting present.
reading: You 'ee' (イ) with surprise when you find the gift — a long 'ee' sound as you open the shellfish and see the treasure inside.

meaning: An eye (目) with two splayed strokes (ハ) and a katakana-mu (厶) on top, plus a shellfish (貝) and a sword (刀) — you trade the shellfish for a sword, exchanging goods.
reading: You trade and say “ボウ” (like “bow” as in bow and arrow) — you exchange a shellfish for a bow, making a deal.

meaning: A shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) and two splayed strokes (ハ) sits on a mouth (口) that is shouting with power (力) — all together, this is a celebration of congratulations and joy.
reading: Imagine a giant shellfish (貝) shouting "GA!" (ガ) as it receives a congratulatory gift — the sound of the cheer is "ga".

meaning: A shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) and two splayed strokes (ハ) is topped with ten (十) and grass on top (艾) — you decorate the shellfish with grass and a ten-spot pattern to make it fancy.
reading: You 'fun' (フン) with delight as you decorate — imagine a 'fun' party where everyone paints shellfish with grass and ten marks.

meaning: A shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) and two splayed strokes (ハ) watches a stooping figure (夂) slip a secret payment into its shell — that’s a bribe.
reading: The stooping figure (夂) is a crooked lawyer who says “ro” as he pockets the cash — think “RO-bbery” for the bribe.

meaning: A king and a person at the side both need to pay — the shellfish (money) and eye (accounting) show the fare or rent they owe for the service.
reading: You pay the fare with a 'chin' (チン) — imagine a cash register going 'ching!' as it rings up the rent.

meaning: A shellfish (貝) sits under a one (一) and a sweeping stroke (ノ), while a month (月) and two splayed strokes (ハ) hover above — like a bribe passed under the table, wrapped in a cloth. The whole scene is a secret supply of money to win favor.
reading: ワイ — Imagine a sly 'wye' (like the letter Y) drawn on a bribe envelope, handed over with a wink. The sound 'wai' is in the word 'wine' — you bribe someone with a bottle of wine.

meaning: A lid (亠) covers a mysterious (玄) short thread (幺) and a sweeping stroke (ノ) above a shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) and two splayed strokes (ハ) — everything is packed in, fully prepared and inclusive.
reading: The lid (亠) snaps shut with a “KAI” sound, sealing the whole kit — like a “KAI-nd” of all-inclusive box.

meaning: A shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) and two splayed strokes (ハ) lacks (欠) ice (冫) — but its assets are still enough to fund a venture.
reading: Your assets are your SHI (シ) — picture a sheep (shi) carrying a treasure chest of shellfish, its wool stuffed with gold coins.

meaning: A shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) and two splayed strokes (ハ) sits under a west (西) sign — that’s a tradesman’s stall where you buy goods.
reading: The west (西) sign reads “KO” — the tradesman shouts “KO-me buy!” to lure customers.

meaning: A dish (皿) of blood (血) sits under two splayed strokes (ハ) next to a shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) — you give this alms to the wounded, a charitable offering.
reading: The blood (血) drips with a “SHUTSU” sound — like “SHUT-s” of mercy, giving alms to the needy.

meaning: A burglar with a halberd (戈) and ten (十) stolen shellfish (貝) — he also has an eye (目) for your valuables, and two splayed strokes (ハ) show his quick getaway.
reading: The rebel yells 'zoku' (ゾク) as he charges — like a comic book villain's 'zok!' sound effect.

meaning: A dotted cliff (广) looms over soil (土) where a shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) and two splayed strokes (ハ) is buried — that hidden stash is bribery.
reading: The soil (土) is dug up with a “SOU” — think “SOU-venir” of dirty money, the bribe.

meaning: A halberd (戈) and two (二) strike down a shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) and two splayed strokes (ハ) — this low-life is despised, living in poverty.
reading: The halberd (戈) swings with a “SEN” — think “SEN-d” the low-life away in disgrace.

meaning: Two splayed strokes hold an eye and a shellfish — these are pearls or shells strung together, hanging as a necklace.
reading: The string of shells makes an 'ei' sound (like 'ay') as they clink together — that's the jingle of the ornament.

meaning: A shellfish with an eye and two splayed strokes, but the sign of the dragon and a garment are piled on top — this bustling crowd makes the market flourish.
reading: The bustling market is so loud you shout 'shin' (like 'shin' as in shinbone) to be heard over the crowd.

meaning: Under a roof (宀), a V.I.P. guest with a shellfish (貝) and an eye (目) sits on a little (小) mat, with a sweeping stroke (ノ) and one (一) line marking their honored spot.
reading: The V.I.P. guest is 'hin' (ヒン) — like a 'hint' of importance that everyone notices.

meaning: A shellfish with an eye and two splayed strokes, but a dot and water drip onto it from above — this is a bribe, a wet and shady exchange.
reading: The bribe is hidden in a cup of 'kyu' (like 'cue' as in billiards) — you pass it under the table.

meaning: A vertical stroke (｜) and two (二) splayed strokes (ハ) sit above an upside-down box (冂) with a mouth (口) and soil (土) — inside, an eye (目) watches a shellfish (貝) being given away — this is charity, giving for the needy.
reading: シュウ — The charity giver shouts 'shuu!' (シュウ) as they toss coins — like 'shoe' but with a long 'u'. Picture a shoe flying into a donation box with a 'shuu' sound.

meaning: A gift is a shellfish (貝) wrapped in a tree (木) with a person (人) and two splayed strokes (ハ) — like a present tied with branches and a person's hand offering it.
reading: ライ — Picture 'RYE' (ライ) bread as a gift, wrapped in a tree (木) leaf, with a person (人) handing it to you, and a shellfish (貝) on top.

meaning: A shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) sees two splayed strokes (ハ) and a person (人) under a large (大) lid (亠) with two (二) strokes — the person approves and praises the sight.
reading: サン — The sun (サン) shines on the shellfish, and everyone praises its beauty.

meaning: A shellfish with an eye and two splayed strokes, plus a 'not' — the shellfish does not keep its treasure, but grants it as a gift to you.
reading: The grant is given with a 'shee' (as in 'sheep') of approval — the sound 'shi' is in 'shee'.

meaning: Previous — picture a crown (冖) placed on a tree (木) that was there before, with two splayed strokes (ハ) marking the old spot, and an eye (目) looking back at a shellfish (貝) that was buried earlier — it's all from the previous time.
reading: チン — Think of a 'chin' (チン) — the previous chin of a statue, now covered with moss, still visible under the old tree.

meaning: An eye (目) and a shellfish (貝) sit under two splayed strokes (ハ), with a mouth (口) and esteem (尚) under a crown (冖) — the esteemed mouth praises the shellfish, giving a prize.
reading: ショウ — Imagine a 'show' (ショウ) of praise: a prize is shown on stage, and the crowd shouts 'show!' as the reward is given.

meaning: A shellfish (貝) sits under an eye (目) and two splayed strokes (ハ) above a mouth (口), all standing on a stand up (立) — this is the pile of compensation you must pay, counted out in shells, with the eye watching the mouth that demands it.
reading: バイ — Imagine a 'bye' (バイ) wave as you hand over a heavy bag of compensation shells, saying goodbye to your money.

meaning: A dotted cliff shelters a crown, and under that three stacked strokes sit above an eye and a shellfish — the eye keeps watching the shellfish, so the cycle continues without pause.
reading: Picture a shellfish that keeps continuing to crawl forward, and each step it takes makes a soft **zoku** (ゾク) sound like a tiny drumbeat — the rhythm never stops.

meaning: A retainer (臣) with a shellfish (貝) and an eye (目) uses two splayed strokes (ハ) and a right hand (又) to count wisdom — the wise one sees the value in every shell.
reading: The wise retainer says 'ケン' (ken) — like 'ken' in 'kendo' — he knows the right strike.

meaning: A gentleman (士) with a shellfish (貝) and an eye (目) under two splayed strokes (ハ) is showing off his goods — he's selling, but also betraying trust by bragging.
reading: バイ — A 'buy' (バイ) sign flashes as the seller shouts, but the buyer feels betrayed by the price.

meaning: A halberd (戈) stabs down on a shellfish (貝) under an eye (目) and two splayed strokes (ハ) — this low-life is so poor he's despicable.
reading: セン — 'Sen' (セン) the beggar sits in the dirt, his poverty making others despise him.

meaning: A stop (止) sign blocks a piling (弋) of shellfish (貝) under an eye (目) and two splayed strokes (ハ) — the levy is a forced poem of taxes, a prose of burden.
reading: フ — 'Foo' (フ) the tax collector reads a long ode about levies, his poem a heavy burden.

meaning: Under a roof (宀) with two (二) little (小) strokes, an eye (目) shows (示) a shellfish (貝) — this tribute cloth is a small show of loyalty from distant tribes.
reading: ソウ — 'Sou' (ソウ) the tribal chief brings cloth tribute, his gift a humble 'sow' of peace.

meaning: Two splayed strokes (ハ) sit on top of an eye (目) and a shellfish (貝) — like a quality inspector peering at a shellfish to judge its substance. The axe (斤) below chops it to test its temperament.
reading: シツ — Imagine a 'sits' (シツ) of quality: a judge sits on a shellfish to test its substance, and the sound of sitting is 'shitsu'.

meaning: The shellfish (貝) on the left is like a ledger, and the long (長) cloth (ハ) on the right is a curtain hiding the accounts. Imagine a long curtain (とばり) behind which a shellfish keeps a bill of debts.
reading: The long (長) curtain flaps as you count your debts — 'cho' like the sound of a cash register 'cha-ching' but shorter: 'cho'. (チョウ)

meaning: An old man (老) with a shellfish (貝) in his eye (目) stares at the day (日) — he's betting his money on a horse race. The two splayed strokes (ハ) are the dice he throws, and the eye watches the result.
reading: He bets 'TO' — like 'toe' — he puts his toe on the line, risking his shellfish money on a gamble. (Reading: ト)

meaning: You rely on the old man (老) who sits by the rice field (田) with a shellfish (貝) — he's the one you depend on for food.
reading: You rely on 'rai' — picture a 'rye' field (like the grain) that you depend on for bread.

meaning: An upside-down box (冂) with two splayed strokes (ハ) and two (二) sits over an eye (目) and a shellfish (貝) — a gift wrapped in a box with a bow.
reading: The gift is 'fuu' — imagine blowing a 'foo' (like a party horn) as you unwrap it.

meaning: A shellfish (貝) sits on a large (大) plate under a month (月) with two short strokes (并) on top — after the feast, only the leftover shells and scraps remain. The eye (目) sees the residue, but nothing more.
reading: The leftover soup is so thick you could 'yo' (ヨウ) a spoon in it — it stands up like a flag.

meaning: A shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) and two splayed strokes (ハ) is coaxed by three stacked strokes (ヨ) — you gently stack compliments to lure the shellfish out of its shell.
reading: To coax a cat, you 'tan' (タン) your fingers on the table — the sound draws it closer.

meaning: A shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) and two splayed strokes (ハ) is placed next to a rice field (田) with a measurement (寸) and a dot (丶) — the condolence gift is a measured portion of rice, offered with a small token.
reading: The condolence gift is a 'fu' (フ) — like a soft puff of air, a gentle offering of breath for the departed.

meaning: An upside-down box (冂) sits on top of a shellfish (貝) that has an eye (目) and a vertical stroke (｜) poking through it, while a one (一) and ten (十) hold it steady below — you are buying a subscription to a shellfish-of-the-month club, and the box is the monthly delivery crate.
reading: コウ — You subscribe to a 'ko' (コウ) — imagine a crow (カラス, but the sound 'ko' as in 'ko-') flying in with the monthly shellfish box, cawing 'KO!' as it drops it on your doorstep.

meaning: Under a roof (宀), a shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) and two splayed strokes (ハ) is guarded by a vertical stroke (｜) — you roll the dice (the shellfish) to decide your temple visit, hoping the roof protects your luck.
reading: You roll the dice and shout 'sai!' (サイ) — the sound of the throw echoing in the temple hall.

meaning: A retainer (臣) with a box-on-side enclosure (匚) holds a shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) and two splayed strokes (ハ), while two (二) and a vertical stroke (｜) cross above — the abstruse meaning is hidden deep inside the retainer's box, too profound for the eye to see.
reading: The abstruse text is so deep you must 'saku' (サク) through layers of meaning, like cutting through rock.

meaning: A shellfish (貝) with an eye (目) is struck (攵) by two splayed strokes (ハ) — the blow spoils and corrupts it, defeating its value.
reading: The spoiled shellfish makes you say "ハイ" (hai) like "hi!" — a sad greeting to a ruined treasure.

meaning: A vertical stroke pierces a mouth, heart, and eye stacked on a shellfish — like a coin slot that swallows your effort and pays out profit. The shellfish is the treasure you earn.
reading: ワン — Imagine a "wan" (one) dollar coin rolling into the shellfish, earning you a profit.

meaning: Nine shellfish are placed under a lid with a spicy stand-up cross and a dot — a ritual offering laid out on a sacred table. The eye watches as you give it up.
reading: シ — "She" (シ) offers a sacrifice at the shrine, bowing before the spicy stand.

meaning: A shellfish with an eye, two splayed strokes, soil, a direction, a strike, and the 乞-shaped part — all piled up — that's luxury, too many things.
reading: Luxury is 'zei' — like 'zay' in 'gaze' — you gaze at all the expensive stuff. (Reading: ゼイ)

meaning: A 'shellfish' (貝) with an 'eye' (目) and 'two splayed strokes' (ハ) on top, plus a 'stop' (止) and a 'sentence' (文) with a 'halberd' (戈) — this is a beautiful decorated shell, so ornate it stops you mid-sentence.
reading: イン — Imagine an 'inn' (イン) so beautiful you stop and stare at its shell-shaped decorations.

meaning: A shellfish and an eye sit above a rice field, and next to them a day and two short strokes on top — you send a present of shellfish from the field, with a note on the day.
reading: ゾウ — Picture a 'zoo' (ゾウ) where a shellfish and an eye are wrapped as a gift — you send this present to the zoo keeper, who awards it to the elephant.

meaning: A 'shellfish' (貝) with an 'eye' (目) and 'two splayed strokes' (ハ) on top, and below a 'one' (一) 'vertical stroke' (｜) in an 'open box enclosure' (凵) with 'ten' (十) and 'day' (日) and 'west' (西) — this is the earnest money placed on a silk label, a deposit wrapped in a box.
reading: タン — The 'tan' of a deposit is like a 'tan' colored silk label you put on a book to mark your earnest payment.

meaning: A person (人) with a shellfish (貝) and an eye (目) under a lid (亠) — the eye sees the shellfish, and the person gives a sweeping stroke (ノ) of approval, standing on soil (土) with legs (儿) to help you up. So 贊 is to help, support, assist.
reading: サン — Imagine a sun (サン) that shines on the shellfish (貝) and the eye (目), and the person (人) says 'サン' (like 'sun') as they help you up. The sun is the helper that supports the scene.
