meaning: A fish with a huge mouth sits in a rice field, its four dots (杰) like bubbles, and it has two short strokes on top (并) like angry eyebrows — this is the big-mouthed flounder.
reading: The big-mouthed flounder says 'KEN' as it snaps its jaws shut on a can (ケン) of tuna.

meaning: A fish with four dots (杰) at the bottom, sitting in a rice field (田), is being watched by a bird (鳥) from above — the bird dives down to catch the squid.
reading: The squid squirts ink and says 'O' (オ) as it escapes the bird — a round 'O' of ink in the water.

meaning: A fish in a rice field (田) has a sword (刀) and a katakana-mu (厶) stuck in its side — this is the mullet, a fish that fights with a blade-like tail.
reading: The mullet leaps out of the water and shouts 'RYU' (リュウ) like a dragon (ryū) — a dragon-fish.

meaning: A fish in a rice field (田) with four dots (杰) at the bottom, and above it a day (日) with soil (土) and measurement (寸) — this fish measures the day's catch, the Reeves' shad.
reading: The Reeves' shad swims upriver and says 'SHI' (シ) — like 'she' — as it passes the measuring stick.

meaning: A fish in a rice field (田) with four dots (杰) at the bottom, and above it an upside-down box (冂) holding a towel (巾) and a mouth (口) — the yellowtail wears a towel over its mouth.
reading: The yellowtail wraps its head in a towel and says 'SHI' (シ) — like 'she' — as it dives into the box.

meaning: A fish in a rice field (田) with four dots (杰) at the bottom, and above it a buy (買) sign with ice (冫) on it — the widower buys ice for his lonely fish, but he's still unmarried.
reading: The widower says 'KAN' (カン) as he opens a can (kan) of fish — a lonely can, no one to share it.

meaning: A fish with a flat body lies on the seafloor, its fins spread like feathers over a rice field, while ice and a day and a say box sit on top — this is the sole, a flatfish that hides in the sand.
reading: The sole fish is so flat it looks like a 'toe' (トウ) — you step on it with your big toe on the beach.

meaning: A fish with a claw and a tin can on its back, flying over a mountain at evening, with a dot and an open box enclosure — this is the ray, gliding like a kite in the sea.
reading: The ray's wings flap like a 'yo-yo' (ヨウ) going up and down in the water.

meaning: A fish with a rice field on its side, and an old man holding a spoon, with a day above — the old man uses the fin as a fan to cool his face.
reading: The fin is what you 'key' (キ) into the fish's side to steer it — like a key in a lock.

meaning: A fish in a box, with a dish and a person on top, and a rice field inside — the person puts the sardine on a dish, but it's trapped in a box, so it's a canned sardine.
reading: The sardine is 'on' (オン) the dish, ready to eat — just say 'on' and it's served.

meaning: A fish with a bow and ice on its side, over a rice field — the sardine is so weak it can't even pull a bow, it just floats with the ice.
reading: The sardine is 'iwashi' (いわし) — imagine saying 'ee-wash-ee' as you wash the fish with ice water.

meaning: A fish with a vertical stroke and a salute on its side, over a rice field — the sandfish salutes you as it burrows into the sand, leaving only its fin showing.
reading: The sandfish goes 'ha-ta-ha-ta' (はたはた) — like the sound of its tail slapping the sand as it jumps.

meaning: A fish with a car and a rice field on its back, crowded by a person at the side — this is the silver carp, which swims in crowded rice paddies.
reading: The silver carp is long and lean, and you say "ren" (レン) as it streaks past your leg — like a train, but a fish.

meaning: A fish with a lid on top, over soil and a direction, struck by a strike — this huge sea turtle carries a whole landscape on its shell.
reading: The huge sea turtle goes "go" (ゴウ) as it surfaces, like a deep, slow "go" from the ocean floor.

meaning: A fish with a mother inside, who says "do not" — the codfish is the one that refuses to leave the cold water, guarded by a sweeping stroke and a strike.
reading: The codfish is a "bin" (ビン) — like a glass bottle, it's cold and slippery, and you tap it to hear a dull "bin".

meaning: A fish with a little tree and a stooping figure, struck by a strike — the minnow darts under the tree root, avoiding the strike.
reading: The minnow is so small it goes "chow" (チョウ) — like a tiny bite, you barely hear it as it nibbles.

meaning: A fish with a retainer's loyalty, working in the rice field under the soil, using a right hand to pull up four dots at the bottom — that's the bonito, always swimming in disciplined schools.
reading: The bonito leaps like a 'ken' (sword) from the water — imagine a samurai's blade slicing through a school of fish.

meaning: A fish with a hat on top, a katakana-mu shape, and three strokes — the horse mackerel wears a hat and has three stripes, like a little sailor.
reading: The horse mackerel is a "so" (ソウ) — you say "so" as you see it swim by, like "so that's what it looks like".

meaning: A fish (魚) that lives in the rice field (田) under the day (日) sun, but you have to buy (買) it with a right hand (又) and it leaves four dots (杰) of slime on your fingers — that's the eel.
reading: Imagine a giant eel named 'Mann' (マン) who wears a bandana and shouts 'MAN!' as he slithers through the rice paddies.

meaning: A fish (魚) that swims in a straight vertical stroke (｜) through the rice field (田), saying (曰) 'one (一) day (日) I'll be a herring' — but it's just a herring now.
reading: The herring says 'SHOO' (シュウ) as it darts away, like a quick 'shoo!' you'd yell at a cat.

meaning: A fish (魚) with a little (小) show (示) of two (二) air sacs, one on the west (西) side and one on the east, all inside a rice field (田) — that's the fish bladder, the floaty part.
reading: The bladder goes 'HYO' (ヒョウ) like a squeaky toy when you squeeze it — 'hyo! hyo!'

meaning: A fish (魚) that has one (一) ten (十) measurement (寸) of length, with a katakana-mu (厶) shaped mouth, an insect (虫) on its back, and it says (曰) 'day (日) in the rice field (田)' — that's a tiny anchovy.
reading: The anchovy is so small it fits in a 'sen' (セン) — like a sen coin, tiny and round.

meaning: A fish (魚) with a brush (聿) that paints three stacked strokes (ヨ) inside an upside-down box (冂) under a dotted cliff (广), with two (二) vertical strokes (｜) and a month (月) of waiting in the rice field (田) — that's a kind of tench, a lazy bottom-dweller.
reading: The tench says 'SHO' (ショウ) like a slow 'show' — it shows itself only once a month.

meaning: A fish (魚) that makes a sound (音) by standing up (立) on ten (十) legs in the rice field (田) under the day (日), with four dots (杰) of ink — that's the octopus.
reading: The octopus says 'SHO' (ショウ) like a 'show' — it puts on a show with its eight arms.

meaning: A fish with three stacked strokes on top, a rice field and water below, under a dotted cliff. The four dots at the bottom are the anglerfish's glowing lure, and the extend part shows its long fishing rod reaching out from its head.
reading: The anglerfish's glowing lure is like a tiny 'ko' (コウ) light bulb bobbing in the dark water.

meaning: Rain falls on a rice field, and a fish swims below — this fish loves cold, rainy weather, so it's the codfish that thrives in the chill.
reading: The codfish flops on deck with a wet 'ta-ra' (たら) sound, like a slapping tail.

meaning: A turtle with a vertical stroke for a spine, two splayed strokes for legs, two short strokes on top for a shell, an upside-down box for the belly, a towel for skin, a strike for its bite, four dots at the bottom for its feet, a rice field for its home, and a fish for its prey — all in one shell.
reading: The turtle's shell is so hard it 'hets' (hits) like a hammer — imagine a turtle headbutting a wall with a loud 'hetsu' sound.

meaning: A ray glides under one open box enclosure, past ten days of west winds, with a sun and a rice field below — its flat body spreads like a fish with four dots at the bottom, skimming the sea floor.
reading: The ray's wing flaps 'shin' (shin) like a drum — imagine its fin hitting the water with a rhythmic 'shin, shin' beat.

meaning: A dried fish hangs from a vertical stroke, with three stacked strokes for its ribs, a left-side kata for its head, a one-sided piece for its tail, and four dots at the bottom for its shriveled fins — all in a rice field, drying in the sun.
reading: The dried fish is so stiff it 'shuku' (shook) like a board — imagine shaking it and hearing a rattling 'shuku' sound.

meaning: A fish (魚) with a measurement (寸) and a rice field (田) plus west (酉) and two short strokes (并) — the salmon trout swims in the measured, western stream.
reading: The trout jumps and you say "son" (ソン) — like a quick splash, it's gone.

meaning: A moray eel with ten mouths, each with a day's worth of teeth, hiding in a rice field under a fish's body — its four dots at the bottom are its slimy spots, and it strikes like a snake.
reading: The moray eel's bite is a 'sen' (send) of pain — imagine it sending a shock through your arm with a single snap.

meaning: An eel with one long body, two short strokes on top for its head, a mouth for its jaw, a king's crown on its back, a sheep's wool for its skin, and four dots at the bottom for its tail — all in a rice field, slithering.
reading: The eel slithers with a 'sen' (send) of grace — imagine it sending ripples through the water as it moves.

meaning: A fish with a mouth (口) that lacks (欠) a proper jaw — it's a mandarin fish, known for its wide, toothy mouth. The rice field (田) and the cliff (厂) with two short strokes (并) and a left hand (屮) all frame this odd fish.
reading: The mandarin fish is a 'ケイ' — imagine a fish saying 'KAY!' as it jumps out of the water, like a surprised kayaker.

meaning: A fish (魚) covered in scales that look like dancing (舛) rice (米) grains in a rice field (田) — each scale is a tiny shiny grain.
reading: リン — The scales ring like tiny bells — 'rin' (リン) as they shimmer and clink together when the fish moves.

meaning: A fish (魚) that swims past a craft (工) and a measurement (寸) in the river — the sturgeon, a huge ancient fish that can be measured by the meter. The mouth (口) and three stacked strokes (ヨ) show its long snout.
reading: The sturgeon's name is 'シン' — think of a sturgeon wearing a shiny 'shin' guard, like a knight's leg armor, as it swims.

meaning: A fish (魚) that lives near a gentleman (士) who plants beans (豆) in a rice field (田) — the sillaginoid, a small sandfish that buries itself in the mud. The mouth (口) and ten (十) show its tiny, probing snout.
reading: The sillaginoid is called 'きす' — imagine a fish that 'kisses' the sand with its mouth, making a soft 'kiss' sound as it digs.

meaning: A fish with a vertical stroke for a spine, two splayed strokes for fins, and a mouth that opens above a rice field — but the field is covered by a day-long net made of two short strokes on top, and the fish's tail is four dots at the bottom. This odd fish is named after the net that traps it.
reading: The fish is called 'eso' because it's so slippery it always escapes — say 'eh-so' as in 'eh, so it got away again!'

meaning: A king crab has a shell like a rice field, but under it, a crown sits on three stacked strokes, and four dots at the bottom are its legs, while two 'to mix with' claws wave above — all under a fish's body? No, the fish is the crab's meaty center.
reading: The king crab's shell is so hard it makes a loud 'KOH' sound when you knock on it, like a hollow gourd.

meaning: A lizard fish swims in a rice field, but it wears a hat on top, and its body is a fish with a day-marked belly, while a 'buy' sign hangs from its mouth — it's a fish that shops for its prey.
reading: The lizard fish darts away with a quick 'KAI' — like a kayak paddle splashing.

meaning: A sturgeon is a fish that lives in a rice field, but it has a lid on its head, a mouth inside a box, and a day on its side — it's a fish that carries a whole house on its back.
reading: The sturgeon's long body stretches out like a 'TAN' — think of a tan-colored ribbon unrolling in the water.

meaning: A conger eel is a fish that hides in a rice field, but it has a vertical stroke for a spine, and its head is a bean pod with a day inside — it's a fish that grows beans in its mouth.
reading: The conger eel slithers with a 'REI' — like a ray of light bending through water.

meaning: A fish (魚) with a mouth (口) and a day (日) under a crown (冖) and a spoon (匕) on a rice field (田) with four dots at the bottom (杰) — this fish is the cod, a bottom-dweller with a big mouth.
reading: The cod is 'shō' (ショウ) — imagine a codfish wearing a tiny 'shō' (a Japanese sho, a bamboo flute) and blowing bubbles in a show.

meaning: A fish (魚) with a lid (亠) and a vertical stroke (｜) and two splayed strokes (ハ) — this small, sharp fish is the anchovy, a tiny silver dart in the sea.
reading: The anchovy is 'sei' (セイ) — picture a school of anchovies spelling 'say' (セイ) in the water, like they're calling out to you.

meaning: A fish (魚) with one (一) vertical stroke (｜) under a lid (亠) and three stacked strokes (ヨ) with four dots at the bottom (杰) — this is the bream, a flat, silvery fish that swims in shallow rivers.
reading: The bream is 'sho' (ショ) — imagine a bream jumping out of the water and shouting 'sho!' like a short, sharp sound.

meaning: A fish with a king on its back, a northeast zodiac sign on its tail, and a sheep eating from a dish — this giant fish is a shark, the king of the sea.
reading: ショウ — The shark shows off its fin, shouting 'shou' as it leaps over a sheep that's eating on the shore.

meaning: A fish (魚) with a mouth (口) and a king (王) inside a rice field (田) is guarded by four dots (杰) — this fish is so fierce it's a crocodile, lurking in the field like a king.
reading: The crocodile snaps its jaws with a loud 'GAKU' (ガク) — like 'GACK' (ガク) the sound of its bite.

meaning: A fish (魚) sits on a dish (皿) next to a rice field (田), with a spoon (匕) and a divining rod (卜) under a cliff (厂) and tiger spots (虍) — this fish is the sea bass, caught and served on the dish.
reading: The sea bass jumps out of the water with a 'RO' (ロ) — like 'LOW' (ロ) it swims low near the bottom.

meaning: A fish (implied by the radical) with a deer on top — the deer's antlers are tangled in the fish's scales. This strange hybrid creature is an eel, slippery and long like a deer's neck.
reading: Imagine an eel slithering out of a 'LEE' (a sheltered side) of a rock, its body coiling like a question mark.

meaning: Three fish, each with a rice field body and four dots at the bottom, are stacked — so fresh and new that they’re rare and delicious.
reading: You bite into the fresh fish and it’s so good you say “SEN (セン)!” — like a chef’s exclamation of approval.

meaning: The four dots at the bottom (杰) are the bird's feet or tail feathers, and the top part is its body and head. It's a bird — or a chicken on a farm.
reading: A bird chirps 'choo' (チョウ) as it pecks at seeds — think of a train's 'choo-choo' but with wings.

meaning: A bird (鳥) with a hook stroke (乙) for a beak and four dots (杰) on its belly — that's a swallow, darting and hooking through the air.
reading: The swallow's call sounds like 'itsu' (イツ) — 'it's a bird!' you shout, pointing at the swooping shape.

meaning: A bird sitting on a table with four dots — a wild duck. Picture a wild duck resting on a table, with four dots of water dripping from its feathers onto the floor.
reading: フ — Imagine a 'foo' (フ) sound as the wild duck quacks loudly from the table, startling everyone.

meaning: A bird (鳥) with a nine (九) on its head — that's a pigeon, cooing and bobbing its head as if counting to nine.
reading: The pigeon's coo sounds like 'キュウ' (kyuu) — a high-pitched 'kyuu-kyuu' as it pecks at crumbs.

meaning: A wild goose perches on a cliff, its four dots at the bottom like webbed feet gripping the rock.
reading: The goose honks 'GAN' — like the start of 'gang' — as it flies over the cliff. (ガン)

meaning: A bird (鳥) sitting on a table (几) — that's a wild duck that has landed on your picnic table, and it stays until the end of the meal.
reading: The wild duck says 'フ' (fu) as it fluffs its feathers — imagine the sound 'foo' when it shakes off water.

meaning: A bird that enters the water — the grebe dives. Picture the bird (鳥) plunging headfirst into a lake, with the enter (入) part as its beak piercing the surface, and the four dots (杰) as the splash droplets flying up.
reading: The grebe says 'nee-oh' as it dives — think of a tiny bird shouting 'knee-oh!' before splashing. The reading is にお.

meaning: A flag is on top, and below it you have four dots at the bottom and a bird. Imagine a bird with a flag on its back, and the four dots at the bottom are the bird's feet — this bird is a turtledove, known for its distinctive call that sounds like a flag flapping.
reading: The bird with the flag is a 'she' (シ) — picture a female turtledove (she) proudly carrying a flag, and you remember the sound.

meaning: A table with four dots at the bottom holds up a bird — but this is no ordinary bird, it's the male mythical bird, perched on its ceremonial stand, radiating importance.
reading: The male phoenix cries 'ホウ' (hou) — like 'ho!' as in 'ho-ho, what a majestic bird!' — as it spreads its wings over the table.

meaning: A bird with a mouth — the mouth is the bird's beak, and it opens wide to chirp, cry, or bark a sound.
reading: The bird's chirp sounds like 'MAY' — as in 'May I sing?' — and the bird answers with a loud 'メイ' (mei) cry.

meaning: A bird with a piling (弋) stuck in its back, and four dots (杰) like sparks — this is the black kite, a bird that dives to snatch fish, and also a fireman's hook.
reading: The black kite's cry is a sharp 'en' — picture the bird diving with a hook, shouting 'EN!' as it grabs a fish.

meaning: A bird with a branch in its beak, perched on a ten-shaped stand, with four dots at the bottom like seeds it's about to drop.
reading: The bird says 'shi' as it shivers its wings, shaking off the branch.

meaning: A bird with a person (人) and a ユ-shaped stroke (ユ) on top — this is the tailor-bird, sewing leaves with its beak like a worker.
reading: The tailor-bird's call is a quick 'ketsu' (ケツ) — like a snip of scissors.

meaning: A bird with a large (大) person (人) and a ユ-shaped stroke (ユ) plus two (二) — this shrike impales its prey on thorns, a bold hunter.
reading: The shrike's cry is a sharp 'kei' (ケイ) — like a key turning in a lock.

meaning: A bird under a crown (冖) with a crooked-big (尢) body — this poisonous bird hides its venom under a regal crest.
reading: The poison makes you 'chin' (チン) — a dizzy ring in your head.

meaning: A bird with a spoon in its beak, standing on four dots at the bottom — this is the crested ibis, a wild goose-like bird. The madam of a brothel is called a 'wild goose' because she gathers birds (women) under her wing.
reading: The crested ibis says 'HŌ' — imagine a hunter shouting 'HŌ!' as he spots the wild goose in the sky, then it lands on a brothel roof.

meaning: A wild goose perches on a cliff (厂) while a person at the side (化) points at it, and the bird (鳥) has four dots at the bottom (杰) for its feet.
reading: ガン — The goose honks 'gan!' like a gunshot echoing off the cliff.

meaning: A bird (鳥) with a tusk (牙) — that's a crow, which has a sharp, tusk-like beak and a harsh call.
reading: The crow's 'karasu' sounds like 'car-ass' — imagine a crow pecking at a car's rear end, making it honk.

meaning: A bird with a box-on-side enclosure and four dots at the bottom — the dots are the seagull's speckled feathers, and the enclosure is its nest on the shore.
reading: The seagull cries 'ow' (like 'ouch') as it flies — the sound 'ou' is in 'ow'.

meaning: A bird (鳥) wearing a hat (个) and a seal (卩) with one (一) stripe — that's a wagtail, a bird that bobs its tail like a seal's nod.
reading: The wagtail's 'rei' sounds like 'ray' — picture a wagtail wagging its tail like a ray of light flickering on water.

meaning: A bird (鳥) with a spoon (匕) under a roof (宀) — that's the Chinese ostrich, which hides its head under a roof-like wing and eats with a spoon-like beak.
reading: The ostrich's 'da' sounds like 'dah' — imagine a Chinese ostrich saying 'dah!' as it kicks a spoon out of its nest.

meaning: A bird (鳥) that appears in the evening (夕) with a seal (卩) — that's the male mandarin duck, which shows off its sealed, colorful feathers at dusk.
reading: The male mandarin duck's 'en' sounds like 'en' in 'envelope' — picture the duck sealed inside an envelope, delivered at evening time.

meaning: A bird with a mouth that is wrapped in a wrapping enclosure, perched above four dots at the bottom — this is the mynah, known for its chattering beak.
reading: The mynah says 'ク' (ku) — imagine it cooing 'coo' but with a hard K, like a tiny 'ku-ku-ku' from its wrapped mouth.

meaning: An owl with a one-stroke brow over a wrapping enclosure and mouth, sitting on four dots at the bottom — the owl's flat face is a single line above its beak.
reading: The owl hoots 'ヨウ' (you) — picture it saying 'yo-ho-ho' like a pirate owl, with the 'yo' echoing through the night.

meaning: A kite (bird of prey) with a family name carved on its chest — the 氏 part is the family crest, and the bird sits on four dots at the bottom.
reading: The kite screeches 'シ' (shi) — imagine it diving with a sharp 'shee!' sound, like a whistle cutting the air.

meaning: A partridge with a mouth and a ten on its head, standing on four dots at the bottom — the ten is a small crown-like mark on its brow.
reading: The partridge calls 'コ' (ko) — hear it go 'ko-ko-ko' as it pecks the ground, a short and stubby sound.

meaning: A female mandarin duck with a large body under a crown, and four dots at the bottom — the crown is the duck's ornate head crest, and the large part is its plump shape.
reading: The duck quacks 'オウ' (ou) — imagine it saying 'ow!' as it waddles, a long drawn-out 'ou' of surprise.

meaning: A bird (鳥) with a vertical stroke (｜) on its head stands in a rice field (田) under the day (日) sun, but the four dots (杰) at the bottom are its webbed feet — it's a wild duck, an easy mark for hunters.
reading: The wild duck says "OW!" (オウ) when you shoot it — it's an easy mark, so it's an "OW" of pain.

meaning: A bird flying fast, swooping — it has a hole (the 穴) as its body, with two splayed strokes as wings, a roof over its head, and a pair of legs trailing behind, all above four dots at the bottom.
reading: It swoops with a 'イツ' (itsu) — think 'it's so fast!' — the 'itsu' is the whoosh of air as it dives through the hole.

meaning: A bird (鳥) that lives in the rice field (田) — a snipe, a shy wading bird that hides among the paddies.
reading: Imagine a snipe with a tiny sign around its neck that says 'SHIGGY' — like a dog named Shiggy — as it pecks in the mud. (しぎ = shigi, sounds like 'shiggy')

meaning: Esteem (尚) for the nightingale is shown by placing a crown (冖) on its head, and its song ends with four dots (杰) of musical notes—this is the bush warbler.
reading: The nightingale sings 'ou' (オウ) from the treetops, a long, round 'ou' that echoes through the forest.

meaning: A bird that says 'and yet' (而) while sitting on four dots (杰) — a swallow that perches on a wire, the dots are its droppings below.
reading: The swallow dives down and says 'JEE!' (like 'gee') — a quick 'ji' sound as it swoops past your ear.

meaning: A bird (鳥) with a tongue (舌) sticking out of its mouth (口) — the crow that caws with its tongue out, making a harsh 'ka' sound.
reading: The crow's caw is a sharp 'KATSU!' (like 'cats') — imagine a crow that says 'katsu' as it pecks at a cat.

meaning: A woman under a roof sees four dots at the bottom — that’s a quail pecking at grain scattered on the floor.
reading: The quail says 'an' as it pecks — imagine it singing 'AN-AN-AN' under the roof.

meaning: A large bird with a bow-shaped beak and four dots on its tail, standing under a roof — that's the pelican.
reading: The pelican's pouch is a 'tay' (like a tea bag) — it holds fish like a big tea strainer.

meaning: A craft (工) floats on water at the side (汁) while a bird (鳥) with four dots at the bottom (杰) — this is the large wild goose, so big it carries the whole lake on its back.
reading: The goose honks 'ko' (like 'co' in 'code') as it flies over the craft — a deep, resonant 'ko'.

meaning: A mouth and a woman sit above four dots and a bird — this quail-like bird chirps with a woman’s voice.
reading: The bird’s chirp is 'jo' — imagine it saying 'JO-jo' while hopping near the woman’s mouth.

meaning: A cow’s head (with the katakana-mu shape) sits on a bird with four dots — the crested ibis has a cow-like tuft on its head.
reading: The ibis cries 'bo' — picture it saying 'BO-bo' as it struts like a cow.

meaning: A mouth with a hat on top (and a one underneath) sits above a bird with four dots — the temple pigeon coos from under its little hat.
reading: The pigeon’s coo is 'ko' — imagine it saying 'KO-ko' while wearing that hat.

meaning: A father under a lid stands next to a bird with four dots — the night heron perches like a father watching over the pond at night.
reading: The heron’s night call is 'ko' — picture it saying 'KO-ko' in the dark, with the father nodding.

meaning: A bird with a person at the side (化) perched on a tree (木), and four dots at the bottom (杰) like its speckled feathers — this is the horned owl, a bird of ill omen.
reading: The owl's hooting sounds like "kyuu" (キュウ) — imagine it crying "kyuu-kyuu" in the dark forest.

meaning: A bird (鳥) reaching its climax (至) — it dives from the sky like a kite, then lands on the soil (土) with a katakana-mu shape (厶) of dust puffing up.
reading: The kite's sharp cry is "shi" (シ) — like a hissing "shhh" as it swoops down.

meaning: A bird (鳥) that goes (行) along the shore, stopping (彳) at each wave — this is the plover, a small running bird.
reading: The plover's call is "chi-dori" (ちどり) — imagine it chirping "chi! chi!" as it darts.

meaning: A bird (鳥) with big ears (耳) — this kite (a bird of prey) listens for prey in the grass, its ear-like tufts visible.
reading: The kite's name is "tobi" (とび) — imagine it doing a "toe-bee" dive, toes first, to catch a bee.

meaning: A bird (鳥) with plain, unmottled feathers — it looks like a craft (工) project made by a person (人) who forgot to add spots.
reading: The unmottled quail says 'boo' (ブ) — imagine it hiding in a bush, going 'boo' to scare you.

meaning: A bird (鳥) that sings at the moon (月) with its mouth (口) open — that's the cuckoo, calling out in the night.
reading: The cuckoo's call is 'KEN' — imagine it shouting 'Ken!' like a friend's name, over and over.

meaning: A bird (鳥) that talks like a person — it has a mouth (口) and a rice field (田) for a brain, but it's still a mynah bird, repeating what you say.
reading: The mynah bird says 'YOKU' — imagine it saying 'yoku' (like 'yoga' but with a 'ku') while doing a little yoga pose.

meaning: A crown sits on a ten, and a child holds it up, but the bird underneath is what makes it a plump pigeon — the crown and ten are just its fancy headgear.
reading: ホツ — The pigeon says 'hots' as it pecks at a hot pot of seeds, burning its beak.

meaning: A shellfish with an eye and two splayed strokes sits on a bird — this shrike impales its prey on thorns, and the eye is the sharp lookout it keeps.
reading: ケキ — The shrike's call is a sharp 'kek' — like a quick, harsh cough in the bushes.

meaning: A bird with a vertical stroke and a sweeping stroke on top, a bow shape in the middle, and four dots at the bottom — this is a cormorant, a bird that dives for fish.
reading: The cormorant's call sounds like 'oo' as in 'boo' — imagine it saying 'oo' while perched on a boat.

meaning: A bird with a barb and a halberd — the goose's neck is the barb, and its honk is the halberd's swing, loud and aggressive.
reading: ガ — The goose says 'ga' — a flat, honking sound like a rusty gate opening.

meaning: Same as 鵝 — a bird with a barb and a halberd, but here the barb is bent down, like a goose lowering its head to charge.
reading: ガ — The goose's 'ga' is the same — it's the sound of a startled shout when it flaps at you.

meaning: A crime scene: a king sits on a bird, but the bird is the buzzard — the king is just a decoy, and the buzzard is the real predator circling above.
reading: キョウ — The buzzard's cry is a long 'kyou' — like a mournful 'kyoo' echoing over the valley.

meaning: A swan with a sweeping stroke for a neck, a mouth open, and a bird body, standing on soil with four dots at the bottom — that's the swan.
reading: The swan's call is a deep 'kok' — like 'kok' in 'coconut' — and it echoes over the lake. (Reading: コク)

meaning: A bird that stops, holding a piling and a halberd, with four dots at the bottom. This fancy bird is a cockatoo.
reading: ブ — The cockatoo says 'boo' as it dances, a playful 'bu' like a bubble popping.

meaning: An angle on a bird — the grosbeak's beak is a sharp angle, perfect for cracking seeds, and the bird itself is the angle's owner.
reading: いかる — The grosbeak's call is a sharp 'ikaru' — like a quick 'I car!' as it darts between trees.

meaning: A bird with a dot, an upside-down box, a right hand, a flag, and a month inside. This owl-like bird is a buzzard.
reading: フク — The buzzard hoots 'fuku' (good luck) from a tree, a soft 'fu-ku' like a gentle wind.

meaning: A large bird with a vertical stroke on top, a day under it, and four dots at the bottom — it's a quail, small and speckled like dots, hiding under the big day sky.
reading: The quail says 'an' as it pecks at an 'an'vil (アン) in the field.

meaning: A bird with a ten and a divining rod on top, and a day below — the pheasant uses the rod to poke the day, making it burst into a colorful display.
reading: The pheasant's call is a sharp 'to' (トウ) — like 'toe' — it pecks your toe to get your attention.

meaning: A phoenix is a giant bird (鳥) that flies so high it touches the month (月) itself, and its fiery tail leaves four dots (杰) of glowing ember behind.
reading: The phoenix cries 'HOU!' (ホウ) as it bursts through the clouds, like a loud 'hoe' (as in garden tool) striking the sky.

meaning: A bird with a ten on top, a rice field in the middle, and four dots at the bottom — the brown eared bulbul hops through the rice field, scattering ten dots of seed.
reading: The bulbul's song is a quick 'hi' (ヒ) — like 'hee' — it giggles 'hee hee' as it flits.

meaning: A bird with a vertical stroke, two, an upside-down box, a mouth, and soil — the eagle carries a box of soil in its beak, dropping it from a great height.
reading: The eagle's cry is a long 'chou' (チョウ) — like 'chow' — it screams 'chow!' as it dives for food.

meaning: A bird with a vertical stroke, one, and a day — the magpie perches on a single day-old branch, its black-and-white feathers like a day and night split.
reading: The magpie's chatter is 'shaku' (シャク) — like 'shack' — it builds a shack of twigs.

meaning: A bird with a seal, an evening, and a roof — the co-worker bird stamps its seal under the roof at evening, clocking out together.
reading: The co-worker says 'en' (エン) — like 'end' — it's the end of the workday, so it flies home.

meaning: A fabulous night bird — imagine a chimera made of a bird, a lid, four dots at the bottom, a person at the side, and evening. The lid is clamped shut over the four dots, trapping the evening inside, while the person at the side watches the bird — this weird mix is the chimera.
reading: The chimera cries 'YA!' at the evening sky — a sharp, startled sound like 'ya' in 'yacht' but short. (Reading: ヤ)

meaning: A pigeon — see an old bird (隹) perched on a bird (鳥) with four dots at the bottom (杰) as its feet. The old bird is teaching the young pigeon to coo, but the pigeon just sits there, plump and calm.
reading: The pigeon goes 'SUI-SUI' as it pecks at rice — a soft, quick double sound like 'swee-swee'. (Reading: スイ)

meaning: A bird resembling the crane — take a spoon (匕), a day (日), compare (比), and four dots at the bottom (杰) under a bird (鳥). The spoon and day are compared side by side, and the bird with four dots stands tall like a crane, measuring the day with its long neck.
reading: The crane calls 'KON!' like a deep drum — imagine a big bird hitting a gong with a spoon, the sound echoing 'kon'. (Reading: コン)

meaning: A hawk — see a pair of legs (儿) standing on a mortar (臼) that sits on four dots at the bottom (杰), all under a bird (鳥). The hawk perches on the mortar, its legs gripping the rim, ready to strike.
reading: The hawk screeches 'GEKI!' as it dives — a sharp, explosive sound like 'geh-kee' from a comic book. (Reading: ゲキ)

meaning: A thrush — a vertical stroke (｜) pierces a tree (木) in a rice field (田), with a day (日) and two splayed strokes (ハ) on top, all under a bird (鳥) with four dots at the bottom (杰). The thrush sings on the tree, its song piercing the field.
reading: The thrush sings 'TOU' like a flute — a long, clear note, as if saying 'toe' but drawn out. (Reading: トウ)

meaning: A quail — a mouth (口) and a child (子) sit under a lid (亠) with four dots at the bottom (杰), all under a bird (鳥). The quail hides its chick under a lid, pecking at the ground with its mouth, camouflaged in the field.
reading: The quail says 'JUN' as it scurries — a quick, soft sound like 'joon' in 'June' but shorter. (Reading: ジュン)

meaning: A bird with a person under a dotted cliff, three stacked strokes, and four dots at the bottom — this odd bird sings so sweetly it's called an oriole.
reading: The oriole's song goes 'koo-koo' — imagine a bird perched on a cliff, singing 'コウ' to the person below.

meaning: A bird with a sweeping stroke, a wrapping enclosure, a day, and a 'not' — this bird's crossed beak says 'not a day for seeds' — it's a crossbill.
reading: The crossbill's beak is like a bent 'isu' (chair) — it sits on a branch, saying 'いすか' as it twists seeds.

meaning: A chicken is a bird (鳥) with four dots (杰) on its tail, and it scratches the soil (土) with its claw (爪) while a person (人) throws two (二) grains of large (大) corn — that's your dinner.
reading: The chicken says 'KEI' (ケイ) — like 'kay' (ケイ) as in 'okay', a short cluck.

meaning: A bird with a sweeping stroke on top, a tree and fire below, and a grain stalk — this large waterfowl with a naked head stands in the reeds, its head bare like a swept stroke.
reading: The waterfowl says 'shoo' to scare away other birds, but it's just a 'shu' sound.

meaning: A bird with a head (疋) and a say (曰) — the hawk says 'say' with its head, and the four dots are the feathers it drops while hunting.
reading: テイ — The hawk is 'テイ' (tay) — it says 'tay' as it dives, like a tea kettle whistling from the sky.

meaning: A bird with a big mouth (口) that scoops up fish — the pelican. The ten (十) and month (月) parts are its long beak and pouch, and the four dots at the bottom (杰) are the splash it makes.
reading: The pelican's beak is so big it looks like a 'ko' (コ) — like the sound of a cork popping from a bottle of 'ko'la it swallowed.

meaning: An osprey dives from the sky, its mouth (口) open, with two (二) wings spread wide, wrapped in a hunting swoop (勹) — the four dots at the bottom (杰) are the fish it grabs.
reading: The osprey's cry is a sharp 'gaku' (ガク) — like a student's 'gaku' (学) shout when it spots prey.

meaning: A crossbill with a twisted beak — the person (人) and wrapping enclosure (勹) show its crossed mandibles, the day (日) is its bright eye, and the four dots at the bottom (杰) are the seeds it cracks.
reading: The crossbill's beak snaps with a 'katsu' (カツ) — like a karate chop cutting through a seed.

meaning: A black songbird that rides in a car (車) under a crown (冖) — the four dots at the bottom (杰) are its shiny black feathers, and the car is its perch.
reading: The songbird's tune is a low 'un' (ウン) — like the hum of a car engine idling.

meaning: A domestic duck waddles with a halberd (矛) in its beak, striking (攵) at the ground — the four dots at the bottom (杰) are its webbed footprints, and the 乞-shaped part (乞) is its quacking bill.
reading: The duck's quack is a soft 'boku' (ボク) — like a gentle 'bok' of a wooden paddle on water.

meaning: A thrush perches on a tree (木), its mouth (口) open, with a vertical stroke (｜) for its tail, and it buys (買) seeds with two short strokes (并) — the four dots at the bottom (杰) are the berries it drops.
reading: The thrush's song is a quick 'tsu' (ツ) — like a short 'tsu' of a flute note.

meaning: A bird with a hat on top (个) and a mouth (口) inside a day (日) — this bird sings all day long, so it must be an oriole. The four dots (杰) at the bottom are its tail feathers, and the bird (鳥) itself is the body.
reading: The oriole's song sounds like 'sow' (ソウ) — imagine it singing 'sow, sow' as it plants seeds in the field.

meaning: A bird with a crown on its head and four dots at the bottom (like a musical note) — this is the nightingale, famous for its song. The crown sits above the bird, and the four dots at the bottom are the notes it sings.
reading: The nightingale sings 'oh-wah' (オウ) — imagine the bird opening its beak wide and letting out a clear 'oh-wah' call that echoes through the forest.

meaning: A bird (鳥) with a roof (宀) and a vertical stroke (｜) plus two (二) — the bird flies up to the roof, then soars straight up past the two beams. The dot (丶) and sweeping stroke (ノ) are the wind it leaves behind.
reading: To soar, the bird says 'ken' (ケン) — imagine it shouting 'ken!' as it kicks off the roof to fly.

meaning: A bird (鳥) with feathers (羽) and ice (冫) — the crested flycatcher has icy-cold feathers on its head. The two splayed strokes (ハ) are its open beak, and the katakana-mu shape (厶) is its crest.
reading: The flycatcher's peep sounds like 'hi-ta-ki' (ひたき) — imagine it saying 'hi, ta-ki' as it snaps up flies.

meaning: A bird (鳥) with four dots at the bottom (杰) stands under a roof (宀) wearing a crown (冖) — an old bird (隹) bows, and the crane stretches its neck to peek out.
reading: The crane's call is a sharp "KAKU" (カク) — like a quick, dry cough in the morning mist.

meaning: A bird (鳥) wrapped in a wrapping enclosure (勹) with a left hand (屮) — the chick is so small it's wrapped in a bundle, and the left hand holds it. The four dots (杰) are its tiny feet.
reading: The chick's peep is 'su' (ス) — imagine it saying 'su-su' as it snuggles in the wrapping enclosure.

meaning: A bird (鳥) with a bow (弓) and ice (冫) — the siskin has a bow-shaped beak that's cold as ice. The two splayed strokes (ハ) are its wing tips, and the four dots (杰) are its greenish-yellow speckles.
reading: The siskin's chirp is 'jaku' (ジャク) — imagine it saying 'jaku-jaku' as it hops on icy branches.

meaning: A bird with a rice field on its back, guarded by a sword and a katakana-mu shape, all perched on four dots at the bottom — this is the owl, silent hunter of the fields.
reading: The owl's call sounds like 'リュウ' — imagine a dragon (リュウ) with owl eyes, perched on a rice field, hooting 'リュウ' at the moon.

meaning: A bird with a large lid on its head, two short strokes on top, and a person standing beside a month — this wagtail bobs its tail like a person checking the calendar.
reading: The wagtail's quick steps sound like 'セキ' — think of a security guard (セキ) chasing the wagtail across a field, shouting 'セキ!'

meaning: A bird with a skeleton inside an upside-down box, crowned with a crown — this falcon dives from the sky, its bones visible through thin wings.
reading: The falcon's dive is 'コツ' — imagine it hitting a bone (コツ) mid-air, cracking it with a sharp 'コツ' sound.

meaning: A bird with two short strokes on top, three stacked strokes, and a dot — this is the fabulous mythical bird, a creature of legend with a strange pattern.
reading: The mythical bird sings 'ケン' — like the sound of a bell 'ケン' echoing in a temple.

meaning: A hawk — its shape is a bird with a sweeping stroke and a sword, ready to strike from above.
reading: The hawk's cry is 'ジュン' — imagine it swooping down to grab a juniper branch (ジュン) in its talons, screeching 'ジュン'.

meaning: A bird with a short thread and two short strokes on top, plus a one — this cormorant dives with a thread tied to its leg, controlled by a fisherman.
reading: The cormorant's splash is 'シ' — think of a shee (シ) — a female sheep — standing on the shore, bleating 'シ' as the cormorant dives.

meaning: The bird is perched on a dish, but the dish is actually a fishing boat — this bird dives from the dish to catch fish, so it's the fishing cormorant.
reading: The cormorant says 'shi' as it dives — imagine it hissing 'shii!' while plunging into the water. (Reading: シ)

meaning: A bird with a dish on its head and two short strokes on top — it tries to fly high, but the dish weighs it down, so it only flies high when the wind is behind it.
reading: The waterfowl shouts 'geki!' as it flaps against the wind — a sharp, strained cry. (Reading: ゲキ)

meaning: The sparrow hawk perches on a tin can (缶) under the evening (夕) sky, its four dots (杰) of tail feathers spread wide, while an open box enclosure (凵) traps its prey below.
reading: The hawk's cry 'yoh!' echoes as it swoops — like saying 'yo!' to get its attention. (readingKey: ヨウ)

meaning: A bird under a roof, with a woman and a day inside — the woman spends the day hiding under the roof with the bird, which is a quail that stays low and hidden.
reading: The quail says 'an' — a soft, muffled sound like a quiet 'ahn' from under the brush. (Reading: アン)

meaning: A large bird with a claw and a short thread — the claw scratches the thread, and the large bird is the chicken that pecks and scratches the ground.
reading: The chicken clucks 'kei!' — a sharp, quick 'kay' sound as it pecks. (Reading: ケイ)

meaning: A bird with two splayed strokes, an eye, and a spoon — the bird uses the spoon to stir its food, and its eye is yellow-white mottled — a songbird with a speckled look.
reading: The songbird sings 'ten' — a clear, high 'ten' note that rings out. (Reading: テン)

meaning: A bird (鳥) sits on a table (几) under a crown (冖), while a gentleman (士) pokes it with a pike (殳) — the chicks (fledglings) scatter from the nest, each with four dots (杰) of fluff at the bottom.
reading: The chicks peep 'コウ' (kou) as they hop — imagine a tiny beak saying 'ko-ko-ko' while a crow (カラス) watches, but the sound is 'コウ' like 'ko' in 'koala'.

meaning: A pheasant (鳥) struts past an upside-down box (冂) with a mouth (口) inside, and a tripod (鬲) stands nearby — the pheasant's tail feathers look like two short strokes (并) on top of the tripod.
reading: The pheasant's call echoes 'ゲキ' (geki) — imagine it shouting 'GEKI!' like a dramatic 'geki' (激) intense cry, but here it's just the bird's loud squawk.

meaning: A yellow-white mottled songbird (鳥) has ten (十) spots on its back, and its eye (目) is ringed with two splayed strokes (ハ) — it perches on a branch, singing with a crown (杰) of feathers at the bottom.
reading: The songbird sings 'テン' (ten) — imagine it counting 'ten, ten, ten' as it hops, like a tiny metronome ticking 'テン'.

meaning: A bird sits under a dotted cliff, with a one-stroke line and an open box enclosure nearby — the partridge hides in rocky, box-like crevices.
reading: The partridge's call is a sharp 'sha' (シャ) — like a quick shush from the bushes.

meaning: An old bird and a bird together, with a mouth and four dots at the bottom — the mouth is open, and the dots are the sound waves of its call.
reading: The bird's call is a long 'yo' (ヨウ) — like a slow 'yo-ho' echoing across the valley.

meaning: A seagull with a large body, a pike in its beak, and a right hand holding a dart — all under a table with a sweeping stroke and a box-on-side enclosure. This bird is a bold hunter of the shore.
reading: The seagull cries 'ei' (エイ) as it dives — like a sharp 'ay!' from a startled sailor.

meaning: A bird with a mouth and four dots at the bottom, inside a box-on-side enclosure — the seagull's open mouth and scattered dots are its cries over the waves.
reading: The seagull's call is a hollow 'ou' (オウ) — like a foghorn's low 'oh' over the sea.

meaning: A bird of prey sits on a stand up, but it's made of nine spicy ten — it's so fierce and rough that even the dot and a lid can't calm it. The four dots at the bottom are its talons, ready to strike — this bird is daring and desolate.
reading: Imagine a fierce bird of prey screaming 'GO!' (ゴウ) as it dives — the sound is a sharp, daring 'GOU' that echoes over a desolate cliff.

meaning: A skylark with feathers and three ice crystals on its back, wearing a hat on top, sings under a sweeping stroke of wind. The four dots at the bottom are its tiny feet hopping through the grass — it's a small anthus, a skylark.
reading: The skylark's song is a long, flowing 'RYUU' (リュウ) that rises like a gentle stream — think of a river (ryuu) of melody pouring from its beak.

meaning: A large bird with four dots at the bottom and to mix with patterns on its wings — this is the turquoise kingfisher, flashing bright colors as it dives. The large body and the mix of hues make it unmistakable.
reading: The kingfisher's dive makes a sharp 'SOU' (ソウ) as it hits the water — like a swift 'sow' of a needle through a pond.

meaning: A phoenix with one sweeping stroke, a large direction, and a dart in its beak, standing on four dots at the bottom. The bird rises from ashes, carrying a dart of fire — a majestic phoenix.
reading: The phoenix's cry is a crisp 'SAKU' (サク) — like the snap of a twig in a sacred grove, quick and bright.

meaning: A bird with a little short thread on its head, a body made of a short thread wrapped around a vertical stroke, and four dots at the bottom for legs — this is the egret, standing in the rice field, its white feathers like tangled threads.
reading: The egret is 'shirasagi' — think 'sheer-a-soggy' — the bird wades in water so its white feathers get sheer and soggy.

meaning: An old bird (隹) and a bird (鳥) both sit on a branch with four dots (杰) — the wren, a tiny bird that flits about. The old bird (隹) is the wren's ancestor, small and quick.
reading: The wren is 'ショウ' — imagine a wren singing a short 'show' tune, a little performance on a branch, like a tiny 'show'.

meaning: A cormorant sits on a gentleman's crown, above a mouth that is chewing beans, while two short strokes on top mark it as a bird of trickery.
reading: The cormorant says 'イ' (ee) — like the squeaky 'ee' of a fishing boat's pulley as it dives for fish.

meaning: A pheasant with a towel draped over its head, struck by a strike, stands under an upside-down box, with two splayed strokes and two short strokes on top — a fancy bird indeed.
reading: The pheasant's cry is 'ヘツ' (hetsu) — like 'hetsu' when you sneeze and the bird flutters away.

meaning: A turquoise kingfisher perches on a one-sided plank, with three stacked strokes on its left-side kata, and two short strokes on top — a bird of the riverbank.
reading: The kingfisher darts 'シュク' (shuku) — like 'shuku' the quick zip of its wings as it snatches a minnow.

meaning: A water hen wades through a rice field, picking rice with its beak, while four dots at the bottom mark its muddy feet — a bird of the paddies.
reading: The water hen calls 'ハン' (han) — like 'han' the splash of its foot in the shallow water.

meaning: A wren, little and large at once, sits on a day that has a lid, with two short strokes on top — a tiny bird with a big voice.
reading: The wren sings 'リョウ' (ryou) — like 'ryou' the echo of its trill in a hollow log.

meaning: A bird (鳥) with a little (小) mouth (口) and a dot (丶) on top, perched on a crooked-big (尢) branch with four dots (杰) — that's the eagle, fierce and still.
reading: The eagle's cry is a sharp "shuu" (シュウ) as it swoops down from the sky.

meaning: A silver pheasant struts through a gate, with a month on its back and four dots at the bottom — a bird that shines in the moonlight.
reading: The pheasant's call is 'カン' (kan) — like 'kan' the clang of a bell as it startles from the brush.

meaning: A bird with a gate on its back, standing on a tree, with four dots at the bottom — this is the silver pheasant badge, worn by officials of the 5th grade. The gate is the badge's frame, the tree is the perch, and the four dots are the silver feathers.
reading: The official's badge is so shiny it makes you say 'KAN' (as in 'can' — 'I CAN see it from across the room').

meaning: A bird with a mouth and a halberd, standing on a pair of legs inside an upside-down box, with four dots at the bottom — this is the kingfisher, which dives like a spear (halberd) into water, and the snipe, which probes mud with its long mouth.
reading: The kingfisher's dive is so quick it's just a flash — 'ITSU' (sounds like 'it's so' — 'it's so fast!').

meaning: A dotted cliff (广) with a person at the side (化) and an old bird (隹) — the hawk perches on the cliff, watching the person below, ready to strike.
reading: ヨウ — The hawk's cry echoes 'yow' (ヨウ) across the valley, a sharp 'yow' that makes you look up.

meaning: A heron stands on one leg (足) with a mouth (口) open, its body a bird (鳥) with a stooping figure (夂) — it bends down to catch fish in the shallows.
reading: ロ — The heron's long neck curves into a loop (ロ) as it strikes — 'ro' like the round shape it makes.

meaning: A long-tailed bird sits on a mortar, but it wears a crown and has four dots on its chest, while its wings are 'to mix with' — it's a bird that stirs the sky.
reading: The bullfinch's call is a soft 'KAKU' — like a quiet cackle from a hidden perch.

meaning: A swallow is a bird that stands up on a heart, but it has a day on its wing and a sound in its beak — it sings a melody that makes your heart stand up.
reading: The swallow chirps a quick 'I' — like the 'ee' in 'eel' as it dives.

meaning: A bird with a large body and a short thread-like tail stands in water at the side, its four dots at the bottom like ripples — this is the mandarin duck, a kind of water bird.
reading: ケイ — Imagine the bird saying 'KAY!' as it splashes in the water, like a loud squawk that sounds like 'kay'.

meaning: A hawk sits on a box with a lid, its mouth open, watching the day pass — this bird of prey hunts by sight, a fierce hawk.
reading: セン — Picture the hawk diving at a 'sen' (a coin, like a sen) on the ground, its talons striking the metal with a clang.

meaning: A bird with an eye and a shellfish on its back, perched above four dots at the bottom — this flashy bird is the mango-bird, the Chinese oriole. The eye sees the shellfish, and the bird sings from the branch.
reading: The oriole says 'ヨウ' — imagine it yelling 'YO!' at you from the tree, a loud 'ヨウ' that echoes through the mango grove.

meaning: A large bird with a dog's head and a crime on its back, standing over four dots at the bottom — this is a kind of large waterfowl with red feathers. The dog barks at the crime, and the bird is big and red.
reading: The waterfowl honks 'ガク' — picture it gasping 'GAKU!' in shock as the dog commits a crime on its back.

meaning: A bird with three stacked strokes on top, a sweeping stroke, and a vertical stroke — this jackdaw is a messy bird that piles up sticks. The three strokes are its nest, the sweeping stroke is its tail, and the bird sits on four dots at the bottom.
reading: The jackdaw caws 'ヨ' — imagine it saying 'YO!' as it drops a stick, a short sharp 'ヨ' like a quick call.

meaning: A bird (鳥) with tiger spots (虍) on its back, a spoon (匕) and a divining rod (卜) under a cliff (厂), standing on a dish (皿) with a rice field (田) — this cormorant is a fishing bird, perched on the dish after diving.
reading: The cormorant's head bobs with a 'RO' (ロ) — like 'LOW' (ロ) it keeps its head low when hunting fish.

meaning: A parrot with a shellfish eye, two splayed strokes for a beak, and a woman's face — it mimics her words, perched on a bird with four dots at the bottom.
reading: イン — The parrot says 'IN!' as it imitates a doorbell, the sound ringing in your ears.

meaning: A Japanese stork with a mouth, grass on top, and an old bird's wing — it stands in a field, its beak open, with four dots at its feet.
reading: カン — The stork lands with a loud 'KAN!' as its feet hit the metal roof, a sharp clang.

meaning: Four dots at the bottom, an eye, an old bird, and a bird — the old bird watches the other bird with a sharp eye, and this is a mynah, known for its talking.
reading: The mynah bird says 'ク' (ku) — a short, sharp 'ク' like a quick squawk, and you remember it by that sound.

meaning: A bird with a deer's head and a spoon for a beak, standing under a dotted cliff. This odd bird sings like an oriole, its song echoing off the cliff.
reading: The oriole's call sounds like 'LEE-ay' — imagine it repeating 'LEE-ay, LEE-ay' from a branch, each note a little bell.

meaning: A fabulous mythical bird — see the 鳥 (bird) at the bottom, and above it a 言 (say) with 糸 (thread) and 幺 (short thread) wrapped around a 小 (little) — imagine the bird’s song tying threads of silk into a crown, an imperial bird.
reading: The reading is ラン. Picture a 'run' — the mythical bird takes a long run before leaping into the sky, its feathers trailing like a banner.

meaning: Salt is stored in a box (囗) with ten (十) grains of salt inside — a solid block of salt, like a brick.
reading: You 'ro' the salt — 'ro' like 'row' — you row the salt boat to shore.

meaning: A mouth, ten, a person, a hat on top, a box, and salt — the salt in the box makes your mouth pucker — that's saltiness.
reading: Imagine a salty taste so strong it makes you say 'ケン!' — like a punch to the tongue from a box of salt.

meaning: A box of salt (鹵) with a halberd (戈) guarding it, and a mouth (口) tasting it — the saltiness is so strong it makes you pucker. The sweeping stroke (ノ) and divining rod (卜) are the salt crystals piling up.
reading: Imagine a salty wave crashing over a can (カン) of soda, making it taste like seawater. The 'kan' in 'can' is the sound.

meaning: Salt (鹵) is ground by a craft (工) worker who uses a king (王) to press it, while a sheep (羊) watches — the salt is mixed with two short strokes (并) and a box (囗) of crystals, all under a one (一) and a sweeping stroke (ノ).
reading: The salt tastes 'サ' (sa) — imagine licking a salty cracker and saying 'sa!' like 'sah' in 'salsa', but the sound is just 'サ'.

meaning: Impure sodium carbonate (natron) sits in a box (囗) with a vertical stroke (｜) and a dot (丶) on top, while salt (鹵) is mixed with three stacked strokes (ヨ) and two short strokes (并) — it's a crusty, salty residue.
reading: The natron fizzes 'カン' (kan) — imagine a can (カン) of soda fizzing with salt, the sound 'kan' like 'can' but with a hard 'k'.

meaning: A person with a hat on top stands on ten boxes of salt, and the salt is so strong it makes the mouth pucker — this is alkaline, lye, or salt.
reading: ケン — Imagine a 'ken' (a Japanese sword) dipped in lye — the blade fizzes and corrodes, making a sharp 'ken' sound.

meaning: A retainer in a box, with ten and a dish below, and the 乞-shaped part on top — this is salt. The retainer guards the box of salt, and the dish catches the grains that fall from the 乞-shaped scoop.
reading: Salt is 'エン' — imagine a chef yelling 'EN!' as he accidentally pours too much salt into the dish, a salty 'エン' of regret.

meaning: A deer is standing under a dotted cliff, comparing its antlers to the cliff's edge — the deer sees its own shape in the rock.
reading: ロク — Imagine a deer wearing a tiny lock (ロク) around its neck, and the key is hidden under the dotted cliff.

meaning: A female deer — the doe. See the deer (鹿) with a spoon (匕) on its head, like a little crown, and the dotted cliff (广) as a rocky ledge it stands on, while the compare (比) part shows two does side by side.
reading: The doe says 'you' softly — imagine a shy doe whispering 'you' to her fawn. The reading is ユウ.

meaning: Rough, crude, coarse — like a deer that hasn't been groomed. Picture a deer (鹿) with a rough, shaggy coat, standing under a dotted cliff (广) with a wrapping enclosure (勹) tied loosely around its body, and a spoon (匕) scraping off mud — all rough and unfinished.
reading: Rough sandpaper goes 'so-so' — imagine rubbing coarse stone and hearing a dull 'so' sound. The reading is ソ.

meaning: A species of deer — the muntjac, small and shy. See the deer (鹿) hiding under a dotted cliff (广), with a table (几) as a low branch it ducks under, and a spoon (匕) as its tiny antler, while the compare (比) part shows it peeking out cautiously.
reading: The muntjac's call is a sharp 'kee' — like a high-pitched squeak. The reading is キ.

meaning: A deer under a dotted cliff, with a spoon and 'compare' above it — the deer uses its antlers to till and plow the soil beneath the cliff, comparing the furrows it makes.
reading: The deer tills the field with a 'HŌ' — picture a farmer yelling 'HŌ!' to the deer as it plows, like calling a horse.

meaning: A deer under a dotted cliff, but with two splayed strokes and a sword instead of a spoon — the deer's fur is coarse and rough, and it rudely swipes its sword at the cliff, leaving rough scratches.
reading: The coarse deer is 'SO' rude — imagine it saying 'SO?' sarcastically as it scratches the cliff with its sword.

meaning: A deer (鹿) with a wrapping enclosure (勹) around its body, a spoon (匕) for a nose, and a 'stop' (已) sign on its flank—this is the small spotted deer.
reading: The deer bounds 'hou' (ホウ) over the hills—say 'hou' as it leaps, like a soft 'ho' and a quick 'u'.

meaning: A deer (鹿) with no antlers, standing under a dotted cliff (广) with a grain stalk (禾) in its mouth, and a tree (木) nearby—this is the hornless deer that gathers in herds.
reading: The hornless deer gather with a 'kin' (キン) sound—like a soft bell 'kin' that calls them together.

meaning: A deer (鹿) with a king (王) on its back, holding a dot (丶) in its mouth, standing under a dotted cliff (广)—this is the moose, and the king uses its tail as a horsehair flapper.
reading: The moose's heavy steps go 'shu' (シュ) through the snow—say 'shu' as it plods, a soft, slow sound.

meaning: A deer (鹿) that compares (比) its antlers to rice (米) stalks — this is the reindeer, with antlers like branching rice plants.
reading: The reindeer's sound is "bi" (ビ) — like a "bee" buzzing around its antlers.

meaning: A deer (鹿) with a large (大) rack of antlers stands on a dotted cliff (广), comparing (比) itself to a smaller buck — this is the stag, the king of the hill.
reading: グ — A stag's antlers look like a giant 'G' hook, and it grunts 'goo' (グ) as it charges.

meaning: A fawn is a young deer (鹿) that still has its spotted coat — the spots are the compare (比) marks on its back, and it hides under a dotted cliff (广) with a mortar (臼) for a feeding bowl.
reading: The fawn's spots look like little 'ko-ji' (こじ) dots — imagine a fawn named Koji with polka dots. The reading is こじか.

meaning: Sweet, deer, two splayed strokes, compare, and a dotted cliff — a sweet deer with splayed horns on a cliff — this is the Chinese unicorn, a genius and bright beast.
reading: The unicorn's horn glows 'キ' (key) — it unlocks the cliff's secret, shining bright like a genius.

meaning: A deer with a compare and a tree under a dotted cliff — the foot of the mountain is where the deer compares the tree to the cliff, standing at the base.
reading: The foot of the mountain is a 'roku' (ロク) — picture a deer counting 'roku, roku' as it steps down the slope.

meaning: A grain stalk, deer, compare, and a box — a deer compares grain stalks inside a box — this shy roe deer hides in the box, eating grain.
reading: The roe deer's call is a soft 'キン' (kin) — like a bell in the box, it rings gently as it chews.

meaning: A deer with a graceful, beautiful face stands under a dotted cliff, while a compare sign (比) and an upside-down box (冂) frame it like a mirror — the whole scene is resplendent and lovely.
reading: A lovely deer is crowned with a wreath of 'ray' (レイ) of sunlight, each ray making its coat shine.

meaning: A deer (鹿) with a grain stalk (禾) and a tree (木) nearby, under a dotted cliff (广) — the scent of the forest and grain wafts from the deer's antlers. The day (日) and say (曰) are the sun warming the herbs, while the spoon (匕) and compare (比) show the deer sniffing to compare scents.
reading: The scent is so strong it fills the whole 'kyo' (キョウ) — like a 'kyo' (a Japanese unit of volume) of perfume. Say 'kyo' as in 'kyoto' but shorter.

meaning: A deer (鹿) with a bow (弓) and an ear (耳) — the fawn's ear is so big it looks like a bow, and it listens for its mother. The dotted cliff (广) is the forest edge, and the spoon (匕) and compare (比) are the fawn's wobbly legs as it compares scents.
reading: The fawn's cry is a soft 'bei' (ベイ) — like 'bay' as in a horse's neigh, but softer. Imagine a fawn calling out 'bei' in the bay.

meaning: A deer (鹿) with a dotted cliff (广) above it has a body (身) that carries a measurement (寸) of musk, and a compare (比) of its scent — the musk deer's gland is like a tiny ruler under its skin.
reading: The musk deer leaps 'ジャ' (ja) — imagine it jumping 'ja!' like 'ja' in 'jaguar', but the sound is just 'ジャ'.

meaning: A deer with a dotted cliff above, a day and compare inside, and a spoon and ten below — this roebuck stands on a rocky ledge. The sound of its hooves on the cliff echoes through the day — a shy roebuck.
reading: The roebuck's call is a soft 'SHOU' (ショウ) — like a gentle 'show' of itself in the clearing, brief and quiet.

meaning: A deer dances with compare and rice, under an evening dotted cliff — this magical creature is the Chinese unicorn, bright and rare.
reading: リン — The unicorn rings a 'lin' (like a bell) as it prances — each step makes a clear 'lin' chime.

meaning: Three deer, each with a spoon and a dotted cliff, are running apart — their rough, coarse movement makes the ground shake and they separate (はな.れる).
reading: The deer’s rough hooves go “SO (ソ)” — like the sound of scraping gravel as they scatter.

meaning: A person (人) walks under a ten (十) sun, then a stooping figure (夂) bends down to harvest the wheat.
reading: Imagine a giant bag of barley (麦) that goes 'BAK' when it bursts open, scattering grains everywhere.

meaning: A stooping figure bends over soil under a lid, planting two rows of barley.
reading: バク — The barley field goes 'bak' as the wind snaps the stalks.

meaning: A person under a lid, with two, ten, a stooping figure, and large — the person stoops under a large lid to bake light wheat-gluten bread, with two ten-shaped loaves rising.
reading: The light bread is 'FU' — imagine it floating up like a 'FU' of air, so light it drifts off the plate.

meaning: A person stops at a head, with ten and a stooping figure — the person stops at the head of the noodle stall, where ten bundles of wheat flour noodles hang, and a stooping figure serves them.
reading: The noodles are 'MEN' — picture a chef shouting 'MEN!' as he throws a handful of noodles into boiling water, like 'men' (people) diving in.

meaning: A person (人) wraps ten (十) grains in a wrapping enclosure (勹), then a stooping figure (夂) stops (已) to eat — it's a sticky rice ball, a snack you bend over to pick up.
reading: The sticky rice ball is 'hou' (ホウ) — you 'hoe' it into your mouth, but it sticks to your teeth.

meaning: A stooping figure (夂) stirs porridge in a pot made of ten (十) parts, with a person (人) adding the katakana-mu shape (厶) of grain, and soil (土) for the fire—this is porridge.
reading: The porridge bubbles 'kyo' (キョ) as it cooks—imagine the pot saying 'kyo' with each steam puff.

meaning: A stooping figure (夂) over a day (日) of work, using ten (十) strokes and a vertical stroke (｜) to mix rice (木) with a person (人) — this is yeast, the leaven that ferments.
reading: Yeast makes bread rise with a "kiku" (キク) — imagine it "kicking" the dough up.

meaning: A stooping figure (夂) carries a ten (十) and a person (人) over a tree (木) to feed a cow (牛) — but the cow only eats barley, so the whole scene is about barley.
reading: The cow (牛) says 'BOO' (ボウ) when it sees the barley — a loud, deep 'BOO' from the field.

meaning: A stooping figure (夂) is mixing rice (米) into a tree (木) stump with a wrapping enclosure (勹) around it, while a person (十) watches — that fermented mess is your yeast.
reading: Kiku — imagine a chef yelling 'KIKU!' as he sneezes into the rice, turning it into yeast.

meaning: A mask (面) made of flour and dough, with a tree (木) as a rolling pin, a person (人) and a stooping figure (夂) kneading it, and ten (十) fingers pressing down. The flour dust forms a lid (亠) on top.
reading: You knead the dough until it becomes 'men' (メン) — like 'men' in 'men's club' but with a soft 'e'. Imagine a chef shouting 'men!' as he serves noodles.

meaning: Under a lid (亠), a person (人) stands on soil (土) with two (二) hands, while a stooping figure (夂) carries a large (大) barley (麦) sack — this is the light wheat-gluten bread made from that barley.
reading: The bread is so light it 'whooshes' (フ) away when you blow on it — like a feathery 'fu' puff.

meaning: A lid (亠) covers a stooping figure (夂) who is mixing barley (麦) and rice (米) into the soil (土) — this is the moldy mash that becomes malt. The two (二) grains are the base, and the wrapping enclosure (勹) holds the fermenting mass.
reading: The malt smells like 'KIKU' — imagine a chrysanthemum (kiku) flower fermenting in a jar of barley and rice. (Reading: キク)

meaning: Barley (麦) is ground into flour, then a mask (面) covers a stooping figure (夂) who kneads the dough with soil (土) and two (二) hands under a lid (亠).
reading: メン — The noodles are so long that they wrap around a メン (men) mask, hiding the face behind a curtain of wheat.

meaning: A dotted cliff (广) overlooks a tree (木) — the tree is hemp, and touching it makes you numb.
reading: マ — Say 'ma' (マ) as you feel numb, like a soft 'ma' of surprise when your hand goes dead.

meaning: A dotted cliff is on top, and below it you have hemp, a tree, and a short thread. Imagine a rope made of hemp fibers, hanging from a dotted cliff, tied around a tree with a short thread — this is all about rope.
reading: The rope is made of hemp, and you use it to tie up a 'bee' (ビ) — picture a giant bee wrapped in a hemp rope, buzzing angrily.

meaning: A person under a lid, with two splayed strokes and a sword — the person is so small and insignificant that they hide under a lid, and the two splayed strokes and sword are just tiny props. The interrogative particle '麽' is a tiny word that questions everything.
reading: The tiny particle is 'MA' — imagine a tiny person saying 'MA?' (like 'what?') in a squeaky voice, so small you can barely hear it.

meaning: A hemp flag on a dotted cliff, with a tree and fur underneath — the general waves this fur-trimmed banner to beckon his troops forward.
reading: The general's command is a sharp 'ki!' — like a key turning in a lock, he beckons with a click.

meaning: A hemp (麻) tree (木) grows by a mouth (口) — this is the ancient personal pronoun 'I' (まろ), a humble self-reference from a person who works with hemp.
reading: まろ — 'Maro' (まろ) sounds like 'marrow' — imagine a person saying 'I am the marrow of this tree' as they point to themselves.

meaning: The color of ripe grain — imagine a field of yellow (黃) where the sun bleaches everything, a common surname for farmers.
reading: The yellow sun shouts 'kou' (コウ) — like a rooster's 'cock-a-doodle-doo' at dawn, waking the field.

meaning: A rice field with two splayed strokes on top — the strokes are yellow straws sticking up from the field, making the whole field look yellow.
reading: The yellow rice field is so bright it’s like a ko (コウ) — a giant yellow cow (コウ) standing in the field, mooing.

meaning: A king (王) in a rice field (田) sees yellow (黄) — he adds a dot (丶) and two splayed strokes (ハ) to his crown to make it more yellow, augmenting his power.
reading: The king shouts 'TOH!' (トウ) as he tosses yellow paint onto his crown — a sharp 'TOH' of augmentation.

meaning: A mortar with yellow rice fields inside, topped with a crown and to mix with — this is a school. The mortar grinds knowledge, the yellow fields are the students, and the crown sits on top as the principal's hat.
reading: School is 'コウ' — picture a teacher shouting 'KOU!' to get the class's attention, a loud 'コウ' that rings through the halls.

meaning: A grain stalk (禾) growing in water (水) — that's millet, a water-loving crop that feeds many.
reading: Millet is 'sho' (ショ) — you 'show' the grains to a friend, but they're so small you have to point them out.

meaning: Millet (黍) with a not (勿) sign on top, plus a grain stalk (禾) and water (水) — all mixed into a dark, black mush. Many grains, many dark seeds.
reading: It's 'rei' (レイ) — like 'ray' of darkness, a black ray that covers many things.

meaning: Millet (黍) mixed with water (水) and a grain stalk (禾) is stirred by a mouth (口) using a divining rod (卜) — the result is a sticky, glutinous glue that sticks to everything.
reading: The sticky millet paste goes 'NEN' (ネン) as it clings — like a soft, sticky 'NEN' sound when you pull it apart.

meaning: A sticky bird-lime is made by boiling millet (黍) in a pot with a lid (亠) and an open box enclosure (凵) underneath, stirred with a grain stalk (禾) and water (水) — the mixture traps birds (鳥) by their feet.
reading: The bird-lime is so sticky that when you try to pull your hand away, it makes a 'chee' sound — like the squeak of a rubber toy — and you say 'チ' (chi) as you struggle.

meaning: The ハ (two splayed strokes) sit on top of an upside-down box (冂) that is filled with four dots — like a dark, evil lid clamped over a box of soot. The whole shape is a black, sinister container.
reading: コク — Imagine a black crow (コク) with splayed claws (ハ) perched on an upside-down box (冂), cawing 'kok-kok-kok' in the dark.

meaning: The ri (里) village is under a dark cloud, and the four dots at the bottom (杰) are like drops of black rain falling from it.
reading: Imagine a black crow (くろ) sitting on a fence, cawing 'kuro, kuro' as it watches the village.

meaning: The black part is on top, and the ri (里) is below — imagine a black hat sitting on a rice field, dyeing everything under it black.
reading: The black hat is worn by a KEN (ケン) doll — think of a Ken doll with a black hat, standing in the field.

meaning: The black (黒) part is on top, and below it the soil (土) is covered with red — like red paint spilled over the black dirt, turning it red.
reading: The red paint spills with a TAN (タン) — imagine a loud 'tan!' as a red can hits the soil.

meaning: A dog (犬) sits under the black (黒) part — the black shadow makes the dog silent and still, not moving or barking.
reading: The silent dog is a BOKU (ボク) — picture a boy named Boku who shushes the dog, making it quiet.

meaning: A black (黒) dog (犬) sits on a ri (里) with four dots at the bottom (杰) — it stays silent, not barking, leaving things as they are.
reading: Say 'モク' (like 'moke') — a silent dog makes no sound, just a quiet 'moke' as it watches.

meaning: A person at the side (化) uses black (黒) powder to draw on the ri (里) of the eyebrow — the piling (弋) of the brush makes the blackened eyebrows, and the four dots at the bottom (杰) are the makeup specks.
reading: タイ — Think of a 'tie' (necktie) dipped in black ink, used to draw a bold eyebrow line.

meaning: A vertical stroke (｜) pokes through black (黒) and a mountain (山) of ri (里) — the four dots at the bottom (杰) are the black ink that draws back, retreating from the stroke.
reading: The black ink draws back with a 'CHUTSU' (チュツ) — like a quick, sucking 'CHUTSU' sound as it retreats.

meaning: Black (黒) covers the ri (里) — a short thread (幺) and power (力) pull the black over the mountain (山), leaving four dots at the bottom (杰) as the only light — all is black.
reading: The blackness whispers 'YUU' (ユウ) — a long, dark 'YUU' as it swallows the light.

meaning: A mouth (口) with a divining rod (卜) points at black (黒) and ri (里) — the four dots at the bottom (杰) are the points, marks, and specks that the rod touches on the black surface.
reading: The divining rod taps each point with a 'TEN' (テン) — a crisp, clicking 'TEN' for every mark.

meaning: Black (黒) soil (土) with four dots (杰) at the bottom, under a ri (里) and a mouth (口) — this is ebony, so black it shines like polished stone.
reading: エイ — 'Ei' (エイ) sounds like 'A' — picture a shiny black 'A' made of ebony, reflecting light.

meaning: A black (黒) gentleman (士) with a mouth (口) and a ri (里) — he's crafty, using his words to trick you out of your land (里).
reading: カツ — 'Katsu' (カツ) sounds like 'cat's' — a crafty cat's sly grin as it plots a trick.

meaning: A cover (奄) over black (黒) soil (土) with a large (大) sun (日) hidden underneath — the blue-black color of deep night. The two short strokes (并) are the stars, and the ri (里) is the village below, while the four dots (杰) are the dark clouds.
reading: The sky turns blue-black like an 'an' (アン) — as in 'an' in 'ant' but darker. Imagine an 'an' (a dark cave) swallowing the light.

meaning: Black (黒) ink is applied to the skin with a little (小) needle, and a mouth (口) screams in pain. The ri (里) is the pattern of lines, and the lid (亠) is the clamp holding the skin, while the four dots (杰) are drops of ink.
reading: The tattoo needle goes 'kei' (ケイ) — like 'kay' as in the letter K. Imagine the sound 'kei' as the needle taps.

meaning: A black (黒) face with a ri (里) pattern of wrinkles, all under a sweeping stroke (ノ) and two short strokes on top (并) — this is the dark, sallow color of an old, tired face.
reading: The dark sallow skin is so bad it looks like it's been 'laid' (レイ) flat in a coffin — imagine the pale-gray corpse color.

meaning: A black (黒) heart under a crown (冖) and esteem (尚) — the party (黨) is a group that esteems its own black-hearted members, all bound together like a faction.
reading: The party leader shouts 'Tō!' (トウ) like a gong to call the clique to a secret meeting — the sound echoes in the dark room.

meaning: Black soil with a box-on-side enclosure, a mouth, sweet, and ri inside — all covered by a lid and two short strokes on top. This dark, unclear private place is so black you can't see the sweet inside.
reading: The darkness is so thick you feel a heavy 'TAN' (タン) — like a dull thud in a black cave, muffled and private.

meaning: The sound (音) of a black (黒) day (日) in a ri (里) village, where even the stand up (立) figures are just four dots (杰) of darkness — everything is black and dark.
reading: アン — Imagine an "un" (as in "un-der") dark cave, where the blackness is so thick you can't see your hand — that's 黯.

meaning: A young girl's black hair (黒) is styled with a shellfish (貝) and an eye (目) on a spoon (匕) in a field of soil (土) with ten (十) mouths (口) and four dots (杰) – that's her hair style.
reading: The young girl's hair style is so shiny it makes your shin (シン) bone hurt.

meaning: Black with a hat on top, two short strokes, the katakana-mu shape, a mouth, soil, three, and four dots at the bottom — this is grey black, the color of soot and ash mixed with soil.
reading: The grey black color is like a 'SAN' (sand) storm that darkens the sky — 'SAN' as in 'sand'.

meaning: Black with a mountain and ri inside, plus stop, strike, and the 乞-shaped part — this is mold, which grows in dark, damp places (black + mountain) and spreads like a creeping strike.
reading: Mold smells like 'BAI' (as in 'bye' — you say 'bye' to fresh food when mold appears).

meaning: A black dog with a day on its back, standing on a ri, with a cliff and four dots at the bottom — that dark spot on the skin is a mole, a blemish from the earth.
reading: アン — The mole is 'an' (アン) as in 'ant', a tiny black dot crawling on the skin, right under the cliff.

meaning: The black gentleman and the shellfish are both covered in dirt from the ri field — the box of four dots at the bottom is stained too. Everything here is made dirty by the mud.
reading: トク — A dirty dock (トク) where the black mud sticks to every shellfish and gentleman's boot.

meaning: The two splayed strokes on top are needles, the upside-down box is a thimble, and the two short strokes on top are stitches — this is the sewing radical, showing needlework.
reading: The sewing needle goes チ (cheep) — like a chick's peep — as it pierces the cloth.

meaning: Two splayed strokes sit on top of an upside-down box, which is filled with sewing (黹) and a dot. The whole thing looks like an embroidered lap robe with a pattern of stitches and a single dot as a decorative mark.
reading: The lap robe is so fancy it makes you say 'FOOT-s' (フツ) as you trip over its long hem while walking.

meaning: Two splayed strokes (ハ) and two short strokes on top (并) sit above a sewing (黹) box with an upside-down box (冂) and a dot (丶) — all stitched onto a utilize (用) cloth as embroidery.
reading: Fu — picture a needle going 'FU-FU-FU' as it embroiders a fancy pattern.

meaning: A green frog that works hard — industry. Picture a green frog (the whole shape) with a vertical stroke (｜) as its backbone, and a one (一) as a lily pad it sits on, while the left-side kata (爿) and one-sided (片) parts are its legs, constantly paddling — industrious frog.
reading: The frog croaks 'bo' — a deep, booming 'bo' from its throat. The reading is ボウ.

meaning: A beginning (元) with a pair of legs (儿) sits on top of a green frog (黽). The frog is so huge it carries the beginning of the world on its back — a giant sea turtle.
reading: The sea turtle's shell is like a 'GEN' (ゲン) — a generation-old rock that never moves.

meaning: A green frog (黽) with one (一) day (日) on its back — this is a sea turtle, slow and ancient, carrying the sun across the ocean.
reading: チョウ — 'Chou' (チョウ) sounds like 'chow' — imagine a sea turtle eating 'chow' (food) on a sunny day.

meaning: A green frog (黽) sits on soil (土) — that's the edible water-frog, ready to be caught.
reading: Wai — the frog goes 'WAI!' as it leaps into the water.

meaning: A green frog with soil on its back, struck by a direction, carries a lid with two乞-shaped legs — this is the great sea turtle that holds up the world.
reading: ゴウ — The turtle says 'GO!' as it swims — a deep, slow 'gou' from its ancient throat.

meaning: A little esteem in an upside-down box, with a strike and a green frog below, and the 乞-shaped part on top — this is a snapping turtle. The little frog strikes the box, and the turtle snaps back from under the 乞-shaped shell.
reading: The turtle snaps 'ベツ' — imagine it biting with a 'BETSU!' sound, like a sharp 'ベツ' as it clamps down on a stick.

meaning: A green frog sits on a rice field, but its mouth is open wide — it's not a frog, it's a huge water lizard. The one thing that stands out is the one big jaw.
reading: The lizard's name is 'Ta' — like a giant 'ta' in a swamp, it snaps its jaws with a loud 'TA!' sound.

meaning: A three-legged kettle — ancient bronze vessel. See the eye (目) as the kettle's round belly, with a vertical stroke (｜) as the spout, a one (一) as the lid, and the one-sided (片) and left-side kata (爿) as the two side legs, plus another vertical stroke (｜) as the third leg — three legs total.
reading: The kettle sits on a 'tei' — think of a tea ceremony where the kettle is called 'tei' by the master. The reading is テイ.

meaning: A three-legged kettle with a one-sided lid, a crown on top, and an eye peeking out — the cover of the tripod cauldron is so tight you can see its eye through the crack.
reading: The lid goes 'beki' — like a cork popping off a bottle, a sharp 'beki' sound as it seals the cauldron.

meaning: A three-legged kettle with a one-sided lid, and a 'from' mark on top — this incense tripod is the one from which all sacred smoke rises.
